title: SSP calculating at incorrect rate
text:
Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a government-mandated payment that offers financial support to employees unable to work due to illness. SSP is calculated based on a standard 5-day workweek, but issues may arise if the system incorrectly divides it over 7 days. 

 

This miscalculation often results from incorrect employee work patterns or system configuration errors, leading to lower SSP payments than employees are entitled to receive.

 

SSP payments are configured at the organizational level to use either an employee's work pattern or qualifying days.

 

To review this configuration, follow these steps in portal.

Click Settings, then under UK Tax Rates, click General.

If the employee's Time/Workforce Management work pattern should take precedence over the OSSP qualifying days, select the Work Pattern indicator.

If necessary, select the Qualifying Days indicator and enable the appropriate days of the week for SSP eligibility.

title: SSP not generating
text:
According to SSP guidance, an employee's average earnings must exceed the Lower Earnings Limit (LEL). The Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) is calculated based on the eight weeks prior to the start of the Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW).

 

To qualify for SSP, ensure that employees have an average above the LEL for the past eight weeks.

 

If you wish to pay the employee SSP despite their AWE being lower than the LEL, you can update the Average Weekly Earnings toggle. 

 

To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Settings then under UK Tax Rates, click General. 

From the Pay Group Code drop down menu, select the relevant pay group

Under General, turn on Average Earnings toggle.

📌Note: Enabling this option means you will pay SSP regardless of an employee's AWE, even if it falls below the LEL. This adjustment will apply system-wide and affect all employees. You cannot configure this setting for an individual employee only.


If the AWE is incorrect, check the incorrect AWE for Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), as it affects all statutory sick pay calculations.

 

If the employee does have an average above the LEL, please raise a new case online, referencing this article's title and include the following details:

The dates for which SSP should have been generated.

The employee number.

title: No salary offset in payroll for an absence recorded in CoreTime
text:
If no salary offset appears for an employee regarding an absence recorded in CoreTime after running the future calculation of hours, generating salaries, and completing a full validation for the pay group, it likely means the employee has not been assigned an Absence/Sickness Category. Without this assignment, no sickness rule applies to the employee, and as a result, the salary will not be offset.

 

To assign a valid sickness category to the employee, follow the steps below in Back Office. 

Click CorePay then click Employee.

Click Maintain Employee Details then click Sundry.

Click Sickness Category. 

🤓Tip: If the field is blank, it indicates that the company has not set a default absence category code. 

Set a default absence category code then click Save.

Re-run the validation job. 

 The salary offset should now be visible for the employee.

title: Error: 'Statutory details must be added to an absence record via the Absence Entry screen'.
text:
If you try to add a statutory absence for an employee on the Maintain Statutory screen and encounter an error, it is because you must first log the absence in the Absences section located above Maintain Statutory.

 

To do this, follow these steps in the portal.

 

 

Maintain Statutory screen 

To make adjustments on this screen, follow the steps below. 

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW.

Click Statutory and Absences then click Absences.

For the relevant required absence, click the three-dot icon. 

Click Add Statutory Detail. 

Once you have added the statutory detail, you can use the Maintain Statutory screen.

 

 

Enable menu option

If you can't see the Add Statutory Detail button, it might be due to a lack of user access.

 

To view this button, you need to enable the Maintain Statutory WFM menu option. To do this, follow these steps. 

🤓Tip: A super user can provide access.

From the dashboard menu, select Security Dashboard.

Click User Management then In the search field, search for the relevant employee.

Click the three-dot icon then click Manage Account. 

Take note of the menu profiles assigned then click Menu Profiles.

Search for the relevant menu profile in step 4. 

Return to the Security dashboard then click Menu Profiles. 

In the search field, search for the menu profile in step 5.

Click the three-dot icon then click Manage Menu Options. 

To filter the systems, click the filter  icon

From the Filter By System dropdown menu, select all options. 

Click Apply then In the search field, search for the following menu option:

MAIN_MENU.MAINTAIN_STATUTORY_WFM ( Maintain Statutory WFM)

Turn on the toggle for the menu option. 

 

 
Absence Type

After providing user access, you need to associate the absence type with the statutory type.

 

To do this, follow the steps below. 

Click Settings then under Absence Configuration, click Absence Pay Parameters.

In the Company Code field, enter the relevant company code. 

From the Select Detail drop down menu, select Absence Types.

Check that the Statutory Type column is filled out appropriately.

 

 

General absence type

After setting the absence type, check that the general absence type has been set on the applicable absence pay code. To do this, follow the steps below.

 

Rules screen 

Click Settings then under Codes, click Pay Codes.

In the search field, search for the relevant pay code then highlight the pay group. 

Click the three dot icon then click Edit. 

Click Rules then set the General Absence Type as applicable.

Click Next then click SAVE.

 

Allowance tab

Click Settings then under Codes, click Pay Codes(Classic).

From the Pay Code drop-down menu, select the relevant pay code. 

Click Allowances/Payments then 

From the General Absence Type drop-down menu, select the relevant type as applicable.

Click Save.

title: Occupational salary offset for absence using wrong hourly date for daily rate employee
text:
If the hourly rate in the occupation salary offset is incorrect and does not match the employee's daily rate, you need to check for an overridden absence daily rate calculation setting for that employee.

 

To do this, follow the steps below in the portal.

 

 

Absence daily rate calculation setting

Check for an overriding absence daily rate calculation setting for the sickness category assigned to the employee by following these steps:

Click Settings then under Absence Configuration, click Absence Daily Rate Calculation.

Click Absence Rule Setting tab then for the relevant category, check the Daily Rate Override settings.

 If nothing is set there, check the Daily Rate Override settings for the relevant pay group.

 If no overrides are found in the previous steps, check the Daily Rate Calculation settings in the Company Settings.

To save changes, click SAVE.

 

 

No override set 

If no override is set and the company is configured to use annual salary, ensure there are no overrides set in the category settings. Follow these steps:

Click Settings then under Absence Configuration, click Absence Pay Parameters.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company.

From the Select Detail drop-down, select Absence Rules.

For the relevant sickness category, click the three-dot menu then click More.

Check the Days In Year Override.  

To save changes, click SAVE.

📌Note: Any value set here will take priority over the pay group settings when applying the sickness calculation for the hourly rate. i.e. ((Annual Salary / Days in Year) * Days in Week) / Employee Hours)

title: Portal: Add a new absence rule
text:
Adding a new absence rule is a crucial process in managing employee leave within your organization. This rule defines the policies and procedures for various types of absences, such as sick leave, vacation, and personal leave, ensuring clarity and compliance with labor laws.

 

Implementing a new absence rule is essential to creating a structured approach to managing leave, reducing potential disputes, and supporting effective resource planning. 

 

To create an absence rule for specific pay codes, or if the pay code absence rule is not configured appropriately, follow these steps below.

📌Note: If you use Back Office, follow these steps. 

Click Settings then under Absence Configuration, click Absence Pay Parameters.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company. 

From the Select Detail drop down menu, select Absence Rules. 

Beside the relevant Rule ID, click the three-dot icon then click Pay Codes.

🤓Tip: At least one paycode must be added in the rule ID

Click Add then fill in the necessary details. 

Click Save then to add a new rule, click the three-dot icon again. 

Click Entitlements then enter the required details.

Click Save then beside the relevant rule ID, click the three-dot icon again.

Click More then configure the necessary parameters.

📌Note: Many parameters may need to be configured. Alternatively, this can be pay code-specific. There are various configurations to choose from, depending on employee circumstances.

Click Save then from the Select Detail drop-down menu, select Absence Categories.

Beside the relevant category, under the Rules for Category section, check the rule ID is added.

To save changes, click SAVE.

title: Amend historical sick leave absence
text:
Amending sick leave when the payroll period is closed involves updating an employee's sick leave records to reflect any changes or corrections after payroll processing has been completed. 

 

If the payroll period is closed and you need to amend the historical sick leave, follow the steps in the relevant section below.

 

 

Portal
Amend absence 

To amend an absence, follow the steps below.

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW.

Click Statutory and Absences then highlight the relevant absence to be amended. 

Amend the absence then click Save.

 

Cancel taken days 

To cancel the taken days, follow the steps below.

Click Manage Payroll then click Inputs.

Click General then click Absence Manager.

From the Employee No drop-down menu, select the relevant employee. 

For the relevant absences that are no longer valid, select Cancel Absence. 

Click Save.

Depending on your software version, the absence will cancel once you amend it in the Absence Summary.
​

📌Note: If the amendment affects pay, complete the following steps. If it does not affect pay, for example, when the employee received full pay during the occupational absence, no pay adjustment is required.

 

Amend employee pay 

Add a manual timesheet to amend the employee’s pay. Follow the steps below. 

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW.

Click Timesheets current period then click ADD.

Enter the pay code for the adjustment then specify the adjustment amount.

Click OK then click Save.

The transaction date will automatically be populated to indicate the next pay period weekend date.

 

 

Back Office

 

Amend absence 

To amend the sick leave absence recorded, follow the steps below.

Click CoreTime then click Time Management. 

Click Record Absence Details. 

In the search field, search for employee.

Select the relevant absence to be amended then amend absence.  

Click Save.

 

Cancel taken days 

To cancel the taken days, follow the steps below.

Click CorePay then click Input. 

Click Advanced Input Features then click Absence Pay. 

Click Absence Manager Maintenance then query the relevant employee. 

For the relevant absences that are no longer valid, select Cancel Absence.

Select the Cancel Absence flag for absences that are no longer valid.

🤓Tip: These absences appear highlighted in wine color on-screen once cancelled, and the system will no longer count them when analyzing how much of the employee’s sick entitlement has been used.

To save changes, click Save.

Depending on your software version, the absence will cancel once you amend it in the Record Absence Details screen. 

📌Note: If the amendment affects pay, complete the following steps. If it does not affect pay, for example, when the employee received full pay during the occupational absence, no pay adjustment is required.

 

Amend employee pay 

To amend the employee’s pay, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePay then click Input. 

Click Timesheets then click Maintain Timesheets.

In the Employee field, search for the relevant employee.

Enter a pay code against which the adjustment should be output.

Enter a value for the adjustment amount.

To save changes, click the save  icon.

The transaction date will automatically be populated to indicate the next pay period weekend date.

title: Back Office: Amend the leave start date or end date for SMP or SPP
text:
To amend the leave start date or end date for Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) or Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) in PeopleXD Payroll, you need to update the official dates related to an employee's leave entitlement.

 

You should take this action when you notice errors in the recorded dates, changes in the employee's circumstances, or necessary adjustments for regulatory compliance.

 

Please make these amendments as soon as you identify any discrepancies, especially before processing payroll or issuing payments.

 

To do this, follow the steps below in Back Office. 

Click CorePay then click Input.

Click Statutory Pay then click Maintain SMP Details.

In the Employee field, enter the employee number. 

In the Leave Start Date field, enter the date. 

In the End Date field, enter a date.

Query the employee number here. 

To save changes, click the save  icon.

📌Note: After re-running the full validation, the payment start date will automatically update to match the new leave start date. The number of SMP days paid will now reflect the corrections made on this screen.

title: Maternity salary offset not generating
text:
The maternity salary offset not generating is where the system fails to automatically calculate or apply the correct salary adjustments during an employee's maternity leave period. 

 

This typically occurs due to incorrect system configurations, missing employee data, or setup errors in the maternity pay parameters.

 

To resolve this, check the settings for the salary offset. To do this, follow the steps below. 

 

 

Check sickness category code

To check if there is a sickness category code is entered for an employee, follow the steps below in Portal.

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant Employee, click VIEW.

Click Employee Pension then click Sundry Profile.

Click the Work Details tab then check if anything is set in Sickness Catergory code field.

 

 

Check the default settings

To check the default settings, follow the steps. 

Click Settings then click Absence Pay Parameters.

🤓Tip: The default will show in the Default Absence Category Code box.

 

If the employee appears with a non-default sickness category, check whether the code is active by following these steps on the screen above.

From the Select Detail drop down menu, select Absence Categories.

Check to see if the Category is turned on.

title: Sickness not paying after change of entitlement
text:
If an employee has changed their entitlement band and the sickness pay is not being processed, or if the employee is now eligible for occupational payment but is not receiving it due to the number of historic sickness days, this issue stems from a configuration problem on the Absence Pay Parameters screen.

 

To resolve this issue, check the configuration of the sickness rule under the Use Payment Multiplier to Get Taken field. To do this, follow the steps below in Portal.

Click Settings then under Absence Configuration, click Absence Pay Parameters.

From the Company Code drop-down menu, select the required company.

From the Select Detail box, click Absence Rules.

Beside the relevant absence rule required, click the three dot icon then click More.

📌Note: If the field below is blank, the system counts all sickness days regardless of the pay multiplier. 

From the Use Payment Multiplier to get Taken, drop- down menu, select Match Against Range Multiplier.

Click Save.

text:
To change the absence category at an employee level, you need to check the absence rule the employee falls under.

title: Set up rolled up holiday pay
text:
Rolled-up holiday pay ensures that employees with irregular hours or patterns receive their holiday pay spread across each pay period, rather than as a lump sum when they take their leave.

 

This method complies with legislation requiring holiday pay to reflect regular earnings, including overtime and bonuses, by adding a proportionate amount to each payment.

 

 

Set up rolled-up holiday pay

Create a percentage-based pay code: Create a new percentage based pay code using the pay code wizard. This should have a percentage of 12.07% to reflect the statutory calculation for allocating holiday pay.

Set up the pay code formula: When setting up the pay code specify which earnings should be considered for the holiday pay calculation. Typically, this includes all basic pay codes and any overtime pay codes. These selections ensure that the rolled-up holiday pay reflects an employee's regular earnings.

Assign to employees: Assign the pay code to your employees. Each pay period, a percentage of the designated earnings will be automatically calculated and added to their pay as rolled-up holiday pay, ensuring compliance with the legislation.

Manage Absences

To account for absences and ensure accurate holiday pay calculations:

Download the Insight report: From the Insight report store, download the  'Irregular Paid Employees - Absence Holiday Pay Calculation' report. This report helps identify employees absent during the current pay period and provides a detailed history of their earnings over a specified period (e.g., 52 weeks) for accurate calculation. 

Override ralculations: With the report's information, you can manually adjust the rolled-up holiday pay for absent employees, ensuring their holiday pay reflects their average earnings accurately.

XD Workforce Management

WFM have introduced a New Holiday Entitlement Accrual screen to allows UK customers to set up Accruals for Irregular hour workers where employees accrue leave to book time off.

Enhanced holiday pay calculation: We recommend you set up the enhanced holiday pay calculation feature, ensuring that holiday pay is correctly calculated and disbursed when employees take their leave.

title: Error: 'ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: number precision too large'
text:
If you enter a negate in the leave details field on the Maintain Leave Without Pay screen, you may encounter the following error:

**Start UnHandled Exception  

SOURCEREF: s37000_insert_day_history  

EMPNO: XXXXXX  

ERRNO: -6502  

ERRMESS: ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: number precision too large.**

 

This error can cause the PAY140 file to fail. To troubleshoot the issue, check the `number_of_units` in the log file. If this number exceeds 999, it will indeed cause the PAY140 to fail.

 

Here are the steps to resolve the issue:

 

1. Retrieve the PAY140.trcXXXX file, where XXXX represents the pay group.

2. Review the ERRDATA row, as the system only permits values up to 999.

 

If the negate value is greater than 999, it is recommended to split the negate into two parts. For instance, negate half of the amount in one period and the other half in a subsequent period. This approach is necessary due to user access rights.

title: Message - SMP not enough service, joined DD-MMM-YY needed to join by DD-MMM-DD
text:
When calculating SMP, the system uses the employee's latest start date. In this example, the employee left the company and rejoined the next day, which counts as continuous employment.

 

The system reflects the rejoin date as the joined date. The company has the TUPE date feature enabled, which means that when this setting is turned on (Y), the system uses the latest start date as the basis for the employee's joined date.


To check the indicator, follow the steps below in Portal. 

Click Settings, then under UK Tax Rates, click General.

Under General, enable the HR Tupe Date toggle.

Click Save.

📌Note: You can either disable this option or enter a TUPE date for the employee to ensure the system uses the correct start date.

title: Absence entitlements are not being applied
text:
If an employee is expected to receive occupational absence pay based on their length of service but is not receiving it, several reasons may be responsible.

 

To help you resolve this issue, we've compiled a few steps to check.

 

 

Check employee's entitlements 

To verify the employee's entitlements, follow the steps below in Portal.

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW then click Absence Summary.

Click the Information Per Absence Type tab.

From the Absence Type dropdown menu, select the relevant absence type. 

If the entitlement appears incorrect on this screen, ensure that the employee is assigned to the correct sickness category code and that the entitlements are configured properly in your settings.

 

If the employee is on the correct sickness category code and the entitlements are set up correctly but the issue still persists, please raise a new case online. Reference the title of this article and include the following details:

Employee reference

Absence start and end dates

Absence pay code

Entitlements currently being applied.

Details of the entitlements you expect to be applied.

title: Incorrect sickness rule applied to employee
text:
When an incorrect sickness scheme is applied to an employee, the system may miscalculate their entitlement. 

 

To ensure accurate processing, assign the correct sickness rule by checking the following: 

 

 

Sickness category code at employee level

First, verify the sickness category code for the employee. To do this, follow these steps.     

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW then click Sundry Profile.

Take note of the sickness category code.

 

 

Rule assigned 

Next, check the rule assigned to the sickness category code. To do this, follow these steps. 

Click Settings then under Absence Configuration, click Absence Pay Parameters.

From the Company Code dropdown menu, select the relevant company.

title: Enter statutory absence record for a dormant employee
text:
When managing statutory absences, it's important to note that absence records cannot be entered for dormant employees. This is because dormant employees are not considered actively employed, which affects their eligibility for statutory payments.

 

 

Verifying employee entitlement

To determine whether an employee qualifies for statutory absence payments, use the HMRC statutory absence calculator. Check the following: 

Populate the correct notice period.

Verify if the employee was in active employment during the qualifying week.

For detailed guidance, refer to HMRC’s Maternity Benefits Technical Guidance.

 

Processing payment

If the employee is entitled, there are three available options to process the payment. By following these steps, you can ensure compliance and accuracy when handling statutory absence records.

 

Option 1

Temporary rejoin the employee in Portal or Back Office.

Input a manual timesheet for a lump sum against the maternity code in Portal.

This option has no absence record, and as a temporary rejoiner, the tax code will be 0T, resulting in extra tax charges. The employee will need to claim a tax return.

 

Option 2

Rejoin the employee (the day after the employee's leave date).

Enter the absence record. To do this, follow these steps:

Click Employee then in the Search field, search for the relevant employee.

Under Statutory and Absences, click Absences.

Click Add then fill the leave type and the details from steps 1 to 6 on the screen.

Click Save. 

For more information on absence records, check the Maintain Statutory Payments (UK) user guide. 

Input a manual timesheet for a lump sum against the maternity code in Portal.

Make employee dormant (same date as rejoin). 

Negate the salary and offset amounts, leaving only the lump sum and its corresponding tax.

 

Option 3

Rejoin the employee (the day after the employee's leave date).

Enter the absence record. To do this, follow these steps:

Click Employee then in the Search field, search for the relevant employee.

Under Statutory and Absences, click Absences.

Click Add then fill the leave type and the details from steps 1 to 6 on the screen.

Click Save.  

For more information on absence records, check the Maintain Statutory Payments (UK) user guide. 

Process the employee's maternity payroll and pay them monthly as usual.

Make the employee dormant when the maternity ends.

title: Configure the Absence Cut Off feature
text:
You can use the Absence Cut Off feature to run payroll validation without automatically including absences from PeopleXD Workforce Management. This gives you more control over your payroll figures, and you can decide when to include PeopleXD Workforce Management absences in your payroll run.

📌 Note: This only affects absences you record in PeopleXD Workforce Management, not absences you enter directly in PeopleXD Payroll.

Enable Absence Cut Off

Once the support team enable the feature flag, you need to turn on the admin setting. To do this, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Site Manager.

Click Open Admin Settings, then search for cp_manual_absence_run.

Click Edit then change the value to Y.

Click OK.

 

 

PeopleXD Workforce Management absence status

After enabling the feature, you can monitor and control PeopleXD Workforce Management absence inclusion from the Payroll Dashboard. The Mode column displays a WFM ABSENCE indicator showing the current status for each pay group.

Green: Means absences were included in the last validation run. If you run validation from the Process Payroll screen, absences are included.

Red: Means absences weren't included in the last validation run. If you run validation from the Process Payroll screen, absences aren't included.

📌 Note: At the start of each payroll period, the default setting includes absences in validation runs.

 

Include PeopleXD Workforce Management absences

If required, to change whether absences are included in validation for each pay group, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

On the Payroll Dashboard, click Manage Payroll. 

For the relevant pay group, click the three-dot menu.

Select Enable WFM Absence or Disable WFM Absence.

title: Configure enhanced holiday pay
text:
To calculate holiday pay based on average earnings in PeopleXD Payroll, you can use enhanced holiday pay. To set this up, you need to configure global settings, pay group and pay code parameters, rules and inclusions. 

 

Configure global settings

To control when enhanced holiday pay processing begins and which employees to include in calculations, follow the steps below.

Click Settings then click Enhanced Holiday Pay.

Click Actions then click Edit Holiday Pay Effective Date.

Update the following fields:

Holiday pay effective date: The date enhanced holiday pay processing begins. Annual leave only processes after this date.

Holiday pay inclusion type: The reference field that identifies employees for calculations, such as job title, position, or department. 

Use standard contract rate: If required, to calculate based on contracted hours rather than FTE hours, turn this on. This only applies to salaried employees.

Statutory cap multiplier: Overwrites the entitlement hours assigned to the pay group when used with holiday pay rules.

Click OK.

 

 

Configure pay group parameters

To control how to calculate and record holiday pay for each pay group, including the calculation method, output pay codes, and annual leave year dates, you need to set the pay group parameters.

Click Settings, then click Enhanced Holiday Pay.

Click the Pay group parameters tab, then search for the relevant pay group.

Click the three-dot menu, then select Edit Row.

Update the relevant fields, as per the table below.

Click OK.

Field
	
Description



Calculation Method

	

To use average earnings, select Average. To use the employee's contract rate, select Contractual. 




Core Time Used for Holiday Recording

	

If you record annual leave in PeopleXD Workforce Management, turn this on. If you record in PeopleXD Payroll, turn this off. 




Processing Range

	

To use payroll period dates, select Period Range. To use submitted holiday dates, select Date Range.




Include Public Holidays

	

If required, to count public holidays as annual leave days, turn this on.




Holiday Pay History Weeks

	

Enter the number of weeks to look back when calculating average pay. This is typically 52 weeks.




Standard Holiday Pay Output Pay Code

	

Enter the pay code for standard holiday pay top-up. This is a requirement for timesheet employees.




Enhanced Holiday Pay Output Pay Code

	

Enter the pay code for the enhanced holiday pay element. This is a requirement for all employees.




Annual Leave Start Date

	

Enter the annual leave year start date.




Annual Leave End Date

	

Enter the annual leave year end date.




Include Salary EE's Absence Validation

	

To include salaried employees in skipping weeks, and bring absences from PeopleXD Workforce Management as separate records, turn this on.

📌 Note: If you use PeopleXD Workforce Management for annual leave, your annual leave calendar settings apply. If you use PeopleXD Payroll, the dates you enter roll forward for future years.

 

 

Configure pay code parameters

To identify which pay codes trigger holiday pay calculations and which earnings contribute to the standard and enhanced rate calculations, you need to set the pay code parameters.

Click Settings, then click Enhanced Holiday Pay.

Click the Pay code parameters tab, then search for the relevant pay code.

Click the three-dot menu, then select Edit Row.

Update the relevant indicators, as per the table below.

Click OK.

Indicator
	
Description



Holiday Pay

	

Turn this on for the pay codes you want to use to record annual leave. This triggers the holiday pay calculation.




Holiday Pay Element

	

Turn this on for the pay codes you want to use to calculate the standard rate of pay.




Enhanced Holiday Pay Element

	

Turn this on for the pay codes you want to use to calculate the enhanced rate of pay.




Exclude Pay Code

	

Turn this on for the pay codes you want to exclude from calculations.




Exclude Hours

	

Turn this on for the positive input employees where you want to include overtime values but exclude hours.

📌 Note: For salaried employees, the holiday leave pay code needs a multiplier of 1. For timesheet employees, it needs a multiplier of 0.

 

 

Configure holiday pay rules

Holiday pay rules determine how many days or hours are paid at the enhanced rate. 

Click Settings, then click Enhanced Holiday Pay.

Click the Holiday pay rules tab, then search for the rule element.

Click the three-dot menu, then select Edit Row.

Enter the enhanced holiday pay days or hours, as required.

If required, to calculate for part-time employees, turn on Apply FTE Proration.

If required, to overwrite the pay group entitlement hours, turn on Statutory Cap.

Click OK.

⚠️ Important: The system works on one rule type only. If you create a new rule with a different rule type, this overrides the previous rule.

 

 

Configure inclusions

To determine which employees to process in holiday pay calculations, based on the reference rule type in global settings, you can set inclusions.

Click Settings, then click Enhanced Holiday Pay.

Click the Inclusions tab, then search for the rule element.

Click the three-dot menu, then select Edit Row.

Turn on Holiday Pay Inclusion, then click OK.

 

 

Configure absence pay parameters

To exclude periods from the holiday pay average calculation, you can set absence pay parameters. 

Click Settings, then click Absence Pay Parameters.

From the drop-down menu, select the relevant company code.

From the Select Detail drop-down menu, select Absence Types.

For each relevant absence type, turn on Holiday Pay Inclusion.

Click Save.

📌 Note: If a period within the previous 52 weeks contains an absence type marked as included, the calculation skips this period and uses an earlier period instead. PeopleXD looks back up to 104 weeks.

 

 

Configure payslip display

To group how holiday pay payments display on employee payslips, you can use the Payslip Pay Code rule.

Click Settings then click Pay Codes.

Search for the relevant pay code, then click the three-dot menu.

Select Edit, then click Step 2 Rules.

Click Add then, select Payslip Code Override from the Rule drop-down list.

Update the Value, then click OK.

Click Next, then click Save.

 

 

Menu options required

To access the enhanced holiday pay configuration screens you need access to the following menu options:

System
	
Menu Option



CorePortal Pay

	

Settings - Holiday Pay

Settings - Absence Pay Parameters

Settings - Pay Codes

title: View an employee's occupational sickness payment details
text:
The Occupational Detail screen in Portal lets you view occupational absence details for an employee, including absence dates and payments. 

 

To access this screen, you need to enable the relevant menu options listed below.

 

View Occupational Detail screen

Follow the steps below to open the Occupational Detail screen.

Click Employee then in the search field, search for an employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW then click Occupational Detail.

📌 Note: By default, occupational absences group by absence start date.

 

View in regular mode

When viewing the absence dates and payments in the Occupational Detail screen in regular mode, the following columns display.

Column
	
Description



Payroll Period

	

This column displays the payroll period in which the absence was processed – format: Monthly = MMM-YYYY, e.g., Mar-2020. Weekly/Fortnightly/Four Weekly = period number, e.g., 202026.




Absence Date

	

This column displays the date on which the absence occurred.




Days/Hours

	

Days/Hours depends on the calculation basis selected in the Absence Entitlement Range.




Multiplier

	

The Pay Multiplier applied to the days/hours to calculate the absence daily rate.




Payment

	

This column displays the occupational absence payment for the absence days/hours taken – Rate x Absence Days/Hours x Multiplier x Roster Multiplier (where applicable).




Salary Offset

	

The occupational salary offset reduces an employee's salary for the absence.




Pay Code

	

This column displays the absence pay code number and the pay code description.




Pattern

	

This column displays the work pattern day, i.e. Work or Rest.




Information Field

	

This column displays the information related to the absence day:

Cancelled

Pending Reversal

Reversed

Predicted




Multi Appointment Only

	

 




Appointment ID

	

This column displays the appointment ID against which the absence was entered.

 

View in full screen

When viewing the absence dates and payments in the Occupational Detail screen in full screen mode, the following additional columns display.

Column
	
Description



Only applicable to Irish people

	

 




SW Days

	

This column displays the social welfare days associated with the absence.




SW Value (Tax)

	

This column displays the taxable value of the social welfare payment.




SW Value (Non Tax)

	

This column displays the non-taxable value of the social welfare payment.




Multi Appointment Only

	

 




Appointment Title

	

This column displays the appointment title against which the absence was entered.




Paid Days

	

This column displays the days paid associated with the absence.




Paid Hours

	

This column displays the hours paid associated with the absence.




Paid Pro-rata Days

	

This column displays the pro-rata days paid associated with the absence, i.e. the paid days * roster multiplier where a roster multiplier is applied to the absence rule.




Paid Pro-rata Hours

	

This column displays the pro-rata hours paid associated with the absence, i.e. the paid hours * roster multiplier where a roster multiplier is applied to the absence rule.

 

 

Calculation explanation

This read-only screen shows how the absence daily or hourly rate was calculated and how the pay multiplier was determined. The following information displays:

Length of Service

Entitlement

Daily/Hourly Rate Calculation

To open the Calculation Explanation screen, follow the steps below.

title: Portal: Reset a bank paypath file
text:
You may need to reset a bank paypath file if the original file contains errors, requires updates to the processing date, or needs to be saved in a different location. 

 

Resetting the bank file ensures accurate payroll processing and helps avoid incorrect payments or file submissions.

 

📌Note: If you use back office, follow these steps.

 

Reset bank file 

To reset a bank paypath file, follow the steps below in portal. 

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group. 

Click Outputs then click Bank File

From the Report Name drop-down menu, select Reset Paypath.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company.

In the Processing Date field, enter the processing date when the paypath was generated. 

On your keyboard, press the Tab key.

🤓Tip: The Sort Code/Account No. or BIC/IBAN and User ID/Orig. ID. fields will auto-populate as you tab through. A list of any pay groups associated with the company number and processing date will appear.

If applicable, check the Reset check box. For older versions, click Exclude Pay Group.

Click the RESET icon to reset pay groups as required. 

Note that no report is generated as part of the reset process.

A notification message will confirm that the reset has been completed successfully.

From the Report Name drop-down menu, select Paypath Processing.

Generate the Paypath file again as necessary.

📌Note: If you reset and regenerate the bank paypath file after completing a Cancel Manual Payment job, the number of employees will remain the same; however, there should be a 'C' next to the employee(s) whose payment was cancelled.

Establishing a foreign bank account is essential for businesses operating internationally, as it facilitates efficient handling of cross-border transactions, currency conversions, and timely payment of employee salaries in their local currencies.

Click Settings and then under Banking, click Bank Identifiers.

If the identifier is not there, set a new line for the bank.

 

Check BIC details

Click Settings then under Banking, click Bank Details.

title: Generate a bank file
text:
Generating a bank file in Portal is a critical step in the payroll process that enables you to facilitate direct deposits for employee salaries and manage other financial transactions efficiently.

 

This process involves creating a digital file that contains all necessary payment details, such as employee banking information, payment amounts, and transaction dates, which can then be submitted to the bank for processing.

 

To generate a bank file, follow the steps below in Portal.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click the Outputs tab then click Bank File.

From the Company drop-down menu, select a Company or turn on the All Companies toggle.

title: Court Order reference not appearing on bank file
text:
If the Court Order reference does not appear on the bank file, it may be due to one of two reasons.

 

We’ve compiled a list of possible reasons and how to resolve them.

 

 

Building Society Reference not populated

The Building Society Reference field is empty. The reference on a Direct Earnings Attachment (DEA) included in the file comes from the Building Society Reference field attached to the employee's deduction.
​ 

To update the reference, follow the steps below in Portal.

Click Employee then in the search field, search for employee.

Beside the relevant employee, click VIEW.

Click Deductions then beside the relevant deduction, click the three-dot icon. 

In the Building Society Reference field, update the value. 

To save changes, click Save. 

 

 

Building Society Reference updated after payroll job

If the Building Society Reference was populated after running the payroll/Complete Update job, it will appear on the bank file when you process the next period.

 

To resolve this issue, please contact our support team to run an update.Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article. Include the following details:

The building society reference

Employee number 

Affected payroll period.

title: Updated BACS and Albany BACS file format
text:
Albany and BACS files are standardized formats used for processing electronic payments, such as payroll and supplier transactions, in the UK. These files ensure that payment instructions are accurately communicated to banks, enabling smooth and secure transfers

 

To generate and submit these files whenever you process payments through the Albany or BACS systems during payroll runs, you need to follow the following formats highlighted below for the files. 

 

 

Albany files

For Albany BACS .csv file, the following fields should be present in the file. 

Sort Code (field length 6) 

Account No (field length 8) 

Account Name

Value

Building Society Ref

Reference (employee name)

 

BACS files

For BACS files, the following fields should be present in the file. 

📌Note: The BACS file should not contain any headers/footers

Sort Code (field length 6) 

Account No (field length 8)  

'099' (field length 3)  

Company Sort Code (field length 6)  

Company Account No. (field length 8)  

'0000' (field length 4)  

Value (field length 11) 

Company Name (field length 18)  

Building Society Ref (field length 18)  

Employee Name (field length 18)  

RTI Hash Tag (field length 4)

title: Error: 'Entry at Start date as least 2 address fields must be populated'
text:
When submitting an RTI file, you may encounter the above error message in the RTI Exception Report. This error appears because the system requires at least two address fields to be populated for an employee. If these fields are missing or incomplete, the RTI file cannot be processed.

 

To resolve this issue, update the employee’s address information and regenerate the RTI file by following the steps below in Portal. 

 

 

Update employee address date

To check the effective date of the employee’s address information, follow these steps. 

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Beside Employees click View.

In the Search Name field, search for employee.

Highlight the relevant employee then click View.

Click Contact Information.

Under My Address Details, check the effective date of at least 2 addresses.

If you need to update the effective date, click the three dot icon.

Click Edit Address Details. 

In the Date effective field, select the appropriate effective date. 

Click Save.

 

 

Regenerate and resubmit the RTI file

After updating the effective dates for the address, regenerate the RTI file and submit file for processing.

title: Load position rates of pay
text:
Loading position rates of pay involves entering or updating the compensation rates assigned to various job positions within your organization. This practice is essential for ensuring accurate payroll calculations and maintaining compliance with internal pay structures and external regulations. 

 

By correctly loading position rates of pay, you ensure that employees receive the appropriate compensation for their roles. 

 

We've compiled a list of steps to guide you on how to load, view, delete and carry out bulk updates for employees on a position rate.

 

 

Upload rates

To upload new position rates of pay for an employee, follow the steps below.  

Create your CSV file.

The table below describes the fields that are available for loading new position rates of pay. The order of the fields is critical and should be aligned with this table.

Field Name
	
Contents



Position

	

Position Scale/Grade as held via the Position References field.




Point

	

Scale Point(s) associated with the Position Reference




Rate Sequence

	

Always 1 (change accordingly for environments that use rate sequence ) 




Date Effective

	

DDMMYYYY




Hourly Rate

	

Define value, otherwise set to 0 if not used




Daily Rate

	

Define value, otherwise set to 0 or leave null if not used




Weekly Rate

	

Define value, otherwise set to 0 or leave null if not used




Annual Salary

	

Define value, otherwise set to 0 or leave null if not used




Unit Type

	

Define value, otherwise set to 0 or leave null if not used

Portal

After creating your CSV file with the fields, log in to portal and follow the steps below. 

Click Uploads then under Rate of Pay Uploads, click Load Position Rates of Pay.

In the Reference field, enter a reference number then for File Type, select CSV.

To locate and upload the relevant CSV file, click Browse.

To complete the upload, click OK.

The new position rates will be uploaded on the PeopleXD system with new effective date. Once the system date reaches the new effective date, the system will create new salary for employees based on the rate effective. 

 

📌Note: Rates are read by date effective and date input. If you input rate today for 01/09/22 and then input new rates in 3 months time for effective 01/09/22 they should all calculate arrears.

 

 

Delete incorrect upload

To delete the incorrect position rate of a pay file, follow the steps below.  

Click Uploads. 

Under Rate of Pay Uploads, click Load Position Rates of Pay.

In the Reference field, enter the reference for the load that was used during the original upload.

Click Delete.

title: Configure payslip parameters
text:
Payslip parameters are specific settings that determine how employee payslips are generated and displayed, including details such as earnings, deductions, and formatting options.

 

Configuring these parameters is essential for ensuring that payslips accurately reflect employees' compensation and comply with legal requirements.

 

To configure payslip parameters:

Click Settings then click System Configuration.

Click Payslip then update the required options.

Click X then click Save.

The fields available to configure the parameters are: 

 

Standard paper payslip
Field
	
Description



Number of Allowance Lines

	

Enter the max number of lines to be displayed for allowances on the payslip. Max number 12.




Number of Deduction Lines

	

Enter the max number of lines to be displayed for deductions on the payslip. Max number 12.




Allowances Miscellaneous Pay Code

	

Enter the Miscellaneous Pay Code that will be used to group the Allowances exceeding the number of Allowance Lines on the payslip.




Deductions Miscellaneous Pay Code

	

Enter the Miscellaneous Pay Code that will be used to group the Deductions exceeding the number of Deduction Lines on the payslip.




Payslip ER Remittance Method

	

Enter 1 or leave blank to automatically print ER remittance on user request. 
Enter 2 to print ER remittance for selected Pay Codes for a range or Payroll Periods.




Pre Tax Deductions Label

	

Enter a label for the pre tax deductions field of the Copy Payslip or leave blank for “Pension”.




Print Payslip Rate

	

Enable to display a Rate column between Hours and Value on the payment side of the payslip.




Enable Advanced Printing

	

Enables advanced printing of payslips on the Print Payslip/Cheque screen.
Only enable if your payslips have been customised to cater for advanced printing. 




Use Complete Update Dates

	

Enable if the Payslip/Cheque screen is to default to the Complete Update date but use the last day of the month for monthly. 




Restrict Cheque Printing

	

Enable to restrict printing of cheques based on the menu profile of the user. 




Display ER Reg Number

	

Enable to display ER Reg Number.




Hide Employer Pension

	

Enable to hide the Employer Pension field.




View Employer Name

	

Enable to display the Employer Name field.




Hide Payslip Logo

	

Enable to hide the payslip logo.




Align Payslip Logo Right

	

Enable to align the payslips logo to the right.




Pre Complete Update UK payslip

	

Enable to allow the UK payslip to be run at validation stage from the View Gross to Nett screen.




Job Title on Payslip

	

Enable for the Portal payslip to show job title instead of the pay code description for salaries against the additional salary pay code. 




Exclude SS from Pension on Payslip

	

Enable to exclude salary sacrifice pension schemes from the pension EE and ER values. 




Print Empno on Payslip

	

Enable to display the employee reference number on the UK/IRE Paper Payslip.




Display Apprentice Levy

	

Enable to display Apprentice Levy on the payslip.




Show Hourly Allowances on Payslip

	

Enable for hourly allowances with no value to be shown on the payslip.

 Copy Payslip
Field
	
Description



Home Address

	

Enter Y to display home address on copy payslip.

title: Update to SEPA mode
text:
The Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) is the European Union's initiative aimed at integrating payment systems to standardize euro transactions across participating countries. This initiative allows for seamless electronic payments using unified formats and procedures.

 

Organizations need to update their SEPA mode settings when they expand operations into new European markets, change banking relationships, or adapt to evolving regulatory requirements.

 

CorePersonnel offers three distinct SEPA modes to meet various banking requirements and operational needs:

Mode 1: Bank sort code and bank account number only.

Mode 2: Bank sort code, bank account number, BIC and IBAN.

Mode 3: BIC and IBAN only.

Initially, we place clients in Mode 2 to allow them to generate both the old bank files and the new SEPA files. Once clients are satisfied with the SEPA files, we switch them to Mode 3, as the old bank details become irrelevant.
​
Regarding Portal:

In Mode 1, users see the account and sort code.

In Mode 2, users see the account and sort code.

In Mode 3, users see the BIC and IBAN.

If you need to update the SEPA mode for all companies or for specific companies, please raise a new case online. Reference the title of this article and include details of the companies that need updating.

title: Configure pay scales
text:
Pay scales are structured salary frameworks that define compensation levels within an organization. They are typically organized by job grades, experience levels, and performance criteria.

 

Scale points establish specific incremental steps within each pay scale, while rates assign actual monetary values to each point. This comprehensive compensation structure ensures fair and consistent remuneration across the workforce.

 

Implementing pay scales helps maintain salary equity and supports career progression planning that aligns with industry standards and internal budgets. It is essential to create scale points and add rates when developing new job classifications, conducting annual pay reviews, or restructuring existing compensation frameworks.

 

To assist you with this, please watch the video or follow the steps outlined below.

 

Add a pay scale

To add a pay scale, follow these steps. 

Click Settings then under Pay Rates, click Position Reference.

Click Add then in the Position Code field, enter new code. 

In the Description field, enter a code description. 

Update any necessary options then add as many pay scales required.

Click Save.

 

 

Set up scale points

To set up a new scale point, follow these steps. 

Click Settings then under Pay Rates, click Scale Point Profile.

From the Position Code drop-down menu, select a code to view or amend.

To add a new scale point, click Add. 

In the Scale Point field, enter the relevant code. 

In the Scale Narrative field, enter a description. 

Update any of the additional options as required then click Save.

 

 

Define rates of pay

Click Pay Rates.

Under View and Add Pay Rate by Code, click Add Position Rates. 

To add new rates, from the Position drop-down menu, select a relevant code. 

From the Date Effective field, select the effective date.

Click ADD then in the Scale Point field, enter a scale point code.

Fill the following fields: 

Hourly Rate 

Daily Rate

Annual Salary 

Weekly Rate 

Unit Rate 

Click Save.

title: Configure the payroll calendar
text:
A payroll calendar outlines the specific periods for processing payroll, including pay and cut-off dates for timekeeping and payroll submissions.

 

Configuring the payroll calendar is essential to ensure timely and accurate employee payments while aligning with the company's financial processes and regulations.

 

Each company within an organisation requires its own payroll calendar. Key points to consider include:

 The calendar divides the year into week numbers, e.g., 202001, 202002, 202003, etc.

It tracks period end dates for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay groups. The period end date for monthly pay groups will always fall on the last day of the month.

The payroll calendar does not track payment dates.

Period end dates can be adjusted at the pay group level.

The calendar must include the current year and future years.

 

To assist in configuring the payroll calendar, please watch the instructional video or follow the steps outlined below.

 

 

Reuse an existing calendar 

You can reuse an existing calendar as a template to create a new one. To do this, follow the steps below. 

Click Settings then under Company Parameters, click Calendars.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company. 

Click Build/Rebuild Year then in the Base Year field, enter the base year you want to copy. 

In the New Year field, enter the new year then click OK.

 

 

Amend week end dates

Click Settings then under Company Parameters, click Calendars.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company. 

Click Amend Dates.

In the No of Days field, enter the number of days by which you want to adjust the week end dates.  

In the From Period and To Period field,  specify the dates you want to amend. 

Click OK then click Save.

 

 

Amend new calendar 

If you create a new calendar, you can make changes such as updating the week end dates or adding an extra week.

 

If you need to add an extra week, such as a week 53, follow these steps:

Click Settings then under Company Parameters, click Calendars.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company. 

Highlight the week you want to copy, then click the three dots menu.. 

Click Duplicate then fill in the required fields. 

Click Save.

title: Configure pay codes
text:
Configuring pay codes is a crucial step in payroll management that ensures accurate classification of employee earnings, deductions, and benefits. This process involves defining specific codes that represent various types of compensation, such as regular pay, overtime, bonuses, and deductions for taxes and benefits.

 

Pay codes in PeopleXD can be configured in different ways, which affects how they calculate payroll values. For example, standard value pay codes can be operated on a hours, days, units or value basis, while scaled value pay codes are paid based on the point the employee is set at on a set scale.

 

It is essential to configure pay codes to facilitate precise payroll calculations, maintain compliance with labor laws, and generate accurate financial reports. 

 

To help you configure pay codes, watch the video or follow the steps below.

Click Settings then under Codes, click Pay Codes.

Click Create New Pay Code.  

📌Note: We recommend cloning an existing pay code, where a similar one exists, by clicking Clone from the three-dot menu.

From the Payment Type drop-down menu, select a payment type. 

From the Payment Subset Type, select a subset type. 

In the Pay Code field, enter a unique number. 

In the Description field, enter a description then click OK.

Complete each step in the Pay Code Wizard screen then click Save.

For further guidance, check the pay code wizard user guide. 

 

Troubleshooting misconfigured pay codes

📌Note: We recommend testing any configuration changes in your UAT environment first to verify the results before applying them to the live system.

Misconfigured pay codes can lead to incorrect payroll calculations, causing discrepancies in employee payments. To resolve these issues, follow these steps:

Identify the configuration type: Determine whether the pay code is a standard value or scaled value pay code.

Clone an existing pay code: Clone an existing pay code with the correct configuration since the creation type cannot be changed after creation.

Adjust the formula: Modify the formula in the cloned pay code to meet specific requirements.

Use the new pay code: Replace the misconfigured pay code with the newly cloned and adjusted pay code for future payroll periods.

title: Error: 'ORA-01400: cannot insert NULL into ("COREHR"."PSOFT_NON_TIMESHEET"."START_DATE") ORA-06512: at "SYS.DBMS_SQL")'
text:
If you encounter this error when attempting to load a PeopleHUB file, it is due to a missing required field in the input file. 

 

This error indicates that a field expected by the system is missing (NULL). Specifically, the START_DATE field is either unpopulated or incorrectly positioned in the file. The system requires this field to insert data, and its absence will cause the load to fail.

 

 

Error handling overview

When processing PeopleHub files, two types of errors can occur:  

Stop Errors: These errors prevent the file (or specific records) from being uploaded due to structural issues in the file format. 

Validation Errors: These errors occur when data passes formatting checks but fails internal system validation.

 Files that pass both types of checks can be successfully uploaded to PeopleXD. 

 

 

 Correct file format

 To fix the file format, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, select PeopleHub Dashboard.

Click Settings tab then beside the External HR Interface file group, click the three dot  icon.

Click Files then locate the appropriate file type:

Allowances/Deductions for NON_001_*** files

Employee for EMP_*** files

To view the expected file format, click the three-dot  icon then click Columns.

Compare the column structure to your file and ensure the START_DATE field is in the correct column.

Correct your file to match the required format and reload it.

title: Set up a cycle to or bike to work pay code
text:
Setting up a Cycle to Work or Bike to Work pay code is a crucial step in promoting a corporate initiative that encourages employees to commute by bicycle. This pay code allows you to effectively manage and deduct costs associated with the program, including providing tax-efficient benefits for participating employees.

 

By implementing this pay code, you can promote sustainable commuting options, enhance employee well-being, and contribute to environmental sustainability.

📌Note: The Cycle to Work or Bike to Work pay code is deducted before Tax, PRSI, and USC.  

 

To set up this pay code according to client requirements, follow these guidelines:

Negative Taxable Allowance.

Taxable Indicator: Set to Taxable.

PRSIable Indicator: Set to PRSIable.

Pay Code Type: Select Allowance.

USCable: This box should be checked.

Pension: This box should not be checked.

ASC Indicator: This box should be checked.

Pension Related Deduction: Check this box where appropriate.

🤓Tip: If you are using a reducing balance pay code, make sure to enable the reducing balance option.

 

As an alternative, to set up this pay code:

Income Continuance Deduction.

Taxable Indicator: Set to Income Continuance.

PRSIable Indicator: Set to Non-PRSIable.

Pay Code Type: Select "Deduction."

USCable: This box should be checked.

Pension: This box should not be checked.

ASC Indicator: This box should be checked.

Pension Related Deduction: Check this box where appropriate.

title: Update pay scales using the pay increase module
text:
Updating pay scales using the pay increase module involves applying systematic salary adjustments across multiple employee pay rates through an automated process. 

 

This module allows you to implement percentage or fixed amount increases to specific pay scales, grades, or employee groups simultaneously rather than updating individual records manually.

 

You need to update pay scales using the pay increase module to efficiently manage organisation-wide salary adjustments whilst maintaining accuracy and consistency. 

 

 

Pay rate ranges: Record ranges and exclusions for rate increases

This option allows you to record the range of position codes corresponding to the rates that will be increased in the Ad-Hoc calculations as described in section 17.

Under Record Ranges and Exclusions For Rate Increases, enter the range of position codes to be included in the calculation in the Position Code From and To fields (e.g., Position 1 to 9999).

Click Next, then under the Record Positions for Exclusions section, input the position codes within the range that should be excluded.

To generate a report detailing all position codes that will be increased, select Generate Report.

Click OK.

 

 

Pay rate changes: Maintain rate increase position

You can manually amend or input position codes to be included in the rate increases on this screen, instead of using the Record Ranges and Exclusions for Rate Increases screen.

 

Pay rate ranges: Delete rate increase ranges

Use this option to clear the range of position codes included in the rate increases.

 

Pay rate calculations: Applying percentage/value increase to position rates (trial mode)

This option allows you to apply increases to position rates. There is a corresponding screen, Apply Percentage/Value Increase to Position Rates, which will actually enforce the increases. The trial mode allows you to preview the increases before applying them.

Rate base date: This date represents when the new rate will be effective. For example, if you intend to increase the rates effective on December 1st, this date should be set to November 30th.

Date effective:  Enter the date that the new rates become effective; in the above example, this would be December 1st.

Percentage increase: Enter the percentage by which you wish to increase the rates. You may leave this blank if you plan to increase the rates by a fixed amount.

Min/Max value: If you enter a percentage increase, you can apply minimum and maximum limits using these fields. The system will use the minimum value if the percentage increase does not exceed it, while the maximum value will cap increases that surpass it. If you intend to increase the rates by a fixed amount, enter this in the Min Value field; you will not be allowed to enter a Max Value.

Reference: The default reference is set to the screen reference, but you can enter your own reference here.

Apply to rates: You can selectively apply the increase to annual, weekly, daily, and hourly rates; all rates are selected by default.

Round to decimal: You have the option to choose the number of decimal places to which the rates will be rounded. By default, the rates will round to the maximum allowed by the system.

title: Error: 'Problem With Record 1 On File'
text:
f the above error appears after uploading an employee’s new pay rates, the file contains incorrect data. This may include an invalid date format, an incorrect employee reference, or an incorrect number of columns.

 

To resolve this, adjust the file by following the steps below.

Leading zeros removal.

Excel can remove leading zeros, which may cause errors in your input.

If dates appear incorrect, open the file in Notepad, manually add the leading zeros, save, and reload the file.

Incorrect Format: 1052022

Correct Format: 01052022

Persistent errors with leading zeros.

If errors persist despite leading zeros being present, try breaking the file into two parts and uploading separately or test by uploading a single line first.

Reference section limit

The reference section in the file must not exceed 10 characters.

Trailing comma removal.

Excel may remove trailing commas, leading to input failures.

Column count verification.

Open the file in Notepad to ensure it contains at least 10 columns (9 commas).

Columns 7 to 10 are optional, but at least one must contain data.

Even if left blank, all columns are required for the correct file format.

For detailed instructions on loading new pay rates, check the required format.

title: Configure Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR)
text:
Before you can generate and transfer your ERR report to Revenue, you need to configure the following parameters in PeopleXD Payroll. 

 

We’ve compiled the list of parameters and provided steps on how to configure them.

 

 

Pay code parameters

To configure your pay code parameters, follow the steps below.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click Outputs then click ROS.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Click Pay Code Parameters then search for the relevant pay code.

From the Category drop-down menu, select the relevant category.

📌Note: If the category is Travel and Subsistence, you also need to select a subcategory.

Repeat these steps for each pay code you need to include in the return.

Click Save.

 

 

Pay group parameters

​To configure your pay group parameters, follow the steps below.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click Outputs then click ROS.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Click Pay Group Parameters then search for the relevant pay group

Amend the Agent TAIN and Previous periods for each pay group as required.

Click Save.

 

 

Employee parameters

To configure your employee parameters, follow the steps below.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click Outputs then click ROS.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Click Employee Parameters then search for the relevant employee.

Turn on the Exclude employee toggle then click Save.

 

 

PMod/ERR parameters

The PMod/ERR parameters are preconfigured so you don't need to configure these. To view the parameters, follow the steps below.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click Outputs then click ROS.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Click PMOD/ERR Parameters.

 

 

Load digital certificates for ERR

Individuals, companies, agents and other entities need the ROS Digital Certificate to access online services for business taxes.
​
Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) is an additional permission under the employer ROS certificate. Revenue is automatically applying these ERR permissions to the employer certificate, and you can assign them to any sub certificate.

 

The cert permissions will have been amended by ROS in mid December 2023, so a new cert must have been retrieved following this date. Older certs will not work for ERR Submissions.

📌Note: To assign ERR to a sub certificate, you need to do this in your ROS permissions screen. For support with this, please contact Revenue.

 

If you use PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense as standalone products with different databases, upload the ERR digital cert in both PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense. If you keep PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense on the same database, only upload the ERR digital cert in PeopleXD Payroll.

 

 

Upload ERR digital certificates

To upload the ERR digital certificates in PeopleXD Payroll, follow the steps below.

📌Note: You need to download the digital cert from ROS before you can follow these steps. The file extension must be .p12 otherwise PeopleXD Payroll can't find the file.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click Outputs then click ROS.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Click Load Digital Certificates.

From the Company drop-down menu, select the relevant company.

Enter the certificate password from ROS then click the upload 

icon.

Select the digital certificate file from your computer then click Save.

If you have multiple companies, repeat these steps for each company.

 

 

Data Mapping 

To identify the country field in an employee's address, you can map address data within the Data Mapping screen. This isn't mandatory and, if you haven't configured this for PAYE modernisation, we recommend you don't configure this for ERR.

 

 

Company parameters

If you're an agent, you need to record the TAIN within the ERR settings. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click Outputs then click ROS.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Click Company Parameters then enter the agent TAIN for each company.

Click Save.

title: Overview of Insight views for Payroll
text:
Name of View
	
Function of View



Allowance Profile Details

	

Contains information on the Employee Allowances as per the Maintain Employee Allowances screen on CorePay. Some of the key items available in this folder include, ‘Allowance Value’, ‘Balance Due’, ‘Allowance Cost Centre’, ‘Pay Code’, ’Start Date’, and ‘End Date’. This folder also includes standard employee details such as name, cost centre details, scale point, PPS number etc.
​Note: This folder will not provide you with a payment history for particular allowances. It only contains the details of particular allowances that employees have been set up to receive. It also shows allowances that are no longer active i.e. where the end date is in the past.
If you wish to see the payment history of an allowance, please see Pay History Details.




Audit Details

	

Contains information on the audited changes made by Usernames and by the Payroll Process to Field Names in Payroll. This folder allows users to audit changes that are made. For example, if a user wants to create a report showing what changes were made to an employees pay scale, who made the changes, and when the change was made, then this folder can provide that data.




BIK Deduction Profile Details

	

Contains information on the Employee BIK Deductions as per the Maintain Employee BIK Details screen in Payroll. Some of the key items available in this folder include, ‘Value’, ‘Start Date’, ‘End Date’, ‘Pay Code’. This folder also includes standard employee details such as name, cost centre details, scale point, Pay Group etc.
​Note: This folder will not provide you with a payment history for particular BIK deductions. It only contains the details of BIK deductions that have been set up against particular employees. It also shows BIK deductions that are no longer active i.e. where the end date is in the past.




Cost Allocation Details

	

Contains details of employees who are allocated across multiple cost centres. This will allow users to report on the allocation for each employee including the following details, ‘Alternative Cost Centre’, ’Percent’ (i.e. allocation percent), ‘Expense Code’. This folder also contains standard employee details such as ‘Pay Group’, ‘Location’, ‘Category’, ‘Pay Scale’.




Deduction Profile Details

	

Contains information on the Employee Deductions as per the Maintain Employee Deductions screen in Payroll. Some of the key items available in this folder include, ‘Deduction Value’, ‘Balance Due’, ‘Capital Sum’, ‘Cumulative Amount’, ‘Start Date’, ‘End Date’, ‘No. Of Deductions’, ‘Pay Code’. This folder also includes standard employee details such as name, cost centre details, scale point, PPS number etc.
​Note: This folder will not provide you with a payment history for particular deductions. It only contains the details of deductions that have been set up against particular employees. It also shows deductions that are no longer active i.e. where the end date is in the past.
If you wish to see the payment history of a deduction, please see Pay History Details.




Pay Code Reference

	

This is a reference folder which will allow users to report on all the pay codes that are currently set up within Core, along with the Analysis Code and Analysis Type they belong to. Some of the key items in the folder include, ‘Pay Code’, ‘Analysis Code’, ‘Analysis Type’, ‘Maximum Value’, ‘Minimum Value’, ‘Multiplier’.




Pay Scale and Rate Detail

	

This folder contains information on the Pay Scales, Scale Points and Rates of Pay as per the Maintain Position Rates screen in Payroll. This folder is unique in that it does not hold any employee information, and is not used to identify the Position & Point of an employee. It just contains details about particular pay scales and rates, and the date effective for each. It provides a history of changes to scales and rates by a date effective.
For example, use this folder to show the rates of pay (annual, weekly, daily) associated with particular scale points.




Pay History Details

	

This folder contains information on the Pay Code history by Payroll Period as per the View History Details screen in Payroll. This is probably the most commonly used folder. Use this folder when you want to see historic payments made to employees i.e. in previous payroll periods. It is important to note that any report created from this folder will contain multiple records for each employee i.e. for each payroll period new records are created for each employee.
Some of the most important and commonly used items in this folder are ‘Pay Code’, ‘Hours’, ‘Value’, ‘Payroll Period’. Also included are standard employee details such as name, cost centre details, scale point, PPS number etc.
​Note: The most important thing to remember about this folder is that it contains a history of all payments made to employees.




Pension Payments

	

Contains Pay History information, however the item Pensionable Pay within, only gives the amount paid per Payroll Period that was Pensionable. Essentially, this folder will only include pay codes that are pensionable. Some of the key items available in this folder include, ‘Pay Code’, ‘Pensionable Pay’, ‘AVC Value’. The folder also includes some pension scheme details (e.g. Scheme Code, Scheme Name), and some standard employee details (e.g. Name, Date of Birth, PPS Number, Current Cost Centre).




Pension Scheme Details

	

Contains information on the Pension Scheme details as per the Maintain Pension Details on CorePay. Some of the key items available in this folder include, ‘Scheme Code’, ‘Employer Value’, ‘Employee Value’, ‘Start Date’, ‘End Date’. The folder also includes some standard employee details such as name, cost centre, rate of pay, and pay scale.
The important point to note is that this folder contains details about specific pension schemes. It will not provide a history of pension payments.




Person Position History

	

Contains information on the changes in Pay Scale, Scale Point and Rate of Pay for each payee (employee). The items available in this folder include, ‘Scale Point’, ‘Date Effective’, ‘Rate Sequence Number’, ‘Position’. Also included are some standard employee details such as name, date started, and employment status.
Use this folder to create reports showing an employees history of position changes, salary amendments etc.




Person Profile Details

	

Contains employee information including Rate of Pay and Cumulatives to date. It is important to understand that this folder contains only current information about employees. For example, ‘rate of pay’ in this folder is the employee’s current rate of pay. Also contains standard employee details such as name, employee number, date started, age, gender etc.
​Note: Does NOT contain Pay Code history.




Summary Payment Details

	

Contains information on the Nett Payment values made to employees by Pay path (Credit Transfer) or Cheque. This folder will not provide a breakdown of payments by pay code, it will simply provide details of the nett amounts paid to an employee, and the payment method used i.e. Pay Path or cheque.
Some of the key items in this folder include ‘Bank Account No’, ‘Cheque Number’, Date Processed’, ‘Pay Method’, ‘Payment Value’. Also included are standard employee details such as name, PPS number etc.




Timesheet Details

	

Contains details of the Pay Code history by Payroll Period as per the View Timesheet Details screen in Payroll.
This folder contains payment details for a particular payroll run, once the timesheets have been generated. This differs from Pay History Details in that Pay History is only populated with payment details once the Payroll Update stage of the payroll run has been completed.
​ 
​Notes:

Use Timesheet Details folder after the timesheets have been generated.

Use Pay History Details after the payroll update has been run.

Remember, this only applies for the current payroll run. Timesheet Details can be used to report on all previously run payroll periods.




Year End Cumulatives

	

Cntains information on the standard payee cumulatives e.g. Employee and Employers PRSI, after the year-end has been run. This folder will not provide a breakdown of payment details by pay code, or payroll period. It will simply provide cumulative figures for each employee, for any year that has been completed in Payroll.
For example, use this folder when you want to see the total Employers PRSI, Employees PRSI, and Pension to Date for a previous year, for each employee.
Also included are standard employee details such as name, PPS number etc.
​Note: Contains cumulative figures AFTER year-end has been run.
