title: Back Office: Creating a historic appointment / contract amendment for an employee
text:
A historic appointment is used to reflect an employee's movements in an organisation and to offer a complete history. It is entered retrospectively via the Appointment History screen in Personnel.

 

Why create an historic appointment?

One can be created for an employee whose appointment history shows the correct history data for an employee's record.
​
E.g. Initially employed for 3 years as a part-time Administrator and then full-time as a HR Manager. The correct post appointment history should show a part-time administrator post for two years followed by a full-time administrator post for one year, as follows:

Part-time Administrator: 01-Jan-2013 to 31-Dec-2014

Full-time Administrator: 01-Jan-2015 to 31-Dec-2015

 

How to create a historic appointment

There must be a Planned and Authorised appointment available. Historic posts are created via Back Office, CorePersonnel, Maintenance, Appointment History.

A gap in the employee's appointment history needs to be created to allow you to fit the historic post into the record.

In this example, the end date on the employee's current part-time administrator post needs to be changed from 31- Dec-2015 to 31-Dec-2014.

On the Appointment History screen, query the personnel number and press the arrow (pointing to the right) on the toolbar - the employee's full appointment history will be displayed.

Change the dates as required - in this example, the end date of the Administrator post is changed to 31-Dec-2014.

Save.

Click on the Create Historic Sequence button.

A new screen will pop up to prompt the user to enter Post Appointment Sequence details.

Enter a valid Post Number - in this example, the Administrator post is selected.

📌Note: You may need to set up the post in Post Management, Post Profile Maintenance.

Tab to Start Date, enter in Mandatory start and end dates, and ensure all mandatory post history fields are populated.

In this example, the Salary Details automatically display - this is because there is already an existing salary for the post start/end dates; if there is no existing salary record for the dates, then enter the salary details here also.

📌Note: When salary details are entered, they will not be written to Pay.

Press OK.

Validation will be applied to the details entered - if this is valid, a message saying that a Generated Sequence number for Post has been created.

 

 

Troubleshooting

Are pay details required?

If yes, ensure the pay details flow through to Pay and that payment arrears are generated in the next payroll.

If no, ensure to select the Planned Pay Details Not Required Indicator when planning the Post Appointment.

Error - Start Date must be within the Start and End Dates for this Appointment ID.

This error message will occur if a start date is entered for a historic sequence where a valid gap in employment service has not first been created (refer to point 2 above).

Also this will occur if updating an open ended post appointment e.g. if the post appointment has 1 commenced sequence. If this is the case, please do not use this functionality to make the required changed. The recommendation is to use the standard Amend Appointment functionality to apply these changes.

Error: "Appointment Record Cannot Exist Before Person Started"

This error will pop up if attempting to create a post appointment for an employee on a date earlier that their overall date started. If this is the requirement, please do not use this functionality to make the required changes.

title: Error - 'Query caused no records to be retrieved'
text:
This error can occur for various reasons, as outlined in the resolutions below.

 

The user doesn't have access to the employee 

Typically, if the employee is not appearing in the Personnel No. LOV on the Search screen (or if the employee name is not retrieved when the correct employee number is keyed into the Personnel No. field) - the issue relates to employee access.  
Employee or data access (i.e. who a user can see) in CorePersonnel is controlled per user via the CorePersonnel, System User screen.
If a user does not have access to an employee they will not be able to view the employee in the Personal Profile screen. If unsure how to address this, we have further guidance.

 

 

The employee is dormant

By default this screen only searches active employees, so if an employee is dormant, they will not be retrieved. Try choosing either the Dormant or All employees search options and re-search.

 

 

Missing employee data on CorePersonnel tables

If the items above have been checked and if the user is still having problems viewing the employee, please raise a new case and reference the title of this article. Please include the user's username and the employee's personnel no.
​
For example, if the employee is appearing on the Personnel No. list of values (LOV) in the Search Criteria section, but the actual details for the employee are not appearing then it's likely to be a data issue. The employee details are not being retrieved because something about the employee record is invalid, e.g. mandatory data is missing or corrupt.

 

 

The employee has temporarily rejoined in CorePay

Where an employee is a temp rejoiner, the system does not allow access to the Personnel Profile, i.e. the user set the employee as a Temp Rejoin using the Set Employee Status screen in CorePay.

This only rejoins the employee in CorePay to be paid as a one off, and then automatically resets as a leaver after the Complete Update, (PAY355), job.

It does not rejoin the employee in CorePersonnel and as such no changes can be made via 'Personnel Profile'.

If changes to employee detail are necessary complete either of the following:

Temp rejoin in CorePay, change Pay group if necessary, Generate Salaries and Allowances, (PAY290) and if e.g. change of Cost Centre required then change on the Timesheet.

Alternatively, rejoin in CorePersonnel, make the required changes, Generate Salaries and Allowances, (PAY290), set employee as a leaver again. (This is not best practice).

 

 

The employee has an incorrect date

The employee has had an incorrect date entered,  e.g.2105 instead of 2015 perhaps.
Please raise a new case and reference the title of this article, include details of the employee affected.

 

 

The home address is inactive

Please raise a new case and reference the title of this article, include details of the employee affected.

 

 

A parameter setting under Client Parameters

Issue is caused by the 'Hide all information when viewing employees you no longer have access to' parameter being enabled.
If this parameter is enabled it can affect access to confirmed future appointments.
To disable this:

In Back Office go to CorePersonnel, Reference, Reference Q-Z, System Parameters - Advanced, Client Parameters.

Search for Hide all information when viewing employees you no longer have access to and disable.

Save.

📌Note: This can also be updated in portal in Data Centre, View All, System Parameters Advanced, Client Parameters.

Please bear in mind, changing this will grant access for all staff, not just the person disabling/enabling the parameter. It is advisable to test on UAT prior to promotion to the LIVE site.

When enabled, users can only view employees whose current active appointments they have access to. 

When disabled, if users do not have access to an employee's current active appointments but have access to an employee's historic ended appointments, they can still view the employee.

 


The current substantive record is cancelled

Issue is caused by the current substantive record having been cancelled.
If the employee has only one appointment, they need a substantive record to be returned on the screen. 

Check the Substantive Maintenance screen to confirm that the existing substantive record has not been cancelled.

 

 

Employee is in a sensitive department

Issue is caused by employee being in a Sensitive Department that you do not have access to.
Grant Back Office/Portal user access to the sensitive department through Back Office, Personnel, Reference, Reference Q - Z, System Users, Sensitive Departments.

 

 

Employee is missing from one of the access tables

Issue is caused by the employee being missing from one of the access tables in the background. Please raise a new case and reference the title of this article, include details of the employee affected.

title: Amend an employee's contract
text:
You can update an existing employee contract to record changes such as hours, FTE, job title, location, or other contract details. PeopleXD tracks all amendments with a complete timeline of changes.

 

Contract amendments fall into two categories depending on whether they affect the employee's salary:

Amendment type
	
Description
	
Example



No salary impact

	

Changes to organisational structure, job details, or employment status that don't affect pay calculations.

	

Location, job title.




Salary impact

	

Changes to hours, weeks, or FTE that require recalculation of the employee's pay multiplier.

	

Reason, FTE, contracted hours.

To amend an employee’s existing contract, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

 

Amend a contract with no salary impact

Follow the steps below to update contract details that don't affect the employee's pay, such as changing location, work group, or job category.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Command Centre.

Next to the Employees option, click View.

Search for the employee and click View.

From the drop-down select the relevant contract, then click the Contracts tab.

In the Amendments section, click Update.

If required, update the organisational structure fields, then click Next.

Select an Effective Date.

⚠️ Important: The effective date must be on or after the current contract effective date. It cannot be earlier than the contract start date/last contract amendment​​​​​​​.

Select a Reason that does not impact salary. 

Update any other contract fields as needed, such as job title, or post type.

Click Save.

📌 Note: If you select a reason code or update any fields that impact salary, the salary amendment step of the wizard opens.

 

 

Amend a contract with a salary impact

Use this process when the contract amendment requires a corresponding salary change, such as a change in hours or FTE. PeopleXD automatically calculates the new pay multiplier based on your changes.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Command Centre.

Next to the Employees option, click View.

Search for the employee and click View.

From the drop-down select the relevant contract, then click the Contracts tab.

In the Amendments section, click Update.

If required, update the organisational structure fields, then click Next.

Select an Effective Date.

⚠️ Important: The effective date must be on or after the current contract effective date. It cannot be earlier than the contract start date/last contract amendment​​​​​​​.

Select a Reason, such as promotion.

Update any other contract fields as needed, such as contracted hours, or FTE.

Click Save.

📌 Note: The Amend Salary screen opens automatically if your reason code is configured correctly.

Review the pre-populated fields, and update the salary information if required.

Click Save.

 

 

View contract timeline

PeopleXD maintains a complete history of all contract amendments, allowing you to view key information.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Command Centre.

Next to the Employees option, click View.

Search for the employee and click View, then click the Contracts tab.

Next to the contract summary, click the three-dot menu, then click Timeline.

title: Length of Service versus Total Length of Service
text:
Total Length of Service

(HR0120 - Personal profile, HR Data/Appointment Details)
​
This is a standard CorePersonnel field used to show the Total Length of Service of employees main appointment history.
​
It is calculated as the length of each post from the Date Started until now. If the Date Started is set to 1990 but there are no posts commenced until 2006 then it will only calculate from 2006 until present day (For example Year 2014: Total Length of Service = 8 Years). If any posts are overlapping (which they should not), then you end up getting duplication in dates.  

 

Length of Service

(HR0120 - Personal profile, HR Data/Appointment Details)
​
This is a standard CorePersonnel field used to show the length of service.
​
It is a simpler calculation which counts from the Latest Start Date to now and doesn't take into account what posts you are in or not. It counts the years from latest start date to present.

title: Portal: Overview of document and email generation
text:
The Document and Email Generation feature on PeopleXD allows a user to automatically generate documents, letters or emails based on employee data, e.g. employee contracts, letters of offer, HR forms etc.

 

Documents

A document refers to a file (MS Word or PDF) that can be generated from PeopleXD by merging employee data into templates that have been stored on the system. These may be used to create employee contracts, pre-populated HR forms, applicant correspondence etc.

Documents that have been generated on PeopleXD may be downloaded by the user to further amend and print, as required.

Documents may also be automatically stored against an employee’s record on their Employee Profile screen, as part of the document generation.

A user may also upload a document to the Employee Profile, independent of generation process e.g. uploading a copy of a passport.

Email

System generated emails can be produced and sent automatically from PeopleXD to an employee or an applicant. Emails are typically used to support the recruitment process e.g. to send an invitation for interview to a candidate. However, these may also be generated to employees within HR Admin.

Template

Templates can be stored on the system to support the production of both documents and emails.

Document Templates: These are created using MS Word mail merge functionality and uploaded to PeopleXD.

Email Templates: These are created and maintained directly on PeopleXD.

Template Group

Templates (document or email) may be grouped into various categories e.g. Contracts, Recruitment, Salary etc. This is an optional grouping and does not need to be used for all or any templates.

Document Type

This is used to group documents that have been generated on the system or uploaded independently to an employee’s or applicant’s record. This is an important setting for controlling the visibility of and access to documents for HR and Recruitment Admins as well as Employees and Managers.

Data Sources

Standard mail merge functionality employs the use of Data Sources which are essentially temporary files pre-populated with the record data that will become merged into a document or email template.
​
In this feature, each screen in HR or recruitment admin, from which a document or email can be generated, is linked to a specified data source (or data sources). This data source is a set of employee / applicant / contract / record fields which will be mapped to a template.

title: Portal: Upload a public document for all employees to view
text:
You can enable and use the document type ESSG to upload public documents. By default, this is typically named General Documents or similar. To complete this process, follow the steps below.

 

Important considerations

Test in UAT first to ensure it works as expected.

Only use this for content that can be seen by all employees, and that it's free of sensitive information.

After uploading, we recommend disabling the ability to add or upload a general document to ensure that sensitive documents are not uploaded accidentally.

 

 

Enable ESSG document type

Ensure the document type is viewable by ESS and MSS users, and available for upload via MSS.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to Reference Data, click OPEN, then click Document Type.

For document type ESSG, click the three-dot menu, then click Options.

Set ESS to enable view only (set the first slider on and the second slider off).

Set MSS to enable view and add (set both sliders on).

Click OK, then click OK.

 

 

Upload document

An MSS user with document upload access carries out this task. The process differs depending on whether you use a standalone PeopleXD system or access it via Access Evo.

 

Standalone PeopleXD

Click your User Profile, then click My Profile.

🤓Tip: The user profile is the circle icon in the top right corner of the screen. It usually contains your photo or initials.

Click EMPLOYEE DETAIL, then click Documents.

Click UPLOAD, then complete the Upload Document template.

Ensure you select the correct Document Type, then click OK.

PeopleXD within Access Evo

In the top left of the screen, click either your name or the My Profile icon.

🤓Tip: My Profile is located in the circle that contains your photo or initials.

Click EMPLOYEE DETAIL, then click Documents.

Click UPLOAD, then complete the Upload Document template.

Ensure you select the correct Document Type, then click OK.

You can create a new request form by cloning an existing form. Follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Against HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN. 

Click Employee and Manager Requests.

Click the three-dot menu of the form to be copied, then click Clone.

Input a Code and a Description, then click OK.

You can now edit the cloned form to make any changes.

title: Deleting or deactivating employee and manager request forms
text:
You can delete an employee or manager request form if it hasn't been used. If it has been used, it can be set as inactive. To do this, follow the steps below.

 

Delete a request form

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Against HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN. 

Click Employee and Manager Requests.

Click Employee Requests or Manager Requests.

Click the three-dot menu of the form to be deleted.

Click Delete, then click YES.

 

 

Set a request form to inactive

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Against HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN.

Click Employee and Manager Requests.

Click Employee Requests or Manager Requests.

Click the form's three-dot menu, then click Edit.

Click Active (to set it inactive), then click SAVE.

title: Restrict access to employee and manager request forms
text:
Employee and manager requests can be assigned criteria groups to ensure that some requests are only available to a subset of staff. These are configured on separate screens by request type. To complete this, follow the steps below.

📌Note: If the request has no criteria group set for it, then all employees and managers have access to it.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Against HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, then click the assignment tile.

For employee requests, click Employee Request Process Assignment.

For manager requests, click UDF Assignment.

📌Note: Manager request forms will have a UDF type of Manager.

Against the request, click ASSIGN, then click ASSIGN CRITERIA GROUPS.

To assign an existing criteria group, click Activate, then click SAVE.

To create a new group, click ADD GROUP.

Enter a Group Description, then click OK.

Select a Criteria Category, then under Available, click on the required reference data.

Click on the > chevron to move the items to Assigned, then click SAVE.

📌Note: Click ADD to repeat the process for further criteria. Once you've assigned all criteria, click SAVE. 

Click Activate, then click SAVE.

title: Workflow process and EMS trigger for employee and manager requests
text:
The approval and notification process for employee and manager requests consists of two elements. These are a workflow process for the request and an EMS alert to trigger the workflow. To complete these, follow the steps below.

 

Workflow process

One or more workflow processes should be configured to ensure requests are routed to the appropriate recipients or approvers.

 

In the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN.

Click Hr Process Configuration.

Click Search to view existing tasks, then click New Process.

Fill in the Add New Process template, then click SAVE once complete.

📌Note: Select Employee Requests or Manager Request Events as the process category.

Configure the required workflow steps, then click SAVE when prompted.

 

 

EMS trigger

Create EMS alerts to trigger the workflow process for requests.

📌Note: The following settings are important when creating the alert to ensure the workflows operate correctly.

An event type of Submitted ensures the event triggers when the request is submitted.

Specify a notification type of Process to trigger the workflow process.

The Conditions tab on the EMS alert defines which process to trigger. E.g., if REQUEST_TYPE is Cycle to Work Scheme, then trigger that workflow.

Configure multiple processes and corresponding EMS triggers to cater for each request type.

To create the alerts, follow the steps below.

In the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Click OPEN against HR Admin Setup Settings, then click Hr Event Configuration.

In Event Category, select Employee Requests or Manager Request Events.

For the submitted event type, click the three-dot ellipsis, then click Edit.

📌Note: Event type name will be Manager Request Status (Submitted) or Submitted. 

Click Add New Notification to create a new alert.

Complete the required event configuration, then click Save when prompted.

title: Status of employee and manager requests
text:
As an employee or manager request progresses through the approval process in PeopleXD, its status updates accordingly. See the table below for details.

Status
	
Description



Saved

	

The request has been created but not yet submitted for approval.




Submitted

	

The request has been submitted for approval, but the approval process is ongoing.




Approved

	

The request has been approved.




Rejected

	

The request has been rejected.




Complete

	

The request has been completed. For this type of request, the outcome is a status that's neither approved nor rejected.

title: Action an employee or manager request
text:
When an employee or manager submits a request form, the system sends a notification to the designated approvers so they can review and take action. Additionally, an HR administrator can oversee and progress requests. These processes are outlined below.

🤓Tip: You can also action employee and manager requests on the PeopleXD Mobile App.

 

Notification Centre alerts

The system displays an alert in the approver’s notification centre when a request is submitted.

The system sends a notification to the request creator once the approver approves the request.

📌Note: Manager requests that don't require approval will trigger an email notification.

 

 

Approve or reject requests

Approvers can review and action request forms from multiple areas within the system.

📌Note: The workflow may include multiple approval stages before the approver completes the request.

Employee Request Approvals widget.

From the dashboard menu search bar, select Employee Request Approvals.

Next to the request, click VIEW, then click APPROVE or REJECT.

My Approvals widget.

From the dashboard menu search bar, select My Approvals Notifications.

Next to the request, click VIEW, then click APPROVE or REJECT.

 

 

HR administrator overview

HR administrators with the required permissions can manage all employee and manager requests via the HR Process Administration screen.

From the dashboard menu search bar, select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN.

Click Hr Process Administration then, in Query Type, select Administrator.

In Process Category, select the request type.

🤓Tip: This will be either Employee Requests or Manager Request Events. 

Assign any additional filters, then click OK.

text:
Employees and managers can view the status of their submitted requests by checking the request history. To do this, follow the steps below.

 

Employee request history

From the dashboard menu, select Employee Dashboard, then click Employee Requests.

Under Employee Requests, click the three-dot menu next to the relevant request.

Manager request history

From the dashboard menu, select Manager Dashboard, then click Manager Requests.

Under Manager Requests, click the three-dot menu next to the relevant request.

🤓Tip: If you can't see the request you're looking for, enter text in Search People or click the filter icon to apply data restrictions. 

Under Request History, review the request status.

text:
Additional configuration is required to ensure that managers are able to create a request for the same employees that appear under their My Team widget. To do this, follow the steps below.

📌Note: Ensure your configuration matches the organisational group and role used in your Reports To Manager setup.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Administrator Dashboard.

Click Site Manager, then click OPEN next to Admin Settings.

In Keyword Search, enter cp_mgr_req_org, then click the search icon.

Review and update the following parameter codes.

cp_mgr_req_org_group - e.g. WRKGRP.

Specifies the organisational group item used in Organisation Roles to build the manager request's employee list. Defaults to DEPT for Department Level.

cp_mgr_req_org_role - e.g. MGRESS.

Specifies the organisational role used in Organisation Roles to build the manager request's employee list. Defaults to 001 for Reports To.

Click Edit for each item, update the text, then click OK.

title: Search for Staff Requests to approve or reject
text:
Search using the HR Process Administration screen

Go to the Data Centre and select HR Admin Setup Settings.

On the next screen open HR Process Administration.

Select Administrator for Query Type.

From the Process Category List of Values (LOV), select Staff Requests.

Select filter using other fields if needed.

Click OK.

 

 

Edit or approve / reject a task within the request

📌Note: if there is more than 1 approval task within the process it is advised to use the back office to set the task(s) to 'Approved'. Approving a second task in the portal can generate a duplicate task with an initial status pending approval. Our Development and Product Teams are aware of the issue. They are looking to improve the portal's HR Process Administration screen in the future.

Click on the three-dot ellipsis next to the staff request and select Edit.

Under Task Status Details, click the task's three-dot ellipsis and select Edit.

On the next screen, under Update Task, set the required status.

Click the Save button.

 

 

Approving task in the back office

Click CoreHR, go to Event Management, and select HR Process Administration.

Cancel out of the Selection Criteria window.

Click the Administrator tab, which will open the Selection Criteria once more.

From the Process Category list of values select Staff Requests.

Select filter using other fields if needed.

Click OK.

On the next screen, click Edit next to the relevant staff request.

Click on the relevant Sequence under Task Details.

Under Task Status Details, click Edit next to the task.

On the next screen, for the Set Status field, select Approved.

Click the Save button.

title: Configure employee and manager request forms
text:
You can create request forms using the employee and manager requests screen. These allow an employee, or a manager on behalf of an employee, to submit a request form within PeopleXD that's then routed to its intended recipient via a workflow process. To learn how to do this, watch the video or follow the steps below.
​

 

 

Create the request form

The initial step is to create a new form for the required request type.

On the PeopleXD People Management dashboard, click the Data Centre tab.

Open the HR Admin Setup Settings option.

Search for and click Employee and Manager Requests.

Click Employee Requests or Manager Requests, then click ADD.

Input a Code and a Description as follows, then click OK.

Field

	

Description




Code

	

Up to six alphanumeric characters, the code must be unique.




Description

	

Descriptive alphanumeric text, up to 40 characters long.

 

 

Add fields to the form

Once the form has been created, you can add a maximum of 40 fields to it.

📌Note: All forms require a section field as the first field, this is generated automatically. 

Click the new form's three-dot menu, then click Edit.

To update the section field, click its three-dot menu, then click Edit.

Alternatively, click ADD NEW to create a new field.

Complete details as shown in the next table.

Click OK, then define the look-up for any list items.

Against the item, click LIST ITEMS, then click Add.

Enter a List Item Description, then click OK.

Repeat for all list items, then click Edit Request Form.

Field

	

Description




Item

	

System-generated item number.




Form Label

	

Up to 50 alphanumeric characters.




Field Type

	

Select one of the following.

Text - User input, alphanumeric value.

Numeric - User input, numeric only.

Date - User input in date format, i.e., DD-MON-YYYY.

List - User selects from a predefined list of items.

Text Area - User input of up to 4000 alphanumeric characters.

Reference - A reference item selected from a list, manager requests only.

Section - Add a section to the form and customise the layout.




Reference Type

	

Note: Only required for a reference field type.
​ 

Select a reference data item from the drop-down list. E.g., to select from a location, set Location as the reference type.




Description Mode

	

Note: Only required for a reference field type.
​ 

Select the reference type's display format from the drop-down list. E.g., Description or Code - Description.




Format Mask

	

Note: Only required if the field type is numeric.
​ 

Specify a number format, e.g., "99.99".




Section Type

	

Note: Only required for section field types.
​ 

Select one of the following.

Grid - Default format, the fields display left to right and are a default width.

Top Down - Fields display from top to bottom and have the default width.

Full-Width - Fields display from top to bottom and span the width of the screen.




Mandatory

	

Turn off the toggle to make the field optional.




Active

	

Enable the toggle to display the field within the form.

 

 

Amend Form Settings

Apply any additional settings, such as,

Show or hide specific fields.

Add a purpose message and link at the top of the form to guide users.

Include a customised statement that users must read and agree to by ticking a checkbox before submitting the form.

To do this, follow the steps below. 

📌Note: Options vary by request type, see the table below.

Click ACTIONS, then click Settings.​

Click the toggles as needed, then add any guidance in the Help Text section.​

You can remove or amend text added by the Admin Settings parameters.​

Enter any required text in the Declarative Statement section, then click SAVE.​

Field

	

Description

	

Request Type




Hide Additional Information

	

Hides the additional information box on the form. 

	

Manager




Appointment Specific

	

Links the form to a contract. The employee selects the relevant appointment.

	

Employee




Hide From & To Dates

	

Hides the form's from and to dates.

	

Employee




Hide Document Option

	

Hides the form's document upload button.

	

Both




Help Text

	

Enter help text to display at the top of the form, or leave it blank. 

	

Both




Declarative Statement

	

Enter a statement to display at the bottom of the form. This adds a checkbox that users must select.
​Note: You can update the checkbox text using the Language Pack.
Leave this blank if users don’t need to confirm before submitting. 

	

Both

 

 

Preview Form

You can preview new and existing forms from the Edit Request Form screen.

Follow the below steps to navigate to this screen.

From the People Management dashboard, click the Data Centre tab.

Against HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, then click Employee and Manager Requests.

Click Employee Requests or Manager Requests.

Click the form's three-dot menu, then click Edit.

Click Preview to review the form, then click Edit Request Form to exit.

title: API details for setup
text:
There are two distinct groups of web service endpoints used to manage data interactions within client databases.

B2B endpoints - These provide non-user-based functionality, such as a machine pushing clockings to the database or a sync job updating employee contact details across multiple locations within an organisation.

User endpoints - These require a PeopleXD portal user's credentials to access. They perform everyday tasks expected of a system user, such as updating a profile photo or submitting leave requests.

More detailed technical information is available for both groups.

title: PeopleXD SMTP server migration
text:
Access is migrating the SMTP server that processes emails sent from PeopleXD. The legacy SMTP server, hosted in a Magnet Plus (formerly BT) data centre, will be replaced with a new SMTP server hosted in a UK-based Access Group data centre.

 

For customers who do not use their own sending domain, the default sending address for PeopleXD emails will change to peoplexd@accessacloud.com. This sending domain has DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) authentication configured to improve email delivery reliability.

 

Why is this change being made?

The current SMTP server does not support DKIM. Without DKIM, emails can be incorrectly marked as spam or junk—particularly by providers such as Gmail and Hotmail.

 

The new Access Group hosted SMTP server supports DKIM, which:

Improves email trust and delivery rates.

Reduces the risk of PeopleXD emails being filtered as spam.

What do I need to do?

 If you need to make changes related to DKIM or a custom sending domain, Access will contact you before applying any changes.

 

Most customers do not need to take any action.

Sending address and configuration

Customers using the default PeopleXD configuration will use peoplexd@accessacloud.com.

Customers using a custom “from” address can continue to do so.

The sending address is configurable within the application.

If a custom address is used, DKIM and/or Sender Policy Framework (SPF) changes may be required.

Timeline

A subset of customers has already been migrated.

Migration will be complete for all notified customers by Tuesday 30 June 2026.

Impact

Improved reliability of PeopleXD email delivery.

Reduced likelihood of emails being flagged as spam.

No downtime and no service interruption during the change.

Data considerations

Following the migration:

The Access Group data centre will store 30 days of SMTP server logs.

The only potentially sensitive data in these logs is the “from” email address.

📌Note: For most customers, this will be peoplexd@accessacloud.com.

The “from” address remains configurable within PeopleXD.

Summary

This migration modernises PeopleXD’s email infrastructure, improves deliverability, and enhances reliability. Most customers are unaffected and do not need to take any action.

title: Migration to the new PeopleXD Ideas Portal
text:
As part of our continued efforts to improve the way we collect and action feedback from our PeopleXD clients, we are migrating to a new Ideas Portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment.

 

This new portal provides a more modern interface, enhanced tracking features, and a stronger foundation for future improvements, including better two-way communication and AI-assisted idea prioritisation.

 

The legacy portal will be permanently retired on 30th June 2025.

 

What's changing? 

From 30th June 2025, the following will occur: 

The legacy portal will no longer be accessible.

The new portal will be the single location for all PeopleXD idea submissions.

Any ideas submitted in the last 12 months or with 10 or more votes will be automatically transferred to the new portal.

Older ideas that don’t meet the above criteria will not appear in the portal, but will still be retained internally by our product team for reference in roadmap planning.

 

How do I access the new portal?

You can access the new ideas portal in one of two ways: either by an invitation sent to your email or by registering manually on the site.

 

Received an invite 

If you’ve received an email inviting you to log into the new Aha! Ideas Portal, this means:

You have previously submitted or voted on an idea in the old portal in the last 12 months.

We have automatically created a user account for you in the new portal.

Follow the link provided in the email to log in, then set a password.

 

Register manually 

If you didn't receive an email inviting you to log into the new Aha! Ideas Portal, you can still register for the new portal manually. To do this, follow the steps below. 

Go to the new People XD Ideas Portal.

Click Sign up.

In the Email address field, eneter your work email address. 

In the First and Last name field, enter your name. 

Click Register. 

You’ll receive a verification email. Follow the link in the email to complete your registration.

Once you've registered, you can:

Browse and vote on existing ideas.

Submit new ideas

Follow ideas to track progress and status changes.

 

What if I can’t find my old ideas?

If you can't find one of your previously submitted ideas in the new ideas portal, try the following: 

Search for the idea: Some titles or categories may have changed slightly.  

If it still doesn’t appear, resubmit the idea as a new entry in the portal.

 

Need help?

If you encounter any issues registering, logging in, or locating an idea, please raise a new case online or speak with your customer success manager, we’re happy to help.

 

Thank you for helping shape the future of PeopleXD.

title: Portal: Creating an event notification (EMS)
text:
The system allows you to generate alerts and notifications based on data changes or dated events. To configure this, follow the steps below.

 

Create new notification

From the dashboard menu, enter Data Centre in the search bar and select it.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, then click HR Event Configuration.

Select Event Category, then click Edit from the three-dot menu next to the required Event Type.

Click Add New Notification.

 

 

Set Indicators

To define the event timing, enter the number of days in Generate Notification, then select Before or After under Days.

Select Active Indicator, then select Test Mode Indicator.

🤓Tip: This enables the event in test mode, email reminders will only be sent to an administrator. You can disable test mode later.

 

 

Identify recipients

Click Recipient, then select a Notification Type.

Update the fields that appear based on the selected notification type.

If Email is selected, update Email Address and, if required, CC Email.

If Organisation Role is selected, enter values in Structure, Organisational Group, and Organisational Role.

📌Note: For manager notifications, set Organisational Role to Reports To Manager, then specify the level in Structure and Organisational Group.

For other Notification Type options, complete the fields that appear.

 

 

Add notification conditions

You can configure up to three conditions to determine when the system should generate the notification.

Click Conditions, then select a view from Table Name.

Under Condition 1 select the field to compare, then select an operator.

Enter the comparison value in Value.

If you need to add another condition, select AND or OR under And/Or. 

As required, complete Condition 2 and Condition 3 using the same steps. 

Click Save.

 

 

Configure notification subject and message body

Click Message, then click Configure Subject.

Select a view from Select Data Source, then enter the required text in Subject Text.

🤓Tip: Click individual data source items to insert them into the subject text.

Click Save, then click OK.

Click Cancel, then click Configure Message.

Select a view from Select Data Source, then enter the message content in Subject Message.

🤓Tip: To add system variables to the message, select an item from the Select Data Source lists.

Click Save, then click OK.

Click Cancel, then click Save.

Click OK, then click Cancel.

title: HR event notification emails not creating and / or sending as expected
text:
Possible causes of this issue:

Cause 1: The EMS On/Off indicator is unticked or the Test Run is ticked.

Cause 2: The Event Type or/and Event Notification is disabled or the Event Notification runs in the Test Mode.

Cause 3: The DBA job related to processing these Event Notifications has not been setup correctly, or is broken.

Resolution 1

📌Note: Switching On/Off the EMS should only be actioned in the Back Office.

Back Office

In CoreHR, go to Event Management, and select EMS Parameter Maintenance.

Select the EMS On/Off indicator check box.

Ensure that the Test Run check box is unticked.

Save.

This will ensure the email process for all HR Event Notifications that have email configurations in place​​​.

 

 

Resolution 2
Portal

Go to Data Centre and click View All.

Find Hr Event Configuration and open this option.

Ensure that the Active Ind. switch is on for the relevant Event Type.

Click on 3 dots next to the Event Type and select Edit.

Click on 3 dots next to the relevant Notification ID and select Edit.

On the next screen ensure that the Active Indicator switch is on and the Test Mode Indicator switch is off.

Click Save.

Back Office

Go to CoreHR, then Event Management, and select Hr Event Configuration.

Ensure that the Active Indicator check box is selected for the relevant Event Type.

Click Edit next to the Event Type.

Click Edit next to the relevant Notification ID.

On the next screen ensure that the Active Indicator check box is selected and the Test Mode Indicator check box is unselected.

Click Save Changes.

 

 

Resolution 3

Check the Email Queue to see if an email has been created for these events. If not, please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article, and please include details about when it was first noticed that there was an issue with the event notification emails.

title: Create system alerts, events and reminders
text:
System Reminders can be generated for any user of the system.

Any role set up on the system through Personnel numbers.

Individual emails.

Group emails.

Persons on the system with an assigned Oracle login.

Examples of this include:

Informing I.T. that a new person is about to commence in the organisation.

Informing managers or HR of changes to a person's Department or impending expiry date.

A diary entry is generated in the system for the users and they will be reminded of the event at a specified number of days prior to the employee's start date. Alternatively, an email is sent to a recipient so they can act on it accordingly. When the user logs onto the system, the user will be prompted to view their current reminders if any exist. Reminders can also be viewed through the system at any time.
​
Accessing Event Management System:

CoreHR Menu, Event Management

The Event Management System can be accessed through the main CoreHR screen by selecting CoreHR, Event Management. There are five main options under Event Management relating to EMS.

EMS Parameter Maintenance: Used to set up the parameters for the reminder system.

EMS User Maintenance: Used to store the usernames for the reminder system.

EMS Event Clear Down: Used to clear down existing reminders.

EMS Enquiry: Used to query existing reminders.

HR Event Configuration: The Main EMS setup screen where the reminders are configured.

title: Manage the EMS Parameter Maintenance screen
text:
📌Note: This article is based on users who are Superusers within an Organisation and any changes within EMS should only be carried out by a Superuser. Certain System Parameters need to be set up prior to using the EMS. These parameters are of a Technical nature. 

This screen can be accessed as follows.

Portal - People Management, Data Centre, EMS Parameter Maintenance.

Back Office: CoreHR, Event Management, EMS Parameter Maintenance.

We have some general guidance to help understand the basics of this functionality. The parameter details are as follows.

EMS On / Off: When checked, EMS is turned on. When unchecked, EMS is globally turned off.

Email Separator: Used to parse / separate usernames on the "EMS Maintenance" screen.

EMS Event Software: Different software can be used to remind people of Events / Reminders. Currently 3 exist: CoreHR, MS Outlook'97 (via an OLE link). If MS Outlook '97 is not installed, then this option should not be selected. None is the 3rd option here.

SQL Dir.Path: The directory where the generated SQL files are stored. Note: '\' must be entered at the end of the path. An error will occur when the system attempts to use this path if this path is not available.

Create Script File: Name of the generated script file. Drop Script File.

SQL Plus Location: The location SQL Plus is executable. This is usually located on a server on client sites.

📌Note: changing this location will affect all users

Mail Server: This stores the DNS Name or IP address of the mail exchange server.

EMS Mail History: Clears processed emails X number of days after email is generated.

EMS Username: This stores the description associated with the email address of the sender. i.e Who the reminder is sent from.

Administrator Email: This is the email address of the administrator of the EMS

Test Run: When checked, the email Functionality within the EMS is in Test Mode. This means that all Reminders sent via email will be sent to the Administrator only and not to their intended recipients.

text:

Create new notification

Set indicators

To establish the event timing, enter a number of days in Generate Notification, then in Days enter Before or After.

Select Active Indicator, then select Test Mode Indicator.
​
​Tip: This enables the event in test mode, email reminders are only sent to an administrator. Test mode can be disabled later.
​ 

Click Save Changes, then click OK.

Configure notification subject and message body

Note: All notifications are built in plain text. It's not possible to use bold, italic, or underlined formats.

Click Configure Subject, then select a view from Select Data Source.

Enter required text in Subject Text, click Save, then click OK.
​
​Tip: Click on individual data source items to add them to the text.
​ 

Click Configure Message, then select the required view from Select Data Source.

Enter the message narrative in Message Text, click Save, then click OK.
​
​Tip: Add system variables to the message by clicking an item in the data source lists.

Add notification conditions

Under Conditions, update Table Name with the required view, then update Condition 1 with the field you're comparing.

In the next field, select an operator such as =, then enter the comparison value in the subsequent field.
​
​Note: Single quotes are needed before and after the comparison value. If checking for a status of P, enter a value of 'P'.
​ 

To enter a second or third condition, select AND or OR in the final field alongside the preceding condition, then update all Condition 2 or Condition 3 fields as described above.

title: EMS - Manage the Event Type Maintenance screen
text:
Event Type Maintenance is accessed through the Hr Event Configuration screen. Below is the path on CorePortal:

Search for Data Centre in the top search bar

Open HR Admin Setup Settings (or click View All)

Hr Event Configuration

The Event Type Maintenance screen is displayed once you choose to edit an event type from the CoreHR Events screen. This drills down into a particular event type. From here, new reminders can be created, and existing reminders can be edited or deleted if necessary. The top half of the screen holds details of the event type. The bottom half displays the details of the event notifications/reminders that are generated from that particular event type.
​
​Event Type: This is the field from which the reminder is generated. Examples are 'Probation Expiry' or 'Change of Cost Centre'.
​
​Description: This is an editable text field that is used to hold a description of the reminder(s) that are being sent from the event type. This can be used to store contacts, or provide a short description etc.
​
​Last Run Date: This is the date that the reminders were last run against the database.
​
​Database Trigger: This indicates that the trigger is generated when an item is changed in the database, i.e. when a new value is saved in the database to the selected field.
​
​Active Indicator: Indicates that the particular Event Type is active, i.e. triggers are currently active against that particular event type. This can be used to switch on or off all notifications associated with this particular event type. When checked an event/reminder is fired when that column changes.
​
​Ignore Event Days: Ignores the event if the date on which the trigger is fired falls after 60 days or more of today. This is where the field is set.
​
​Run on Monday – Run on Sunday: Indicates the day on which the reminder is generated. If this is blank the reminder is triggered every time the database job is run (usually every 30 minutes). This is set in the Edit Event Notification Screen.
​
​Save: This allows the user to save any changes they made on the Event Type Maintenance Screen.
​
The Event Notification section of the screen holds details of the reminders that are being generated from the Event type. It stores details of who the mail is being sent to as well as the subject of the mail. Each row refers to a separate notification with an individual notification type. These are all read only at this level and have to be accessed through the edit button:
​
​Notification ID: This is the unique ID given to every notification that is created.
​
​Subject: This is the subject that appears when the reminder is sent to the recipient (either through email or through the PeopleXD/CoreHR system). This is configured in the Event Notification Configuration Screen.
​
​Active: Indicates whether or not that particular notification is active. When checked an event/reminder is fired when that column changes.
​
​Test Mode: Indicates that the Notification is currently running in test mode. When checked, the email functionality within EMS is in test mode. This means that all reminders sent via email will be sent to the Administrator only and not to their intended recipients.
​
​Notification Type: This states the type of notification that is currently used for that particular reminder. The recipient type can be one of

Email

Employee

Organisation Role

Person

Process

Reports To Manager

Username

Recipient: This is related to the Notification Type and shows who the recipient is. Note: there can only be one recipient listed, however this may be a global email or organisational role.
​
​No of Days: Displays the Number of days in advance of the event (e.g., new starter) that the reminder should be sent. If this is set to zero, then the reminder is sent straight after the column has changed. This is used in conjunction with the next heading which states whether the event is sent before or after the specific date. For example, a reminder is sent to HR 14 days before a person is due to commence work.
​
​Before/After: This is used in conjunction with the No of Days fields. This indicates whether the event is sent before or after the event date.
​
​Edit (three-dot ellipsis): This allows you to edit the configuration of the highlighted event. This brings up the event Notification Configuration screen with the current settings displayed and available to editing.
​
​Add New Notification: This is used to add a new notification/reminder to the event type. This brings up a blank event Notification Configuration screen from which a new notification can be created.

title: Send test emails to users in a non-production environment
text:
Your non-production environments, for example User Acceptance Testing (UAT), are typically configured to send emails to a test queue based on the Test Run setting being enabled. You can temporarily disable this setting, whilst testing, to validate email-based processes against real recipients.

⚠️ Important: Make sure you re-enable Test Run after testing to prevent unintended email delivery.

Turn off test run mode

To allow emails to reach real inboxes, turn off the Test Run toggle.

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Click View All, then click EMS Parameter Maintenance.

Turn off the Test Run toggle.

Once you turn off this setting, the system sends emails to configured recipients.

Check emails in the queue

When you turn off Test Run, the system begins processing emails already in the queue.

The system processes the most recent emails first.

The number of emails processed depends on client configuration.

To view the email queue:

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Click View All, then click View Email Queue.

Review this screen to check which emails are waiting, processing, or sent.

Trigger a test email

Trigger an action in the system to generate a test email.

Ensure the Test Run toggle is off.

Trigger an email, for example by uploading an employee document.

Open View Email Queue.

Check that the email:

Appears in the queue.

Processes successfully.

Arrives in the correct inbox.

Turn test run mode back on

After testing, turn Test Run back on to stop further emails from reaching real inboxes.

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Click View All, then click EMS Parameter Maintenance.

Turn on the Test Run toggle.

text:
HR process task lists define a set of steps that must be completed as part of a new starter, new contract, additional contract, rehire or leaver process. To learn how to create and manage HR task lists, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, enter and select Data Centre.

Click OPEN on the HR Admin Setup Settings option.

Click HR Task Lists.

Click the relevant process type tab.

Click ADD.

Click the relevant task from the dropdown list.

Enter Optional Information, if required.

Click SAVE.

Re-order the task by clicking and dragging it to the desired position.

text:

On the three-dot ellipses, click Edit to open Event Maintenance.

Then click on Add New Notification.

Under Generate Notification, select when you would like the notification to be generated, typically a number of days before.

Below Recipient, supply Notification Type, Email Address.

📌Note: If it's to go to managers, the Notification Type should be Organisation Role, and Organisation Role should be set to Reports To.

Under Message, select Configure Subject and Configure Message in turn.

For each, select the Data Source you would like to use and insert your Subject Text and Message Text.

Once configuration is complete, the event can be set active via the Active indicator on the Event Maintenance screen.  Where possible, the process should be trialed first in a test environment.

title: How to report on surveys
text:
Reporting on surveys using Insight
To facilitate reporting on surveys, special survey views exist in Insight only.
When a survey is created, a dynamic view is created for Insight with the same name as the survey.
If the name of the survey is 'New Job Survey', then the view in Insight will be 'New Job Survey (Personnel)'.
You will also have to include the HR PERSON MASTER view with fields person reference, forename and surname so you can see what employees the survey answers are linked to.
​
​Reporting on surveys using an external reporting tool
When linked to PeopleXD database via an external reporting tool, it is usually possible to view all views and tables and use them for reporting purposes.  However, it is not possible to see/use the survey views above as they exist only in Insight. The table where the survey data is held is available i.e. cp_custom_forms.
As Insight has a specially configured views, it might be best to use Insight for reporting purposes.

title: Portal: Language pack overview
text:
The language pack contains a library of all labels and phrases used within PeopleXD. Authorised users can update the labels and phrases displayed on screen, either through the Site Manager widget or by selecting the Enable Language Pack option from their user profile menu. Watch the video or follow the steps below.

📌Note: While multiple languages are available, they are managed and provided to customers by Access. However, you can update the default labels supplied for any language.

 

Site Manager widget

On the dashboard menu, enter and select Site Manager in the search bar.

Against Language Pack, click Open, then select your language if not English.

Enter your label text in Search for a label, then click the search icon. 

Labels that contain the search text will be returned with the following detail.

Label - The text that is currently used.

Default Label - The default text supplied at installation.

Updated On - The date the label was last updated. If blank, the default has never been changed.

For the required phrase, click the Label field, then replace the text. 

📌Note: Changes are saved automatically, and all label instances in the system are updated.

 

 

Enable Language Pack mode 

Navigate to the screen with the label to be updated, then click your user profile.​

🤓Tip: The user profile is the circle icon in the top right corner of the screen, it usually contains your photo or initials.

Click Enable Language Pack, then click YES to reload screen.

Labels that can be updated are highlighted in green, hover your cursor over the field to be amended.

In the pop-up window, overtype text in New Phrase, then click SAVE to update all occurrences of that label. 

Click your user profile, then click Disable Language Pack.

Click Yes to exit Language Pack mode and return to normal screen operation.

 

 

Other considerations

It can take up to 72 hours for the changes to become effective. If you can't see your amendments after this time, try the following.

Clear the cache from your browser.

Switch your browser to private or incognito mode.

title: Portal: Create a new User Defined Field
text:
User Defined Fields (UDFs) are used to hold data on the system that are specific to an individual organisation and are not available as standard. To find out how to configure your user defined data, watch the video or follow the below steps.

 

📌Note: We recommend you apply configuration changes in a test environment first to confirm they work before deploying to live.

 

 

Go to the People Management Dashboard.

Click the Data Centre tab.

Click Open on the HR Admin Setup Settings option.

Click User Defined Objects.

Click Add.

Input a Reference Code and Description.

Click Save.

Click the three dot menu on the relevant UDF, then click Data Labels.

Create the data labels, ensure the Active toggle is on, then click OK.

Click the three dot menu on the relevant UDF, then click Advanced.

Select Employees, or Post Appointments as required.

Enable or disable the following toggles.

Display on CorePortal allows employees and managers to view the UDF, provided they have the relevant menu options enabled.

Allow Update on CorePortal allows employees and managers to update the UDF, provided they have the relevant menu options enabled.

Hide Dates on CorePortal hides the From Date and To Date fields on all Portal screens, and will impact on the employee's, manager's and HR administrator's view of the UDF.

Click OK

title: ModSecurity checking and issues
text:
ModSecurity is an Application Firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application. By inspecting HTTP traffic, it can prevent attacks stemming from web application security flaws, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), file inclusion, and security misconfigurations.

Items that are likely to be blocked or cause an error/conflict include the following.

📌Note: This is not an exhaustive list.

SRC

Style

()

 !,=, <>

/bold

Using url's with ?ref=Link

images/logos

If you are getting a 403 error and are using any of these items in text or comment fields, you should remove them and save your input again.

Related Articles

title: System emails not being delivered
text:
Emails may not be reaching their intended recipient as they are being treated as spam by their email provider or an error occurred whilst being processed by the system. To check this, follow the below steps.

 

Review the email queue

You'll need to view the email queue to determine if the email has been generated and processed by the system.

 

Portal guidance

Go to the People Management dashboard.

On the Data Centre widget click View All. 

Search for View Email Queue and open it.

Back office guidance

Go to CorePersonnel.

Click Reference dropdown.

Select Utilities, then View Email Queue.

Follow up activities

If the emails are Processed in the Email Queue and there are no errors displayed it means that all is working as expected on in PeopleXD, i.e. the emails have left the server correctly. In this case, please contact your local IT or/and your email provider. The email may be being treated as spam or junk.

 

Check EMS Username setting

If the EMS Username is configured incorrectly, this can cause it to be treated as junk mail by the recipient's email provider. This frequently occurs with Gmail and Hotmail accounts.

 

Portal configuration

Go to the People Management dashboard.

On the Data Centre widget click View All.

Search for EMS Parameter Maintenance and open it.

Back office configuration

Go to CorePersonnel.

Click Reference dropdown.

Select Utilities, then View Email Queue.

Parameter setting

Ensure that the contents of the EMS Username field match that of the Administrator Email field. It should be peoplexd@accessacloud.com in both fields.

title: Create a HAR file in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge
text:
There will be very rare occasions that the support team are not able to replicate an issue that has been raised to us. In these cases our Developers will require some information from the browser you are using when you experience the issue. This can be recorded and sent to us via HAR file, which you can get without having to access or download third party software.
​
A HAR, also known as a HTTP Archive, is a JSON-formatted archive file for logging a web browser's interaction with a site. Our developers can use this file to look at the code to help identify any issues.
​
To create a HAR file in Chrome or Edge to send to the development team:

Navigate to a point before the issue arises.

Open the Chrome or Edge Developer Tools by pressing F12.

Within the Developer Tools click on the Network tab. If you do not see the Network tab you might need to expand the view by clicking the >> icon.

Tick the Preserve log checkbox. This allows the tool to record data as you move between tabs.

Try to recreate the issue or error that you have reported to us. For example, take the steps you followed when first encountering the issue. As you do, you will see the Developer Tools automatically fill with data. 

Once you have fully replicated the issue, click the download icon to download the HAR file.

Save the file to a location on your computer. We recommend that you zip and password protect the file.

Locate the file and attach it to the email replying to our request. Provide the password in a separate reply.

title: Org Chart: Details that can be displayed on an employee card
text:
The employee card in the org chart includes the following information.

Job title.

Name.

Initials / employee photo.

Department (configurable).

Email address.

Phone number (configurable).

 

 

Org Level

The organisational level displayed on the employee card defaults to department. To amend it to another level follow the steps below.

Go to the Administrator Dashboard.

Click on the Site Manager.

Open Admin Settings.

Search for cp_org_structure_element.

Update the value with the code for another structure level, e.g. LOC for Location.

Click OK.

 

 

Contact Type

There are two parameters, that control the display and choice of contact type on the org chart cards.

 

Update Contact Type

 

To display a different contact type on the employee card, i.e. instead of the home phone number, follow the steps below.

📌Note: For this parameter to take effect, the home phone number must first be set to display.

Go to the Administrator Dashboard.

Click on the Site Manager tab.

Open Admin Settings.

Search for cp_org_contact_type.

Edit the parameter.

Update the value with the code for a different level e.g. MOBILE for work mobile phone.

Click OK.

Show home phone number

This option must be set to ensure that a contact type can be displayed, rather than the employee’s extension. To display the default contact type of home phone number, Follow the steps below.

Go to the Administrator Dashboard.

Click on the Site Manager tab.

Open Admin Settings.

Search for cp_org_show_home_no.

Edit the parameter.

Update the value to Y.

Click OK.

The Data Migration tool allows you to bulk upload specific data during the initial stages of the system setup.

title: Portal: Upload data migration files
text:
To upload a data migration file, download the required template, open it to enter the necessary data, then save and upload it. Follow the steps below.

Download the template files from the Data Migration Templates widget.

You might need to rename the file with a .csv file extension.

Open Microsoft Excel and select File, then Open to open the template file.

The text import wizard should then appear.

📌Note: Always open the file using this method—do not open the template file directly. Select the pipe character (|) as the delimiter, and choose Text as the data format.

Once the template file is open, open the helper file for guidance.

After completing the import wizard, enter data from the row under the headings.  PeopleXD uses the headings to identify the template file type during upload.

🤓Note: Ensure the top two rows in the file match the blank template exactly. Do not add extra data, such as pipe characters, to these rows.

When saving, select Save as and choose the .csv (comma delimited) format.

title: Portal: Maintaining employee addresses
text:
The system is designed so that only HR admins have the effective date option when changing the address, employees just overwrite the current value.

 

To update an employee address as an administrator, follow the steps below.

In the portal, go to People Management dashboard.

Go to the Command Centre widget, select VIEW next to Employees.

Search for the Employee you wish to update, then click View.

Go to Contact Information tab.

Under My Address Details, select the three dot ellipsis on the line Default Address.

Select Edit Address Details.

Update Effective Date and new address details.

Save.

To keep a history of addresses, click Add Address in the address maintenance screen.

Choosing an Address Type of Home and a greater effective date than the current address. This will then update the address on the Personal Profile screen and add a second row to the Address Maintenance screen.

Choosing an address type of Default with a greater effective date than the current address would not update the Personal Profile screen but it would add a second row to the Address Maintenance screen.

Editing the address on the personal profile screen will just update the existing entry and won't create a record on the Address Maintenance screen.

Updating the Address via Portal will also only update the existing address.

title: Back Office: Generating an Employee Status report
text:
An Employee Status report can be generated through the personal profile of an employee. This will highlight the main details for an employee on CorePay and CorePersonnel, including certain audit aspects of the software.

 

Generating the status report

Click CorePersonnel, Maintenance, Personal Profile.

Query the employee.

In the Select Detail list, select View Employee History.

Click Status Report.

Use the Report Destination drop-down and select required screen. A PDF report will be produced.

📌Note: Ensure that pop up blockers are switched off and if the status report does not pop up, check the task bar or other browser windows for tabs containing the Status Report.

Save this file and attach it to any case relating to Employee's Appointments or Payroll Status. If an example employee is given for a larger issue then the Status Report for that Employee should be attached.

 

 

Things to check on a status report

Once an employee has been created in CorePersonnel and then added to CorePay, they should appear as Fully Active (unless setup with a future End Date).

Once an employee has been ended and Payroll has processed them as a leaver then they will appear as Fully Dormant.

From these main Status', an employee can be marked as leaving or rejoining, and from there, an employee can be marked as leaving to rejoining or rejoining to leaving.

Payroll cannot account for more than two changes of Status (i.e. Leaving to Rejoining to Leaving is not possible to be processed in one Payroll Period even if the Effective Dates fall into different periods).

 

 

Summary of statuses

Payroll Status must match the Appointment History.
Status relates primarily to the Primary Appointments shown in the Appointment History section.

 

Fully Active Employee

Secondary Status = 'S'.

New Secondary Status = NULL.

Date Leaving = Orig Leaving = Rejoin Date = NULL.

Appointment History contains one Primary (Substantive) 'CO' Post which has the newest Actual Start Date populated.

 

Fully Dormant Employee

Secondary Status = 'Z'.

New Secondary Status = NULL.

Date Leaving = DD-Mon-YYYY.

Orig Leaving = Rejoin Date = NULL.

Appointment History contains all EN Appointments. Most recent Actual End Date is the same as the Date Leaving in CorePay.

 

A Fully Active employee can be leaving in previous, current or future periods.

 

When someone is marked as a Leaver, their Payroll Status becomes the following. These Employees are Leaving but not yet processed as Left.

Secondary Status = ' S'.

New Secondary Status =  'Z'.

Date Leaving = DD-Mon-YYYY.

Orig Leaving = Rejoin Date = NULL.

Appointment History contains all EN appointments. Most recent Actual End Date is the same as the Date Leaving in CorePay.

If the Date Leaving is in the current or any previous period and Generate Salaries and Allowances has run then their Secondary Status will become 'L'.

 

A fully dormant employee can be Rejoined in Current or Previous periods.

 

When the employee has been marked as a rejoiner in CorePersonnel, then their payroll status becomes the following:

Secondary Status = 'S'.

New Secondary Status = 'X'.

Date Leaving = NULL.

Orig Leaving = DD-Mon-YYYY.

Rejoin Date = DD-Mon-YYYY (different to above Orig Leaving).

Appointment History contains one CO post which has an Actual Start that matches the Rejoin Date and the previous post which should have an EN post with the Orig Leaving as the Actual End.

If someone is rejoined for a date which is less than or equal to today but is in considered to be in a Future Payroll period then their Secondary status will be Z and the Date Leaving will also be populated.

If someone is rejoined to a date in the future then their payroll status will only update once that Date arrives and the Confirmed Future job runs.

 

Someone who is marked as Leaving (but not yet processed as Fully Dormant)

 

They can be rejoined in the same period if the Rejoin Date is within the Continuous Employment number of days OR in any subsequent period. These are known as   Leaver - Rejoiners.

Secondary Status = 'S'.

New Secondary Status = 'Y'.

Date Leaving = 'DD-Mon-YYYY'.

Orig Leaving = NULL.

Rejoin Date = DD-Mon-YYYY (different to above Orig Leaving).

Date Leaving is the Actual End Date of second newest post and rejoin date is the Actual Start Date of newest post (should be 'CO' status).

Outside of Continuous Employment but within the confines of the Payroll Period an employee cannot leave and rejoin as they must be processed Fully Dormant before being Rejoined in the next payroll run.

Someone marked as rejoining can be ended, they are known as Rejoiner - Leavers.

 

Their payroll status will be as follows:

Secondary Status = 'Z'.

New Secondary Status = 'T'.

Date Leaving = DD-Mon-YYYY.

Orig Leaving = NULL.

Rejoin Date = DD-Mon-YYYY (different to above Orig Leaving).

Most recent post is EN and the Date Leaving is the Actual End Date with the Rejoin Date being the Actual Start Date, previous appointment is also EN

Employee must be a Rejoiner only for this status to take place.

Once Generate Salaries and Allowances has run the Secondary Status can be S, L or Z depending on the effective periods of the rejoin and the leaving.

title: Data Migration Tool - Migrate and completed screens
text:
The Errors screen lists all files that have completed validation and have encountered file or line errors.
​
The errors can be viewed per file or all at once and each list is paginated to 50 results per page.
​
The errors page should be displayed by line number when viewed by file and by file and line number when viewing all.
​
The observations page will give distinct error messages grouped by their codes to allow for easier identification of common or recurring errors.
​
Options available per file are:

Re-upload File: This allows the user to replace the file with a new or amended version. The user would do this if there were format, syntax or value errors in the file that could only be corrected by amending the file

Re-validate File: This allows the user to clear down the errors for that file and re-validate without replacing the file. This would be done if for example reference data was added in the software

View Errors for File: This displays an error screen limited to the file in question

Delete File: This allows the user to delete the file and errors associated with it and begin again

 The View All Errors or View Errors for File options return a screen like the below. This screen will list the errors generated by the validation on a file by file and line by line basis
​
For lower numbers of errors (less than 100) it is advised that this screen is best used. This screen is ideal for identifying validation errors with a particular record or records
​
Once all reference based errors have been corrected the user can re-validate the file without needing to re-upload. This only applies to errors where the data on the file is correct but something needs to change in the system to allow validation (i.e. setting up a Department).When files have been set to re-validate the Upload tab will show the below status
​
Once the file or files have passed validation the status on the Upload Tab will change to Validation Complete. No Errors and the files appear in the Valid Files section of the Migrate tab.
​Note: Users should wait until all the files they are loading have been validated before Migrating. This is to ensure data integrity is maintained between the files and the actual system
​
Once happy that all the necessary files are uploaded and validated then you should press the Migrate button to set the files as ready to Migrate into the CoreHR main database tables (this option is menu controlled and will not appear without the correct access).
​
Files that are queued to Migrate appear with the following status
​
A second DBA job runs (<V23 this runs every 5 minutes, V24+ this runs on demand when the 'Migrate button is selected) to migrate the files into the database. Once this has completed and the rows have been inserted in the database they appear in the Completed Files section of the Migrate screen and are removed from the File Upload screen allowing additional files of that type to be uploaded.

title: Insight: Employees missing from a report with diversity or UDF fields
text:
Insight reports that source data from multiple views include only employees who have data present in both views, as demonstrated below.

If a person has no diversity entries in their record, they will not appear in a report built from a personnel view (e.g. HR Person Master) and the Person Diversity (Personnel) view, because they do not exist in the diversity table.

If an employee has no user defined fields in their record, they will not appear in a report built from a personnel view (e.g. HR Person Master) and the Person User Data (Personnel) view, because they do not exist in the UDF table.

To return all employees or applicants in such a report, regardless of whether their records include diversity or UDF data, an outer join must be enabled. If this scenario occurs, contact your support team or Customer Success Manager (CSM) to determine whether an outer join can be added to the report. This will allow the report to include employees with data is present in only one view.

⚠️Warning: If a report includes columns from a transactional (large) table or view (e.g. Appointment History, Salary History), it may negatively affect system performance. In such cases, Access might not enable the outer join.

title: Insight: Exported file cannot be opened in Microsoft Excel
text:
If Microsoft Excel displays an error when attempting to open the exported file, or if the file appears empty, there are several possible causes. Please review the following.

 

Firefox web browser

Mozilla Firefox may not automatically generate the file in a valid format for Excel. The simplest solution is to use another browser, such as Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. However, if you prefer to continue using Firefox, you must change the default program Firefox uses to open .xlsx files to Microsoft Excel. Follow the steps below.

Go to the relevant report in Insight, click Actions, then click Export Data. 

Select Excel and click OK.

Firefox will present a pop-up box about the file you are about to download. Under the "What Should Firefox do with this file?" section, if any program other than Excel appears (e.g. 7-Zip File Manager), you need to change it. 

Click the dropdown menu and select Excel if available. If not, click Other.

If Excel appears in the new list, select it. If not, click Browse.

Locate the EXCEL.EXE program on your PC.  This is usually found at C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE, but the location may vary. 

📌Note: You can also use the search function to find excel.exe, although this may take some time.

Once you have selected EXCEL.EXE as the default program, tick Do this automatically for files like this from now on, then click OK.

 

 

Invalid data format

Check the data within the report. If you find any irregular characters, symbols, or emojis, the export will fail. Remove such data from individual fields, then try exporting again.

 

 

Export as a CSV file

Select the option in Insight to export the report as a CSV file. You can then open the file in Excel and save it in .xlsx format.
