title: Insight: Organisational roles audit
text:
The system does not create values for a specific employee in the audit table against entries that were done in the HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON table which stores the organisational roles data, thus it cannot be precisely established which user actioned the change/update to the org role of an employee. 
​
However, you can create an Insight report that returns related information, i.e. who updated and ended an org role recently with a particular end date.

From the dashboard menu, search and select Insight.

Click on Actions, and select Create Report.

Enter a name for your report, then click OK.

Click ADD, then select Column.

Select the Audit Details (Personnel) view, and add the following columns.

Audit Type.

Table Name.

Date And Time.

Date And Time 24hour Format.

Field Name.

Old Value.

New Value. 

Username.

Select Filters from the dropdown, click ADD, and create the following filters.

Table Name Equal to HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON.

Field Name Equal to DATE_TO.

New Value Contains "the end date in question"  in the format DD-MMM-YY.

Select Sorts from the dropdown, then click ADD. 

Select the Date And Time column Descending.

Once you run the report the Username column will show who entered the end date in question recently, the Date And Time column will show when this took place, and the Date And Time 24hour Format column will show the exact time.

📌Note: There might be a case that more than one user has entered the end date in question for an org role recently. This would need to be further verified internally as the report will not show for whom exactly the end date has been entered, nor for which org role.

title: Insight: No data displaying in a UDF user defined report
text:
Reason 1

A UDF(User Defined) report with Person User Data,  HR Person Master and Appointment History views generates no data. When the Appointment History view fields are removed, data displays.


UDF Codes can be linked to either personnel number or appointment ID. When linked to personnel number, the appointment id remains blank for employees. Therefore, no data will display for this type of UDF when the Appointment History view is included in the report.


If the Appointment History view is required for the report, create calculations for each field required with the function PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD and do not use Person User Data.

 

 

Reason 2

The UDF report is referencing Person User Data and HR Person Master.
The report Access Type is Manager so would expect employees that the manager has access to display on the report but the report is blank.


The Person User Data view works differently to other views. It requires a user, including a Manager user, to be granted access via Security Dashboard > Setup > System User > Personnel Access.


If this is an issue, the UDF reports can be setup using HR Person Master view and the function PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD to report on the UDF fields.  Then the Manager will see data when the report runs and will not need access via System Users.

 

 

Reason 3

If a UDF is setup in Data Centre, User Defined Objects with the Security field enabled, then the user logged in will require access to that UDF in the Security dashboard, Setup, System Users for security type User Defined.
​

 

Report configuration reasons 1 and 2

If data is not displaying in a user defined (UDF) report because of reason 1 or reason 2, then create an Insight report using HR Person Master and the function PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD. If Appointment data is required, add Appointment History view.

In Insight, add Calculation and select XD Functions tab.  Enter Calculation Name.

Enter PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD in the Search field and select this.

A window pops up ‘Enter Parameter Functions’.

The three mandatory fields are P_EMPNO, P_REFERENCE_CODE,P_TEXT.

Enter Person Reference and select this field for P_EMPNO

Enter the UDF Code in P_Reference_Code  field and press Enter to add to the list.

Enter DATE1 in P_Text field and press return to add to the list.

You should see something like example below when the UDF Code is ‘ASSOC’.

PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD(P_EMPNO=>PRCI_HR_PERSON_MASTER.PERSON_REFERENCE, P_REFERENCE_CODE=>'ASSOC', P_TEXT=>'DATE1').

This will display the dates held in the 'From Date' field for the UDF Code.

Repeat these steps for each field required e.g. TEXT1, TEXT2.

title: Insight Report displaying Audit Information on removal of access in System User screen
text:
Create Insight Report using view Audit Details (Personnel).
Include fields e.g. Audit Type, Date Audited, Username, Old Value, New Value, Table Name, Field Name.
​
The main table for access to personnel data is PERS_USER so you can use that in filter.
The best field to use here is PERSONNEL_NO i.e. personnel_no of an employee whom access was removed from.
​
Examples for the Filters are as follows:
​
Table Name Equal to PERS_USER
Filed Name Equal  to PERSONNEL_NO
Audit Type Equal to Delete
Date Audited Between XX-XX-XXXX and YY-YY-YYYY
​
This will give you the name of the user who removed access from an employee.
​
The other Audit Types are Insert, Update but Delete is the relevant one to find when access has been removed.
​

title: Bank Details Update notification sent when no update made
text:
These notifications are sent even if there was no actual change of bank details i.e. in cases when the screen was accessed by a user and the existing values such as bank account number, sort code have been saved without any update.


It is recommended to rely on the audit report rather than on the one showing the notifications. The audit report shows changes only when a new value is entered which means that if the same value is entered/saved the audit does not treat this as an update/change. However, in such cases, the system sends the notification that the bank details were updated.

 

We provide guidance if you are unsure how to generate a bank details audit report.

title: Insight: Employee not visible in report
text:
Resolution 1

Please verify in the report has filters. If a report is filtered it may cause the employee to not appear on the Insight Report. To check the filters please follow the below steps:

Navigate to Portal

Go to Insight

Select Admin Area on the left-hand panel

Search for the report

Click Manage Report

Select Filters

Disable filter and test


Resolution 2

Review the configuration of the report to verify whether it does include views in Insight which are not built off Personnel tables, e.g. Person Master (Pay) or Person Profile Details (Pay) views. If there is no outer join enabled on the report it will exclude staff who are not appearing on both Personnel and Payroll tables. Where a report contains columns that are based off both Personnel and Pay views, the suggested course of action is to clone the report and amend the configuration of columns/fields where necessary to exclude Insight views that are built off non-personnel tables and instead use personnel equivalents or calculations to retrieve the relevant data. Should you have further queries around this please raise a new case with Support and reference this article.

title: Amend salary details for an employee
text:
To correct an employee’s salary entered in error, you can’t delete the original amendment once it’s approved or rejected. Instead, submit a new salary amendment with the same effective date and the correct salary. The system uses the input date to distinguish between amendments. Both entries will appear in the employee’s salary history, but the latest one will override the incorrect version.

 

To amend the salary for an ended appointment, submit a new salary amendment with an effective date earlier than the appointment’s end date. The system will then generate the salary as expected.

 

To amend an employee’s salary, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

Portal instructions

Go to the People Management dashboard.

Go to the Command Centre widget.

Click View on the Employees option.

Search for an employee and click View.

Click the Current Salary tab.

Ensure you have selected the correct contract from the dropdown menu at the top of the page.

Click Add.

Enter the details on the New Salary section.

Click Save.

Back office instructions

Go to CorePersonnel.

Click on Maintenance.

Go to Salary Administration and click Maintain HR salary amendments.

Search the employee in question and click on Add button.

Enter the salary details and save the record.

title: Cancel an allowance
text:
Canceling an allowance ensures that the employee does not get paid for this allowance. This is useful if the allowance has been set up in error by HR.

This process ensures that the cancelled allowance record:

Is effectively ended in both HR and Payroll

Is searchable in HR with a status of Cancelled

Is searchable in Payroll with a status of Cancelled

An Allowance can be cancelled if all of the following conditions are met.

The Allowance is fully approved, i.e. if using Salary Approvals, it's not possible to cancel an Allowance that's in a status of Outstanding.

The Allowance is visible in Payroll i.e. employee payroll setup has been completed.

An Allowance cannot be cancelled if any of the following conditions are met.

Allowance is Outstanding.

Allowance is not visible in Payroll, i.e. this implies the employee payroll setup hasn't been completed.

If the allowance is fully approved but not visible to payroll, i.e. employee payroll setup has not been completed, then the cancel option is not applicable. In this instance, it is possible to directly delete the allowance from the system.
​
To cancel an allowance. follow the steps below.

Go to the People Management dashboard.

On the Command Centre widget, click View for the Employees option.

Search for an employee and click View.

📌Note: If the employee has multiple contracts, you need to select the relevant one from the drop-down menu.

Click the Current Salary tab.

Click the Allowances section.

Click the three-dot menu of the Allowance to be edited, then click Cancel.

If the allowance does not meet the conditions required to cancel, the user will be prevented from doing so. If the Allowance does meet the conditions to cancel (i.e. it is fully approved and passed to payroll) then clicking Cancel Allowance will be effective immediately.

⚠️Important: The retrospective taking back of the money for the cancelled allowance only takes place if it's open when the cancellation is made. If an allowance was ended before the cancellation, the system won't claw back the money paid. In this case, the arrears need to be manually calculated and entered as a timesheet entry.

title: Planned salary is not showing for approval
text:
When a planned salary appears against an employee record, this isn't a true salary that applies to them.


On creating a post, HR can enter an indicative salary that should apply to the post, this is the planned salary. When you appoint a new starter to a post, you'll still need to enter a salary for the employee. If that's not done, the system will show any planned salary that's been entered in its place.

📌Note: Valid statuses for a true salary line against an employee are as follows.

Pending – The salary hasn't been approved at any level.

In Approval – The salary's been partially approved but not by all approvers.

Approved – The salary's fully approved by all approvers.

Future – As approved, but the effective date's greater than today.

Rejected – The salary's been rejected and won't be paid.

Select the required appointment.

At the top of the screen, click Salary Details, and note the increment due date.

title: Assigning default menu profiles
text:
The Security Access screen include a list of roles and indicators. The purpose of these indicators is to provide a quick way for a user to identify the role that the employee has in the organisation and assign them to a default menu profile. These  may be managed in a number of ways, some of them are as follows.

 

The Security Access screen includes a list of roles and indicators. These indicators help users quickly identify an employee’s role within the organisation and assign a default menu profile. You can manage these in several ways, including the following.

Directly assigning menu profiles to the employee's portal user account in PeopleXD Security.

Automatic assignment via Self Registration (Menu Profile Matrix Account Provisioning).

Assignment via the organisational role rules defined in the Menu Profile Matrix.

To complete these tasks, follow the steps below.


Manually assign a menu profile

Go to Security, click User Management.

Search for the employee that needs to be updated.

Click the three-dot ellipsis on the account and select Manage Account.

Click Menu Profiles. 

Activate any menu profiles that need to be added to the user's account.

 

 

Automatically assign via Self Registration

📌Note: Menu Profile Matrix account provisioning can only be used where self-registration is enabled.

Go to Security, click Self-Registration.

Within the Self Registration Profiles widget, turn 'Off' the Status on Default.

Click on the three-dot ellipsis, then click Edit.

Go through the steps, on step 5 enable the Matrix Rules.

Select the Default Menu Profile to assign to newly created accounts via self-registration.

Click Next, then click Save.

 


Assign via the organisational role rules in the Menu Profile Matrix

Go to People Management, click Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click View All.

Click Menu Profile Matrix, then click Add.

Configure by using the dropdown options.

Click Ok, then click Save.

title: Single sign-on with LDAP
text:
When you have delegated your SSO authentication to an LDAP (e.g. Microsoft Active Directory), users log into PeopleXD Portal using their LDAP Account. When you use LDAP:

Authentication is delegated to an LDAP (e.g. Microsoft Active Directory).

LDAP allows for a user to log on to shared applications on their network using a single username and password.

LDAP username must be unique and recorded in the Contact Information screen of the employee’s record.

A user logs on to Portal using their LDAP account. The LDAP manages the Password Policy.

Users provides their login credentials

Navigate to the Command Centre and open the Employees option.

Search for the employee and click View. 

Click the Contact Information tab. 

Next to the Ldap user field expand the 3-dot menu.

Click Edit. 

Enter the username and click OK. Note: LDAP usernames must be unique.

title: Rehire still appearing on dormant employee list
text:
Note: The key to avoiding a rehire from showing on a dormant list is ensuring that the employee is fully dormant before being processed as a rehire. This will prevent any issues from occurring.

Scenario 1

The software is behaving as expected -- no manual intervention is required.
​
Simply wait for the employee's status to update automatically the next time you run the Complete Update Payroll Job (Pay355).
​
For a period of time after a rejoin, the employee may still appear in the CorePersonnel dormant list with a date left (and a latest start/rejoin date). This is due to the current stage of your payroll processing, and will update by itself to fully active ('S') as further steps are completed.
​
The employee is usually not dormant on CorePay - the only actual dormant status on CorePay is Z - so approved salary would not be affected.
​
​Note: The Customer Support team cannot manually intervene to make the employee active earlier, as this can create knock-on effects in CorePay.
​

Scenario 2

When an employee is in a pay group that is not processed / no payroll runs are completed for it, then the employee will remain dormant until the employee is moved to a pay group that is processed.
​

Scenario 3

When an employee is in a pay group  A , rejoined and moved to Paygroup B before complete rejoin 
​

title: Portal: Add new reference data to your organisation structure
text:
You may need to update your organisation structure to reflect changes in your company, for example, when you create a new department or open a new location. 

 

To do this in PeopleXD People management, you need to create the relevant reference data, then update your structure setup. 

 

Create a new organisation unit

To create new a new organisation unit in PeopleXD People Management, watch the video or follow the steps below.

📌Note: You need to create companies in PeopleXD Payroll and work groups in PeopleXD Workforce Management.

 

 From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Click VIEW ALL or, next to Reference Data, click OPEN.

Search for and select the relevant reference data. This can include: 

Management Units.

Divisions.

Departments.

Cost Centres.

Location Codes.

Any other units used in your structure.

Click Add then complete the required fields.

If available, turn on the Active toggle, then click Save.

 

 

Add an organisation unit to the hierarchy

After creating new reference data, you need to add it to your organisation structure. To do this, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Click VIEW ALL, then click Structure Setup.

Search for the relevant structure and click HIERARCHY. 

Click EXPAND ALL, then search for the relevant hierarchy item.

Click the three-dot menu, then select Add.

From the filter list, select Include Linked Items.

Search for the reference data then turn on the Add to Hierarchy toggle.

Click SAVE.

title: Back Office: Configuring org roles and groups
text:
Organisation roles and groups  - Terminology

The first step of understanding Organisation Roles and Groups is to have a clear understanding of the terminology involved:

Reporting to Type - This is either Employee ('E') or Organisational ('O') Role and Group. If this is set to 'E' then logic is simply the employee's 'Reports To Person' (Employee 1 reports to Manager A). Otherwise the Org. Role and Group are used as outlined below.

Organisational Role - This refers to the managerial role selected to organise this module. Example roles are 'Line Manager', 'Timesheet Approver' and 'Head of Department'.

Organisational Group - This is the level in Core|HR at which the organisation is performed. Example groups are 'Company', 'Department', 'Cost Centre' and 'Pay Group'.

 

 

Set-up of organisational role

Setting up Organisational Roles and Groups is performed through CorePersonnel. The first step is to create the Organisational Role using the Organisational Role Types screen (Personnel, Reference K - P, Organisational Role Types). 
​
Once these roles have been created, they can be assigned at specific levels, for specific functions.
​
In the case of the ‘Reports To’ functionality in CorePersonnel, select CorePersonnel Main Menu, Reference Q - Z, System Parameters.
​
The Reporting To can be set at an individual level (By Employee Number: Select Employee's Manager from List of Values) or can be based on the Organisational Role setup (By Org Group). The ‘Allow Override’ indicator becomes active when the By Org Group option is selected. This means that the manager that displays against the employee based on Org Roles can be overwritten, if required.
​
The Reporting to Org Group determines at what level the Reporting To structure will be against. By default this will be Workgroup level. This is used by the majority of clients. The Reporting to Role is set to the Organisational Role that was created in the previous step.
​
The Reporting To Text displays as the label against the Reporting to field. This can be changed to Reporting To Manager or Supervisor or Line Manager, etc.

 

 

Set-up of managers

Having defined the organisational role, the next step is to set-up the actual manager(s) per "Group Item". Using Org Roles and Groups allows for the "Group Item" level to be set at different levels. Currently these are:

Company.

Cost Centre.

Department.

Division.

Location.

Management Unit.

Pay Group.

Project Code.

User Field 1-5.

Work Group.

For example  the "Group Item" level by default is 'Work Group'.
Note also that there is a Date From and Date To field so the date range can be set for this to be applicable.
Note there is no 'shortcut' option to copy (for example Work Group) access over from one user to another on this screen. A higher level of the hierarchy such as 'Company', can be used to minimize the number of manual entries required.

 

 

Maintaining organisational roles

These can created and maintained under two screens.

Reference - Maintain Organisational Roles.

Reference - Maintain Organisational Roles by Person.

 

 

Maintain organisational roles by person

This Organisational Role setup can be done by Person instead. Navigate to CorePersonnel Main Menu, Reference, Maintain Organisational Roles By Person

Select the employee from the list of values.

Select the Role, Org Group (Work Group, for example) from the drop down lists.

Input a Date From and select an Org Group Item (such as a particular Workgroup).

 

 

Overview of steps for creating & maintaining organisational roles​

Ensure the Organisational Role is created (Reference K-P, Organisational Roles).

In the case of ‘Reports to’ ensure this parameter is set (this will be done by default in the initial install) (Reference Q-Z, System Parameters).

Set up the Organisational Role against the employee against the appropriate level (Reference, Maintain Organisational Roles or Maintain Organisational Roles by Person).

text:
In the back office, you can create new organisation units in your business structure, then add them to the hierarchy as follows.

 

Create a new organisation unit

You have two alternate methods to create a new business unit.

To configure it via the reference menus, follow the below steps.

Click CorePersonnel, then click Reference.

Click the alphabetic reference group of the element name you want to add, then select it from the list.

E.g. To add a location, click Reference K - P, then select Location Codes.

Enter the details for the new business unit, then click the save   icon.

You can add the new element via the organisational hierarchy configuration.

Click CorePersonnel, then click Maintenance.

Click Post Management, then select Organisational Hierarchy.

Click Edit next to your structure, then click Yes.

Click Reference of the unit you're updating, then click the query  icon if present.

Click the insert  icon to create a new record.

Enter the details for the new business unit, then click the save  icon.

 

 

Add an organisation unit to the hierarchy

Click CorePersonnel, then click Maintenance.

Click Post Management, then select Organisational Hierarchy.

Click Data next to your structure, then click the expand   icons to the level required.

E.g., to add a new location to a department, you'll expand to the department it's to be added to. 

Click Add Department, or Add Location, or the unit that you're adding.

Check Include Linked Items to display all available elements.

Search for the item to be added, then select Add To Hierarchy.

Click Add, then click Save.

title: Assign organisational roles to employees
text:
Organisational roles need to be linked to the actual employee record of the user that will be fulfilling the role on PeopleXD. Hence, organisational roles cannot be assigned to external users.

 

For example, in order for an employee to receive notifications as the Head of Department for the Technology department, their PeopleXD employee record needs to be flagged with the corresponding org role for that organisational unit.

 

Assign a role via the Maintain Org Roles screen

Back Office: Click CorePersonnel, Reference, Maintain Organisational Roles

Portal: Go to People Management, Data Centre, View all, Maintain Organisation Roles

Use the Structure drop-down and select the required Org Structure.

This will be defaulted if there is only one structure set up on PeopleXD.

Select the Organisational Group that the role will be defined against. E.g. Department for the Head of Department; Pay Group for Payroll Salary Approver; Work Group for Reports to Manager etc.

The Group Item list will update to display all of the items that are currently defined on the system, for the selected group.

From the Group Item list, select the required level. Any employees that already have an org role for that group will be listed on screen.

To assign an Org Role for the selected level, click into the next available row on the centre of the screen.

Click the Date From field to make row editable.

Use the Role drop-down and select the Org Role.

Enter a Date From. Format DD-MON-YYYY. This is the date the employee will be recognised on PeopleXD as having that role.

Enter a Date To. Format DD-MON-YYYY. This is optional. Identifies the date that the employee ceased in that role.

Update Person field. Directly input the personnel number if known.

Click Save. That employee is now identified as having the org role for the selected element of the organisation. They will now be able to engage in any system processes that use that org role on PeopleXD.

 

 

Assign a role via the Maintain Org Roles by Person screen

Back Office: Click CorePersonnel, Reference, Maintain Organisational Roles by Person

Portal: Go to People Management, Data Centre, View all, Maintain Organisation Roles by Person

Search for the employee using a variety of options:

Use the search option at the top of the screen to do a keyword search on employee name, enter the employee name.

Click Find. The active employees matching the search criteria entered will display on the Personnel No list on the left.

Click the employee that the Org Roles should be assigned to. Any org roles already assigned to the selected employee will be listed in the centre of the screen.

To assign an org role to the selected employee, use the Structure drop-down and select the required Org Structure. This will be defaulted if there is only one  structure set up on PeopleXD.

Use the Role drop-down and select the Org Role.

Select the Organisational Group that the role will be defined against. E.g. Department for the Head of Department; Pay Group for Payroll Salary Approver; Work Group for Reports to Manager etc.

Enter a Date From. Format DD-MON-YYYY. This is the date the employee will be recognised on PeopleXD as having that role.

Enter a Date To. Format DD-MON-YYYY. This is optional. Identifies the date that the employee ceased in that role.

Select the Org Group Item. This list is directly related to the Org Group already selected e.g. a list of departments if the Org Group is set to Department.

Click Save. That employee is now identified as having the Org Role for the selected element of the organisation. They will now be able to engage in any system processes that use that Org Role on PeopleXD.

title: Identifying a case priority
text:
When raising a new case for the support team's attention, it’s important to assign the correct priority to ensure the issue is resolved within an appropriate timeframe. The available priority levels and the conditions under which they apply are outlined below.

 

Priority 1
Critical Impact

Service unavailable on any platform for any user, or business-critical software is inoperable.

Portal unavailable for any user.

Bank file submission failing.

Pay runs not completing.

 

 

Priority 2
Significant Impact

A partial loss of service access, or business-critical software has been significantly affected but it's still operable.

Module unavailable for all users.

Salary amendments.

Invalid IBAN code.

Payroll submission not appearing in ROS.

Bank file deadline.

 

 

Priority 3
Minimal impact

Minor degradation of the system performance, or a problem is reported in non-business-critical software, for example UAT, causing minimal impact.

Amendments or updates to individuals.

Cancelling a payment.

Deleting a timesheet.

Error on a cost allocation.

 

 

Priority 4
No Impact

Problem in non-business-critical processes, causing negligible or no business impact.

A user account is locked.

Access to a screen.

Cannot see staff qualifications on personnel.

title: Duplicate cases in the support portal
text:
The support team may close a case without providing a solution if it is identified as a duplicate. A case is considered duplicate when an existing ticket already addresses the same issue. This can happen for several reasons.

A customer accidentally creates two cases for the same issue. In this scenario, the support team closes the second case and adds the case owner as a collaborator on the original.

A customer raises a new case to escalate an existing one. In this instance, the escalation procedure should be followed.

A case has been marked as resolved, but the customer opens a new case to continue the investigation instead of reopening the original.

In all such cases, the support team closes the duplicate and continues to provide updates via the original ticket.

title: Portal: Grant HR access to a user
text:
Access to employee data in People Management is determined by a user's HR access. You can choose any of the below methods to configure the access their role requires.

 

HR User Access (Basic)

If you have access to the Data Centre widget, you can use the HR User Access (Basic) screen to assign and manage user access.

 

On the People Management dashboard click the Data Centre tab.

On the Data Centre widget click VIEW ALL.

Search for and click HR User Access (Basic).

Search for the user and expand their three-dot menu then click HR Admin.

Select a Structure Code, then select a Structure Level.

Turn on the Active toggle to grant access to a field, or click ENABLE ALL.

 

 

Employee record

If you have access to the employee's record you can use the Assign Access screen to grant them HR access and the relevant menu profile access.

 

On the People Management Dashboard click the Command Centre tab. 

Next to Employees click View. 

Search for the employee and click View.

Expand the Actions menu and click Assign Access.

Click the HR User Access tab. 

Select a Structure and Structure Level.

Select an item and click the Arrow to move to the Assigned column.

 

 

System Users

If you have access to the Security dashboard, you can assign Personnel Access to a user via the System Users screen.

 

On the Security dashboard click the Set Up tab.

Next to System Users click OPEN.

Select Portal then search for and select the employee from the Username list.

Select Personnel Access from the Security Type list.

Select a Structure Code and Access Level.

Turn on the Access Granted toggle for each item and click OK to confirm.

text:
Organisational roles (org roles) are used to identify employees that have certain managerial or approval responsibilities for specific tasks in the organisation. The following roles are available by default.

HR Salary Approver.

Payroll Salary Approver.

Under Organisation Group, select the grouping the role will be defined against, for example.

Department for the Head of Department.

🤓Tip: You can locate the employee by entering their name or personnel number.

title: Portal: Salary not visible for approval
text:
Before a user can approve salaries, they will need to have the required personnel or pay group accesses and the relevant organisation roles assigned to them. Follow the steps below.

📌Note: A user can be an approver in the portal or the back office. This is controlled by an entry in the user's contact details as described below.

Personnel access

From the dashboard menu, click Security, then click Set Up. 

Under System Set Up, scroll to System Users, then click OPEN. 

Click Portal or Back Office, then search for and select the employee in Username.

🤓 Tip: The employee can be located by entering their name or personnel number.

Under Security Type, select Personnel Access, then select a Structure Code. 

Select an Access Level, then click Show Access.

Enable Access Granted for individual items, or click Select All.

Click OK.

 

 

Pay group access

From the dashboard menu, click Security, then click Set Up. 

Under System Set Up, next to CorePay Pay Users, click OPEN. 

Close the Filter window, then click Portal Account or Back Office Account.

Click the Filter icon, select the employee in Username, then click Filter.

🤓 Tip: You can locate the employee by entering their name or personnel number.

Click Add, then enter Pay Group, Username, and Description.

Click Save, then click OK.

 

 

Assign organisational roles

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, enter and select Data Centre.

Click VIEW ALL, then click Maintain Organisation Roles by Person.

Search for and select the employee in Personnel No.

🤓 Tip: You can enter either their name or personnel number to locate them.

Select Structure, then click Add.

Select Role, for example, HR Salary Approver, then enter the new role details. 

Click Save, then click OK.

 

 

Salary user contact details

📌 Note: Complete this step if the user is to process approvals in the back office, it's not required for portal approvers.

Under Command Centre, next to Employees, click VIEW.

Search for the user's employee record, then click VIEW.

Click ACTIONS, then select Personnel Profile.

Under Contact Details, scroll to Salary User, then click the three-dot menu.

Click Edit, enter a Salary User, then click OK.

🤓 Tip: The value entered will be the user's back office username.

title: Password policy
text:
Subject to their authentication type, new and existing system users will be required to update their PeopleXD portal account password. The new password will need to comply with the password policy. To confirm the password policy, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click Password Policy, then locate the profile to be reviewed.

📌Note: COREPORTAL is the standard profile for portal users.

Click ACTIONS, then select Policy Details.

Under Password Rules, review the policy settings.

Minimum length - The minimum number of characters that must be used.

Maximum length - The maximum number of characters that can be used.

Allow username for password.

Enabled - User can use their username as a password.

Disabled - User cannot use their username as a password.

Prevent incrementing - Incrementing a number on your password,

e.g. password1 to password2.

Enabled - Passwords can be incremented.

Disabled - Passwords cannot be incremented.

Upper case characters - Minimum number of upper case letters to be used.

Lower case characters - Minimum number of lower case letters to be used.

Digits - Minimum number of digits to be used.

Special characters - Minimum number of special characters to be used.

The new password will need to conform to these rules.

📌Note: A user cannot re-use previous passwords in the portal.

People Management, Employee Search.

text:

Cause 1 - Contact details for employee not populated.

 

Cause 2 - Forgotten password labelled incorrectly as enter Email when should be enter Portal Username.

Resolution 2 - Enter your portal username rather than email when email address is requested.

🤓Tip: The password recovery messaging can be updated in the language pack. Search for the narrative currently displayed when requesting a reset.

 

Resolution 3

From the dashboard menu, search and select Site Manager.

Click Open next to Admin Settings. 

Search for parameter code forgotten_email.

Click Edit, enter a sending email address (peoplexd@accessacloud.com is recommended) and click Ok.

 

Resolution 4 

Enter employee number into username box.

Click Forgot password or security question below.

Enter employee number (username) when prompted and date of birth.

Password reset email will be sent.

title: Managers see employees on the My Team widget that they do not have direct access to
text:
As a manager, it is possible to view all employees below them by using the All Levels option on the My Team widget as shown.

A manager has three direct reports - Employees A, B and C.

A, B and C also have three direct reports - employees D, E and F.

On the My Team tab of the Manager Dashboard, the manager will see Employee A, B and C.

On the All Levels tab of the Manager Dashboard, the manager will see Employee A, B, C, D, E and F.

On the All Levels tab managers will be able to drill into the employee and view specific details. They will not be able to see appointment specific details e.g. contract details, salary/allowance, manager requests, appointment specific documents, appointment UDF's.

title: Back Office: Configure a CorePersonnel user
text:
To configure a CorePersonnel Back Office user there are up to three stages.

Configure Personnel Access in System Users (access to employees).

If applicable, configure Post Management User Security access. This is only applicable to sites using Post Management.

If applicable, configure additional access. Certain areas of functionality in CorePersonnel may require additional access per user (e.g. diversity data, recruitment, etc.).

🤓Tip: You can provide a user with similar access in the portal.

 

Personnel access configuration

In CorePersonnel, click Reference, Reference Q - Z, and select System Users. 

Select Back Office Accounts and find the user from the List of Values (LOV).

Select Security Type as PERS - Personnel Access.

Select the required Structure Code.

Select the level of the Organisation Structure which determines the employee information the user will have access to. For example: 

Selecting Company grants user access to all employees in that Company.

Selecting Department grants access to certain Departments in the Company.

Click Show Access.

Under Access Granted tick the box for the Access Codes that the user will have access to.

Click Save.

 

 

Post management user security configuration

In CorePersonnel, go to Maintenance.

Select Post Management, then select Post Management User Security.

Scroll to the relevant user or search for them via the query mode.

Grant the user access to the following options as required:

Authorise Appointment.

Appoint a Person.

End Appointment.

Amend Appointment.

Click on the Save icon.

 

 

Configure additional access

In CorePersonnel, click Reference, Reference Q - Z, and select System Users. This can also be accessed in the portal in Security, Set Up tab, System Users.

Select Back Office Accounts and find the user from the List of Values (LOV).

Use the Security Type field, to select the functional area.

The following options are available for selection:

Diversity Access: Grants access to the Diversity screen in Person Profile.

Document Access: Used for Document Management access.

Letter Template Access: Used to generate letters in separate structures.

Personnel Access: Required for viewing employee details.

Process Access: Required for Workflow.

Recruitment Access: Used in conjunction with the CoreRecruitment module.

Salary Access: Required for salary access.

Sensitive Department Access: Users should be granted this access separately from Department access.

Training Access: Used for the CoreTraining module.

User Defined Access: Used to grant access to User Defined Fields where the Security Required option has been ticked on.

Click Show Access.

Tick on the relevant access. The screen options may change depending on the item selected.

Click Save.

title: Adjust the idle time for a user's session
text:
Resolution 1

From the dashboard menu, search and select Security. 

Select the Password Policy tab.

All profiles are displayed on the Password Policy widget.

Search for the relevant account profile.

Click the Actions and select the Policy Details option.

Update Idle time(minutes).

Click Save.

 

 

Resolution 2

To set the Portal default Idle time.

From the dashboard menu, search and select Administrator Dashboard.

Click Site Manager/Admin Tools and open Admin Settings.

Search for the parameter ess_timeout.

Set this parameter to the timeout time in seconds by clicking Edit.

📌Note: In the same way as above, you can also edit the value for thesession_expired_timeparameter which defines Session Expire Time in Hours.

title: Amend a post in Post Profile Maintenance
text:
Edit an Existing Post Profile

To edit a post profile, follow the steps below:

Go to the People Management dashboard.

Click the Data Centre tab.

Click Open on People Management.

Search for Post Profile Maintenance and click on the corresponding option.

Use the selection criteria available to narrow the search for the required Post Profile e.g. Post Title, Post Number etc.

Click View on the relevant Post Profile row.

Edit any fields as required. See restrictions below.

Click Save to save the changes made to the Post Profile record.

Restrictions/Considerations when Editing a Post Profile record

The following fields cannot be directly edited by the user on this screen:

Post Number: This can never be amended by the user as it is a system derived unique ID for the record

Locked hierarchy’ fields will not be editable. Other non-locked hierarchy fields will be editable including: Work Group; Cost Centre; Location; User Field 1 – User Field 5

Impact on Existing Post Appointment / Contracts: If a Post Profile is edited, this will not have an impact on any existing active or historic Post Appointments / Contracts created from that Post Profile. For example, if the Cost Centre was edited, this would not be updated on any existing active or historic Post Appointments / Contracts created from that Post Profile. However, any future contracts to be created from that Post Profile will now inherit the latest update for that field.

title: Employee has completed onboarding checklist but onboarding showing as not completed
text:
If the status next to an onboarding checklist item e.g Bank Details, Next of Kin, Files to be uploaded shows as 'Not Started', it is likely that the employee has updated these details in the 
​My Profile screen and not in the Onboarding Checklist.
Some items in the checklist can be updated in My Profile as well.
​
If updated there, the Onboarding Status of the checklist item will show as Not Started and therefore the overall Onboarding Status will be incomplete and the complete date will be blank.
​
If files are uploaded via My Profile instead of via Onboarding checklist, check the document type of the file loaded in My Profile and compare with document type for the Onboarding checklist.  If different, will also indicate that the files were loaded via My Profile.

title: Organisational role delegation overview
text:
Org role delegation is available to managers, to allow them to delegate their org role responsibilities to another manager, to cover periods where they are unavailable e.g. during leave. 
​
This allows the manager to redirect approval items to their colleagues, without the need for HR to intervene. The manager can control the following.

Which of their org roles will be delegated.

Who they will be delegated to.

How long they will be delegated for.

Why they are to be delegated.

HR can control what org roles can be delegated e.g. it may be suitable to delegate annual leave approvals but not salary approvals.
​
Delegation is not a suitable solution where the manager is leaving their role e.g. 

They are moving role within the company and will no longer be responsible for these approvals.

They are leaving the company.

title: Portal: How to configure a back office account
text:
After you created a back office account on portal, you need to configure it. Follow the steps below. 

Go to Security, click User Management, then on the System Users widget, search for the relevant user.

Click the three-dots and select Manage Account.

🤓Tip: On the System Users widget, select All Back Office Accounts.

Go to the General tab, then select a value for Database Profile:

If the user is a Security user, select Manager.

For all other users, select End User.

Go to the Menu Profiles tab, then enable the toggle for the relevant menu profiles.

🤓Tip: Search for a menu option and check if the option is enabled in any of the menu profiles assigned to the user in the previous tab.

Go to the Object Profiles tab, then select COREHR OBJECT PROFILE profile and all other applicable object profiles.

🤓Tip: If relevant, to link the account to the user's employee number, click LINK TO HR. Search for the employee and click OK.

In the Security module, go to the Set Up tab.

On the System Set Up widget, next to Corehr Security, click OPEN.

Type the password university and click Submit.

On the next screen, select Back Office Account and click the filter icon.

Find the username from the dropdown and click Filter.

📌Note: If you don't link the account to an employee number, you need to configure the user account in the back office. To do so, go to CoreHR then click Security. The password is the same.

Select a company and enable the toggle for each module.

CorePersonnel Access.

CorePay Access.

CoreTime Access.

Click Save.

title: Enable/Disable two factor authentication
text:
As an Administrator:

To enable/disble two factor authentication at Company Level:

In Portal, go to the Administrator Dashboard

Select Site Manager

Within the Site Manager widget, 'Open' Admin Settings

In the search bar, type cp_reg_authtwofactor

Update the parameter labelled cp_reg_authtwofactor from N to Y to enable two factor authentication.
Update the parameter labelled cp_reg_authtwofactor from Y to N to disable two factor authentication.


By default, all users can access and update two factor authentication at employee level.
To ensure this option is still switched on, check by following the below steps:

In Portal, go to the Administrator Dashboard

Select Site Manager

Within the Site Manager widget, 'Open' Admin Settings

In the search bar, type cp_reg_authtwofactorupd

Ensure the parameter labelled cp_reg_authtwofactorupd is set to Y if you wish for it to be enabled. Set it to N if you wish to switch this option off for users


As an Individual User:

The option to switch off the two factor authentication on your own account/at user level is only available on our Classic UI. To access and update this setting, follow the below steps:

In Portal, click on your account icon at the top right hand corner of the screen

From the dropdown list, select Account Settings

Toggle the Modern UI button 'off' to switch Portal to our Classic User Interface

Click 'OK' on the pop-up message

Once the Classic UI version of Portal has appeared, select your name and icon from the top right hand corner of the screen again

Select Account Security

Within the Authentication / Recovery section, toggle the Enable / disable two factor button 'off' to disable two factor authentication at user level


Note: A User will not be able to switch 'on' the two factor authentication option on an individual level when cp_reg_authtwofactor is set to N.

title: Bulk adding/removing menu profiles to employees
text:
You can add or remove menu profiles to employees in bulk via the Bulk Assign Access feature.
​
Firstly, the system needs to know what employee records to update. This is identified using an Insight report. The report runs from the Bulk Assign Access screen and returns the required employees on screen, ready to be updated. 
​
Follow these steps to update access for a group of employees in bulk:

Create an Insight report to retrieve the list of employees to be updated

the Person Reference column from the Hr Person Master (Personnel) view needs to be included in the report

any other columns that you add to the report are not displayed in the Bulk Assign Access screen but may be useful to you to add to the report to ensure that the correct set of data is being retrieved e.g. name, department, etc.

Go to Data Centre, click View All, and open the Bulk Assign Access option

Once the Select Report pop-up appears, select your report from the Insight Reports drop-down list and click Apply

The screen updates to display the employees in the report

Note: The screen does not display the full report data. The columns displayed on the screen are fixed. The Insight report is only used to confirm what employee records display.

Toggle on/off the Selected switch for the employees that you want to include in the bulk update

Click the Assign Access button - the Assign Access screen opens

Select the Date Effective that access is to be granted from

Select the Menu Profiles tab from the list available on the left-hand side of the screen - once selected, the screen updates to display the list of menu profiles

Click ADD or REMOVE next to the menu profiles that you want to assign or unassign to employees selected on the previous screen

title: Bulk update employee records
text:
You can use bulk update templates to update employee records at scale. There are default templates, or you can create custom templates to update various contract elements across multiple employee records.

📌Note: Coordinate with your Payroll team before processing bulk updates, as changes automatically flow through to PeopleXD Payroll.

 

To update employee records in bulk, watch the video or follow the steps below.

Download and populate a template

You can use the two default templates to end allowances and update salaries across multiple employee records.

 

You can also create custom templates to update contract elements in bulk. This can include updating areas such as creating broadcast contract announcements within an employee's record.

📌Note: You can only update commenced or confirmed future contracts. Updates can't be made to fields specified on the Organisation Structure.

 

Create a custom contract template

To create a custom contract template, follow the steps below in portal. 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Bulk Update Templates.

Click Actions then select Create Contract Template.

Search for the required fields and select the checkboxes.

Click the right arrow icon to move the fields to the Selected column.

Click Save, enter a name then click OK.

 

Download and populate a template

To download and populate a template, follow the steps below. 

📌Note: The file type needs to be CSV with pipe-delimited records, and you can't update fields to a null value.

 From the dashboard menu, search for and select Bulk Update Templates.

Search for the relevant template then click the three-dot menu.

For guidance on populating the template, click Download Helper.

Click Download Template, then open the file and populate the fields.

 

 

Upload and process records

After downloading and populating your template, you need to upload it. You can then use the Processing screen to fix any errors, configure settings, and apply updates to your employees' records.

 

Upload a template

To upload a template, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Employee Bulk Updates.

Click LOAD FILE then select the file from your device.

Click OK, then review the information on the processing editor screen.

 

Change file visibility

Templates you upload are marked as private by default, so only you can access them. You can make a file public to allow other users with widget access to view it.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Employee Bulk Updates.

Search for the relevant file then click the three-dot menu. 

Click Set Public, then click Yes.

 

Correct errors

Records with errors display the status failed on the processing editor screen. You can make updates to the records to correct highlighted issues.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Employee Bulk Updates.

Next to the relevant file, click the three-dot menu then click Edit.

Click the relevant record, then click Display Errors.

Review the error description then update the relevant field. 

If prompted, click Yes to update other identical errors.

🤓Tip: Where a correction has been made and cascaded to all records, you can reset all record statuses with errors using the Actions menu. 

 

Process records

Depending on the file type, you can apply additional settings before processing the updates.

Bypass salary approvals: When you upload a salary amendment file, turn on the toggle to bypass the salary approval process.

Apply these changes to future dated amendments: When you upload an end allowance file, turn on the toggle to cascade field updates to existing future-dated amendments.

 

To apply additional settings and process records, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Employee Bulk Updates.

Next to the relevant file, click the three-dot menu then click Edit. 

Click Actions then click Settings.

Turn on the toggles as required, then click OK.

Select a record then click Process Record or click Process All Records.

 

 

User access 

To access the bulk update functionality, you need to add the widgets to a PeopleXD dashboard and grant users the correct menu option access.

 

Add widgets to a dashboard

To add widgets to your dashboard, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Site Manager.

Next to Dashboard Configuration, click Open.

From the drop-down menu, select the relevant dashboard.

From the Dashboard Tabs section, select the relevant tab.

From the Tab Widgets section, search for and turn on Bulk Update Templates and Employee Bulk Updates.

 

Menu options

text:

The payroll user will need to go back to the generate salaries and allowances screen, clear the Final Run indicator check box and re-run generate salaries.

If timesheets were confirmed, then reversing the timesheets is required. This will bring payroll back to before the Pay290 is generated. CorePay, Input, Reverse Timesheet Confirm.

title: Error - '403: Forbidden'
text:
Where system updates produce a '403: Forbidden' error - for example, during an employee rehire - there are two common causes.

 

Multiple active sessions

403 forbidden errors often occur when more than one active session is open.

Ask the user to log out and log back in.

Ensure no multiple portal tabs are open.

 

 

ModSecurity checks

Some text input may trigger ModSecurity, the security layer that blocks suspicious HTTP traffic. During a rehire, this can be caused by the email address and/or home address of the employee. Override the error as follows.

Remove the email and/or home address, then continue with the process.

You can re-enter these details later without triggering the error.

title: Message 'Error: oops, something has gone wrong. no employee mapping found..'
text:
This error in PeopleXD or eRecruitment may result from various scenarios.

Cause 1 - No LDAP row for the employee in the Contact screen.

Cause 2 - No email address for the employee in the Contact screen.

Cause 3 - Portal username is not linked to the back-office account.

Cause 4 - Incorrect recruitment URL for AD clients.

 

Resolution 1
Portal guidance

In People Management, Command Centre, click Employees.

Search the employee in question and click View.

Click on the Actions button in the right top corner and click on the Personnel Profile.

Under Contacts, enter the network username for LDAP/Oracle User Name and click Save.

Back Office guidance

In CorePersonnel, click on Maintenance, Personal profile.

Search the employee in question.

Under select detail click on Contacts.

Add the new row with contact type as LDAP and enter their network username and click Save.

 

 

Resolution 2
Portal guidance

In People Management, Command Centre, click Employees.

Search the employee in question and click View.

Click on the Actions button in the right top corner and click on the Personnel profile.

Under Contacts, enter the Email address and click Save.

Back Office guidance

In CorePersonnel, click on Maintenance, Personal Profile.

Search the employee in question.

Under select detail click on Contacts.

Add the new row with Contact Type as EMAIL and enter their email address and click Save.

 

 

Resolution 3
Portal guidance

In Security click on User Management.

Select All Back Office Accounts from the dropdown and search employee in question.

Click on the three-dot menu and click Manage account.

Click on 'Link to HR Person' in the top right corner and select the personnel no of the employee from dropdown.

Click OK.

 

 

Resolution 4:

Check what url are you using, if you are using:
​https://my.corehr.com/pls/coreportal_CLIENTCODE/erq_search_package.search_form?p_company=1&p_internal_external=E
​
If you are using the above url as AD user, you might get the error. Instead use the following url:
​https://my.corehr.com/pls/CLIENTCODErecruit/erq_search_package.search_form?p_company=1&p_internal_external=E

title: Error - 'Sorry But Page Not Found' when logging into portal
text:
If you are encountering Error - 'Sorry But Page Not Found' when logging into Portal, please ensure that you carry out the below checks. 

Contact your local IT team to check for any network problems internally.

Please check if this issue is impacting your Live environment and/or your UAT environment.

Please identify if this issue is impacting one user or if this is a widespread issue. (For example, if this is just impacting one user, please ask the user to log off and back on, clearing cache and browser history before attempting to log back in).

Potential causes

See below potential other causes and resolutions for this error message.

 

Cause 1

CorePortal account has been locked.

 

Cause 2

LDAP Core User configuration was changed.

 

Cause 3

CP_POST_LOGIN_PAGE has been updated to an incorrect value.

 

Cause 4

Employee has not accepted completed self registration process.

 

Cause 5

Onboarding processes are not used but employees are being directed to an Onboarding Page.

 

 

Possible resolutions
Resolution 1

A Super-User who can unlock this through the Core Back-Office (BO):

Select CoreSecurity, Tools, User Management.

Enter CorePortal in user field.

Click Unlock.

Resolution 2

Ensure that the LDAP Core User is Enabled / Disabled correctly.

 

Resolution 3

Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article.

 

Resolution 4

In the case where this impacts a single employee, please ensure that the employee has accepted the registration email. the Self Registration email can be resent if necessary. 

 

Resolution 5

Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article.

title: Error - 'ORA-12154: TNS could not resolve the connect identifier specified'
text:
An attempt to login to the PeopleXD back office fails with an 'ORA-12154: TNS could not resolve the connect identifier specified' message. Possible causes for this error are outlined below.

An incorrect URL has been specified.

The database identifier supplied is incorrect.

The user's updated their PC or browser, and the URL isn't on the trusted site list.

The URL hasn't been whitelisted by the customer's IT team.

The user's password contains an @ or a / symbol.

📌Note: The back office URL is formatted as follows.

https://uatwshradm.corehr.com/forms/frmservlet?config=ccu (your UAT site).

https://wshradm.corehr.com/forms/frmservlet?config=ccp (your production site).

 

Where cc denotes your unique client code, this can be more than 2 characters.

title: Insight report output is blank
text:
If your Insight report returns blank when you attempt to include PeopleXD Workforce Management (WFM) data, it’s likely due to one of the following reasons:

The employee doesn't have the correct work group access.

To resolve a blank Insight report, watch the videos or follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration, then click WFM System User Configuration.

Search for the relevant employee, then click the three-dot menu.

Select View/Edit, then click Access Details.

Add the respective work groups and departments.

From the dashboard menu, search for and click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration, then click WFM System User Configuration.

Click Create New User, then select Portal Access from the Access Type list.

Select the employee from the Person list.

📌Note: The employee needs to exist in PeopleXD to show in the Person list.

Select a Company, then click OK.

Click the Access Details tab, then click Add.

Select a Work Group from the list, then select the relevant Departments, 

Click the right arrow to move the criteria to the Assigned Departments column.

Repeat steps 7 to 8 as required.

 

 

Grant security access

If you don't have access to the WFM System User Configuration screen, to get access, watch the video or follow the steps below.

📌Note: You need access to the PeopleXD Security to do this.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click User Management, then search for the relevant employee.

Click the employee's three-dot menu, then select Manage Account. 

Click Menu Profiles, then search for WFM_SYSTEM_USERS_CONFIG.

Turn on the Enable toggle.

title: Report on clockings
text:
You can report on employee clockings to review attendance, hours worked, and time in/out records from either the Portal or Back Office.

This article explains the different ways you can run clocking reports in Workforce Management. Choose the method that suits your reporting needs.

 

Run the Daily Clocking Hours report from the Portal

Use this report to view daily clocking hours by department, work group, or individual employee.

To configure and run the Daily Clocking Hours report:

From either the WFM Admin Dashboard or the Workforce Management Dashboard, select Reports.

In the Report Type drop-down menu, select Daily Clocking Hours.

Use the Period and Group By fields to choose the time period and grouping method for the report.

(Optional) Use the additional fields to refine your report further.

Click Run Report.

Once the report has run, you can:

Print the report.

Export to Excel.

📌Note: If you select Export to Excel, you may see a message stating that the file format and extension do not match. Click Yes to open the spreadsheet.

Run clocking reports from Back Office

There are two reporting options in Back Office, depending on how you want to filter your data.

Option 1: Run the Daily Clockings / Hours report

Use this option to report on clockings for a specific calendar period.

In Back Office, go to CoreTime > Reports > Daily Clockings / Hours.

Select your criteria.

If you only want to report on clockings (without hours), tick the Clockings Only box.

Click Run Report.

📌Note: This report is for a single calendar period only. You cannot select a date range or run it across multiple periods.

Option 2: Run the Daily Attendance report

Use this option to report on clockings across a date range.

In Back Office, go to CoreTime > Reports > Daily Attendance.

Select your criteria.

Choose the date range you want to report on.

Click Run Report.

📌Note: The Daily Attendance report shows only the First In and Last Out clockings for each day.

title: Enhanced pay code instance report
text:
The enhanced pay code instance report allows you to analyse absence patterns across multiple pay codes treated as a single absence category. This helps you identify trends and make data-driven decisions regarding absence management policies.

 

Previously, you could report on only one pay code at a time. Now, you can group related pay codes and apply advanced filtering to analyse employees based on specific day or instance thresholds. This streamlines your reporting process and reduces the time spent on manual analysis.

From the Report Type drop-down menu, select Pay Code Instance.

Enter a start date and an end date for the reporting period.

Click Pay Codes, then select the relevant pay codes to analyse.

In the Selection Criteria fields, enter the threshold values for the report.

Further refine your report using the Report Details options.

Click Run Report.

The report displays employees who meet the specified criteria across all selected pay codes.

📌Note: Selected pay codes are treated as a single absence type for analysis purposes.

 

 

View detailed absence patterns

After generating your report, access the integrated Insight view - Pay Code Instances (Time) for detailed analysis.

Review the breakdown of absences across the selected pay codes.

Use filters to refine your view by specific pay codes or date ranges.

🤓Tip: Export your report results to analyse absence trends over time or share findings with your management team.

title: Configure a return to work interview template
text:
You can use Return to Work Interview (RTWI) templates to standardise questionnaires and ensure consistent return to work conversations across your organisation, while giving you the flexibility to tailor templates to different absence types and workflows.

 

To set up and manage an RTWI template.

 

Create an RTWI Template

From the dashboard menu, select WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration then search for and select Return to Work Interview.

Click Add then enter a code and template name.

Select the pay codes you want to assign the template to.

Turn on the relevant toggles then click OK.  

 

Add sections

To build structure into your questionnaire, you can create headings using sections. To do this, follow the steps below.

For the relevant template, click the three-dot menu.

Select Add/Edit Section then click Add.

Enter a section heading then select the relevant section type.

Enter a description then click Save.

Repeat this process to create the required sections.

Once you've created the structure of your questionnaire, you can add your questions to each section and format them to your organisational requirements. For example, you can set whether questions are mandatory. To do this follow the steps below.

For the relevant section, click the three-dot menu.

Select Add/Edit Question then click Add.

Enter the question and a description.

Select the question type then click Save.

Fill in the configuration requirements then click OK.

Repeat these steps for each question you need to create.

Rtwi Access (Time): Displays a log of who has viewed return to work interview forms.

title: A leave type doesn't appear in the Absence drop-down
text:
If an absence type is missing from the Leave Type drop-down when recording an absence, it’s likely that the pay code isn’t assigned to the employee’s pay code group. To resolve this, follow the steps in each section below in order.

 

Mark the pay code as an absence

From the dashboard menu, Click WFM Admin Dashboard

Select WFM Configuration, then Click Pay Codes.

Next to the relevant pay code, click the three-dot menu.

Select View/Edit Pay Code then select the Absence indicator check box.

Click Save.

 

 

Add the pay code to a pay code group

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard. 

Click WFM Configuration then click Pay Code Groups.

Select the relevant pay code group.

Add the required pay code to the group’s list.

Click Save.

 

 

Verify Pay Code Group Access for the Employee

Verify the following three areas to ensure the employee is assigned the correct pay code group.

 

Employee Level

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard, then WFM Person Maintenance.

Next to the employee, click the three-dot menu, then View/Edit.

Go to the Personal Groups section and check the assigned Pay Code Group.

If the correct group is missing, add the required Personalised Pay Code Group.

System User Level

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard, then WFM Configuration

Click on WFM System Users Configuration.

Next to the employee, click the three-dot menu, then View/Edit.

Under Access Privileges, check Pay Code Access Groups.

If the correct group is missing, add the required Personalised Pay Code Group.

Work Group Level

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard, then WFM Configuration

Click Work Group.

Next to the employee’s Work Group, click the three-dot menu, then View/Edit Work Group.

Go to Group Codes and check for the correct Personalised Pay Code Group.

If it’s missing, add the appropriate group.

 

 

Check if the Pay Code is Marked as HR Only

In the WFM Admin Dashboard, go to WFM Configuration > Pay Codes.

Locate the relevant Pay Code, click the three-dot menu, then View/Edit Pay Code.

If HR Only is enabled, only system users with the HR User privilege can access this Pay Code.

 

 

Grant HR User Access (If Required)

If the Pay Code is marked HR Only, ensure the employee has the HR User parameter enabled.

 

On the Portal:

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard, then WFM Configuration > WFM System Users Configuration.

Next to the employee, click the three-dot menu, then View/Edit.

If the user isn’t created yet:

Click Create New User.

Set Access Type to Portal Access.

Enter the employee number and select the company number.

Assign the required Access Privileges, Work Groups, and Departments.

Turn on the HR User toggle.

On Back Office:

Go to CoreTime, then System Params, then System Users.

Search for the employee.

If the user isn’t registered:

Set Access Type to Manager Self Service.

Enter the employee number.

Tick the Active checkbox.

Assign the required Access Privileges, Work Groups, and Departments.

Enable the HR User parameter.

 

 

Grant Access to WFM System User Configuration (If Needed)

If the user doesn’t see WFM System Users Configuration:

In the search bar, search for Security, then click the menu.

Select User Management.

Next to the relevant user, click the three-dot menu, then select Manage Account.

Under Menu Profiles, search for WFM_SYSTEM_USERS_CONFIG.

Enable the Active toggle.

Log out and back in to apply the change.

title: Leavers in CorePersonnel still active in CoreTime
text:
There are a few reasons this could be happening. To resolve this, check each of the following in order.

Employee hasn't been ended in Personnel

The calendar used by the employee has yet to be advanced passed their end date

The LE (Leaver) code has been deleted from 'Employee Status' in CorePersonnel

Known issue when Current Period / Week is being automatically advanced via Overnight Job

The calendar in Core Time hasn't been advanced since the employee was made a leaver.

📌 Note: If a User Defined Calendar is assigned to the employee's Work Group then this will need to be advanced passed the employee's end date. Check the Pay Frequency parameter in System Params, Work Groups. If the value here isn't Weekly, Fortnightly or Monthly, a UDC is in use.

To resolve this, follow the points below.

 

Resolution 1

End the employee in Personnel. Status will be updated when the period is advanced next.

📌 Note: An advanced option is available to set all employees with historical Date Left entered to Leaver and is set at company level. If this is required, please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article and ask for this option to be enabled.

Resolution 2

Employee will be updated to a leaver when the period is advanced passed their end date. See article description for the three scenarios where a period is advanced.

 

Resolution 3

Click CorePersonnel, Reference, Reference D-J, Employee Status. 

Set up an Employee Status for Leavers. The employee status is LE

Click Save.

📌 Note: Employee will not automatically become a Leaver/Dormant in the system and will need to be updated.

Resolution 4

Resolved in versions 20.0.23+, 21.0.20+, 22.0.5+

 

Resolution 5

Need to wait for calendar to be advanced again in Core Time for them to be made a leaver or else raise a support case if you do not wish to wait.

 

Employee has a leave date of 10-MAR-22.


The calendar linked to the employee has the current open period as 01-MAR to 31-MAR.


The employee won't become a leaver until the calendar is automatically advanced by closing period 01 to 31-MAR and making 01-APR to 30-APR the current open period
​
Period End can be run manually via (should not be done if this calendar is used to generate timesheets).

Portal, WFM Admin Dashboard, Advance Period

Click 'Monthly User Defined Calendar'

Click 'Advanced Period'

Click 'Yes' to exceptions

This will update any employees to leavers  linked to this calendar who had a leave date on or before this period


​

title: Remove rounding from taken leave
text:
How Rounding Works in Leave Balances

By default, rounding is applied to both taken and booked leave. The system rounds up to the nearest half hour, which can sometimes result in employees losing a small portion of their leave.

 

Example:

If an employee on an 8.5-hour day books half a day’s leave, the system rounds this up by 15 minutes. As a result, the employee would lose an extra 15 minutes of their leave balance.

How to Update Rounding Settings

You can choose where rounding is applied in the Balance Configuration screen. To adjust this:

Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard and select WFM Configuration.

Click on the Balance Configuration tile.

Search for and select the relevant Balance.

Expand the 3-dot menu and click View/Edit Balance.

From the Summary tab, scroll to the Rounding Rules section.

In the Apply Rounding To field, use the dropdown to select where you’d like rounding to be applied.

Click Save.

By default rounding is performed on taken and booked leave. The system rounds balances up to the nearest half hour which means it rounds up the leave taken amounts, which is not in the employees favour. For example, If an employee on an 8.5 hour day booked a half day leave, this would round up by 15 minutes so the employee is losing 15 minutes of their leave.
​
Options are available on the Balance configuration screen for you to select where you want rounding for the balance to be performed.  To update this:
​ 

Navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard and select WFM Configuration.

Select the Balance Configuration tile.

Search for and select the relevant Balance.

Expand it's 3-dot menu and select View/Edit Balance.

From the Summary tab scroll to the Rounding Rules section, locate the Apply Rounding To field.

Use the dropdown options to select where rounding should be performed.

Click Save.

 


The options available from the Apply Rounding To dropdown are:

All - This will apply to Taken & Entitlement (default option)

Entitlement - This will apply rounding to Reserved, Floating, Accrued and Carried balances.

Taken - This will apply rounding to taken and book leave.

title: Remove the display of cancelled Annual leave from Manager's team calendars
text:
Why Cancelled Leave Still Shows in the Team Calendar

It is not possible to remove notifications of cancelled annual leave from a manager’s team calendar.

 

Why?

The section being referred to in Team Scheduler is called Leave Request. This view will display all leave requests, regardless of their status. This includes:

Submitted

Approved

Rejected

In short, the Leave Request filter cannot be customised to exclude specific statuses—it will always display the full history of leave actions.

 

 

Can This Feature Be Turned Off?

If you prefer not to display any absences at all on the team scheduler, you can turn off the entire feature.

To do this, update the following parameter:

SCH_SHOW_ABSENCES → Set this to ‘N’

This will remove all absences from appearing in the Team Scheduler, including cancelled, approved, and pending requests.

title: Why the Department + Work Group Filter and Team Calendar Button May Not Appear on the WFM Admin Bulk Leave Approval Screen
text:
The Admin Security Type setting controls how a user’s access is managed, which impacts the visibility of filters and buttons such as Department, Work Group, and Team Calendar.

 

Check Your Admin Security Type Setting

Go to WFM Admin > Config > General Settings.

Find the setting called Admin Security Type.

 

Understand the Three Admin Security Types
Structure Code Access:

Access is based on your Personnel system user access (Company/Division level).

Work Group and Department filters will NOT show.

This means you cannot filter leave approvals by Work Group or Department.

Team Calendar button will also not appear.

System User Access:

Access is based on the Work Groups and Departments assigned to your WFM System User account.

Work Group and Department filters WILL appear.

You will only see employees within those Work Groups and Departments.

Team Calendar button will appear.

This controls access on screens like Bulk Leave Approval, Approve Hours, Employee Calendar, and Balance Re-Calculation.

Team Area Access:

Used only for clients with rostered Team Areas.

Filters will show based on Team Areas assigned to your account.

Team Calendar button will appear.

 

 

Determine Which Admin Security Type You Are Using

If the Work Group and Department filters are missing, you are likely using Structure Code Access.

To get the filters back, the Admin Security Type must be changed to System User Access.

 

 

How to Change Admin Security Type

Only users with the correct system permissions can change this setting.

To change it:

Go to WFM Admin > Config > General Settings.

Change Admin Security Type from Structure Code Access to System User Access.

Save your changes.

 

 

Confirm Your Work Group and Department Access

Confirm Your Work Group and Department Access

Go to WFM Admin > Config > WFM System Users.

Select your username and verify which Work Groups and Departments you have access to.

You will only see employees and filters relevant to those assigned groups and departments.

 

 

Verify Filters and Buttons Appear

Log out and log back in if needed.

Go to the Bulk Leave Approval screen.

The Work Group + Department filters and the Team Calendar button should now be visible.

📌Note: Changing this setting affects what employees you see on several screens, including Approve Hours and Balance Re-Calculation.

The Sign Off Hours screen always shows all employees regardless of this setting.

If your organization uses rostered Team Areas, the Team Area Access option applies instead.

title: What is the difference between Days and Occurrences for Absence Triggers
text:
When configuring Absence Triggers, it's important to understand how Days and Occurrences are calculated in the Sum Rule.

 

How the system counts absences:

Absence Type

	

Days

	

Occurrences




Full day absence

	

1

	

1




Half day absence

	

0.5

	

1

Example:

If an employee has:

3 full day absences

2 half day absences

The system will count:

Days: 3 + (2 × 0.5) = 4 days

Occurrences: 3 + 2 = 5 occurrences

Which option should you use?

If you want to count a half day absence as…

	

Use




0.5

	

Days




1

	

Occurrences

Summary:

Days = Tracks total time off.

Occurrences = Counts the number of absence events, regardless of duration.

Choose the option that matches your reporting or trigger requirements.
