title: Use roster attributes in Workforce Management
text:
Roster attributes let you label an employee's scheduled pattern with the job or task they are assigned to complete, such as Cashier, Floor, Security or Training. You can assign a default attribute to each employee, override it at day level, view and filter by attributes on the Roster Details screen, and report on attribute data via CoreInsight. This article covers everything you need to manage roster attributes, from initial configuration through to day-to-day use.

 

You'll need Team Manager access to assign and maintain roster attributes. An administrator must enable the Roster Attribute Active parameter before the feature is available.

 

What is a roster attribute?

A roster attribute is a label applied to an employee's rostered pattern to identify the job or task they are scheduled to complete for that pattern. Attributes are user-defined — examples include Cashier, Floor, Security and Training.

 

Roster attributes give you the ability to:

 

Assign attributes to employees at employee level, pattern level, or across multiple employees in a team area.

View each employee's assigned attribute on the Roster Details screen.

Identify what job or task an employee is scheduled to complete by their attribute.

Filter the Roster Details screen by one or more attributes.

Report on attribute data in CoreInsight.

There are some current restrictions you should be aware of:

 

You cannot set up a demand rule based on an attribute (Phase 1 only).

Each employee can only have one attribute assigned per pattern — patterns cannot be split across multiple attributes.

Attributes are not displayed or maintained in HR Admin.

AutoRoster and Uncovered Shifts cannot be used against an attribute (Phase 1 only).

📌Note: This feature is delivered in two phases. Phase 1 covers the fundamental ability to assign jobs and tasks to employees. Phase 2 will extend attribute support to AutoRoster, Rules, Statistics and Uncovered Shifts screens.

Enable roster attributes

One parameter controls access to all roster attribute functionality across every screen. You must enable it before attributes can be assigned or viewed.

 

Quick jump to Roster Links.

Click Open General Settings.

Turn on the Roster Attribute Active indicator.

If you want attributes to display on rest days, turn on the Display Attribute on Rest Days indicator.

Click Save.

Create attributes and attribute groups

You create and manage attributes via the Roster Attribute Setup wizard, which walks you through three steps. You do not need to complete every step each time — you can follow each step individually, and you can reuse existing attributes and groups.

 

Create an attribute

Quick jump to Roster Links.

Click Open Roster Attribute Setup.

Select the Add button to create a new row.

Enter the attribute code.

Enter the attribute description.

Click Save.

Select Next to move to Step 2 — Create Group.

Create an attribute group

Select the Add button to create a new row.

Enter a description for the new group.

Click Save.

Select Next to move to Step 3 — Assign Attribute.

Assign attributes to an attribute group

Select the required attribute group from the drop-down list.

Select the Add button to create a new row.

Select the required attribute from the drop-down list.

Click Save.

Assign attribute groups to team areas and employees

Attribute groups filter which attributes are available for selection when assigning to employees and team areas. If no attribute group is assigned, all attributes are available.

 

Assign an attribute group to a team area

Quick jump to Team Area Configuration.

Specify the team area.

Click Open General Parameters.

Select the required attribute group from the drop-down list.

Click Save.

Assign an attribute group to an employee

Go to Back Office > CoreTime/CoreRoster > Pers Data > Person Maintenance.

Specify the person.

Select Rostering from the Select Detail menu.

Select the required attribute group from the drop-down list.

Click Save.

Assign roster attributes to employees

You can assign attributes at employee level (setting a default for all patterns), at individual pattern level (overriding a single pattern), across multiple employees in a team area, or across an entire week using the weekly view.

 

Assign a default attribute at employee level

A default attribute applies to all of an employee's patterns from the start date you specify. Each employee can only have one open-ended attribute at any one time.

 

Quick jump to Roster Details.

Click on the employee name you want to add the attribute to.

Select Person Attributes from the options.

Select Add to create a new row.

Select an existing attribute from the drop-down list.

Select a start date from the calendar.

If required, select an end date from the calendar.

Click Save.

When you return to the Roster Details screen, you'll see the default attribute displayed on the employee's patterns from the effective date.

 

Override an attribute for one pattern

Use this option to change the attribute for a single pattern without affecting the employee's default.

 

Hover over the employee pattern you want to change.

Select Change Roster.

Select the required attribute from the Attribute drop-down list.

Click Save.

📌Note: The attribute list is filtered by the attribute group assigned to the employee or team area. If no group is assigned, all attributes are available in the drop-down list.

Update attributes for multiple employees

Use Change Roster – Many to update the attribute for multiple employees in a team area at the same time.

 

Quick jump to Roster Details.

Click the Actions button.

Select Change Roster.

Select the required attribute from the Attribute drop-down list.

Click OK.

Select the applicable employee shifts.

Click Save.

Ensure the correct attribute is selected on the Change Roster screen, then click Save.

Click OK to confirm, if prompted.

Return to Roster Details, click the Actions button, and select Refresh This Week.

📌Note: For full guidance on the Change Roster screen, view the Roster CorePortal Administration User Guide on CoreHR University.

Update attributes for the week — weekly view

The weekly view lets you update attributes for all seven days in a single save, making it quicker to maintain attribute data across the week.

 

Quick jump to Roster Details.

Click on the employee's name.

Select Assign Attributes.

Click Assign on the applicable day.

Select the required attribute from the Attribute drop-down list.

Click OK.

Repeat steps 4 to 6 for all required days.

Click Save.

Filter the roster by attribute

You can filter the Roster Details screen by one or multiple attributes. When the filter is active, only employees with the selected attribute on that day are displayed — employees assigned a different attribute are hidden from the view. A count of active filters is displayed on screen.

 

⚠️Important: The attribute filter cannot be used to re-order the screen. The Attribute column always remains in its last available position and cannot be moved higher.

Quick jump to Roster Details.

Click the Day view.

Select the filter button.

Select the Attribute filter.

Enter the required attribute name in the field and select it from the results.

To add more attributes to the filter, select them from the drop-down list.

Click Apply.

Report on roster attributes

Roster attribute data is available to report on in CoreInsight, under the Core Time area. When creating a report, join the Person Day view with the Roster Attribute views.

 

The following views and reportable items are available:

 

View

	

Reportable items




Person Day

	

Attribute Code




Roster Attribute

	

Code, Description, Roster Attribute




Person Roster Attribute

	

Appointment ID, Assigned By, Date Assigned, Start Date, End Date, Person Reference, Roster Attribute

📌Note: For guidance on creating a report in CoreInsight, view the CoreInsight training material on CoreHR University.

title: How to Change a Single Day Work Schedule for an Employee
text:
Sometimes you may need to adjust an employee’s schedule for a single day — for example, to cover a shift swap or temporary change in duties. Portal allows you to update the pattern for a specific date while keeping the employee’s normal schedule unchanged.

⚠️ Important: This change only applies to the specific day you select. The employee’s regular schedule pattern remains unchanged for all other days.

Use this process for one-off schedule changes only, not long-term pattern updates.

If you are making significant changes to an employee’s schedule, consider:

Informing the employee

Reviewing any related processes such as payroll, absence management, or balances

 

Update a single day using WFM Person Maintenance

Follow these steps to update the employee’s schedule for one day.

From the WFM Admin Dashboard, select WFM Person Maintenance.

Use the search function to find the employee.

Open the three-dot menu next to the employee’s name and select Timesheet.

Click Actions, then select Weekly Work Schedule.

Navigate to the week that contains the day you want to change.

In the Pattern field for the relevant day, click to edit.

Select the new pattern or shift.

Move away from the field to automatically save the change.

Alternative method: update from Roster Details

You can also update the schedule directly from the roster view.

From the WFM Dashboard, select Roster Details.

Select the day you want to change.

Click Change Roster.

In the Change Roster screen, select the pattern you want the employee to work.

Click Save.

title: Advance the system calendar without using advance period
text:
This involves a two-step process. To do this, follow both steps below.

 

Step 1: Move the Control Parameters current Period forward.

Click CoreTime, then click System Params.

Click Reference A-C, then click Control Parameters.

Key Features of Shift Types
Cycle Shift

The Cycle Shift option ensures that the schedule repeats on the same weekly cycle. Enable this feature if you want the same work pattern to recur every week. This is particularly useful for consistent scheduling needs.

 

Sequence Number 1

The Sequence Number 1 represents the weekly schedule, typically from Sunday to Saturday. When setting up a new shift type, you can add entries for each day’s work pattern within this sequence. If the Cycle Shift option is enabled, this sequence will automatically repeat each week.

Alternatively, we recommend copying an existing shift type, where a similar one exists, by clicking Copy from its three dot menu.

Cycle shifts are considered best practice as they reduce future shift maintenance.

title: Manage work patterns, including deletion and inactivation?
text:
Work patterns in PeopleXD are essential for defining employee schedules and operational workflows. However, there are specific limitations and processes to be aware of when managing these patterns. This provides an overview of how to handle work patterns, including setting them to inactive and understanding their visibility.

 

Overview of Work Pattern Management

You can’t delete work patterns in PeopleXD once you create them. If you no longer need a work pattern, set it to inactive instead. This prevents it from being used in future while keeping it available for reference.

 

Steps to Set a Work Pattern to Inactive

Go to the work pattern management section in PeopleXD.

Locate the work pattern you wish to deactivate.

Change the status of the work pattern to Inactive.

Once a work pattern is inactive, it will no longer be available for use in scheduling or other operations. However, it will remain visible in the system interface.

Limitations of Work Pattern Management

Deletion: Work patterns cannot be deleted once created. This ensures that historical data and references remain intact.

Visibility: Even when set to inactive, work patterns cannot be hidden or archived. They will continue to appear in the configuration or management interface.

FAQs
Can I delete a work pattern that was created by mistake?

No, work patterns cannot be deleted. If you don’t want a work pattern to be used, set it to inactive.

 

What happens when I set a work pattern to inactive?

Setting a work pattern to inactive prevents it from being used in future operations. However, it cannot be hidden or archived and will remain visible in the system interface. By understanding these guidelines, you can effectively manage work patterns in PeopleXD while maintaining system integrity and operational clarity.

title: Error – you are not allowed to modify this personal shift override
text:
If you see the error “You are not allowed to modify this personal shift override”, it means the system is preventing the override because the shift falls outside the current open calendar period.
Shift overrides can only be applied to shifts that fall within the current open period or in a future period.

Why this error occurs

This error happens when:

The date effective on the shift is before the current open period on the system calendar

The system calendar does not allow edits or overrides for past or closed periods

A personal shift override is being added to a shift that is no longer editable

How to resolve the error
Assign a new shift within the open period

Go to the employee’s profile.

Assign a new shift with a date effective that falls within or after the current open period.

Save the new shift.

Apply the personal shift override to the newly assigned shift.

📌Note: The system does not allow overrides on shifts dated before the current open period.

Always ensure the date effective is within an open calendar period before applying overrides.

If you need to make changes to historical shifts, contact your system administrator to review calendar settings.

 

🤓Tip: If you frequently see this error, check the system calendar open period before assigning or modifying shift overrides to avoid rework.

title: Delete unused or mistakenly created shift types?
text:
Managing shift types effectively is crucial for maintaining an organised workforce schedule. If you have unused or mistakenly created shift types in PeopleXD, you can delete them to keep your system clean and efficient. This article provides a step-by-step guide to deleting shift types, including prerequisites and troubleshooting tips.

Prerequisites for deleting shift types

Ensure the following conditions are met before you delete a shift type:

No Assignments: The shift type must not be assigned to any employees. You can only delete a shift where it has never been used. If a shift has ever been assigned to an employee or a work group the system stops you from deleting it.

Necessary Permissions: Ensure you have the required permissions to delete shift types. This may involve assigning specific menu profiles or roles to your user account. If you do not have the necessary permissions, contact your system administrator for assistance.

Process to Delete Shift Types

Follow these steps to delete a shift type in PeopleXD: go to the list of shift types, find the shift type you want to delete, click the three-dot menu next to it, select Delete, and confirm the deletion when prompted.

📌Note: The Delete option will only appear if the shift type has never been assigned to any employee.

Troubleshooting Common Issues

Delete Option Not Visible: If the Delete option does not appear, verify that the shift type is unassigned and that you have the necessary permissions. Assigning the appropriate menu profile or role to your user account may resolve this issue.

Permission Issues: If you lack the required permissions, contact your system administrator to update your user profile with the necessary access rights.

By following these steps and ensuring the prerequisites are met, you can efficiently delete unused or mistakenly created shift types in PeopleXD, keeping your workforce management system streamlined and accurate.

title: Assign shifts to employees without fixed schedules in Workforce Management
text:
You can manage shifts for employees who do not have a fixed schedule in PeopleXD's Workforce Management module. Use REST shifts as a default placeholder, manually override shifts for specific working days, or configure Flexi Work Patterns for more advanced scheduling needs.

 

REST shifts as a default for flexible employees

For employees who do not have a fixed shift pattern, assign a REST shift type as their default. This acts as a placeholder, ensuring every employee has a shift type assigned at all times. You can then manually adjust their schedule as needed.

 

Override shifts for specific working days

To roster an employee on specific working days, update the default REST shift for those days directly in the Roster screen or Weekly Work Schedule.

 

Open the Roster screen, or go to Timesheet Input and select Weekly Work Schedule.

title: Portal: Grant user access using System Users
text:
To give users access to work groups and departments, you need to first add the work group or department to the user and then grant their access.

This includes permissions for viewing employee calendars, which are determined by the assigned Work Group and Department combinations.

 

To do this, follow the steps in each section below in order.

 

Add Work Groups or Departments for Calendar Access

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration then select WFM System User Configuration.

Next to the relevant employee, click the three-dot menu.

Select View/Edit then select the company.

Click Access Details then add the relevant work groups and departments.

Click Save.

 

 

Grant access

If you're a super user, you can grant access to all work groups and department combinations. To do this, follow the steps below.

This also applies to granting permissions for viewing employee calendars.

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration then select WFM System User Configuration.

Next to the relevant employee, click the three-dot menu.

Select View/Edit then select the company.

Click Access Details then click Actions.

Select Access All Groups / Departments.

 

Limitations of Calendar Access Control

It is important to note the following limitation when managing calendar access:

 

Inability to Restrict Calendar-Only Access: The system does not allow restricting access solely to calendars. If a user has access to other dashboards, such as People Management or Payroll, they may also view sensitive information like salary details. To limit visibility, you must control the user’s broader dashboard and data access permissions.

title: Configure user access privileges
text:
To enable access privileges for a user, follow the steps below.

 

Portal

Click the dashboard menu at the top left then click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration then click WFM System Users Configuration.

Next to the relevant user click the three-dot menu then click View/Edit.

Click the Access Privileges tab.5. Under the Team Area Access section, assign the required team areas as needed. 🔑 Note: Users without assigned team areas cannot see employee data in the Roster module. Ensure the correct team areas are allocated to resolve this issue.

 

Back Office

Click CoreTime then click System Params.

Click System Users then click Access Privileges.

Additional Privileges

Team Area Access: This access option allows assigning users to specific team areas. Ensuring correct allocation can mitigate visibility issues in the Roster module. Menu Profile Options (Roster Details): Adjusting menu profiles, such as disabling the WRKMGMT_MENU.WRKMGMTVIEW option, can restore editing capabilities if users face view-only access issues.

Field
	
Description



HR User

	

This indicator is used if the System User is also to be a H.R. User. The H.R. User can see and maintain pay codes that have been marked as H.R. Only. Other System Users who do not have this indicator will be unable to view these pay codes




Always Access all Work Groups/Departments

	

This access privilege grants the Core | Time user access to all employees (i.e. without having to specify all work group/department combinations on ).




Use Employee Access in Person Maintenance

	

This indicator when selected always allows access to all the work groups and departments attached to the company the System User has been attached to. It is important to note that if employees move between work groups and departments, then this indicator will automatically pick up the changes.




Approve Hours

	

This access privilege allows the Core | Time user to approve hours recorded against pay codes set-up as 'requires approval'. By default, this access privilege is assigned to all Core | Time users. However, this access privilege can be removed from a Core | Time user if required.


​Note: This indicator is only applicable if the 'requires approval' Pay Code functionality is being used




Sign Off Hours

	

This access privilege allows Core | Time users to sign off hours for employees in their remit.




Restrict Person Setup

	

This indicator restricts the set-up of an employee to the company that the user is attached to e.g. if the user is attached to company one, then he or she can only set up employee that are attached to company one also




Lock User After Sign-Off

	

This indicator prevents the user from making any changes to the current week once the week has been signed off




Reset Clock Type

	

This indicator allows the users to enter manual clockings for employees regardless of whether or not the employee has been setup to allow 'Maintain clockings'.




Maintain Historical Clockings

	

By default, input of clock times on the Maintain Hours screen is restricted to the current CoreTime week. The Maintain Historical Clockings access privilege allows the CoreTime user to input/amend/delete clockings within the open rolling period via the Maintain Hours screen.




Maintain Historical Hours

	

By default input on the Maintain Hours screen and the Record Absence Details screen is restricted to the current Time and Attendance week and future Time and Attendance weeks This access privilege allows the CoreTime user to input/amend/delete historical hours via the Maintain Hours screen and historical absences via the Record Absence Details screen SUBJECT to the date being within the open rolling period.




Automatically Approve Hours

	

Turning on this indicator for a user will mean that all hours recorded for an employee under this person's remit will be automatically approve. Use of this option is NOT recommended.
​
​Note: This indicator is only applicable if the 'requires approval' Pay Code functionality is being used.




Pre-Approve Future Absence

	

This indicator allows the user to pre-approve a future absence through the Record Future Absence form.
​
​Note: This indicator is only applicable if the 'requires approval' Pay Code functionality is being used.




Modify Automated Clockings

	

This indicator, when selected, will allow the System User to modify the clockings generated automatically when an employee clocks in/out. Other System Users who do not have this indicator will be permitted view only access to automated clockings.




Access all Work Groups/Departments

	

This indicator when selected allows access to all the work groups and departments attached to the company the System User has been attached to. It is important to note that if employees move between work groups and departments, then this indicator will need to be refreshed in order for the System User to detect the changes.




Ignore Data Entry Restriction

	

Turning on this indicator will allow the System User to enter data historically as far back as they wish,override any time restriction that is in place for entering historical data ( for example, the 'Roll Back Weeks for Data Entry' value specified for the company or work group is ignored.)




See Hidden Balances

	

The See Hidden Balance access privilege allows this Core Time user to view balances configured as 'Hide on CoreTime'. CoreTime users without this access privilege will not be able to view balances configured as 'Hide on CoreTime' i.e. the balances will not appear in drop-downs etc.




Hide Narrative

	

This indicator when selected hides narratives from the user on the Pay Code Occurrences Report.




Hide Reason Code

	

This indicator when selected hides reason codes from the user on the Pay Code Occurrences Report.




Move Automated Clockings

	

This indicator, when selected, will allow the System User to move automated clockings from one to another within the current system week. The original automated clocking is retained, along with the automated indicator on the clocking. This can be useful if employees are working shifts, starting in one day and finishing the following day.




Allow Historical Calculation

	

This indicator allows the user to run a re-calculation on a historical period. This should be used in conjunction with 'Maintain Historical Clockings'




Leave Request Admin user

	

The Leave Request Admin User access privilege allows the CoreTime user to view the Approve Leave Request screen in admin mode . This user will only see requests from employees in his/her remit (based on work group/department combination).




Allow Medical Cert Entry

	

The Allow Medical Cert Entry access privilege allows the CoreTime user to input sick certificate details via the Record Absence Details screen.
​
The Medical Cert details button on the Record Absence Details screen is only enabled if (1) the Pay Code is a sick Pay Code and (2) the user has the Allow Medical Cert Entry access privilege




Allow Future Calculation

	

Select if the user is allowed run a calculation into the future.




Limit Absence Detail Start Date

	

Select to limit the start date that an absence can enter ( dates greater than or equal to the start date of the Input Period or Flexitime Period)




Maintain Rate of Pay

	

Select to allow users to maintain the rate of pay field on the Maintain Hours screen




Override Leave Request

	

This access privilege allows the CoreTime user to amend (or delete) absences created as a result of an approved leave request via the Record Absence Details screen

Administrators can further manage Roster-related permissions by tweaking individual menu profiles or adjusting privileges at the user level for specific editing capabilities.

title: Can the Team Scheduler filter be changed so it returns Departments, Locaton etc instead of Work Group
text:
You can update the Admin Dashboard filter to use Work Group, Department, Cost Centre, Location, or Project.

This article explains how to update the filter settings.

title: Create a Period Closure
text:
The period closure screen allows administrators to pre-book company closure periods, such as Christmas or a summer shutdown, and automatically deduct the relevant leave from staff entitlements. 

 

You need to complete four steps to set up and enable a period closure. These must be completed in order to ensure your closure period works correctly.

 

To set up and manage a Period Closure in Workforce Management (WFM), watch the video of follow the steps below.

 

 

Create a period closure

On the WFM Admin Dashboard, click the Period Closure tab.

Click Add Period Closure.

Fill in the closure details for example, the name, dates and Pay Code.

Click OK.

 

 

Create a Criteria Group

On the WFM Admin Dashboard, click the Period Closure tab.

Expand the three-dot menu next to the relevant Period Closure.

Select Assign Criteria Groups, then click Manage Criteria Groups.

Click Add, then fill in the Name and Type, then click OK.

Select the required reference data from the left-hand menu.

Select the required values from the Available list.

Click the right arrow to move the criteria to the Assigned column.

Repeat steps 5 to 7 as required.

 

 

Assign a Criteria Group

On the WFM Admin Dashboard, click the Period Closure tab.

Expand the three-dot menu next to the relevant Period Closure.

Select Assign Criteria Groups, then click Manage Criteria Groups.

Click Assign New Group, then select the required Criteria Group.

Click OK, then repeat to assign additional groups.

 

 

Retrieve employees

On the WFM Admin Dashboard, click the Period Closure tab.

Expand the three-dot menu next to the relevant Period Closure.

Select Retrieve Employees, then review the list of employees.

Turn on the Exclude toggle to remove employees from the closure, if needed.

Click Assign.

title: Portal Error: Entry/Modification/Deletion of the data during this period is restricted
text:
When deleting an absence record in the Portal for a historic period, you might see this error message:

This happens because the system is set to block changes to data from past periods to protect payroll integrity. However, you can resolve this by enabling the Ignore Data Entry Restriction access privilege for the relevant user.

 

How to enable the Ignore Data Entry Restriction access privilege

Follow these steps to update the user’s access:

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration.

Click WFM System Users Configuration.

Find the relevant employee and click the three-dot menu next to their name.

Select View/Edit.

Click Access Privileges.

Enable the checkbox for Ignore Data Entry Restriction.

Click Save.

What happens next?

Once this privilege is enabled, the user will be able to delete historic absences in the Portal without receiving the restriction error.

📌 Note: Be cautious when deleting historic data, as this can affect payroll records or reporting.

title: How to Set Up Auto Advance Periods
text:
The Auto Advance Periods feature ensures that your system calendars automatically stay up to date.
When enabled, the system will check if any calendars are in the past. If they are, it will automatically advance them by one period.

This helps prevent calendars from falling behind the actual date.

 

Steps to Set Up Auto Advance Periods

Navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click on WFM Configuration.

Select the Company and Calendar Config tile.

Click on Auto Advance Periods.

Click Add.

In the pop-up, select:

The Day of the Week when you want the auto advance to run.

The Time you would like the process to occur.

Click OK.

Once configured, the system will automatically check and advance your periods based on your settings.

In Access People XD, user defined periods are managed through the system calendar. If a period has been marked as completed but needs to be reopened—for example, to correct data or process additional transactions—you can roll it back by following the steps below.

title: Back Office: Extend the system calendar
text:
Extending the system calendar each year is essential to avoid errors such as "Failed Contact Support" when you generate timesheets. PeopleXD uses both yearly and weekly calendars:

Yearly calendars: Ensure the full year is covered.

Weekly calendars: Used for day-to-day time tracking.

You should extend both calendar types to cover the next calendar year.

🤓 Tip: Always complete these steps before the start of the new year to avoid any service interruptions.

Extend the yearly calendar

Click CoreTime then click System Params.

Select Calendars then click System Calendars.

Enter the relevant company number then click Calendar Years.

On the next available row, enter the year, start date, and number of weeks.

Click Save.

 

 

Extend the weekly calendar

Click CoreTime then click System Params.

Select Calendars then click System Calendars.

Enter the relevant company number then click Generate Period.

For End Period, enter the week number for the final week of the new year.
​
For example, for the last week of 2025, enter 202552.
​

Click OK then click Save.

title: Migration to the new PeopleXD Ideas Portal
text:
As part of our continued efforts to improve the way we collect and action feedback from our PeopleXD clients, we are migrating to a new Ideas Portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment.

 

This new portal provides a more modern interface, enhanced tracking features, and a stronger foundation for future improvements, including better two-way communication and AI-assisted idea prioritisation.

 

The legacy portal will be permanently retired on 30th June 2025.

 

What's changing? 

From 30th June 2025, the following will occur: 

The legacy portal will no longer be accessible.

The new portal will be the single location for all PeopleXD idea submissions.

Any ideas submitted in the last 12 months or with 10 or more votes will be automatically transferred to the new portal.

Older ideas that don’t meet the above criteria will not appear in the portal, but will still be retained internally by our product team for reference in roadmap planning.

 

How do I access the new portal?

You can access the new ideas portal in one of two ways: either by an invitation sent to your email or by registering manually on the site.

 

Received an invite 

If you’ve received an email inviting you to log into the new Aha! Ideas Portal, this means:

You have previously submitted or voted on an idea in the old portal in the last 12 months.

We have automatically created a user account for you in the new portal.

Follow the link provided in the email to log in, then set a password.

 

Register manually 

If you didn't receive an email inviting you to log into the new Aha! Ideas Portal, you can still register for the new portal manually. To do this, follow the steps below. 

Go to the new People XD Ideas Portal.

Click Sign up.

In the Email address field, eneter your work email address. 

In the First and Last name field, enter your name. 

Click Register. 

You’ll receive a verification email. Follow the link in the email to complete your registration.

Once you've registered, you can:

Browse and vote on existing ideas.

Submit new ideas

Follow ideas to track progress and status changes.

 

What if I can’t find my old ideas?

If you can't find one of your previously submitted ideas in the new ideas portal, try the following: 

Search for the idea: Some titles or categories may have changed slightly.  

If it still doesn’t appear, resubmit the idea as a new entry in the portal.

 

Need help?

If you encounter any issues registering, logging in, or locating an idea, please raise a new case online or speak with your customer success manager, we’re happy to help.

 

Thank you for helping shape the future of PeopleXD.

title: Set up job title mappings in Workforce Management
text:
Job Title Mapping lets administrators group multiple job title variants under one standard reference title in Workforce Management. These variations often occur due to different employment types, legacy setups, or workforce pool structures.

Once configured, all mapped titles are treated as equivalent in Required vs Rostered calculations, providing a more accurate view of staffing coverage across diverse workforce groups.

This feature is available to UK and Irish clients.

 

Access job title mapping

To open the Job Title Mapping configuration:

Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.

Select WFM Configuration from the left-hand navigation.

Under Roster Configuration Settings, select Roster Job Title Mapping.

You can also search for "mapping" in the WFM Configuration search bar to locate it quickly.

The Job Title Mapping form

The Job Title Mapping form contains the following fields.

Field

	

Required?

	

Description




Job Title

	

Yes

	

The job title variant you want to consolidate. Select from the dropdown list of available job titles.




Mapped Job Title

	

Yes

	

The reference title to map to. All variants mapped to this title are treated as equivalent in Required vs Rostered calculations.

📌Note: Each row in the Job Title Mapping list shows the job title and its mapped job title. The numbers displayed beneath each title are the job title codes.

Create a job title mapping

To create a new mapping:

Click Add.

Select the Job Title you want to map from the dropdown.

Select the Mapped Job Title from the dropdown.

Click OK.

The new mapping appears immediately in the Job Title Mapping list and takes effect straight away.

Delete a job title mapping

Removing a mapping will stop job titles from being grouped together in calculations.

⚠️Important: Deleting a mapping removes the consolidated grouping. Required vs rostered calculations will revert to treating each job title separately.

To delete a mapping:

Locate the mapping you want to remove.

Select Delete on that row.

Click Yes to confirm.

Menu Option

	

System




ROS_CONF_MENU.ROSTER_JOB_TITLE_MAPPING

	

Parent Link




•   WS_ROSTER_MENU.GET_JOBTITLE_LOV

•   WS_ROSTER_MENU.GET_JOBTITLE_MAPPINGS

•   WS_ROSTER_MENU.POST_JOBTITLE_MAPPINGS

•   WS_ROSTER_MENU.DELETE_JOBTITLE_MAPPINGS_ID

	

Webservice

📌Note: Adding the parent link enables all webservices listed above.

title: Error: [Pay Code] must be entered in XXX days segments
text:
Cause 1

Ensure each of the below requirements are met by ensuring the employee is applying for the relevant segment of leave in their request.

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard.

Select WFM Configuration.

Click on Work Patterns.

Query the Work Pattern.

Check the Work Pattern Full Day Value. 

Click Misc - 1, Full Day Value should be the same as the Default Hours of work pattern.

📌 Note: The balance will be reduced by 0.50 Days rather than 1 Day and will allow leave to be approved in Approve Leave Request

Cause 2

This error can occur if the users balance was set up to only allow for full, half, quarter day segments. Thus, changing the Balance Segment value to 'Blank' will resolve the issue

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard

Select WFM Person Maintenance

Query Employee

Click on Balance tab

Select 3 dots next to the required balance and choose 'Edit Setup'

Change Balance Segment value to 'None'

Click Save 

Cause 3

This error can occur if the employee is trying to book 'Absence' for Full Day but the 'Work Pattern' on that day for the employee has 'Default Hours' less than the hours needed for Full Day absence

Take note of the Work Pattern the employee is working on the day of the absence.

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard

Select WFM Configuration

Click on Work Patterns

Query the Work Pattern

Check the Default Hours

User does not have enough entitlement on the affecting balance

Select System Users

Query the employee

title: Error: 'You are not rostered to work on this day' when applying for leave
text:
There are four possible causes for this error. To fix this, follow the causes and resolutions below.
​

The employee has no shift type attached.

To resolve this, assign a shift to the employee.

Day in question falls on a CoreTime Period that was not configured correctly. 

To ensure that the period is correct, follow the steps below.

Click CoreTime, then click System Params.

Click Calendars, then click System Calendars.

Click the Question mark symbol, then click the relevant company.

Edit the week in question to the correct value. (E.g. change from 11-FEB-2015 to 11-FEB-2016)

Click Save.

Unrostered Booking functionality is not configured correctly

Assuming Unrostered Booking is allowed (i.e. customer has an active Roster license). To configure this, follow the steps below.

Click CoreTime, then click System Params.

Click Reference A-C, then click Control Parameters.

Click the Question mark symbol, then click the relevant company.

Under Select Detail, click Contract Hours, then tick the Allow Functionality and the Enable Functionality check boxes to enable the options.

Click Save.

Bank Holiday Scheme doesn't have the RFA (Record Future Absence) option enabled

To enable this option, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard, then click WFM Configuration.

Click Bank Holiday Schemes, then next to the relevant scheme, click the three-dot menu.

Click View, then next to the relevant bank holiday, turn on the Allow RFA toggle to enable the option.

Click Save.

System Calendar is not extended until the day the employee is applying for leave.

To resolve this, extend the system calendar.

text:
This error message usually appears because either the 'Maintain Historical Hours' privilege isn't enabled for the Manager's Org Role OR Work group does not have user defined calendar enabled (if not enabled, the system calendar current period is used as the open date) OR If the user does not have 'Ignore Data Entry Restriction' and 'Maintain Historical Hours' privilege Enabled.

Go to CoreTime.

Click on System Params.

Select System Users.

Use the Access Type drop-down and select Organisation Roles.

Query the Org Role.

Check the Maintain Historical Hours check box is selected.

Click Save.

📌 Note: If System Users have been set up individually for Managers, enable the privilege for the System User instead of Org Role

To check if Maintain Historical Hours is enabled in Portal, follow the steps below.

Go to Security

Click on Setup

Select CoreTime System Users

Use the Access Type drop-down and select Organisation Roles

Query the Org Role

Check the Maintain Historical Hours check box is selected

Click Save

Back Office

Go to CoreTime.

Click on System Params.

Select Work Groups.

Query the Work Group.

Click General Parameters - 2.

Select the User Defined Calendar Group check box.

Click Save.

Portal

Go to WFM Admin Dashboard, WFM Configuration, Work Groups.

Select Work Group, View/Edit Work Group.

Select General Parameters tab.

Select the 'User Defined Calendar Group' check box.

Click Save.

Additionally if using UDC ensure that the Data Entry Offset value is greater or equal to 0 (Back Office), follow the steps below.

Go to CoreTime.

Click on System Params, Calendars, System Calendar, User Defined Periods.

Query related Calendar Code.

If Data Entry Offset is blank enter 0.

Click Save.

Go to CoreTime.

Click on System Params.

Select System Users.

Query the employee.

Select Access Privileges.

Enable 'Ignore Data Entry Restriction'.

Select MSS Access Type

Query employee

Select Access Privileges

title: Error: 403 Forbidden appears when updating the notification body of a trigger point
text:
Why Am I Seeing This Error?

This error is triggered by ModSecurity due to the number of special characters in the text you’re trying to submit.

 

 

Why Can’t This Be Changed?

For security and performance reasons, it isn’t possible to adjust this setting. ModSecurity is in place to protect the system from potential threats, so certain limits need to remain in place.

 

 

What’s the Workaround?

The best way to resolve this is to use a different link or remove the link altogether. Simplifying the text will help prevent this error from occurring.

text:

instead of the expected:

This is a known bug causing the calendar periods to be ordered incorrectly.

title: Employees are able to clock outside their geolocation

Enable geofencing in the Portal menu profile

In the Portal, navigate to Security and select Menu Profile.

Search for the relevant menu profile, for example, COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE.

Click the ellipsis (...) next to the profile and select Manage Menu Options.

Search for WS_CLOCKINGS_MENU.GET_GEOFENCING.

Enable the menu option Clockings > Get geofencing.

Save your changes.

Once this option is enabled, all users assigned to this menu profile who also belong to a geolocation group will only be able to clock within their designated area.

title: Error: Invalid File Format during File Upload
text:
If you receive an Invalid Date Entered error when uploading a file via PeopleHub, it usually indicates a mismatch in the expected Date Format.

 

How to resolve this

Navigate to People Hub and then Load Files.

Select the relevant Pay Group.
The corresponding File Group will display next to it.

Click the Settings tab.

Locate the File Group (identified in step 2) and click the 3-dot menu and then Files.

Find the correct file by checking the Description field.
Use the 3-dot menu next to the file and select Columns.

On the error screen, check the Table Name—this will match the File Number and Description.

Locate the relevant column, then click the 3-dot menu and then Edit.

In the Date Format field, enter the correct format to match the error message.

Click OK to save changes.

Upload the file again

Go back to the Load Files tab and select the relevant Pay Group.

Click Upload and select the file.

Once uploaded, click Actions and then Process Files.

title: Hours not calculating on Maintain Hours for all or a group of employees
text:
You can troubleshoot and fix issues where hours are not calculating for one or more employees in Maintain Hours by understanding potential causes and applying the correct resolutions. This article outlines ten common reasons for calculation failures and provides step-by-step solutions.  Common causes and resolutions.

 

Cause 1: Scheduled overnight calculation did not run for employees

Resolution:
Manually run a calculation and confirm hours have calculated.
If the overnight job failed, contact Support by raising a case online with this article’s title for database script investigation.
See also: How to run a manual calculation for multiple employees.

Cause 2: System Calendar and Control Parameters current period are out of sync

Resolution:
Update the System Calendar or Control Parameters to ensure both are in sync.
See: How to advance the System Calendar without using Advance Period.

Cause 3: System Calendar has not been extended

Resolution:
Extend the T&A system calendar as required.

Cause 4: Calendar-based Shift Types have not been extended

Resolution:
Extend the relevant standard Shift Types.
See: How to extend a standard Shift Type.

Cause 5: Work Group(s) do not have the 'Calculate Clockings' parameter configured

Resolution:

Go to CoreTime > System Params > Work Groups > General Parameters -2.

Tick the Calculate Clockings checkbox.

Click Save.

Cause 6: Overnight jobs are scheduled too close together and interfere

Resolution:
Contact Support by raising a case online referencing this article for further investigation.

Cause 7: Overnight jobs scheduled via Batch Jobs are hanging

Resolution:
Contact Support by raising a case online referencing this article for resolution.

Cause 8: Employee(s) have incorrect start dates set up

Resolution:
Review and update the employee’s original and latest start dates.
See: How to change an employee's original Start Date and Latest Start Date in CorePersonnel.

Cause 9: Calculation is outside Back Office default 42-day period

Resolution:
Ensure the calendar is up to date.
Note: From Back Office version 24+, calculations only run back 42 days; from version 26 onwards, this extends to 90 days.

Cause 10: 'Calculate to' parameter set to 'End of Input Period'

Resolution:

Navigate to CoreTime > System Params > Reference A-C > Control Parameters > General Parameters -1.

Set the Calculate to field to Yesterday or Today.

title: Floating Entitlement for Re-Hired Employee is Incorrect
text:
Issue:

When an employee is re-hired within the same Annual Leave period, their entitlement calculation may not prorate based on their new joining date. Instead, the system prorates the period during which the employee was not employed.

For example:

Annual Leave Balance period: 1st January to 31st December 2022

Employee re-joined on 19th September 2022

The system prorates the gap period from 13th May to 19th September 2022, rather than calculating entitlement from the re-join date.

Resolution

You will need to manually adjust the employee’s balance to reflect the correct entitlement.

Steps to perform a Manual Balance Adjustment:

Go to People Management Dashboard > Command Centre.

Click View next to Employees.

Search for and select the relevant employee, then click View.

Navigate to the Balances tab.

Locate the relevant balance and click the 3-dot menu, then select Balance Adjustment.

Enter the adjustment details:

Effective date

Affecting element

Adjustment amount

Reason for adjustment

Click Save to apply the manual adjustment.

📌Note: This process does NOT apply to Multi-Appointment clients.

title: Resolve overtime hours not displaying on approve/sign off screens
text:
You can resolve missing overtime hours on approval screens by ensuring employee email addresses are correct and that managers have the appropriate role access for their work groups. This guide explains how to update email addresses in both the Portal and Backoffice and how to verify and assign manager roles.

 

Cause 1: Employee email address missing or incorrect

Overtime hours may not display if the employee’s work email address is empty or incorrect. Update this information using the steps below.

 

Update work email address in Portal

Log in to the Portal.

Go to People Management.

Search for the employee and select View.

Choose Contact Information.

In the Work Email Address field, click the ellipses (…) and select Edit.

Add or update the employee’s Work Email Address.

Click Save.

Update work email address in Backoffice

Log in to CorePersonnel in the Backoffice.

Select Maintenance.

Choose Personal Profile.

Click on Addresses / Contacts.

Update the Email Address as needed.

Click Save.

Cause 2: Manager role access not set for employee’s work group

If the manager lacks the required role access for the employee’s work group, overtime hours may not show on approval screens.

 

Verify and assign manager role access in Backoffice

Log in to CorePersonnel.

Select Reference.

Click Maintain Organisational Roles.

Query the employee’s Work Group.

If the manager is not listed, assign the manager with Manager Role Access for that Work Group.

Verify and assign manager role access in Portal

Log in to the Portal.

Go to People Management.

Select Data Centre.

Choose People Management.

Click Maintain Organisational Roles.

Query the employee’s Work Group.

If the manager is not present, assign the manager with Manager Role Access for that Work Group.

If overtime hours still do not display after these steps, verify the employee’s and manager’s profiles for any other missing or incorrect details, or contact your system administrator for further assistance.

title: Error: You do not have access to this person's calendar on Employee Calendar
text:
Managers can view employees' schedules using two different calendar screens:

Team Calendar

Employee Calendar

These two calendars work differently and use separate access controls. Even if a manager can view an employee on the Team Calendar, they may still get an error when accessing the Employee Calendar if the correct portal parameters are not set.

Why this happens

The Team Calendar uses the Org Chart/Structure to determine visibility.

The Employee Calendar uses portal parameters:

cp_pers_maint_org_role

cp_pers_maint_org_group

If these parameters are not aligned to the manager's access, they will see the message:

"You do not have access to this person's calendar."

How to check the Employee Calendar access settings

Go to the Admin Dashboard.

Select Site Manager, then Admin Settings.

Search for cp_pers_maint.

Check the values for the following parameters:

cp_pers_maint_org_role

cp_pers_maint_org_group

For example:

Parameter

	

Example Value




cp_pers_maint_org_role

	

MGRESS




cp_pers_maint_org_group

	

WRKGRP

This configuration means a manager’s access to the Employee Calendar is based on MGRESS (Reports to Manager) at the WRKGRP (Work Group) level.

⚠️Important: The Team Calendar allows you to view employees in the reporting structure, even multiple levels down.  The Employee Calendar requires direct org role access based on the portal parameters.  If the manager does not have the correct MGRESS/WRKGRP access for the employee, the system will display the error message.

Resolution steps

Confirm that the manager has the appropriate org role access for the employee’s work group.

Update the cp_pers_maint_org_role and cp_pers_maint_org_group if needed, or adjust the manager’s access levels to match.

title: Error: You may not have access to this leave request, please try again in 10 mins or contact an administrator
text:
Root Cause

There are two main reasons this error occurs:

The manager does not have the required Menu Profile.

The manager does not have the correct Organisational Role (Org Role) access for the employee’s Work Group.

How leave approvals work in WFM

Access Point

	

Requirement




Team Calendar

	

Requires Org Role Access (Reports to Manager at Work Group level)




Notification Centre

	

Requires Menu Profile Access + correct Org Role Access

📌Note: Admin users cannot approve leave via the Team Calendar unless they have the correct Org Role Access for the employee’s work group.

 

How to resolve the issue
Check Menu Profile Access (For Notification Centre Approvals)

To enable Notification Centre approvals:

 

Portal Steps

Go to Security → User Management.

Search for the relevant Menu Profile (e.g., COREPORTAL_MANAGER).

Select Manage Menu Options from the 3-dot menu.

Search for CorePortal - Notification Actions Tab.

Enable this option.

This allows managers to approve requests via the Notification Centre, assuming they have the correct Org Role Access.

Check Org Role Access (For Team Calendar Approvals)

To approve leave via the Team Calendar, managers need Reports to Manager role access at the Work Group Level.

 

Back Office Steps:

Go to Core Personnel.

Select Reference and then find Maintain Organisational Roles.

Query the Work Group of the employee.

If the manager is not present, assign them Manager Role Access for that Work Group.

Click Save.

Portal Steps:

Go to People Management.

Select Data Centre and then click on People Management.

Click Maintain Organisational Roles.

Search for the Work Group of the employee.

If the manager is not present, assign them Manager Role Access.

Click Save.

Important Scenario to Consider

If the manager did not have the required Org Role Access at the time the leave was requested, they cannot approve it later via the Team Calendar, even if access was added afterward.

 

Example:

Date

	

Action




01-Feb

	

Employee submits leave request for Work Group ADM123.




01-Feb

	

Manager does not have required Org Role.




02-Feb

	

Manager is granted Org Role Access.




Result

	

Manager cannot approve the request because they lacked access at the time of submission.

Workaround Options

Option

	

Action




Cancel & Resubmit

	

The employee can cancel the request and submit it again (post Org Role setup).




Admin Approval

	

An Admin user with access can approve the request directly.




Direct Entry

	

The absence can be entered manually into the system.

Summary

Team Calendar approvals require Org Role Access.

Notification Centre approvals require Menu Profile Access + Org Role Access.

Requests submitted before access is granted cannot be approved retroactively via Team Calendar.

title: Error: No permission to add documents when trying to add a document to an absence type or pay code
text:
This error occurs when the document type is not active or permissions are not properly set in the Portal, or when the pay code does not support the required document type. You can fix this by activating the document type, updating permissions, and ensuring the pay code supports the document type in both Portal and Back-Office.

Activate document type and set permissions in the Portal

Before you start, ensure you have appropriate administrator access in the Portal.

To activate the document type and set permissions:

In the Portal, go to People Management.

Select Data Centre and click View All.

Search for Document Types.

Select the relevant document type (for example, Absence Supporting Documents).

Click the ellipsis (...) and select Options.

Enable MSS to allow managers and admin users to add this document type.

Enable ESS to allow employees to add this document type.

Enable the Active slider to make the document type active.

Click Save.

Ensure the pay code supports the document type in the Portal

Follow these steps to check and update the pay code:

In the Portal, go to WFM Admin Dashboard.

Select WFM Configuration.

Select Pay Codes.

Search for the relevant pay code.

Click View on the pay code.

Scroll to the Leave Request Documents section.

Update the document type if needed.

Save any changes.

Verify and update pay code settings in Back-Office

Before proceeding, ensure you have access to Back-Office with the necessary permissions.

In Back-Office, go to Core Time.

Select System Params.

Click Pay Codes.

Search for the pay code in question.

Select Documents.

Untick or update the field Supporting Documentation Required as needed.

Click Save.

Once these steps are completed, users will be able to add documents to the relevant absence type or pay code using the activated document type.

title: Bulk Leave Approval screen displays 'Nothing to See Here'
text:
If the Bulk Leave Approval screen shows 'Nothing to See Here', this usually means the user doesn’t have the correct level of Personnel Access. Even if the Menu Profile is assigned, without the right access level, the screen will not display any data.

Under Security Type, select Personnel Access.

Enter the required Username, Structure Code, and Access Level.

Click Show Access.

Enable the desired level of access for the user.

Click Save.

Update Personnel Access in the Back-Office

If you prefer, you can also update Personnel Access using the Back-Office system:

Go to CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q–Z > System Users.

Under Security Type, select PERS.

Enter the required Username, Structure Code, and Access Level.

Click Show Access.

Enable the required level of access for the user.

Click Save.

Verify Manager Role Access for the employee’s work group

Select Reference.

Click Maintain Organisational Roles.

Click the ? symbol to search.

Select the relevant work group.

Check if the manager is listed with Manager Role Access for that work group.

Select Maintain Organisational Roles by Person.

Click the ? symbol to search.

Select the relevant manager.

Confirm the manager has Manager Role Access for the employee’s work group.

title: How to Enable the Return to Work Interview Option
text:

Additionally, there are other methods to enable the Return to Work Interview feature, such as configuring menu profiles and dashboard widgets, which will be discussed later in this guide.

 

Enabling Return to Work Interviews via Pay Code Configuration

The Return to Work Interview option is configurable and must be enabled within the relevant Pay Code(s) for it to appear when recording absences.

This is one of several methods available to enable the feature, providing flexibility depending on organisational needs.

Follow the steps below to enable this setting:

Click Pay Codes.

Next to the relevant pay code, click the three-dot menu, then choose View/Edit Pay Code.

Click Absence Settings, then turn on the Return to Work Interview toggle.

Click Save.

📌 Note: The Return to Work Interview option will now appear when absences are recorded using this pay code.  The Return to Work Interview widget is currently accessible only through the desktop version of PeopleXD and is not available on the mobile app.

title: Configure the Employee Calendar
text:
Set up the Employee Calendar to control how events, pay codes, and colours display for different user types in Workforce Management.

You can configure the Employee Calendar in Workforce Management to customise how calendar events display for your employees. This includes setting start days, choosing calendar formats, assigning colours to events, and managing which pay codes appear on the calendar for different user types.

By following the steps below, you can ensure the Employee Calendar is configured to meet your organisation's needs.

 

Configure Global Calendar Settings

Global Calendar Settings control the general layout of the calendar and how the calendar displays across your organisation.

To configure the Global Calendar Settings:

In the Global Calendar Setting section, use the drop-down menus to set up the calendar.

Choose the calendar Start Day.

Select whether the calendar uses Rolling months or Fixed months.

Use the Colour selectors to set colours for different calendar sections.

Your changes will save automatically and appear on the Employee Calendar.

Configure Pay Code Settings

Use the Pay Code Settings tab to choose which pay codes display on the Employee Calendar and assign colours to them.

To set up pay codes:

Click the Pay Code Settings tab.

Search for the pay code you want to add to the calendar.

Use the toggles to enable the user types who should see the pay code when viewing an employee's calendar.

In the Colour column, choose the colour that will display for this pay code.

Repeat these steps for each pay code you want to display.

Once enabled, the selected pay codes will appear on the relevant User Type Pay Codes tabs.

Manage pay codes and calendar events by user type

You can manage which pay codes and calendar events display for each user type.

To do this:

From the User Type Pay Codes tabs, click Add if you need to directly assign additional pay codes for a specific user type.

For each user type, enable the Calendar Events you want to display when that user views the Employee Calendar.

Review your configuration

Once you’ve completed the steps, the Employee Calendar will display the configured pay codes and calendar events for all selected user types.

title: Allow users to enter clockings for employees in Time and Attendance
text:
Person Maintenance: Enable Maintain Clockings for employees

The Maintain Clockings parameter controls whether users can input or maintain clockings for a specific employee. If this is not enabled for an employee, no user—regardless of their own permissions—can modify that employee’s clockings.

 

To enable Maintain Clockings in Portal:

Go to WFM Admin > Person Maintenance.

Query the employee.

Click the ellipsis (...) and select View.

Select Person Settings.

Enable Maintain Clockings.

Click Save.

To enable Maintain Clockings in Back Office:

Go to CoreTime > Pers Data > Person Maintenance.

Search for the employee.

Select the General -1 tab.

Enable Maintain Clockings.

Save changes.

System Users: Assign clocking privileges to users

Users must have appropriate privileges enabled to input or modify clockings for employees. However, these privileges are ineffective if Maintain Clockings is disabled for the employee.

Available clocking privileges in Portal:

Modify Automated Clockings
Allows updating or deleting clockings received from devices or employee ESS clock-ins.

Maintain Historical Clockings
Allows entry, update, or deletion of clockings in past weeks. Historical entries are marked with a clock type prefix H.

Move Automated Clockings
Allows moving automated clockings to a different day without changing the clock time (useful for night shift adjustments).

Reset Clock Types
Allows changing the clock type attached to a clock time. (Refer to related Knowledge Base articles for clock type explanations.)

To assign privileges in Portal:

Navigate to WFM Admin > Config > System Users Configuration.

Query the user.

Click the ellipsis (...) and select View/Edit.

Under Access Privileges, tick the relevant options.

Click Save.

To assign privileges in Back Office:

Go to System Params > System Users.

Query the user.

Select Access Privileges.

Tick or untick the relevant privileges as appropriate:

Modify Automated Clockings

Maintain Historical Clockings

Move Automated Clockings

Reset Clock Types

Save your changes.

⚠️Important: If a user does not have any of the clocking privileges enabled, they can still input or modify manual clock times (marked with prefix M).  To prevent all clocking input or modification for an employee, disable Maintain Clockings for that employee in Person Maintenance.

title: Assign menu profiles to users
text:
Menu profiles control user access to system functionality in PeopleXD. Users require at least one menu profile to access the system.  The Security dashboard serves as the central hub for managing user access, roles, and menu profiles, providing a streamlined approach to access management.

 

 You can assign multiple profiles depending on the user's role. For example, an employee profile for the Employee Dashboard, a manager profile for the Manager Dashboard, and an HR admin profile for the People Management Dashboard.

Assign menu profiles to a user

To assign or remove menu profiles for a user,  watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, select Security then click User Management.

On the System Users widget, in the search field, search for the user.

Beside the relevant user, click the three-dot menu then click Manage Account.

Click Menu Profiles.

Use the search field to find a menu profile or use the drop-down filter to display:

All: All menu profiles configured on PeopleXD.

Assigned: Menu profiles currently assigned to the user.

Not Assigned: Menu profiles not assigned to the user.

To assign a menu profile to the user, turn on the Active toggle.

To remove a menu profile from the user, turn off the Active toggle.

 Configure the Menu Profile Matrix

The Menu Profile Matrix allows you to automatically assign menu profiles to groups of employees based on rules. There are two types of assignments available:

Assignment type
	
Description



Employee Organisation Role

	

Menu profiles are assigned based on an organisational role. A nightly process identifies employees with a matching role and assigns or removes the profile based on whether the role is active.




Employee Account Provisioning

	

Menu profiles are assigned during the self-registration process. If an employee's current substantive contract meets the rule requirements, they receive the corresponding menu profile.

Best Practices for Configuring Access

Regularly review user roles and menu profiles to ensure they align with organisational needs.

Use descriptive names for menu profiles to make them easily identifiable.

Limit access to sensitive features by assigning roles and profiles only to authorised users.

Document changes to menu profiles and access settings for future reference.

Menu options required

To assign menu profiles to users, users require the following menu options:

Menu option
	
System



• Menu Profiles - View Only 
• Menu Profiles - Update

	

Security

Additionally, ensure the following menu options are enabled for specific functionalities:

 

HR_CONFIGURATION_MENU.EMPLOYEE_MANAGER_REQUESTS for Employee and Manager Requests.

$_R00T menu profile for full access.

title: Error: Pay Code must be entered in full day segments – Timesheet Claim
text:
This error occurs when submitting a timesheet claim against a balance that is incorrectly configured to require full day segments.

 

Root Cause

At the employee level, the Balance Segment validation is set to enforce full day segments. This prevents partial day entries (e.g., 3 hours) from being processed for the affected pay code.

Back Office Steps

Go to CoreTime.

Click Person Data.

Select Person Maintenance.

Locate the relevant employee and click on Current Balances.

Identify and select the Balance linked to the pay code causing the error.

In the Balance Segment drop-down, change the selection to:

cssCopyEditNone

Click Save.

Why This Works

By setting Balance Segment to None, the system removes the restriction that forces claims to be entered in full day units. This allows the employee to submit claims for partial day hours without error.

title: How to Assign Non Group Payroll Codes (NGPC) to Employees or Work Groups
text:
Purpose

Non Group Payroll Codes (NGPC) are used to control which payroll codes are excluded or skipped when generating timesheets for specific employees or groups.

⚠️ Important: Assigning an NGPC directly to a Work Group will impact all employees in that group.  If you have a mix of salaried and non-salaried employees in the same group, it is recommended to assign NGPCs at the employee level.

Viewing and Managing NGPCs
Back Office Steps

Go to CoreTime

Click System Params

Select Ref D to J

Open Group Non Payroll Codes Menu

title: Pay code not appearing on the create leave request screen drop-down
text:
If you cannot see a specific pay code when creating a leave request, there are three common causes to check. Each cause has a corresponding resolution that you can apply both in the back-office system and the portal to restore visibility of the pay code.

 

Cause 1: Pay code is not marked as an Allow Leave Requests code

The pay code must be enabled to allow leave requests in both CoreTime (back-office) and the portal. Additional parameters may also need enabling for the pay code to appear on CorePortal screens.

 

Steps to enable Allow Leave Requests
Back-office (CoreTime):

Go to CoreTime.

Select System Params.

Click Pay Codes.

Search for the relevant pay code.

Select the General Parameters-1 tab.

Enable Allow Leave Requests.

Click Save.

Portal (WFM Admin Dashboard):

Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration.

Select Pay Codes.

Search for the pay code.

Select the Leave Request Settings tab.

Enable Allow Leave Requests.

Click Save.

⚠️Important: There is a parameter called Restrict input of this code on the ESS in the General Parameters-4 section of the pay code screen. If this is enabled, it will prevent the pay code from being used in CorePortal or restrict its use to certain days relative to today’s date.

To ensure the pay code appears on various CorePortal screens, make sure these parameters are enabled:

Allow Leave Requests

Allow Future Absences

Allow Absence Details

Cause 2: Employee has not been assigned a personalised pay code group

Employees must be assigned to a personalised pay code group for the pay code to appear in their leave request options.

 

Steps to assign a personalised pay code group
Back-office (CoreTime):

Go to CoreTime.

Click Pers Data.

Select Pers Maintenance.

Search for the employee.

Go to the Personal Groups tab.

Add a personalised pay code group.

Click Save.

Portal (WFM Admin Dashboard):

Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Person Maintenance.

Search for the employee.

Select the Personal Groups tab.

Add a personalised pay code group.

Click Save.

Cause 3: Pay code is set to 'HR Only'

If a pay code is marked as HR Only, it will not appear on the leave request screen for general users. Disabling this setting can restore visibility, but confirm this change internally as it is often intentional.

 

Steps to disable HR Only setting
Back-office (CoreTime):

Go to CoreTime.

Select System Params.

Click Pay Codes.

Search for the pay code.

Select the General Parameters-1 tab.

Disable HR Only.

Click Save.

Portal (WFM Admin Dashboard):

Go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration.

Select Pay Codes.

Search for the pay code.

Select the Summary tab.

Disable HR Only.

Click Save.

Granting access to the Pay Codes screen on the portal

If you cannot access the Pay Codes screen under WFM Configuration, follow these steps to gain access:

Go to Security.

Select User Management.

Search for your employee number.

Click Manage Account for your record.

Go to Menu Profiles.

Search for the menu profile named WFM_PAY_CODES_ADMIN and enable it.

Log out and log back into your portal account to see the option.

title: An employee's hours haven't transferred to PeopleXD Payroll
text:
If you've linked PeopleXD Workforce Management to PeopleXD Payroll, but the hours worked aren't transferring for an employee, there are several factors that could be causing this.

 

To resolve this, check each of the following in order.

 

Hours aren’t signed off

In order for the timesheets to successfully transfer to PeopleXD Payroll, you need to sign the hours off. We recommend you double-check that the hours are signed off. 

 

 

Employee paid in advance

If you paid the employee in advance, for example, for a company shutdown, there will be no timesheets for the current period.

 

When you next generate timesheets, any outstanding hours, such as overtime, will transfer to PeopleXD Payroll. 

 

 

Employee marked as Non Generate Timesheets

If the employee is marked as Non Generate Timesheets, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Next to the relevant employee, click the three-dot menu.

Click View then click Work Group Override.

Next to Non Generate Timesheets, click the three-dot menu.

Click Edit Override then turn on the Non Generate Timesheets toggle.

Click OK.

 

 

Pay code is configured as Group Non Payroll

If the pay code is set as a Group Non Payroll code, follow the steps below.

Click CoreTime, then click System Params.

Click Ref D-J, then select Group Non Payroll Codes.

Click Group Non Payroll Code Details, then click Next.

Remove the pay code in question, then click Save.

 

 

Employee’s work group not set to generate timesheets

To enable timesheet generation for the employee’s work group:

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration, then Work Groups.

Next to the relevant Work Group, click the three-dot menu.

Click View/Edit Work Group then turn on the Generate Timesheets toggle.

Click Save. 

 

 

Work group wasn't included when generating timesheets in test mode

To ensure the timesheets transfer successfully, you need to ensure you include the employee's work group in both the To and From work group ranges when you generate timesheets in test mode.

 

 

The employee isn't set up in CorePay

The employee needs to exist in CorePay for the transfer to work. If they aren't already, set them up in CorePay, then re-run Generate Timesheets. 

 

 

Hours processed for a different payroll period

You may have accidentally processed the hours against a different payroll period. If this is the case, to roll the period back, follow the steps below.

Click CoreTime, then select System Params.

Click Calendars, then System Calendars.

Search by Company Code, then click User Defined Periods.

Search by Calendar Code, then clear the check box for the affected period.

Click Save.

 

The employee doesn’t have a shift assigned

In order for the transfer to work, the timesheet needs to have an associated work pattern or shift, even if you've signed off the hours.

 

To resolve this, you need to remove the existing hours, assign a work pattern or shift, then re-enter and sign off the hours.

Click CoreTime, then click System Params.

From the list of values, select the relevant balance.

title: WFM year end tasks
text:
The WFM year end tasks screen eliminates guesswork by giving system administrators a centralised view of all tasks and actions needed to keep the WFM system up to date.

 

WFM year end tasks screen

To see how WFM year end tasks could benefit you, watch the video or follow the steps below.
​

Open the WFM Admin Dashboard and select WFM Year End Tasks.

For Action Required tasks, click the three-dot menu, then click View.

Click View for each active company, calendar or scheme and extend.

 

 

Create custom year end tasks

You can create your own year end tasks, so they become part of your year end task list actions. To do this watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

On the WFM Year End Tasks screen, click Add Check List Item.

Enter the task name, description, due date and comments, then click OK.

📌Note: Check list items need to be manually completed. Click the three-dot menu, then select Mark as Complete and add a new due date.

 

 

Set email parameters

To ensure the system sends the relevant email notifications for each year end task at a relevant time for your organisation, email parameters must be configured. There are three email parameter to configure for year end task notifications.

ct_year_end_email_fromn - The subject of the email notification.

ct_year_end_email_frome - The address the notification will be sent from.

ct_year_end_email_to - The admin/individual admin’s inbox email address.

To do this watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

On the Administrator Dashboard, select Site Manager.

Next to Admin Settings, click OPEN, and search ct_year_end.

Click Edit and update the value(s), then click OK.

 

 

Notification threshold

Email notifications for tasks that require action are sent when the default 30 day threshold is met. You can adjust this threshold to suit your organisation's needs. To do this, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

On the WFM Admin Dashboard, select WFM Configuration.

Click General Settings, update the Year End Limit, then click Save.

 

 

Menu profiles

Before you can access the WFM year end tasks functionality, the following menu profiles must be assigned.

WFM_YEAR_END.

WFM_COMPANY_SETTING_ADMIN.

WFM_BANK_HOLIDAY_CONFIG.

WFM_BALANCE_CONFIGURATION.

WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES.

title: Additional Details options when assigning appraisals
text:
The Additional Details settings give you control over whether you include employees in an appraisal, based on their probation expiry date or start date.

 

In the table below, we've outlined what each option means 👇

Option
	
Description



Do not include employees with a future probation expiry date

	

Employees are excluded if their probation expiry date is on or after the appraisal start date.

 

Use this to avoid assigning appraisals to employees still on probation.




Only include employees with a future probation expiry date

	

Employees are only included if their probation expiry date is on or after the appraisal start date.

 

Use this if the appraisal is specifically for employees currently in, or just finishing, probation.




Automatically assign to employees whose probation expiry date occurs within X days of the start date

	

Once the appraisal starts, the system checks daily for the number of days set in the Number of Days field.

 

If an employee’s probation expiry date falls within that period and is populated on their profile, the appraisal will automatically be assigned to them.




Automatically assign to employees whose start date occurs within X days of the start date

	

Similar to the above option, the system checks daily for the defined number of days after the appraisal start date.

 

If an employee’s start date falls within that timeframe, the appraisal will be automatically assigned.

These automated options help ensure new starters or probation-ending employees don’t miss relevant reviews, even if their details are added after the appraisal begins.
