title: Review and action HR changes
text:
⚠️ Important: HR Changes is currently available as part of an early adopter programme and is not yet in general release. Speak to your customer success manager for further details.

The HR Changes screen in PeopleXD Talent shows leaver and manager changes from PeopleXD People Management. Changes sync overnight, so you can review and approve or reject them the next day.

 

When you approve a change, appraisals and objectives update automatically, keeping data consistent across both modules.

📌 Note: 

You need to have admin access to the Talent Dashboard to use this feature.

Changes made in modules other than PeopleXD People Management won't appear in HR Changes.

Types of HR events

There are two types of HR events in the HR Changes screen:

Leaver: Employee with a past end date and active appraisals or objective cycles.

New HR Manager: Employee whose manager has changed, with active appraisals or objective cycles.

 

 

Review HR changes

Open the HR Changes screen:

From the dashboard menu, click Talent Dashboard.

Click the HR Changes tab.

The screen displays all pending HR events. You can search by employee name or personnel number, and filter by HR event type using the Filter by HR Event drop-down.

 

 

Approve or reject a change

To action changes individually or in bulk, watch the video or follow the steps below:

⚠️ Warning: Manually Assigned indicates whether an administrator has set a specific manager for the employee’s appraisals or objectives. If it shows Yes, review carefully before approving a manager change.

Single employee

To action a change for one employee:

From the dashboard menu, click Talent Dashboard.

Click the HR Changes tab, then search for the employee.

Turn on the Approve or Reject toggle, then click Yes to confirm.

Multiple employees

To action changes in bulk:

From the dashboard menu, click Talent Dashboard.

Click the HR Changes tab, then select the checkboxes next to the employees.

Click the Approve or Reject button, then click Yes to confirm.

 

 

What happens when you approve

The outcome depends on the event type.

 

Leaver

The relevant appraisals and objective cycles update to Cancelled status.

The previous and indirect managers can no longer see the employee in the Talent Dashboard.

Cancelled employees are excluded from assigned employee counts and do not appear in active employee views, such as Manager Overview.

🤓 Tip: To view or restore cancelled employees, click Admin Options, then use Manage Review for appraisals or Manage Objectives for objective cycles.

 

New HR Manager

The relevant appraisals and objective cycles are reassigned to the new manager.

The previous manager and indirect manager can no longer see the employee in the Talent Dashboard.

title: Unable to change the stage dates in a cloned review
text:
When you clone a review or appraisal and want to update the dates for a new year or period, PeopleXD won’t let you change the stage dates unless the main review dates are aligned first. To resolve this, you need to adjust the dates in a specific order.

 

The review is already cloned

If the review you cloned already has its date range moved into the new year, but the stage dates are stuck, follow the steps below.

In Edit Details, change the Review Start Date back to its original date.

Extend the Stage End Date forward into the new year.

Update the Stage Start Date so it also moves into the new year.

Move the Review Start Date forward again into the correct year.

 

 

The review hasn't been cloned

If you haven't cloned the review into the new year yet, or to avoid any issues in future years, we recommend you complete the process in the following order:

Extend the Review End Date into the new year.

Extend the Stage End Date into the new year.

Move the Stage Start Date into the new year.

Update the Review Start Date to the new year.

title: Objectives visibility explained
text:
When you set up an objective type within an objective cycle, you have the option to decide who has visibility. When you enable this, you allow users to select who can view the objectives that they create for this objective type.

 

There are three visibility types to choose from:

Public: All users can view the objective.

Private: Only the user who created the objective can view it.

Confidential: Only the user who created the objective and their manager can view it. 

📌Note: If you don't enable the Decide who has visibility option, each objective defaults to Confidential. 

Once you've activated the objective cycle, you can disable or enable the option for users to edit the visibility of their objectives. 

 

Amend the option to edit visibility

From the dashboard menu, select Talent Dashboard.

Click Objective cycles then create or edit an objective cycle.

Click Types then, next to the relevant objective, click the three-dot menu.

Select Options then enable or disable Decide who has visibility.

Click Save.

Once you've done this, to edit the objective visibility, the user can follow the steps in the next section.

 

 

Edit objective visibility

From the objectives widget, for the relevant objective, click the three-dot menu.

Select Edit Objective then click the Key Fields tab.

From the Visibility drop-down menu, select the relevant visibility type.

Click Save.

title: Configure custom workflows for objectives
text:
When you configure objective cycles, you can add an approval stage for each objective type. If enabled, when an employee creates or completes an objective, their manager is prompted to accept or reject it. You can also customise the statuses employees use when updating objective progress.

 

Set up the workflow

To create the workflow, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, click Talent Dashboard.

Click Objective cycles.

Next to the relevant objective cycle, click the three-dot menu.

Select Edit then skip to step two of the wizard, titled Types.

Next to the relevant type, click the three-dot menu.

Select Options then click the Key Fields tab.

Turn on the Custom Workflow and Statuses indicator.

Click Workflow & Status Setup.

Complete the steps in the wizard then click Save.

 

 

Approval stages

To configure the approval stages, enable or disable the indicators on the following questions:

Do you want the manager to approve the key fields before the employee can start working on the objective?

Do you want to open up the key fields for the employee after approval?

Do you want the manager to approve the final objective?

 

 

Workflow statuses

You can customise the standard workflow statuses by updating their display names. You can't deactivate these system statuses, but you can enter a new name in the Custom Description field to change how they appear to users.

 

 

Objective statuses

You can also assign a group of custom workflow statuses to the objective type. When an objective is in progress, employees can update progress by selecting a status from the list provided.

 

Assign an existing group

From the drop-down menu, select the relevant group.

Review the statuses displayed on screen.

Create a new group

Click Manage Statuses then click Add Group.

Enter a title then, from the Rating Type drop-down menu, select Status.

Click Add Status then configure your status details:

To set the display order, enter a numeric rating. 

To set the display name, enter a description.

From the drop-down menu, select a colour. 

Turn on the Active toggle.

Click OK then, once you've added all statuses, click Save.

Edit an existing group

Click Manage Statuses.

Next to the relevant group, click the three-dot menu.

Select Edit then, for the relevant status, click Edit Status.

Enter the rating, description, and colour.

If required, turn off the Active toggle.

Click OK then click Save.

title: Error: '404: Not Found'
text:
If you're attempting to print a review, but the error 404: Not Found appears, this is typically because of special character in the objective text fields, or the review's text fields. This can also be caused by spaces in a field with no text, or double blank lines at the end of the text.

 

To resolve this, you should back up data from those fields then set them all to blank. Once you've done this, attempt to print the review again.

 

If you're able to successfully print the review without the error appearing, you can re-add the backed up fields one at a time, to identify which field caused the issue. Alternatively, you can re-enter the information but ensure there are no special characters or additional spaces in the fields.

text:

title: Applicant Cleardown overview
text:
In PeopleXD Recruitment, you can use the Applicant Cleardown feature to automate the removal or anonymisation of applicant details. This process runs nightly and targets closed vacancies with a closed date older than six or twelve months.

 

The Applicant Cleardown process doesn't apply to successful applicants, which includes:

Applicants who appear on the Successful Applicants screen because they were linked to a job offer and their status indicates the offer was accepted.

Applicants who were hired from the Successful Applicants screen and for whom an HR record has been created.

When an applicant is unsuccessful for a vacancy, the following actions apply:

Their application for that vacancy is deleted.

If they have other active applications, their applicant record and those other applications remain unchanged.

If they have no other active applications, their applicant record is also deleted.

 

Manage the Applicant Cleardown process

To manage the Applicant Cleardown process, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

📌Note: This only works for vacancies with a Closed status and a closing date.

From the dashboard menu, click Recruitment Dashboard.

Click the Toolbox tab.

From the My Recruit Toolbox widget, open Applicant Cleardown.

From the Clear down data after drop-down menu, select the relevant option.

Click OK.

Option
	
Description



Do not clear

	

This is the default setting. Applicant data is not cleared.




6 Months

	

When the nightly process runs, this clears down applicant data from vacancies with a close date of over 6 months ago.




12 Months

	

When the nightly process runs, this clears down applicant data from vacancies with a close date of over 12 months ago.

text:
Cause 1: E-Recruitment Web Parameters not configured correctly for the Forget Password option
Cause 2: Email has been sent. Email is being filtered by the client's email
Cause 3: Applicant has two email addresses associated with their Applicant ID. Email will not fire unless the correct email address is entered
Cause 4: The Recruitment account associated with the applicant's email address doesn't exist 

 

Resolution 1:

In Back Office select CorePersonnel, Recruitment, Recruitment Reference, E-Recruitment Web Parameters, Email Parameters tab

Ensure that the Reset Password parameter is not blank

If blank - go to Details and Enter Reset Password in the Email Subject and enter in Email Body

Resolution 2:

Check the spam folder of your email client

If this is the case then navigate to the below screen:

Portal

Go to Data Centre and click View All 

Search for EMS Parameter Maintenance and open it

Back Office

Go to CoreHR

Click CoreHR dropdown

Select Event Management, then EMS Parameter Maintenance

Ensure that the contents of the EMS Username field match that of the Administrator Email field. It should be peoplexd@accessacloud.com for both fields.

Resolution 3:

If the above two do not resolve the issue, Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article.

Resolution 4:

Advise the applicant to try to register a new account with the email address they are trying to reset the password for

title: Generate and merge applications
text:
Generating and Merging in Portal:
Generating:

Click Recruitment

Query a Vacancy

Click Actions, View applicants

Click Actions once more and select Generate Applications

Select all or some of the applications you wish to generate

Click Actions

Click Generate Applications.

A message will appear on the screen informing that the job has been submitted, and the recipient will receive an email when complete. Once the Merge has been completed the date and time will appear.

Merging:

Click Recruitment

Query a Vacancy

Click Actions, View applicants

Click Actions once more and select Merge Applications

Select all or some of the applications you wish to merge

At the bottom, click Merge Applications. A message will appear on the screen informing that the job has been submitted, and the recipient will receive an email when complete. Once the Merge has been completed the date and time will appear.

Generating and Merging in Back Office:
Generating:

Generate applications to combine all documents associated with an application into one PDF Document. This step can be done from either the Application Status screen or the Document details screen.

Click CorePersonnel, Recruitment, Maintenance, Applicant Status

Query a Vacancy

Click Generate Applications. The Generate Applications Screen opens.

In the detail window of the screen, select all or select particular applicants to Generate.

Click Generate Applications.
​Note: You may have to exit the screen and reopen it for the date to appear.
A message will appear on the screen informing that the job has been submitted, and the recipient will receive an email when complete.
Once the job has been completed the date and time will appear on the right of the applicant details.

To view the combined PDF double-click the date and time. The PDF Document opens in a new browser Window on PC. 

Merging:

Merging applications creates a combined PDF Document with all the applications for that competition or vacancy.

Click CorePersonnel, Recruitment, Recruitment Maintenance, Applicant Status

Query a Vacancy

Click Generate Applications

To select all or select particular applications, select the required check box(es).

At the bottom, click Merge Applications. A message will appear on the screen informing that the job has been submitted, and the recipient will receive an email when complete. Once the Merge has been completed the date and time will appear.

To view the PDF Document of the merged applications, double-click the date. The PDF opens on a new browser window on your PC.

title: Unable to Merge Applications in 'Vacancy Maintenance' screen
text:
The process runs out of memory when trying to merge a large number of applications simultaneously. The number of applications it is possible to merge at the same time will depend on how many documents per employee (CV, qualifications, images) are included. It is possible to generate a larger number of applicants where there are not as many additional documents, and fewer when there are more documents or large images.
​
Break up the merging of applications into smaller chunks of ~20 applicants per merge, or as many as can be combined at the one time.

title: Applicant country populated by the system
text:
This issue commonly occurs because every employee and applicant needs to be linked to an address template in order to be able to view them. These templates are linked to country codes.
If there is no country on the application, the system selects the country from the template that has the most recent date_effective.
There is a Portal parameter called cp_volc_default_country, this needs to be a valid country code.

To update the parameter, follow the below steps in Portal:

Go to the Administrator Dashboard.

Click Site Manager.

Click Admin Settings.

Search for cp_volc_default_country.

Click Edit.

Enter the Country Code.

Click Save.

Use the below if this does not work. It may be the case you need to add the country code to the address types.

To add country code to address types

Click CorePersonnel, Reference, Reference A-C

Select Address Type Codes

Click Add new Layout

Enter Effective Date - has to be later than current date effective

Select the Country

Ensure correct Address Type is assigned to Default Home Address

Add Country line as it is mandatory and necessary to make this work

Click Save

title: Unable to change e-Recruitment email address / username in Core e-Recruit
text:
This issue usually occurs because the Change E-recruitment Email Address / Username functionality is not enabled.

 

Step 1: Turn on Change Email Address Option

This will change the email address for the applicant for their applicant recruitment account - Switch on this option if you want to allow the user to change their email address for notification alerts and for future applications.

Click Portal, Recruitment, Toolbox, Recruitment Admin.

Click Navigation Section, My Account and enable the Change Email Address option.

Click Portal, Recruitment, Toolbox, Recruitment Admin.

Select My Account.

Ensure the Change Email Address options (listed below) are all selected:

Allowed change email address

Change email section heading

Old Email Address

New Email Address

Confirm Email Address

Change

Email change request failure message

Email details updated message Email change failure message

New and confirm email addresses do not match

New and confirm email not entered

If you want users to enter their password when changing their email address you can also select the Password option.

Step 2: Configure Change Email Address Alert

This is an email alert that can be configured to send to the applicant after they have changed their email address. This is to allow the applicant to verify that the new email address by selecting the link within the email that is sent to the applicant.

In Core back office, click CorePersonnel, Recruitment, Recruitment Reference, E-Recruitment Web Parameters, Email Parameters, Applicant Email Change

Click Details.

The message which sends to the alert can be configured.

Step 3: Ensure URL is configured

In Core back office, Navigate to CorePersonnel, Recruitment, Recruitment Reference, E-Recruitment Web Parameters, Web Parameters.

Ensure Applicant_Change_Email_URL is populated with a valid URL.

Note: Internal applicant email addresses will be the same as their email address within the PeopleXD system. This is the email address that will be used when applying as an internal applicant. If an applicant wishes to apply to a vacancy with a different email address, they will need to create a new applicant account with that new email address and they will be flagged as an external applicant.

title: Vacancy is not displaying in portal recruitment admin
text:
There are two possible causes of this issue:

Cause 1: HR Admin user does not have access to department for Recruitment Access Security Type, and/or

Cause 2: HR Admin user does not have access to sensitive department for Sensitive Department Access.

Resolution 1

Grant HR Admin user access to relevant departments for Security Type = Recruitment Access. To do this:

In CoreHR Back Office, click CorePersonnel, Reference, Reference Q-Z, System Users. Ensure that the Portal Account option is selected and use the HR Admin user's personnel no.

You can do the same from Portal:

In People management dashboard, go to Data Centre, View all, search access, and click on HR User access.

Query employee and select 'Recruitment Access' in security types, show access, and enable 'Access granted' for the required department.

Resolution 2

Where the Department is a sensitive department, grant HR Admin user access to the department. To do this

Click CorePersonnel, Reference, Reference Q-Z, System Users

For the Security Type, select Sensitive Department

Select Grant Access.

Click Save. If the department does not display - it is not a sensitive department.  

You can do the same from Portal:

In People management dashboard, go to Data Centre, View all, search access, and click on HR User access.

Query employee and select 'Sensitive Department Access' in security types, show access, and enable 'Access granted' for the required department.

title: Unable to find competition in Competition Detail Screen in CorePersonnel
text:
There are seven possible causes of this issue:

Cause 1: No Start Date was entered when creating Competition

Cause 2: User has not been granted Recruitment access to the relevant Department

Cause 3: User who created the Post, is not ticked on as a Post Administrator in the Recruitment User Profile

Cause 4: The competition was set to Restricted upon creation

Cause 5: Post Admin has been removed.

Cause 6: "Unsuitable Answer Option" field on database contains invalid character

Cause 7: Internal, External and Recruitment Open Times are not set at 15 minute intervals e.g. 10:40

 

Resolution 1:

Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article to have the correct start date entered for this Competition

Resolution 2:

Select Personnel, Reference Q - Z, System Users

Input Username effected

Change Security Type to REC

Click Show Access

Tick Access Granted against the relevant Department

Click Save

Resolution 3:​

Select Personnel, Recruitment, Reference, Recruitment User Profile 

Scroll to User effected

Tick on Post Administrator

Click Save

Resolution 4:

User who created the Competition needs to be logged in to carry out the next steps

Select Personnel, Recruitment, Maintenance, Competition Detail, Query Competition ID

In the Select Detail box, Authorise

Untick Restricted option

Click Save

If Competition ID cannot be viewed at this stage to change the Restricted Ind Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article to have the Restricted Indicator turned off.

Resolution 5:

User who is listed as the Post administrator has been removed from the system.
This value will need to be updated for the competition in question.

Resolution 6:

Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article to have the correct "Unsuitable Answer Option" input for this Competition

Resolution 7:

Please raise a new case online and reference the title of this article to set the Internal, Open and Recruitment Opening Times to a 15 minute time interval e.g. 10:00,10:15.

title: What are Talent Pools in recruitment
text:
Talent Pools and Talent Pool Categories can be configured in Recruitment, as per an organisation'ss requirement to define and group a set of employee or applicants.
Employees can be added to these Talent Pools in HR Admin, from a given Date Added. An employee can be a member of many Talent Pools if required.
Talent Pools are also available in Recruitment. If an employee applies for a vacancy on Recruitment, an applicant record is created for them. If that employee is a member of a Talent Pool, that will display in the relevant Talent Pool options in Recruitment for the recruitment administrators to review.
Talent Pools are managed at Person level on the system i.e. they are directly associated with an employee or applicant record and not linked to a Post Appointment/Contract.

 

How to View Employee Talent Pools

Click the ellipsis icon for the employee and select View Dashboard

There is no requirement to select a contract on the dashboard. Talent Pool assignments are managed at person level and not at a contract level.

Slide to the second page on the Dashboard

Click on the Talent Pool option

Please Note: The number displayed here will reflect the total number of Talent Pools that the employee is assigned to.

If not Talent Pools are currently assigned, this will display 0.

The Talent Pool screen will pop up.

This screen will show any Talent Pools that the employee is already a member of, including the date that they were added to it.

title: Generate an email for Applicant Status update
text:
Emails will be automatically generated for an applicant when their Applicant Status value is updated to a value that has been configured to send emails on status change, i.e. if the selected Applicant Status has the 'Email Template after status change' indicator enabled.
​
To configure this, follow the steps below:

From the Recruitment Dashboard navigate to the My Recruitment Toolbox widget.

OPEN Applicant Status.

For the required applicant status expand the 3-dot menu and select Status Details.

Turn On the Email Template after status change toggle and click OK.

Click Save to capture changes.

To configure the template, for the applicant status, expand the 3-dot menu and select Email Template.

Configure the template and click Save.

NOTE: The feature to send an email is only available when the Applicant Status is changed on the View Applicants screen for a single applicant, i.e. emails will not generate when Applicant Status is updated on any other screen in Recruitment e.g. the Bulk Update screen, Interview Panel (this will not work for hiring managers from the Manager Dashboard), Schedules, Assign Applicants, etc.
​
To generate an email notification, follow the steps below: 

From the Recruitment Dashboard navigate to the Vacancies widget.

For the applicable vacancy expand Actions and select View Applicants. 

To update an applicant's status, expand their 3 dot menu and select Edit Status.

Update the status and click OK.

The Email Template window will appear automatically where the applicant's email address will be updated to reflect the candidate's actual email address, as per their application.

From here you can update the subject or message body and use the Attachment button to attach a document, if required. 

Click Send.

Notifications configured in Back Office via the below path alert Back Office users when applicants' application data has been generated and merged into the PDF format (for more details please review PeopleXD Recruitment: Generate and merge applications).

Go to CorePersonnel

Click the Recruitment menu, then Recruitment Reference, and select ERecruitment Document Tracker 

On the next screen under Email Alert Setup use the Details button to configure the required notification

These notifications will send to the email address populated for the Administrator Email Address field on the ERecruitment Document Tracker screen (Parameters tab).

However

if the Back Office user account (ORUSER) has their Back Office Username (ORUSER) attached to a Personnel number and the Personnel number has an Email defined in Personnel Profile, Contacts then these notifications will send to this address

or this will default to the Email Address field in CoreHR, CoreHR (Top Menu), User Profile screen if no ORUSER is populated in the contacts screen of personal profile.

title: Process a Right To Be Forgotten Request
text:
GDPR gives individuals the right to ask organisations to delete their personal data. For example, if a candidate has registered on an organisation's website e.g. Careers Portal, or has submitted an application but been unsuccessful, they may request the right to be forgotten. The Right To Be Forgotten feature in PeopleXD Recruitment allows users to action this request by deleting any candidate information retained in PeopleXD.

 

Process Candidate Right to be Forgotten Requests

To process a request, follow the below steps: 

Navigate to the My Recruit Toolbox widget on the Recruitment Dashboard.

Click Open on Right To Be Forgotten.

Search for the applicant to be deleted using their name, applicant number, or email address. Alternatively, click OK to view all available candidates.

Click Delete on the relevant row.

Click Yes to confirm the deletion.

Note: Only candidates who are eligible to be deleted will be available on the Right To Be Forgotten screen. These are candidates who:

Do not have an employee record (i.e. an applicant record with a personnel number attached)

Do not have another application at the accepted stage

What Data is Deleted?

The following are all deleted when a Right to be Forgotten request has been processed: 

All Candidate Data held within the PeopleXD ATS i.e. Portal View of PeopleXD Recruitment

Generated PDF View of the Candidate Application

Candidate Data held within eRecruitment website

The following candidate data is not deleted: 

Candidate Data held within the new Careers Website (powered by Volcanic). However, customers have a self-serve facility to delete this data. 

Merged PDF Packs of Candidates (where multiple candidates are merged into one PDF document). These merged documents can be deleted manually by users, or when closing the vacancy. These documents can also be deleted as part of the automated Applicant Cleardown process, subject to the vacancy and candidate being eligible for cleardown.

Security Access

To access to the Right To Be Forgotten option, the following menu options must be enabled on the user’s menu profile:

System

	

Menu Option

	

ID




Web Services

	

Delete rtbf

	

WS_RECRUITMENT_MENU.DELETE_RTBF




Web Services

	

Get rtbf

	

WS_RECRUITMENT_MENU.GET_RTBF




CorePortal

	

Recruitment - Right to be forgotten

	

MAIN_MENU.RIGHTTOBEFORGOTTEN

Select Staff Requests within the My Recruit Toolbox widget

On the My Requests tab, click on the three dot ellipsis button against the staff request that needs to be edited

title: Amend applicant status codes
text:
Note: The below configuration changes will impact the system on a Global Level. As always if any configuration changes are to be made this needs to be completed first on a Test environment and confirmed to be working as expected before promoting to the Live Environment.
​
The Applicant Status Code is used to track an applicant through the various stages of the Recruitment Process.
​
To see these codes
Click CorePersonnel, Reference, A-C, Applicant Status
The indicators available are:

Applicant Applied: All applicants are marked initially with this status.

Applicant Offer: An applicant marked as Offered once they have been identified as being successful.

Applicant Acceptance: The successful applicant has accepted the offer.

Applicant Panel: Applicants can be places on an applicant panel.

Online Enquiry Update: Allows interviewers make enquiries online.

Each indicator must be linked against one of the Applicant Status types.
A mandatory record is here: AP - Applicant Applied
​
​Note: The Applicant Acceptance Status is necessary for the successful promotion of an applicant to an employee
​
To insert a record:

Select Edit Mode

To Insert New Record, press the Green Plus icon on the toolbar. 

Add in the necessary details.

If required, tick the indicators

Click Save to update the changes

Click Quit, Red Door icon to return to Main Menu.

title: Error - 'Error with broadbean integration further details in Logs (filter logs by broadbean).'
text:
Reason 1

Review the Job Description for any symbols and characters such as trademark symbols, ampersands, hyphens, etc.
If there is a large number of these either in the description or on other free text fields, this can cause the system to reject the export.

 

Reason 2

There might be an issue with the Broadbean credentials stored in XD for connecting to Broadbean. In this case, it is advised to raise this with Broadbean providing values set for the below parameters (Admin Settings) along with details of the error from the debug logs. 
​
cp_bb_username
cp_bb_password
cp_bb_apikey
​
Please raise a case with PeopleXD Support referencing this article along with the competition(s) affected and if we are ok to test by trying to export the affected vacancy to Broadbean to generate the logs and verify them to confirm the error.

title: Add volcanic custom mapping to my recruit toolbox
text:

A maximum of 5 custom fields are included in the integration

Any of the hierarchy fields plus a new ‘Recruitment Custom’ field can be selected

For migrating customers who already use the old custom fields, which were fixed, the new screen can be used to choose what fields they use for the integration.

To use the job advert custom fields, you will need to:

Add the reference data in PeopleXD (People Management > Reference Data > Recruitment Custom Data)

Ensure the same custom categories exist in Volcanic

Volcanic configuration

When creating an application form in Volcanic you can link it to the custom field from PeopleXD. To do this, set the usage conditions on an application form in Volcanic to ‘Custom Category Options’

text:
The staff request functionality enables managers and recruitment administrators to apply for additional staff. If you need to produce a report on staff requests and their status, please follow the steps outlined below.

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, enter and select Insight.

From the Actions dropdown, select Create Report.

Click Add, then select Column.

Search for relevant data items from the list on the left.

Request No.

Job Title.

text:
There are 2 columns that can be used in Insight for reporting the type of applicant.
​
The first is Applicant type from Recruitment Applicant master. This will report on the applicants current status which include internal/external. If an applicant is External and they are hired after completing recruitment then their status will change to Internal


The second is Application type which reports the applicants status of internal/external for that specific application. So even if an applicant was hired as part of recruitment, this status does not change from External for a specific competition. It will change once they apply for a job internally however.

title: Getting 'Error(s) has been found while sanitizing data, further information available in logs'
text:
Error about sanitizing data is caused by ModSecurity. ModSecurity is an Application Firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application. By inspecting HTTP traffic, it can prevent attacks stemming from webion, and security misconfigurations.
Items that are likely to be blocked or cause an error application security flaws, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), file inclusror/conflict are the following:
SRC, Style, !=, <>, /bold. This is not an exhaustive list.
​
As for the hyperlink, we would advise using any online to shorten URL https://www.shorturl.at/ as a long URL might also cause this issue.
​
And for copying text from Word, it is better to do formatting in Portal as text in Work might contain whitespace characters and non-Unicode characters. Copying text directly from Word will copy those as well and you might not spot them. So it would be better to type text in Portal.


To Resolve

You would need to determine which paragraph is causing the issue (by copying and pasting it into the portal). Once you know it try typing the words and saving after two or three words.

Sometimes words like 'from' and 'create' can trigger the error - If so, you must update the wording of the text.

If there are URLs then try shortening the URL.

text:
The applicants usually display in alphabetical order and the error usually displays
for the impacted applicant. No other applicants will display after the impacted applicant.
​
​This error can display in the following scenario:
The applicant is an internal applicant i.e. has personnel_no populated in pers_applicant.
A record should exist in hr_person for this personnel_no.
If it does not exist, then this error will display.
This can occur when the employee record in hr_person has been removed in People Management, ACTIONS, Delete Person. This can be checked in the audit.
​
To resolve the personnel_no can be set to NULL on relevant tables.

title: Mileage rate is generating incorrectly
text:
If a claimant is receiving an incorrect mileage rate when claiming an expense or the mileage rate is generating a zero value,  there are various reasons why this might occur.

 

We've compiled a list of steps that can be applied to resolve this issue. To do this, follow the steps below in back office. 

 

Resolution 1

To ensure the mileage rate is accurate, confirm if the car has been approved.

Click Core Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference C-C, then click Car.

In the Claimant field, enter the claimant number.

Click the query  icon.

Check that the claimant has an approved car set up.

If it is a company vehicle, select the Company Vehicle checkbox beside the claimant's primary car.

 

 

Resolution 2

After confirming if the claimant's car is approved, check if the car details have been adjusted after submitting the expense trip. 

Click Core Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference C-C, then click Car.

In the Claimant field, enter the claimant number.

Click the query  icon.

To check the car details, click View Car Audit.

📌 Note: When a claimant edits their car details on the portal after submitting a mileage trip for approval, the system sets the mileage rate to 0.

Before the trip is processed (generate payment claim is run), if the car details are changed after approval, the mileage rate will return to 0. 

 

 

Resolution 3

After checking if the car details have been adjusted, the claimant's YTD mileage needs to be confirmed to set up the correct rate on the mileage screen.

Click Core Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference C-C, then click Claimant.

In the claimant field, enter the claimant number.

Click the query  icon.

Beside the Kilometres YTD field, click Detail.

Verify that the selected mileage calendar for the year is accurate in the Kilometres Year field.

Compare the claimant's total miles per year to the mileage threshold rates to ensure the correct mileage rate is available for the claimant.

 

 

Resolution 4

If the car details haven't changed and the mileage rates are still being generated incorrectly, check if any rates are set up for the claimant's YTD on the mileage screen.

Click Core Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference M-R, then click Mileage.

Check if there is a rate set up that the claimant falls under.

If there is no rate, enter a new mileage rate as appropriate. 

To add a new mileage rate, click the add  icon, then fill in the following fields:

Company Car: Specify rates based on company or private car usage.

Vehicle Type: The Vehicle Type list can be dynamically created and assigned to vehicles and travel rates. The original scope includes Car & Vans, Motorcycles and Bike.

Mileage Fuel Type: This contains a predefined list of fuel types e.g Petrol, Diesel, Hybrid e.t.c

Engine Capacity From To: Configure rates based on Engine Capacity or CC’s range.

Date Effective: Provide the effective date of rates.

Kilometres Threshold: Configure rates based on kilometres threshold traveled i.e. mileage distance.

Kilometre Rate: Enter the applicable mileage rate.

F.C.A Ind.: If a Fixed Car Allowance Indicator is entered here, the mileage rate is the rate that will apply for that Allowance.

To save this, click the save  icon. 

📌 Note: Rates are based on the claimant's car and mileage YTD. The claimant will receive a certain rate based on the type of vehicle. For example, you can have a mileage rate for a petrol car fuel type with an engine capacity of 1-1400.

If the claimant's car is petrol and has an engine size between that capacity 1 and 1400, they would be paid the rate for petrol car fuel type, but there is also a mileage threshold associated with this rate.
​
A claimant's mileage rate may vary depending on how many miles they claim in a year. For example, a company can have a kilometers threshold ranging from 0-5000 to 5001-10000 km; if the claimant has traveled between 0-5000km this year, they will be paid Rate A, whereas if they have driven between 5001-10000 km, they would be paid Rate B.

title: Error: Mileage seems to be spanning expense year
text:
If you see this error when you attempt to save an expense report, this is because the mileage expense calendar for the current expense year hasn't been configured. 

 

To do this, follow the steps below in back office. 

Click CoreExpense, then click Reference. 

Click Reference M-R, then click Mileage Calendar.

To add a mileage year, click the add  icon.

In the Company Code field, enter the company code.

In the Expense Start Year and Expense End Year fields, enter dates for the current year.

Click the save  icon.

If you've configured the mileage calendar and the issue persists, check that the claimant is not attempting to save the expense report with dates spanning across another expense calendar year, as the system will not allow this.

title: Incorrect subsistence rates generated for trips in an expense run
text:
If you're conducting an expense run and the subsistence rate generated for the trips is incorrect even though the subsistence rates have been updated with the new rates, it is because the expense trips were entered before the subsistence rates changed.
​
The new subsistence rates cannot be picked up by the system as the expense trip has already been logged. The expense trip will need to be rejected in back office and the employee will have to create a new expense trip in order for the system to pick up the new subsistence rates.

title: Set up a reduced mileage rate
text:
To set up a reduced mileage, a scalable expense code will need to be created with a corresponding subsistence rate.

 

Set up expense code

Go to Back Office, then click CoreExpense.

Click Reference D-L, then Expense Code.

Create a new code with an expense type of Scaleable.

Under settings, check that the overwrite subsistence option is ticked.

📌 Note: How the code is set up (pay codes, settings) will vary depending on the organisation. Compare existing mileage expense codes already set up and the new code should use the same pay codes as the existing mileage code.

 

Set up subsistence rate

Go to Back Office, then click CoreExpense.

Click Reference S-Z, then Subsistence.

Create a new subsistence rate using the expense code you created. Input the rate to be used for reduced mileage.

This process can be repeated for any additional rates. For example, if you want different rates to be used based on engine CC, you will have to set up a new expense code and corresponding subsistence rate for each rate.

title: Mileage expense is calculating incorrectly
text:
There are multiple reasons why the mileage expense is not being calculated as expected.

 

The car's details were changed. If changes are made to a claimant's car after they submit a mileage trip before the change has been approved by their manager, the system will not pick the car's CC. 

 

To check if an update has been made to the car details :

Navigate to CoreExpense, Reference C-C, Car

Search for the claimant's car

Click View Car Audit

Check to see whether the car had been updated around the time of the trip in question

The F.C.A Start Date has not been populated

Navigate to CoreExpense, Reference C-C, Claimant.

Ensure that F.C.A. Start Date field has been populated.

📌 Note: F.C.A. Start date may not be used depending on your environment.

There is no mileage rate setup that the claimant falls under.

Go to Expense, Reference, Reference M-R, Mileage. 

Ensure there is a rate set up that this claimant falls under. 

If not, check that the car details saved against the claimant are correct or enter a new mileage rate as appropriate. 

If you've tried the above options and the issue still persists, please raise an online support case and reference this article in the case.

title: Add or update subsistence rates
text:
Subsistence Rates Configuration provides the means of recording and maintaining Subsistence Rates that are to be used in the system.
​ 

Bulk Upload

New subsistence rates can be uploaded into back office via CoreExpense, Reference, Reference S-Z , Subsistence upload .
​

This is used to upload bulk subsistence rates.
​ 

 

Manual Input

These rates can also be entered manually in Back Office on the Subsistence screen.
​

To enter a new Subsistence Rate in Back Office please follow the steps below.

Go to CoreExpense, Reference, Reference S-Z, Subsistence

Click on the Green Plus Icon to Insert New Record

Enter the relevant Subsistence information into the fields available

From Position Code: Either a Scale Code or a Scale Class (A to B) can be entered here

To Position Code: Either a Scale Code or a Scale Class (A to B) can be entered here

Expense Code: A valid Expense Code can be entered here

Location Code: A valid Location Code can be entered here

Currency Code: A valid Currency Code can be entered here

Date Effective: This is the date on which the Subsistence is effective from (format DD-MON-YY)

Upper Limit: The Upper Limit on the number of units for the Expense up to which this rate applies

Unit Rate: The Rate per Unit

Click Save

title: Subsistence claim is generating 0 value
text:
If an employee's overnight expense claim is generating an incorrect value, this is because the subsistence rates aren't set up correctly or the claimant doesn't  fit into an existing subsistence rate.
​ 

Solution 1

Subsistence rates will need to be reviewed. Rates can be seen through CoreExpense, Reference S-Z, Subsistence
​ 

 

Solution 2

The Claimant's Scale Code might not have a Scale Class set up. This can be reviewed through CoreExpense, Reference S-Z, Scale Codes.
If the Scale Class is missing this will need to be entered using the steps below.

Search the claimant's Scale Code

Enter the Scale Class (This is case sensitive)

Click Save.

Other Possible issues may include:

A rate has not been set up for the claimant's Company Code / Location Code / Currency Code.

An End Date has been populated for the rate that should be applying to the claimant.

A rate has not been set up for the Expense Code the claimant is claiming for.

The From/To fields are used for Scale Classes. Ensure the claimant's Scale Class is within the range specified by the From/To fields. For example, if the range is A - C, the claimant will need to be on Scale Code A,B or C.

title: Electric vehicle home and away rates
text:
We're implementing the recent HMRC changes to electric vehicle mileage reimbursement rates that came into effect from 1st September 2025. HMRC announced these changes on 22nd August, introducing split rates based on charging location: 8p per mile for home charging and 12p per mile for public charging.


This enhancement allows you to accurately reimburse employees based on where they charge their electric vehicles, ensuring legislative compliance whilst maintaining P11D Section E classification.

 

​What is this feature for?

The new EV split mileage functionality enables your organisation to charge different mileage rates based on where electric vehicle miles were charged. This feature is based on changes to UK legislation and can be configured according to your requirements.


Key benefits:

Complies with the latest HMRC guidelines for EV reimbursement.

Maintains existing audit trail and reporting capabilities.

Offers flexibility to use traditional threshold rates for some vehicles if preferred.

 
​How it works

When employees submit mileage claims for electric vehicles:

They enter the total miles travelled and the miles charged away from home (public charging).

The system automatically calculates home-charged miles: total miles - away miles = home miles.

The blended reimbursement is calculated using: (away miles × public rate) + (home miles × home rate).

The calculation breakdown is displayed transparently on the expense claim.

For example: An employee travels 11 miles total with 1 mile charged away from home:
1 mile × 12p (public rate) = £0.12
10 miles × 8p (home rate) = £0.80
Total reimbursement = £1.20

 


​Implementation timeline

 

Development prioritisation: This has been fast-tracked due to the short notice period from HMRC.
​UAT availability: 30th October 2025
​Live release: 6th November 2025
​Mobile app enhancements: Early 2026
​Note: The web app version will provide mobile access from the initial 6th November release, so employees can submit claims via mobile browser while we complete the native app updates.

 


​How to set it up
Step 1: Enable the feature

The enhancement operates behind a feature flag (exp-ev-split-mileage) and must be activated for your organisation. To request activation, please raise a support ticket.

 

Step 2: Configure the Car Rates Configuration widget

In the administrator dashboard, you'll need to set up the new widget:
Navigate to Dashboard Configuration
Select the Car Admin row from the Dashboard Tabs grid
Search for 'car' in the Tab Widgets section
Toggle the Car Rate Configuration widget on

 

Step 3: Set up your EV mileage rates

Access the new rates configuration screen:
Navigation: Administrator Dashboard > Car Rates Configuration Widget > EV Mileage Rates.


Setting rates: 

Rates are configured by vehicle type (e.g., "Electric")
You can set different rates by company code and car ownership (private/company)
Each rate requires an effective date (when it comes into force)
Specify both the home charging rate and the away from home rate


Important considerations:

Rates where the company field is left blank apply to all companies unless overridden by a company-specific rate with a more recent effective date
You can edit or delete rates, though we recommend not modifying rates already in use
If you add an EV rate for a vehicle type that already has traditional threshold-based rates, you'll receive a confirmation warning
The system will use whichever rate (EV split or threshold) has the most recent effective date for a given vehicle type

 


​Step 4: Employee access

Once configured, employees will see the new field automatically:
Navigation: My Dashboard > Expense Report > New Expense Report > Add expense detail > Select mileage pay code
When creating a mileage claim for an electric vehicle, the Miles Charged Away from Home field will appear
This field only displays if there's a valid EV rate for the selected date range

 
​Technical changes

The solution includes updates to:

Calculation engine with automatic blended rate calculation
Portal input screens (desktop and mobile web)
Back office validation and warnings
Enhanced vehicle configuration supporting dual rate fields
Modified mileage entry interfaces


The calculated values are stored in the same fields used for existing threshold rates (mile_unit and mile_unit_rate on trip and claim detail tables), ensuring compatibility with existing Insight reports and audit processes.

 

 

Important validation rules

Employees must split mileage claims into separate items if the rate type changes during the trip period (e.g., if switching from threshold to EV split rates mid-journey)
Miles charged away from home cannot exceed total miles
The EV rate must be valid for the entire date range of the expense claim
If an EV rate is deleted, claims will automatically fall back to traditional threshold rates
Expense claims already submitted and processed for September and October will not have these split rates applied retrospectively. However, you can set the effective date as 1st September 2025, meaning any unsubmitted trips will automatically use the new rules when processed

 


​Mobile access

Initial release (6th November 2025): Full functionality available via mobile web browser
Native mobile app: Enhanced features will be available in late November or December 2025

 


​Further information

To have this feature enabled for your organisation, please raise a support ticket.
For technical queries or assistance with configuration, our support team is ready to help.

title: Expense job stuck at status 1
text:
When you process an expense run in Core Expense, you can confirm that the expense process has been completed by checking the job queue in back office.

 

To review the job status, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense, then click Tools.

Click Job Queue. 

From the Task Type drop-down menu, select Completed Tasks.

This will display all the completed expense processes and the back office user who completed each step. 

If the job Status field shows 2, then the job has been completed.

From the Task Type drop-down menu, select Uncompleted Tasks.

If the job Status field shows 1, then the job hasn't been completed.

If the  job status remains stuck at status 1 for more than five minutes, a locked object on the database causes this issue when the expense job is attempting to run. This occurs when a back office user accesses data required for the expense job to run, resulting in a lock on the database. 

 

The job will not be complete until the lock is resolved, which can be done by the back office user leaving the Core Expense screen or allowing their session to time out.

title: Checklist when comparing reports generating during Expense Run
text:
When doing an expense run, it is highly recommended that you compare the reports to ensure they match. 

 

To help you process your expense run from start to finish with the relevant reports, we've put together a checklist to ensure you're generating the relevant reports.

 

Expense Trip Enquiry - Approved

Before you can process the expense run, you need to generate an expense enquiry report. This will generate a report with all the trips that are to be processed in the current run. This report will be used as a reference for the following reports to be compared to. 

 

To do this, follow the below steps.

Click Expense Trip Enquiry, and on the expense group field, enter the expense group number in question.

Select the Approved checkbox, then clear other options from the status section.

Click Generate report.

 

 

Expense Trip Enquiry - Processed

After the Generate Payment Claims has been run, it is recommended to generate another enquiry report to compare the report with that of the approved expense trip enquiry report. 

Click Expense Trip Enquiry and on the expense group field enter the expense group number in question.

Select the Processed checkbox then clear other options from status section.

Click Generate report.

📌 Note: This figure can be slightly different from the approved figure in the approved expense report, if you have mileage claims processed. This has to do with the different mileage rates set up when employees go over a certain amount of kms.

 

Validation Report

Once Expense Run Validation has been run, a report will be generated in your browser. Compare this report to the previous reports and ensure totals match. 

 

 

Paypath/Timesheets Report

Once the Paypath/Timesheets have been run, a report will be generated in your browser. Compare this report to the previous reports and ensure totals match

📌 Note: If any of the reports don't match, don't continue the expense run until the difference has been found. Check that all trips and claims on the reports match.

title: Expense run process
text:
To help you complete the expense run from start to finish, we've put together everything you need to do in order.

 📌 Note: These are the general steps, part of the process depends on how you've configured your environment.

Expense enquiry report 

Before you can process the expense run, generate the expense enquiry report. To do this, follow the steps below in back office.

Click Core Expense, then click Enquiry.

Click Expense Trip Enquiry, then enter expense group number.

Select Approved and clear other options from status.

Under Report Settings, tick all boxes and click Generate Report.

Download the report and note the amount on the report.

To exit the screen, click the exit  icon.

 

 

Generate payment claims 

After generating the expense enquiry report, run the generate payment claims. To do this, follow the steps below in back office.

Click Core Expense, then click Input.

Click Generate Payment Claims.

Search for the relevant expense group, then click Submit Update. 

To save, click the save  icon.
Trips will move from status approved to processed.

Claim numbers will be generated for each trip ID.

Claim numbers will have a “HO” (hold) status.
​

To exit screen, click the exit  icon.

 

 

Expense trip enquiry processed report 

After processing the trips, generate the expense trip enquiry report again to confirm the amounts to be paid. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense, then click Enquiry.

Click Expense Trip Enquiry.

In the expense group field, enter the expense group number in question.

Select the Processed checkbox, then clear other options from status section.

Click Generate report.

📌 Note: This figure can be slightly different from the approved figure in the approved expense report, if you have mileage claims processed. This has to do with the different mileage rates setup when employees go over certain amount of kms.

To exit screen, click the exit  icon.

 

 

Approval processing - approve claims on hold

Before you can process the expense run validation, you'll need to approve the claims at hold to change the status of the claims. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense, then click Input.

Click Approval Processing.

In the expense group field, enter the relevant expense group number.

Clear all options except the Hold status and press Tab on your keyboard.

Check the figure if this corresponds with the figure in the processed expense trip enquiry report. 

In the relevant claim, click Approve.

Alternatively, to approve multiple claims at once, select the claims and click Bulk Approval.

Click the save  icon.

 

 

Expense run validation 

This validates the claim and creates the validation report for comparison against the expense trip enquiry processed report. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense, then click Update.

Click Expense Run Validation. 

Adjust the cheque and bank processing dates to the desired dates.

Search for the relevant expense group, then select Submit Update check box.

Check the number of claims and the total value.

Click Run Validation.

📌 Note: Depending on how your environment is configured, you will need to either process the generate timesheet or paypath file and send it to PeopleXD Payroll.

 

Generate timesheet

Once you're happy with the figures on the reports, before you generate the timesheets to payroll you need to review and approve them in PeopleXD Expense.  
Before you follow the steps below, you need to check:

The expense run validation must be complete. 

Only transactions with a pay method of ‘SP’ are processed with timesheets.

The pay method for the expense group:

In back office, click Core Expense.

Click Reference, then click Reference D-L.

Click Expense Group, then click Pay Method.

Once the above information has been confirmed, follow the below steps.

Click Core Expense, then click Update.

Click Generate Timesheets.

To preview a copy of the data, click Generate Report.

To transfer the timesheet to payroll for the relevant expense group, click Submit. 

Click OK.

 

 

Create paypath details

Once you're happy with the figures on the reports, create the bank file to transfer to payroll. To do this, follow the steps below in back office.

Click Core Expense, then click Update.

 Click Create Paypath Data.

In the company code field, enter the company number. 

Press Tab on your keyboard through the fields and information will be displayed. 

Click Browse, then select a location to store the bank file. 

Select the appropriate bank, from the Bank Name dropdown.

Click Create.

 

 

Complete cheque update 

To mark all claims as paid and roll the expense run forward, complete the cheque update. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense, then click Update.

Click Complete Check Update. 

In the expense group field, enter the relevant expense group number.

Press Tab on your keyboard.

Check that the run number is correct and click OK.

 

 

Interface processing

To close the expense run and move to the next run number, run the interface processing. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense, then click Update.

Click Interface Processing.

In the expense group field, enter the expense group number.

In the Run Number field, enter the run number.

If you need to run files for previous years, change the run number. 

Click OK, then click the save  icon.

title: Payments by company have a status of processed and not paid
text:
If an expense claim still shows as PROCESSED after the expense run it was included in has been finalized, this is because the claims are set as Payment by Company.
​
When claims are set to Payment by Company, it means that payment was made using a company credit card and the claimant will not be reimbursed for any expenses. Claims will show a value of 0.00 because the claimant is not receiving reimbursement, so the system does not recognize a payment being made. This is why the status of the expense claims remains PROCESSED.
​
If all the expense items on the report are marked as 'Paid by Company', the status will not move past PROCESSED. If the expense had a few items and only one of them was ' set to Paid by Company' rather than all items, then that one line would stay as '0' and the trip would get to PAID.

title: Duplicate expense detection
text:
To configure the duplicate expense detection and alerts to indicate its a duplicate claim, follow the steps below in back office.

Go to Back Office, then Core Expense.

Click Reference S-Z, then System Parameters.

Click Common, under duplicated items, tick the following alerts you'd like to setup.

Duplicate detection: Checks for duplicates if enabled.

Duplicate expenses allowed: Allows user to enter duplicates but a reason must be provided on the portal screen. If set to N then users cannot enter a duplicate.

Duplicate based on cost centre: Checks if the dates, expense code and cost centre are all identical on more than one trip item line.

Duplicate based on dates: Checks if the dates and expense code are identical on more than one trip item line for the current claimant.

Duplicate based on time: Checks if the dates, expense code and times are identical on more than one trip item line for the current claimant.

Duplicate based on AC1: Checks if the dates, expense code and analysis code 1 are identical on more than one trip item line for the current claimant.

title: Error: FRM-41214 Unable to run report
text:
It is possible that the reason the error message displays on the expense run validation detail screen is that the process has been run already.
​
To confirm, check the following.

In Back Office, click CoreExpense.

Click Tools, then click Process Logs.

Search for the expense group and current run number to see the expense process that has been carried out.

The following processes should appear on the process log:

Submitted EXP4000 - This is displayed when the generate payment claims is run.

Validation Complete - This is displayed when the validation run process is run. 

Paypath Generated  - This is displayed after running the create paypath data process.

text:
If an error message appears when you attempt to set up a claimant, this is because the claimant is missing a scale code. To resolve this, follow the steps below in back office.

title: Upload P11D CSV details
text:
To perform bulk changes to employees’ P11D details, you can populate and upload a predefined CSV format file with your information. 
​
​Note:

Populate the sections column for every entry. 

Configure your computer to use a comma as a list delimiter. 

Populate the car number in column 32 AF with 1 for one car. You can't leave this blank. If an employee has a second car, enter 2 and so on in sequential order.

On the paper-based reports, you can see the cars numbers in the final column. In the paper or portal P11D, odd number cars show in the Car1 column and even numbers in the Car2 column.

Include descriptions in sections A, B, L, M, or N. 

Section A through to N is fully loadable for P11D purposes using one of the predefined CSV formats.

Load CSV file

To load the CSV file, follow the steps below in back office.

Click Core Expense then click Input.

Click P11D then click Load P11D Details.

 Select Upload P11D Data from External Source.

Fill the following fields:

Company 

Tax Year

Employee Number: For all employees, leave this blank.

Click Browse then select the CSV file from the file location.

Click OK. A PDF report is generated.

If errors exist, you can view these in the exception report.

You need to amend the incorrect records in the CSV file and repeat the above process until no errors exist to ensure your data is intact.

If no errors exist, no report is produced. This indicates the data has been successfully loaded.

View loaded data

To view the data you loaded in Core Expense, follow the steps below in back office. 
​Note: The data source for the uploaded data will be listed as UPLOAD on the Create/Maintain P11D Details screen.

Click Core Expense then click Input.

Click P11D then click Create/Maintain P11D Details.

Tips
Rule
	
Details



Load  

	

You can upload CSV files multiple times.




Each time you upload a company file, it overwrites the previously uploaded company file.

	

 




You can make corrections to the CSV file, and repeat the upload process.  

	

 




You keep the historical data in the system by year. For example, when you upload a 2022 data file, you can still view the 2021 CSV data.

	

 




Data

	

When populating G2 or G3 on the CSV file, use the cash equivalent field in column six.




Cash equivalent for van and cash equivalent van fuel should be separate records.

	

 




Section M valid XML transfer values are:

Class 1A items: M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, M9.

Non-qualifying Class 1A items: M10, M11, M12, M13, M14, M15.

But if these don't exist then M3 Tax Paid is mandatory. This is the same field for the existing paper solution.

	

 




The data in these files follow the HMRC Test Information: PAYE internet submissions, expenses and benefits: schema 2020 to 2021

	

 


​

title: Company car available from date disappearing from car administration centre
text:
When you process your Year End Rollover in Core Expense, if the company car's 'Available From' date disappears in the car administration center, this is because the car Available From date has been manually updated. 
​
When processing your Year End Rollover, the following car BIK values reset: 

Available From (available_from).

Days car unavailable(days_car_unavailable).

Dates Free Fuel Provided(dates_free_fuel_prov). 

Once you complete the Expense Year End, the system will always clear out the Available From date when no 'Available To' date is populated. The system will automatically set the Available From date to the start of the new tax year, eliminating the need for manual input at the beginning of each new tax year.
​
For the 'Available To' date, it will not be cleared out during the Expense Year End. If there is an existing Available To date, this indicates that the car has been returned on that date and the record is complete. A new Available To date should only be provided once the car is returned. A new record can be created when the car is available again by updating the Vehicle Cash Equivalent.

title: Upload a new expense policy document
text:
If you have a new expense policy, to upload this into PeopleXD Expense, you need to update the new file name parameter.
​
If your document is stored online, you can use the online link. If your document is stored locally, raise a case online so the support team can upload it to the server. Once they've done this, they'll provide the file name.
​
To update the parameter with the new expense policy, follow the steps below in portal. 

From the dashboard menu, click Administrator Dashboard.

Click Site Manager, then click Admin Settings.

In the Search field, enter the relevant parameter:

ex_submit_trip_decl_doc: This is the document the claimant sees when submitting an expense item.

cp_my_appterms_doc_trip: This is the document the approver sees when approving an expense item.

cp_my_appterms_doc_car: This is the document used for My Approval Car and Vehicle widget.

cp_my_vat_doc: This is the VAT document the claimant sees when submitting an expense. In your environment, this may not be used. 

Click Edit, then enter the online link or file name from the support team as required.

📌 Note: If the support team uploaded your document, you need to enter /coredocs/ followed by the exact file name.

Click OK.

📌 Note: If the new document doesn't appear straight away, we recommend clearing your browser cache.

title: Create an expense proxy claimant in portal
text:
Proxy claimants are claimants who create trips on behalf of other claimants. To set up an expense proxy claimant in portal, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Click Data Center, then click Reference Data.

In the search field, search for Organisational Role Types.

Click Add and insert a new record with the following:

Role Type: EXPTR

Description

Approval Group: HR

Active ticked

ESS approver ticked 

Questionnaire access: None

No Delegation ticked

Click Save.

Return to the Data Centre, click People Management.

From the dropdown menu, select View All.

Under Employee Administration, select Maintain Organizational roles per Person. 

In the Personnel No field, select the relevant employee number. 

To create a new role, click Add, then fill in the following details:

From the Role drop-down menu, select the newly created Proxy role

Org Group: WRKGRP . Depending on clients approval process this could be department or cost centre etc

Date from: Date applicable from

Org Group item: i.e. Work group. cost centre department etc

To save this, click Save. 

Return to the dashboard menu Administrator Dashboard then click Site manager. 

Click Admin Settings.

In the Search field, search for exptr_org.

Two parameters will appear with a name exptr_org_role and exptr_org_group.

exptr_org_group: The field is set to either WRKGRP or COST or the organisational group that you've set for your approval process

exptr_org_role : The field is set to the new role EXPTR

 

 

Create new profile

To assign menu access to the newly created proxy claimant, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, select Security.

Click Menu Profile, then click Create New Profile.

In the Code field, enter a code for the new profile.

In the Description field, enter a new menu profile Core_Proxy_Portal. 

Click OK. 

Return to Menu Profile, then in the search field, search for Core_Proxy_Portal

Click the three-doticon, then select Manage Menu Options.

Search for the following menu options, then enable the active toggle:

CorePortal - Administrator Dashboard

CorePortal - Administrator Expense update

CorePortal - Employee Expense Update

CorePortal - Employee expense view

Widget - Expense - Administrator Update

 

 

Assign menu profile

To assign the proxy claimant menu profile to an employee, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, select Security.

Click User Management.

In the Search field, search for the employee.

Click the three-doticon, then select Manage Account.

Select Menu Profiles. 

In the Search field, search for the new menu profile Core_Proxy_Portal.

Set menu profile to active. 

📌 Note: If you've not migrated to portal, to set up a proxy claimant follow the back office steps.

title: 2026/27 Tax year changes
text:
As part of the UK expense year end software release, we've made the following software changes.

 

 

Car benefits charge

The car benefit charge is based on the BIK rates for 2026/27. This value may vary where:

The car was unavailable for at least 30 consecutive days.

You were providing fuel for private use but stopped doing this.

Car fuel benefit charge 

The car fuel benefit charge for the 2026/27 tax year rate is £29,200 which calculates based on the appropriate percentage from BIK rates for 2026/27 multiplied by the fixed figure of £29,200.
​
You can reduce the car fuel cash equivalent if:

The employee can't use the car for 30 days in a row.

The employee pays you back for all their private fuel.

You stopped providing fuel during the tax year.

 

 

Van benefit charge

The van benefit charge for the 2026/27 tax year rate is £4,170. You can reduce the van cash equivalent if:

The employee can't use the van for 30 days in a row.

The employee pays you to use the van privately.

Other employees use the van. In this scenario, divide £4,170 by the number of employees.

Van benefit charge zero emissions

Since April 2021, there has been no van benefit charge for vans that produce zero carbon emissions. 

 

Van fuel benefit charge

The van fuel benefit charge for the 2026/27 tax year rate is £798. You can reduce this if:

The employee can't use the van for 30 days in a row.

The employee pays you back for all their private fuel.

You stopped providing fuel during the tax year.

 

Check the Vehicle Cash Equivalent and Vehicle Fuel Cash Equivalent values.

 

 

P11D changes
New P11D Schema for 2025/26

The P11D Schema has updated to reflect the 2025/26 changes. These schema updates linked to the expense tax year are automatically handled within the system.


Section F

Data Item 46. Change to date in title from 2024/25 to 2025/26.

Data Item 47. Change to date in title from 2024/25 to 2025/26.


Section H

Data Item 53. Change to date in title from 5 April 2024 to 5 April 2025.

Data Item 54. Change to date in title from 5 April 2025 to 5 April 2026.

Data Item 55. Change to dates in title and business rules from 5 April 2024 and 5 April 2025 to 5 April 2025 and 5 April 2026.

Date Item 56. Change to dates in title from 5 April 2024 and 5 April 2025 to 5 April 2025 and 5 April 2026.

Data Item 57. Change to date in title from 2024/25 to 2025/26.

Data Item 58. Change to date in title from 2024/25 to 2025/26

Class 1A NIC rate

The Class 1A NIC rate is now 15.0%. Manually update it after processing the year-end cleardown. If generating a P11D for the previous tax year, revert the rate to 13.80%.  
​
To update the Class 1A NIC rate, follow the steps in the relevant section.


Portal

To update the NIC rate, follow the steps below. 

From dashboard menu, click Payroll Dashboard.

Click Settings then click General.

Click System configuration.

Click General then click P11D.


Back Office

To update the NIC rate, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePay then click Update.

Click Utilities then click System configuration.

Click General then click P11D.

P11D(b) only

For sites who need to generate a P11D(b) only, review these steps to generate a P11D(B) XML file.

title: Payrolling benefits meaning (UK)
text:
When you payroll benefits, you account for the tax on benefits provided to employees through the PAYE system by adding notional pay to the employees’ taxable income.  

The benefits you payroll are benefits in kind (BIK).

If intending to payrolling benefits including vehicle BIK, register your intention to do so with HMRC before the start of the new tax year.

Give your employees a letter explaining that you’re payrolling benefits, and what it means for them.

Payrolling benefits and expenses remove the need to submit a form P11D. 

You need to work out the class 1A national insurance contributions on the cash equivalent notional value and return a form P11D(b).

If you choose to payroll company car benefits, you don't need to submit a form P46(Car). The PeopleXD system doesn't currently support the production of a P46 car return.

You can payroll all benefits except: 

Employer provided living accommodation. 

Interest-free and low-interest beneficial loans. 

📌 Note: You need to report these benefits on a P11D, even if you’re payrolling other benefits for the same employees.

title: Generate P11D(B) XML file only (UK)
text:
To generate the P11D(b) file, you don't need to submit a P11D for an employee if you’re already paying tax on all their benefits through your payroll. However, you still need to submit P11D(b) to pay any Class 1A National Insurance.

 

To do this, follow the steps below in Back Office. 

 

 

Pay codes

Before you generate the P11D(b) file, check that the pay codes are configured correctly. To do this, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePay, then click References. 

Click Pay Codes.

In the Pay Code field, to select a pay code, click the LOV  icon.

Under the General Tab, edit the P11D section.

In the P11D Section Field, to select a section, click the LOV  icon.

If the employer incurred the cost of the benefit, enable the Cost to You checkbox.

To save this, click the save  icon. 

You should not extract benefits from payroll by compiling your data or uploading P11 data from external source using the following screen.

Click Core Expense, then click Input.

Click P11,D then click Load p11D details.

Also, we advise you not enter data manually using the screen below.

Click Core Expense, then click Input.

Click P11D, then click Create/Maintain P11D.

📌Note: If records exist with the source "COMPILE" we need to clear this data for the current year. To accomplish this, please raise a new case with support, referencing this article, and provide the following details:

Company Number 

P11D Year/ Tax Year.

 

 

Generate P11D(b) XML file

After checking the pay codes, generate your P11D/P11D(b) XML file. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Core Expense then click Update.

Click Generate P11D.

From the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Generate EXB files.

The file type should be EXB.

Under the Live/Test Run section, select either Live or Test.

In the company field, to select the relevant company code, click the LOV icon.

In the P11D Year field, enter the tax year i.e. Start Year – For 2023/2024, enter ‘2023’

Press Tab on your keyboard. 

To select a location to save the file, click Browse.

Click OK.

A window pop-up displays 'There are no P11d records to be processed' 

Click OK.

📌 Note: Your P11D/P11D(b) XML file saves to your chosen location. The file will contain your P11D(b) without displaying employee P11D data.

 

 

P11D(B) Adjustments

After generating your P11D(b) XML file, review your P11D(b) figure and make any necessary adjustments. To do this, follow the steps below. 

Click Core Expense then click Update.

Click Generate P11D.

From the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Generate EXB files.

Under the Live/Test Run section, select either Live or Test.

In the company field, to select the relevant company code, click the LOV 

 icon.

In the P11D Year field, enter the tax year.

Leave the Employee Ref field blank then click P11D(B) Adjustments.

Adjust the following fields:

Box B: Add any amount not included in the box A on which Class 1A NICs are due. 

Box C: Deduct any amounts included in the box A on which Class 1A NICs are not due.
