title: Exception report for P11D
text:
To understand the exception messages on the exception report for P11D, read the causes and take the actions in the table below:

Issues
	
Cause
	
Action



Fuel type must be A, D, or F

	

HMRC only expect a single character of either A, D, or F.
​
Incorrect values exist on the load file which include spaces. For example:,D , or ,D  , instead of ,D.

	

Remove space and regenerate the data load file. 




Middle name contains a 
space. 

	

HMRC doesn't accept two names for an employee’s middle name. For example, the middle name Anthony Patrick.  

	

Enter a ahyphen or remove space and regenerate the file.




Section I Cash Equivalent needs to equal the Cost 
Amount less the Amount Made Good. 

	

The basic cash equivalent formula is the cost to the employer of providing the benefit including VAT minus the amount made good by the employee out of their net pay.

	

Enter the correct values and regenerate the file.




List Price must be less than 
£1000 

	

Some issues may not have a direct visual resolution. In this case, a blank record was created with no accompanying data leading to a data issue. 

	

Delete the record and regenerate the file.

title: Load digital certificates for Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR)
text:
Individuals, companies, agents, and other entities need the ROS Digital Certificate to access online services for business taxes. 
​
Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) is an additional permission under the employer ROS certificate. Revenue is automatically applying these ERR permissions to the employer certificate, and you can assign them to any sub certificate.

📌 Note: To assign ERR to a sub certificate, you need to do this in your ROS permissions screen. For support with this, please contact Revenue.

If you use PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense as standalone products with different databases, upload the ERR digital cert in both PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense. If you keep PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense on the same database, you only need to upload the ERR digital cert in PeopleXD Payroll.

 

 

Upload ERR digital certificates

To upload the ERR digital certificates in PeopleXD Expense, follow the steps below.

📌 Note: You need to download the digital cert from ROS before you can follow these steps. The file extension must be .p12 otherwise PeopleXD Expense can't find the file.

Click Expense, then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Double-click 05 - Load Digital Certificate.

In the Expense Company field, enter the company code.

From the drop-down menu, select the relevant company tax registration.

Enter the certificate password from ROS, then click Browse.

Select the ERR digital certificate file from your computer.

Click Load Certificate, then repeat these steps for all companies.

Once you've done this, you need to configure the rest of the parameters for ERR.

title: Claimant parameters for Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR)
text:
Before you can generate and transfer your ERR report to revenue, you need to configure some parameters in PeopleXD Expense. One of those parameters is the Claimant parameter.
​
To update claimant/employee parameters, follow the steps below in back office.

Click CoreExpense then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Double-click 03 - Claimant Parameters.

Update the relevant  fields:

Claimant

Exclude Claimant: Enable the checkbox to exclude a claimant from an expense ERR return. If the employee is to be excluded from a Payroll ERR return, this needs to be completed on the ERR Employee Parameters screen in Payroll.

Company Tax Registration: This is used to input a Company Tax Registration Number Override. If filled out, this TRN will take precedence for the claimant over the TRN at the expense company level.

Employment ID: This is used to record an override for the Employment ID, which may be necessary when submitting ERR returns for a different employment ID than the one currently held by the revenue.

Note: It is important to check that the Company Reg Number Override field is maintained when managing Company Tax Registration Numbers on a claimant level.


Once you've done this, you need to configure the rest of the parameters for ERR.

title: Check ERR Run
text:
If you've submitted multiple Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submission files for the same period, we recommend you run the Check ERR Run process.

This requests the overall ERR totals for that period, for you to reconcile. 
​
To run the Check ERR Run process, follow the steps below in back office.

Click Expense, then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

From the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Check ERR Run.

From the Company Tax Registration drop-down menu, select the relevant company.

In the Run Reference field, enter the run reference, then click Browse.

Choose where you want to generate the file, then click Check Expense Run.

Click OK.

When the Check ERR Run response file generates, each expense has one of the following statuses:

Completed - all valid expenses: All expenses successfully validated. The process is complete.

Completed - invalid expenses: There are some errors in the expenses. You can check these on the json file that generates. You need to make any necessary corrections in PeopleXD Payroll then generate and transfer a new ERR file to Revenue. 

Pending: Awaiting validation at Revenue.

title: Transfer the (ERR) file to Revenue
text:
In every expense run where you've processed ERR qualifying payments, you need to report the values to Revenue on or before the date you pay the employees.
​
Once you've generated the file in PeopleXD Expense, to transfer it to Revenue, follow the steps below in back office.

Click Expense, then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

From the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Transfer Submission Files.

In the Expense Company field, enter the relevant expense company code.

For each relevant expense group, select the Transfer File check box.

Click Browse, then choose where you want to save the file.

Click Transfer, then click OK.

Revenue then responds to the transfer, and the Status column shows one of the following:

Acknowledged: Revenue successfully received the transfer.

Rejected: Revenue rejected the file. The rejection reason also appears in the Status column.

Pending: You've transferred the file to Revenue, however, they haven't processed it yet.

📌 Note: If the status is Pending, to request an update from Revenue, click Run Check. You shouldn't re-generate and attempt to transfer the submission file again.

If you've transferred multiple submission files for the same period, for example, an original submission and a correction submission, we recommend you also complete a Check ERR Run process.

 

 

Confirm transfer

Once you've transferred the file and completed the Check ERR Run process, you need to confirm the transfer. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

From the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Transfer Submission Files.

In the Expense Company field, enter the relevant expense company code.

For the relevant submission, select the Confirmed check box.

Click Save, then click Yes.

title: Generate a full resubmission ERR file
text:
If you've amended the pay date for an employee, after you've already submitted the ERR file to Revenue, you need to generate a Full Resubmission File. You can generate the file at expense group or Employee level. To do this, follow the steps below in back office.

📌 Note: The Full Resubmission File only includes any amendments you've made since Revenue accepted your normal ERR file for that period. If you haven't already submitted a normal file, instead of following the steps below you need to submit a normal file either for the current period or the relevant previous period.

 

Current period

To generate a Full Resubmission File for the current period, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

From the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Generate Submission File.

From the Submission Type drop-down menu, select Full Resubmission.

Enter the relevant expense group code.

In the Company Tax Reg Number field, either:

Leave it blank: This generates an output file for all company TRNs with associated employees within the expense group.

Select a company TRN: This generates one file for the TRN you select.

If required, to generate the file for an individual employee, enter their employee reference in the Claimant field.

If required, in the Override Payment Date field, enter a date, then click OK.

 

 

Previous period

To generate a Full Resubmission file for a previous period, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Update.

Click Enhanced Reporting Requirements.

Double-click 02 - Expense Group Parameters.

For the relevant expense group, select the Previous Run Number check box.

Click OK then, from the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu, select Generate Submission File.

From the Submission Type drop-down menu, select Normal Submission.

Enter the relevant expense group code.

In the Company Tax Reg Number field, either:

Leave it blank: This generates an output file for all company TRNs with associated employees within the expense group.

Select a company TRN: This generates one file for the TRN you select.

In the Claimant field, the relevant employee reference.

If required, in the Override Payment Date field, enter a date, then click OK.

title: Retrieve ERN
text:
The ERN provides non-payroll systems with the employment ID information Revenue holds on individual employees. 

 

You need to retrieve and upload ERNs if:

You don't have PeopleXD Payroll or

You have PeopleXD Payroll held on a different database to PeopleXD Expense.

📌 Note: You don't need to retrieve ERN if your PeopleXD Payroll and Expense share the same database. PeopleXD will automatically use the Employment ID from PeopleXD payroll for ERR. 

When you upload ERNs in PeopleXD Expense, this generates and uploads all employment IDs for new or existing employees within the company. To do this, follow each of the sections below in order.

 

Generate claimant ERN

To retrieve the latest ERNs, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference CC, then click Claimant Bulk ERN.

Under Load Claimant ERN Certificates, select Generate Claimant ERN.

From the Tax Register Number drop-down menu, select the relevant company.

Click Browse, then choose a location to save your file.

Click OK.

 

 

Retrieve ERNs from Revenue

After generating the ERN, retrieve the ERN file from Revenue. To do this, follow the steps below.

Log into ROS, then click Request ERN's by file upload.

Click Browse Files, then browse to the file you saved in the previous section.

Enter your password, then click Sign and Submit.

 

 

Upload Revenue response

After retrieving the ERN file from Revenue,  upload the response file. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Expense then click Reference.

Click Reference CC then click Claimant Bulk ERN.

Under Load Claimant ERN Certificates, select Upload Revenue Response.

Click Browse then select the Revenue response from your computer.

Click OK.

 

 

Maintain claimant ERN

To review the details of the latest ERNs you retrieved, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference CC, then click Claimant Bulk ERN.

Under Load Claimant ERN Certificates, select Maintain Claimant ERN.

 

 

Update ERN details

Once you retrieve ERNs from Revenue, you need to update the claimants' records with the latest information. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference CC, then click Claimant Bulk ERN.

Under Load Claimant ERN Certificates, select Update ERN Details.

From the Tax Register Number drop-down menu, select a company.

Click OK.

 

 

Cleardown records

If you run multiple ERN retrieval requests without completing the update employee ERN details process, to remove any duplicates, you can use the Cleardown Records option. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Expense, then click Reference.

Click Reference CC, then click Claimant ERN.

From the Tax Register Number drop-down menu, select a company.

Click Cleardown Records, then click OK.

Once you've done this, you need to complete the steps under the Update ERN details section of this article.

There may be times when you need to override an employee’s retirement age, for example, to reflect a contractual agreement, a change in retirement plans, or a correction to previously entered data. 

 

To do this in PeopleXD Pension, follow the steps below in back office.

 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance. 

Click Employee Pension Details.

📌Note: If you can't access the Employee Pension Details screen, you need to activate the menu option.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee reference number.

Press Tab on your keyboard then click Edit.

Click the next  icon three times to get to the fourth page.

In the Retirement Date field, enter the relevant date.

Click the save  icon.

title: Correct an employee's pension benefit scheme
text:
If you've accidentally set an employee up under the incorrect single pension scheme (SPS) and they've made contributions towards it, to correct this, you need to move them to the correct scheme and make single scheme adjustments to transfer the pension values.
​

To do this, follow the steps below in back office.

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Single Scheme Adjustment Centre.

Click Adjustments tab then fill in the following fields: 

Employee Reference.

Payroll Period: The date the employee should have started on SPS.

Pay Code.

Pensionable Pay.

Pensionable Remuneration: CSP to 0.

Pay Multiplier: Check is set to 1.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon.

Regenerate the employee pension benefits.

If the employee has been on the incorrect SPS for multiple tax years, to ensure the contributions are reflected in their pension benefits, you need to repeat this process for the first period of each year that they were on the incorrect SPS.

title: Transfer an employee's pension scheme
text:
If you need to move an employee onto a different single pension scheme (SPS), follow the steps in each of the sections below, in back office.

 

Add an end date 

To add an end date to the day an employee joined the SPS, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Employee Details.

In the Employee Ref. field, enter the employee number.

Select Maintain Employee Pension Details. 

In the Pension End Date field, enter the end date for the SPS.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon. 

 

 

Generate a pension benefit statement

To generate a pension benefit statement at the end date of the SPS, follow the steps below.

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Generate Employee Pension Benefits.

Fill in the following fields: 

Employee Ref: Leave blank if generating employee benefits for all employees

Pension Scheme: To select a pension scheme, click the list  icon.

Calculation date: The date the pension benefit will be based on.

Click OK then click the exit icon.

Click Maintenance then click Single Scheme Adjustment Centre.

Click the Adjustments tab then enter the values generated in step 2.

Adjust contributions, setting the superannuation refund paycode to zero.

Adjust pensionable pay to zero by work pattern.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon. 

Click Maintenance then click Employee Pension Details.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee number.

Press Tab on your keyboard. 

In the End Date field, enter the scheme leave date.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon. 

Click Maintenance then click Record Pension Option.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee number.

Press Tab on your keyboard. 

In the Pension Scheme field, enter the pension scheme code.

In the Retirement Date field, enter the date generated in step 2.

From the Chosen Pension Option drop-down menu, select the relevant option.

Press Tab on your keyboard then check the benefits data is correct.

If required, set the Lump Sum and Pension override fields to zero.

If required, click Text then enter a memo relating to this calculation.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon. 

 

 

Check the start date

To check the start date of the SPS is correct, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Employee Details.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee reference number.

Press Tab on your keyboard then click Maintain Employee Pension Details.

Check the start date is correct.

To exit the screen, click the exit  icon.

 

Check the employee pensionable appointments

To check the employee's pensionable appointment date, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance. 

Click Employee Appointments.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee reference number.

 Press Tab on your keyboard then check the appointment dates shown.

To exit the screen, click the exit  icon.

 

Generate a new pension statement

To generate a new pension statement for the employee, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance,

Click Generate Employee Pension Benefits.

Fill in the following fields: 

Employee Ref.

Pension Scheme.

Calculation date.

Click OK.

title: Process a pension refund
text:
If you need to refund an employee's pension contributions, for example, because they're exiting the single pension scheme (SPS), you need to generate a pension benefit statement on the date they're leaving the scheme and after they've left the scheme.

 

To do this, follow the steps in each section below, in back office.

 

Generate a pension benefit statement

First, you need to generate a pension benefit statement on the date the employee is leaving the SPS.

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Generate Employee Pension Benefits.

Fill in the following fields:

Employee Ref: Leave blank if generating employee benefits for all employees

Pension Scheme: To select a pension scheme, click the list  icon.

Calculation date: The date the pension benefit will be based on.

Click OK then click the exit icon.

Click Maintenance then click Single Scheme Adjustment Centre.

Click the Adjustments tab then enter the values generated in step 2.

Adjust contributions, setting the superannuation refund paycode to zero.

Adjust pensionable pay to zero by work pattern.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon.

 

 

Generate a new pension benefit statement

Once the employee has left the pension scheme, you need to generate a new pension benefit statement for them, to reflect their final pension details based on their exit date.

📌Note: You need to run the calculation using the same date you're processing the refund. This ensures the employee becomes dormant in the Pension module and is excluded from future calculations.

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Generate Employee Pension Benefits.

Enter the relevant data, ensuring the pensionable pay and contributions are zero.

Click Maintenance then click Employee Pension Details.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee number. 

Press Tab on your keyboard.

In the End Date field, enter the pension leave date.

Click the save  icon then click the exit  icon.

Click Maintenance then click Record Pension Option.

In the Employee Reference field, enter the employee number. 

Under Chosen Pension Option, select Refund of Contributions. 

Check the benefits are correct. 

If required, click Text then enter a memo.

To save this, click the save  icon.

title: Cease purchasing of notional service before the maturity date
text:
If an employee decides to stop purchasing the notional service before its maturity date and this results in an inaccurate benefit statement being generated, there are a couple of possible reasons for this occurrence. For example:

No employee pension benefits were generated on the date they completed paying for notional service.

In the Maintain Employee Notional Service screen, no new row was entered.

To resolve the issue causing the incorrect benefit statement, follow the steps below in back office. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Generate Employee Pension Benefits.

Enter the required data on the following fields: 

Employee Ref: Leave blank if generating employee benefits for all employees.

Pension Scheme: To select a pension scheme, click the list  icon.

Calculation date: Enter the calculation date of when the purchase of the notional service was ceased.

Click OK then to exit screen, click the exit  icon.

Click Maintenance then click View Employee Pension Benefits.

In the Employee Ref field, enter the employee number.

Press Tab on your keyboard then select View Benefit Details.

To expand Accrued Benefit (Pension), click the  icon.

Take note of the amount for Gross Notional Service.

To exit screen, click the exit  icon.

Click Maintenance then click Employee Notional Service.

To enter a new row, click the add  icon and fill the following fields.

Employee reference number 

Pension Scheme 

Years: Enter the gross notional service figure.

Grant Date and Maturity Date: Date the notional service was ceased. 

Enter the actuarial code for lump sum reduction and pension reduction to pull in the tables corresponding to the Pension Actuarial Rates. 

Select the Conf. and Dep. check box for this new row. 

Clear the Conf. and Dep. check box for the previous row that had been entered.

To save this, click the save  icon.

title: Incorrect pension contribution on the benefit statement
text:
If you've run the employee pension benefit and notice that the pension contribution values are incorrect, this is caused by a mismatch between the Employee Pension Benefit Details screen and the View Pension Benefit Details screen. 

 

To resolve this, you need to check which pay codes were included in the contribution calculation then assign the correct ones.

 

View pay codes

To view which pay codes were used to calculate the incorrect contributions on the View Pension Benefit Details screen, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then Reference.

Click Pension Reference Data.

In the Pension Scheme field, click the list  icon.

Select the required pension scheme then click OK.

From the Reference Option drop-down menu, select 08 - Scheme Contribution.

Check that the pay codes here match those in CorePay.

To exit screen, click the exit  icon.

 

 

Assign pay codes

To resolve the incorrect pension contribution displayed on the employee benefit statement, assign the pay codes. To do this, follow the steps below.

Click CorePension then Reference.

Click Pension Reference Data.

In the Pension Scheme field, click the list  icon.

Select the required pension scheme then click OK.

From the Reference Option drop-down menu, select 08 - Scheme Contribution.

To delete all non-pension scheme pay codes, highlight the scheme code.

Click the delete  icon.

Insert all pension pay codes applicable to the single pension scheme.

To add a code, click the add  icon. 

Enter a new scheme code and scheme description.

Click the save  icon.

🤓Tip: We recommend you generate a new pension benefit statement to show the correct values.

title: Reasons for incorrect pension benefits
text:
There are several reasons why your pension benefits might be incorrect. To help you resolve this, we've put together a list of possible reasons below 👇
​

Joining and end dates 

You should first check that the date of joining and pension end date are entered correctly, depending on whether the employee is active on the scheme. To check this, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Employee Details then click Pension Details.

If the dates are correct, move on to the next section.

 

 

Employee's appointments

Next, you should check the employee appointments. To do this, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click Employee Details then click Employee Appointments.

Check all fields are correct.

Check that the appointment is set as pensionable or non-pensionable, as required.

If the appointment details are correct, move on to the next section.

 

 

Retirement date override

Lastly, you should check if the retirement date has been overridden, and check that the retirement date doesn't conflict with other dates set up. 

 

For example, if an employee has a retirement date input for their 60th birthday, if they generate a statement for an age past 60, the benefits will result as 0.

Each paycode in the report has a drop-down called Allowance Category. One of the options in this dropdown is Salary. If you select Salary as the allowance category, the CSP amount automatically applies to that paycode for the relevant pay period.

 

You’ll see this reflected when you drill down into the benefit statement details for each employee.

title: Update the CSD method for pensioner uprating
text:
If you're thinking of updating the CSD methods for pensioner uprating, before making any changes, we strongly recommend taking time to fully understand the potential impact.

 

Updating these methods without a thorough review can lead to issues. For example, members may be recorded against one method and then start generating under a different one, which can cause confusion and data inconsistencies.

 

Correcting this kind of historical data can be complex, especially if it involves reversing previous records and redefining members.

 

If the CSD method needs to be updated because it’s incorrect, we highly advise involving a consultant from our Optimisation Services team. They can help assess the situation and guide you through any changes safely and effectively.

title: Add an employee's previous service to their benefit statement
text:
To add or modify an employee's previous service in an organisation, you need to adjust the values on the additional service history and remuneration adjustment screen. To do this, follow the steps below in back office. 

 

Modify the employee’s service history

To add an employee's previous service history in an organisation, follow the steps below.

Click Core Pension then click Maintenance. 

Click Employee Additional Service History.

In the employee reference field, enter the employee reference. 

Fill the following fields:

Start Date 

End Date 

Pension Scheme 

From the Type dropdown list, select the relevant option.

Tick Conf. indicator: If this isn't selected, then this service hasn't been confirmed and isn't reckoned in the calculation of pensionable service.  

Dep. Indicator: Activating this means that the appropriate dependence contributions have been made.

In the Text field, enter a text to describe the record details.

In the Position and Value (Transfer Value) field, enter any extra information.

In the Lump Sum Reduction field, if relevant, enter the value of the reduction.

To save, click the save  icon.   

 

                                                                                                          

Adjust the employee’s pension remuneration

An employee’s pension remuneration is calculated based on their pensionable salary and pensionable allowances, if they exist. A situation may arise where the pension remuneration calculated by the system is incomplete. To resolve this, follow the steps below. 

Click Core Pension then click Maintenance. 

Click Employee Pension Remuneration Adjustment.

In the employee reference field, enter the employee reference. 

Fill the following fields:

Pension Scheme

Pay Code: To identify the type of payment.

Effective Date and End Date: To determine the period of time the adjustment is effective.

Adjustment Value: The value of the pension remuneration adjustment. This can be a positive or negative value.

To save, click the save  icon.

title: Pension benefit statement displaying an incorrect referable amount
text:
If the referable amount on a pension benefit statement appears incorrect, it’s usually due to an issue with the employee’s pension record. This is most often an incorrect pension start date, or cases where an employee has left and rejoined the scheme without a refund being processed.

 

To check where the incorrect value originates, follow the steps below in back office.

Click CorePension then click Maintenance.

Click View Employee Pension Benefits.

In the Employee Ref. field, enter the employee number.

In the Pension Scheme field, enter the scheme number.

In the Calculation Date field, enter the calculation date.

Press Tab on your keyboard then click View Benefit Details.

If a field on the statement has a plus sign to the left, click this to expand it and check how the calculation was derived.

 

If you notice a negative contributory state pension or other unusual figures after checking the benefit details, review the employee’s record for inconsistencies and make any necessary corrections. Once the start date and refund information are accurate, the pension benefit statement should display the correct referable amount.

title: Error: 'Not permitted to generate benefits X years beyond last Banked date'
text:
If you see the above error message when you attempt to generate pension benefits for employees, this indicates the banked years have been reached. To determine the number of years set as the banked years for the single pension scheme in back office, follow the steps below.

📌Note: If you can't access the Pension System Parameters screen, you need to activate the menu option.

Click CorePension then click Pension System Parameters. 

Click Maintain System Parameters.

At the bottom of the screen, the Banked Years field shows the number of banked years.

 

You can only calculate pension benefits for a number of future years that’s equal to or less than the value in the Banked Years field. For example, if you set Banked Years to 20, you won’t see an error until 20 years after the last banked year. To avoid this error, you should increase the Banked Years value as needed.

title: Error: 'An unknown error has occurred' when using Pen Pension Person Merge view
text:
This error usually pops up when a report includes columns with numbers that aren’t formatted correctly. To resolve this, you need to convert those columns using a calculation and remove the original versions from the report so Insight can read the data properly.

 

Which columns can be calculated?

Allowed: Columns with purely numeric values, such as Current Salary and Pension Scheme.

Not Allowed:

Date fields, such as Date of Birth and Pension Start Date.

Mixed-type fields, such as Employee Code, which may contain both numbers and text.

 

 

Apply the calculation

Open the report in Edit Mode.

Click Add then click Calculation.

Enter the calculation name, this appears as the column header.

Select the relevant column.
​
For example, if you select Pension Scheme, the field populates with PECI_PEN_PENSION_PERSON_MERGE.PENSION_SCHEME.
​

In the Calculation Text field, enter the following calculation: 
​

to_number(nvl([instert column name from step 4], 0), '99,999,999.9999')

 

Save the calculation then remove the original column from the report.

Once you've done this, only the calculated version remains. 

⚠️Important: You need to repeat these steps for every numeric column in the report.

title: Merge fields display the incorrect value
text:
If you’ve generated a pension benefit statement but noticed that some merge fields are displaying incorrect or unexpected values, this usually indicates an issue with how the letter template and data source are linked. This can happen when the merge fields in your Microsoft Word letter don’t correctly match the headers in the data source that provides the pension information.

 

Before generating the pension benefit statement, make sure you create the correct data source and set up your letter template with the appropriate mail merge fields. Ensuring that each field matches between the data source and the letter template is essential for displaying accurate information.

 

Merge fields typically display incorrect values when they're linked to the wrong header in the data source. Any mismatched or incorrectly inserted merge fields will cause the wrong information to appear in the letter.

 

When editing your letter template in Microsoft Word, avoid renaming merge fields manually. If you need to change a field, delete the existing one and reinsert the correct field using the Insert Merge Field option. The same approach applies if you want to use the same merge field in multiple places; rather than copying and pasting with Ctrl + C, use Insert Merge Field each time you add it.

 

Using Insert Merge Field consistently helps ensure that each field connects correctly to the data source and prevents errors from appearing on the pension benefit statement.

title: Add collaborators to a conversation
text:
There may be times when you're speaking with our support team and want to loop in a colleague, similar to how you would CC someone into an email. For example, if the solution to your query needs input from your IT team. 

⚠️Important: When speaking with the support team via the Access Digital Assistant, only one user can participate in a conversation. If you add a collaborator, they can only participate via email.

 

Add a collaborator

To add a collaborator, just let the support agent you’re speaking with know and provide the person’s email address. The agent will then add them to the conversation on your behalf.

 

 

How this works

Once the support agent has added the collaborator to the conversation:

All participants will receive replies via email only.

When replying via email, participants can add or remove users to their replies in the same way you would for any email.

All replies will be threaded within the same conversation.

 

In-product experience

If you're the person who started the conversation via the in-product Access Digital Assistant:

You'll see a notification in your conversation whenever collaborators are added or removed from the conversation.

Any replies you send in-product are emailed to all other participants in the conversation, and the sender address appears as john.doe.onchat@examply.intercom-mail.com.

Only you will receive replies in-product.

 

Email experience

If you're a collaborator participating in the conversation via email:

You'll only receive replies via email.

You can add and remove participants from the conversation using the To and CC fields in your email.

In the email thread, the original user appears under an alias address. If anyone replies and removes that alias from the recipients, it creates a brand‑new email chain, so it’s important to keep the alias included.

title: Check whether PeopleXD is down
text:
Clear communication is essential, especially during high‑impact incidents or unexpected downtime. To keep our customers informed, we publish live service information on StatusHub, where you can track the real‑time status of your Access products. 

 

From StatusHub, you can: 

Register for product alerts, including new events, updates, and high‑priority incidents. 

Receive notifications about planned maintenance. 

View current and historical events in one place. 

Stay informed as we share root‑cause details and prevention measures. 

View your StatusHub dashboard 

To access and navigate the dashboard, follow the steps below.

Go to your StatusHub >

In the top right, to select your time zone, use the time zone  list.  

To see products that have had recent issues, select Show Affected Only. 

Statuses explained 

On your dashboard, you’ll see one of the following statuses for each day: 

 

 Service is operating normally. 

 Performance issues.

 Service disruption. 

 

For days with incidents, you may also see the following: 

One incident. 

Multiple incidents. 

Use the Calendar view 

By default, the dashboard shows a list of affected products. To see this information in a calendar view, under Service Details, click Calendar. 

 

 

View planned maintenance 

The dashboard includes a monthly Maintenance view, and you can move between months using the navigation arrows. If there’s planned maintenance for a specific date, a blue dot appears on that day. 

 

To see more details, select the date, then click the link at the top. From here, you can see full information about the timing, affected sites, and what work is involved. 

 

 

PeopleXD isn't showing as down, but isn't loading 

If StatusHub shows no issues but PeopleXD still isn’t loading, there may be a local environment issue. We recommend you try logging in using a different browser. 

 

If you see one of the following error messages, it may indicate an incorrect URL or a browser setting preventing the page from loading: 

400 Bad Request 

404 Not Found 

📌Note: If PeopleXD loads but is slow, this won't appear on StatusHub. 

 

 

Subscribe to alerts 

To register for StatusHub alerts, follow the steps below:  

Go to your StatusHub >

In the top-right, click Subscribe, then click Email. 

Enter your email address. 

Read and accept the terms and services. 

Click Next, then, under Customisations, select either: 

All services: You’ll get all service notifications for Access MLB products. 

Selected Services: Select the services most relevant to you.  

If required, select Only send me the minimum number of notifications. 

Click Save 

 

Unsubscribe from alerts 

To unsubscribe from alerts, follow the steps below.

🤓 Tip: If you’ve already received an email notification, simply open it, click Unsubscribe from these alerts, then click Email. 

Go to your StatusHub >

In the top-right, click Subscribe. 

Click Forgot your link?, then click Email.  

Enter your email address, then click Resend. 

Click Unsubscribe from these alerts, then click Email.

 

 

If PeopleXD is unavailable

In the rare event that PeopleXD becomes temporarily unavailable, you may not be able to access the in‑product Access Digital Assistant. During these instances, there’s no need to take any action; our teams will already be aware of the issue and actively working to restore full service as quickly as possible.

 

You can continue to monitor progress and updates on StatusHub, where we’ll share information as soon as it becomes available.

title: Support made simple in PeopleXD
text:
What to expect when you contact support

When you need help, your journey begins with the Access Digital Assistant. It guides you through answers, troubleshooting steps, and relevant help content, all designed to get you moving quickly and confidently.

 

If the Access Digital Assistant can’t resolve your issue, it will hand things over to our human support team.

⚠️Important: The Access Digital Assistant is available only to named support contacts within your company. If you aren’t a named contact, you may still see the assistant, but your experience may differ from what’s described here.

You can find the Access Digital Assistant for PeopleXD here 👇

 

 

What is the Access Digital Assistant?

The Access Digital Assistant provides quick, automated answers to help you resolve questions efficiently. It can guide you through troubleshooting steps, offer tailored suggestions, and surface relevant help content.

 

If the assistant can’t resolve your query, it will seamlessly pass the conversation to our human support team for more complex issues.

✨ Instant answers: Get immediate support for common questions.

📚 Direct help access: Jump straight to relevant help content.

🌙 Available 24/7: Get support whenever you need it.

🤝 Easy escalation: Move smoothly to human support when required.

📌Note: If you request to speak to the support team outside normal hours, the Access Digital Assistant will still pass your query to the team, and they'll respond as soon as they're back online.

 

 

Use the Access Digital Assistant
Via PeopleXD

To use the Access Digital Assistant within your PeopleXD site, watch the video or follow the steps below.

Use the assistant within the product you need help with; guidance is tailored.

Keep questions short and clear.

Rephrase or break down complex issues if needed.

Start a new conversation for unrelated topics.

Avoid overly specific, personal-data-focused queries.

Provide feedback

At the end of your conversation, the Access Digital Assistant will ask whether your question was answered. Your feedback helps us improve both the assistant and your overall support experience. It also ensures you’re routed to human support when needed.

 

 

Further support

Your Customer Success Plan determines which support channels are available to you:

Named support contacts on any Customer Success Plan level can use the Access Digital Assistant.

title: Update cookie policy
text:
We have introduced a comprehensive cookie consent management system in PeopleXD to ensure full compliance with EU and UK GDPR regulations. This feature gives users transparent control over their cookie preferences while maintaining compliance with data protection requirements. 

For the software to run correctly, you must accept all essential cookies.

To retain access to the Access Digital Assistant, you must enable the Intercom functional cookie.

📌​Note: You will be prompted to refresh your cookie options every 180 days or whenever we add or remove cookies from our list of vendors.

If you accidentally reject a cookie option, don’t worry, you can reselect it by following the steps below. The process varies depending on whether you use a standalone PeopleXD system or access it via Access Evo.

 

 

Standalone PeopleXD

Click your User Profile then click Cookie Preferences.

🤓Tip: The user profile is the circle icon in the top right corner of the screen. It usually contains your photo or initials.

Enable or disable your options as required, then click SAVE PREFERENCES.

 

 

PeopleXD within Access Evo

In the top right corner of the screen, click your name, then select My Settings.

In the left-hand menu, click Cookie Preferences.

📌Note: The resulting view displays top-level categories, such as Functional.​ 

Enable individual categories as required, then click the down-pointing chevron to expand the list of individual cookies.

Enable or disable individual cookies as needed, then, in the top right corner, click Save.

Click Save & Reload, then return to a PeopleXD tab to complete the refresh.

 

Frequently asked questions
What does this mean for users?

This does not change how we process or protect your data.

All users must provide one-time consent to use features that require non-essential cookies.

Consent preferences are stored for 6 months, after which the user will be prompted to confirm again.

These can be updated anytime via the user’s profile.

📌Note: Administrators do not need to take any action to deploy this feature and they cannot disable it.

 

Why is this being introduced now for PeopleXD?

Under EU and UK GDPR Regulations, we are required to ensure that users:

Know what cookies are being tracked when they use People XD.

Have the option to opt-out of non-essential cookies.

 

Are you tracking new cookies in PeopleXD?

No, there is no change to how PeopleXD uses cookies.

 

This recent update to include Cookie Consent Capture from users is to make clear the existing cookies that have always been captured and provides the option to opt-out of non-essential cookies when using People XD.

 

What essential website cookies are used for People XD?

These are used to remember preferences in the system e.g. authentication for session management.

 

What happens if i choose "required only" as my preference?

You will lose access to the following features which require Functionality Cookies:

Intercom which is used for Support Bot assistance in People XD.

Wootric for ad hoc user surveys.

There is no impact to features supported by the Essential Website Cookies.

 

Can I update my consent preferences for People XD? 

Yes, we will save your preference for a period of 6 months once you provide it.

 

You can change this preference at any time through the Cookie Preferences screen. Simply follow the steps outlined above, whether you are using a standalone PeopleXD system or accessing it via Access Evo.

 

If you are not seeing the Access Digital assistant it could be related to your cookie consent

title: How to troubleshoot an Insight error
text:
Resolving an Insight error begins with isolating the issue. Errors such as "ORA-01476: divisor is equal to zero" usually occur due to an Insight calculation not liking particular data being passed through to the calculation.
​ 

Identify the Problem

Identify the problem by isolating the column causing the error. To isolate the error, we recommend the following steps.

Run the original report.

Save a copy of the report. This copy will be used to troubleshoot.

Using the copy of the original report, remove a calculation* column from the report, save, rerun the report making sure to refresh the data.

Repeat step 3. until the error no longer displays.

Once the error no longer displays, this confirms the last column removed as the cause of the issue.
​ 

Investigate the Data

Interrogate or review what data is returning for this column in relation to the error message.
e.g. A common cause of "ORA-01476: divisor is equal to zero" is that an employee incorrectly has a 0 entered for fte hours, contract hours or salary. The solution may be to update the employee's contract with the correct data OR add an NVL to the calculation.

*Unsure if it's a Calculation? Simply remove each column one-by-one, beginning with number columns.
​ 

Error Console

If still unsure, try using the Error Console for further assistance. To use the Error Console.

Run the original report until the error displays.

Select Actions.

Select Error Console.

Select the relevant error message based on Run Time and Run By.

Scroll down to see a more detailed error message.

Use the error message to further help troubleshoot the issue.
​
​Note: the error message displays technical information which may require a Business or BI analyst to review. This information may also be shared with Customer Support.

title: Delete standard reports
text:
Insight users aren't able to amend a standard report, they're only able to view it. If updates are needed, the recommended process is to clone the original report. The new copy can then be updated. Follow the below steps to complete this.


​Note: First, ensure the user account has all the required accesses.
​ 

From the dashboard menu search bar, enter and select Insight, then click the Admin Areaicon.

Enter the report name in Search Reports, then click the searchicon.

Click the three-dotmenu against the report, then click View.

Click CANCEL, then click ACTIONS.

Click Clone, then enter a new report name in Name.

Click OK, then click CANCEL.

Click Actions, then click Edit.

The user can now make changes to the cloned report.

title: How does the function prbi_get_post_profile_detail work
text:
PRBI_GET_POST_PROFILE_DETAIL can be used to get two details for a  Post.
​
A.  The Post Type Code which is sometimes know as the Employee Status at employee level e.g. permanent, temporary
​
OR
​
B.  The Post Title Code or Job Title Code i.e. the reference code linked to the job associated with this post.
​
In both cases, only the reference codes are output - not the descriptions.
​
When creating the calculation in Insight using this function :
​
If you require the Post Type Code,  select post_number for the field p_post_number.
Then enter the word  TYPE  for  p_item_type  and press Return.
​TYPE should display, click in the box to select it for p_item_type.
​
If you require the Post Title Code, enter  TITLE  for  p_item_type.

title: Current Commenced Appointment does not show an end date on report when there is a future appointment
text:
When a contract has a commenced appointment sequence, the end date on that sequence will remain NULL.
Each night a job runs which checks for appointments with a future start date.
When an appointment has a start date for that night, the job updates the status on that to commenced and it updates the status on the previous commenced appointment to ended.  It is only then that the end date is populated on that previous commenced appointment.
​
It is not possible to report on end dates for current commenced appointments where there is also a future appointment sequence.

title: Report on Absences and Leave Requests in Insight
text:
When absences are entered directly into the system (one which don't come from approve leave requests) they are held on a different table from leave requests.
​
On Insight, you would use 'Person Absence Details(Time)' to report on Absneces, This will include approved leave requests and Absences entered directly into the system. You would use 'Person Leave Requests(Time)' to report on Leave Requests, this can include Unprocessed, Approved, Rejected and Cancelled Requests
​
It's possible to add columns from  both Person Absence Details(Time) and Person Leave Requests(Time) to the same report but you may end up with duplicate entries.
You would have one entry for the approved leave request and another entry for the absence from that approved leave request.

title: Display date columns in hours and minutes format
text:
Columns of type DATE automatically show in full date format.
​
In order to display Insight columns that default to displaying dates rather than hours and minutes, use the TO_CHAR conversion to change the date format.
​
to_char([INSIGHT_ITEM}, 'HH24:MI')
​
For example, to display DEFAULT_START_TIME on the Work Pattern view as 08:00 rather than 12-AUG-2022, use the following:
​
to_char(CTCI_WORK_PATTERN.DEFAULT_START_TIME, 'HH24:MI')

title: Email Address not populating on Insight Report
text:
Solution 1:

You can report on contact details using the 'Person Contact (Personnel)' table. Here you can filter by person reference number or by Contact Type, for example.

 

Contact Type Key:

HEM = Personal Email Address

EMAIL = Work Email Address

MOB = Personal Mobile Number

HTN = Home Telephone Number

You may be limited on what data you can pull in conjunction with contact details on this report. Meaning, if you try to add in a column that does not overlap the Person Contact table, the report will return as blank. Just delete the additional column(s) to revert.

 

Solution 2:

Instead of adding in a new 'Column' for email addresses, add the following 'Calculation' and the email addresses should pull successfully:
​
PRBI_GET_CONTACT_TEXT(P_EMPNO=>PRCI_HR_PERSON_MASTER.PERSON_REFERENCE, P_CONTACT_TYPE=>'EMAIL')


​

title: Report on Reference Data or LOVs in Insight
text:
Create a report in Insight and select Add Columns.
In the Filter Columns by View, enter  'Data Validation'.
You will see a number of Insight views with details of Reference Data.
Scroll down and you will see views such as 
​Hr Reference1(Data Validation) and Hr Reference2(Data Validation).
​
Reference codes can have either be numeric or alphanumeric.
Reference data with numeric codes is in Hr Reference1(Data Validation) e.g. Locations.
Reference data with both numeric and alphanumeric codes is in Hr Reference2(Data Validation) so this is the best view to use for reporting on reference data.
​
​ Hr References (Data Validation)  - This has all the reference data from Hr Reference2(Data Validation) and in addition has reference data for Work Groups, Pay Codes, Pay Scales/Grades and Pay Groups.
​
It is also possible to report on a specific reference data type using the 'LOV' views e.g. Employee Status LOV (Personnel).

title: How is the call-to-action link generated in an Icue Email
text:
The first part of the Icue button link is generated from the parameter CP_INSIGHT_EMAIL_URL.
You will find this in Administration Dashboard, Site Manager, Admin Settings.
This is usually in the format of  https://my.corehr.com/pls/clientid/  in a production environment.
If the clientid is coreportal_abcp  then the CP_INSIGHT_EMAIL_URL is https://my.corehr.com/pls/coreportal_abcp/
​
The middle part has  i#locate/widget/   hard coded.
​
The last part is based on what system area was selected when configuring the Call-to-Action for the Icue.  
The system area is usually a dashboard tab.
Icues are saved in ci_voxtalk_alert_setup and the system area is in the field link_to_system_area.
​
select alert_recipient_type, alert_header, link_to_system_area
from ci_voxtalk_alert_setup;
​
​URL = cp_insight_email_urli#locate/widget/ci_voxtalk_alert_setup.link_to_system_area
​
​ 


​

title: Insight Report reduces in Size when 'Save As' is selected
text:
Your file is changing size because hidden, unneeded data is being removed.

 

When a file is downloaded from a database server, it will keep the formatting associated with the server.
This formatting is hidden as it is just a reference for the server and can only be read by a server and will not affect the data.
​
When you download a file from the database server, in this case via insights, it will keep the hidden formatting of the server on the file as well as it is essentially just copy pasting and sending you the file.
​
Once you then save the file elsewhere or rename it etc., it will save the correct size as it will get rid of this hidden formatting.

title: Extract characters up to a symbol
text:
If you need to input a calculation to extract/get characters up to an '@' symbol from an email address you can use the below calculation:

substr(contact_text, 1, instr(contact_text, '@')-1)

title: Claim number not pulling through on insight report
text:
The reason all the trip IDs are not showing is because in back office if a Trip Id has multiple rows with the exact same data . The way insights were designed, multiple rows with the same data would be seen as duplicates and grouped to one.
​
For the Insights report, the Trip ID is not a unique enough identifier  but by including the Trip Detail Id, it is possible to see the four rows with the same information separately because the Trip Detail Id is unique.
​
The grouping is determined by the report's columns. Queries with grouping do not display duplicate rows, and these rows are seen as duplicates by Insights because there is no differentiation between these rows, trip Id, expense code, dates, and amounts all are seen the same. When you add the trip detailed ID column, those rows are no longer duplicates because the trip detailed ID makes each row unique and produces the expected results.

title: Error - 'ORA-01722: invalid number' when running a report
text:
This error message usually appears because an existing DECODE calculation based on Person Status treated all data as a number. As Person Status can be a number of characters (e.g. 1, 2, A, Z etc.) a mismatch of datatypes existed.
​
There are two options to resolve this issue:

 

Option 1

Add single quotes to the DECODE calculation so all data is treated as characters and not numbers.

 

E.g. Update this calculation:

 

DECODE(Person Type, 1, Balance, 2, Balance, 'A', Balance, 0) to

DECODE(Person Type, '1', Balance, '2', Balance, 'A', Balance, 0)

 

Option 2

Systematically remove the columns and see which column is causing the issue. If it is a large report, do it in batches to narrow it down.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select the Evo Configuration widget.

title: Copilot HR Document plugin
text:
The HR documents plugin for Copilot allows you to query policy, process, or information documents that have been uploaded to PeopleXD in .pdf or .doc format. There are two categories of document you can upload for Copilot:

Policy Documents (documents used specifically in Social Onboarding).

General Documents  (other general documents stored in PeopleXD).

For further guidance check the PeopleXD Evo User Guide or read some example questions.

📌Note: This article is only applicable to PeopleXD solutions that have upgraded to Evo.

 

 

General documents

To add general documents, follow the steps below:

Navigate to the Document Upload widget.

Click Upload and enter a title.

Select the relevant file from your device.

Click OK.

 

 

Policy documents

Policy Documents can be uploaded within the People Management Dashboard using Policy Groups. You can: 

Have as many policy groups as required.  

Upload one or multiple documents to a group. 

Assign or restrict access to a policy group using criteria groups.  

 

To create a policy group and upload documents, follow the steps below.

Go to the Data Centre widget on the People Management Dashboard. 

Open HR Admin Setup Settings. 

Search for and click Policy Documents. 

Click Add. 

Enter a Title and click OK. 

Click Upload, select the relevant file(s) from your device.

Click OK then Save. 

 

To make a policy group available in Copilot you need to assign a criteria group. This can be used to assign access to all employees or restrict access. Note: To make a policy group available to all employees in Copilot, create a criteria group with no rules and assign it to the relevant groups.

Navigate to the Policy Documents screen, expand the policy groups 3-dot menu and click Criteria Groups.

To create a criteria group, click Manage Criteria Groups. 

Click Assign New Group.

From the drop-down list, select a Criteria Group.

Click OK.        

 

 

Copilot Documents widget

You need to add the Copilot Documents widget to a dashboard to allow employees to view and download the General and Policy documents that have been uploaded to co-pilot. This will only display documents the employee has access to and only those in .pdf or .doc format. When an employee has access to this widget and uses the HR Documents Skill: 

A link to the document(s) referenced in the response is provided in the read more section.  

The link opens in new browser or Access Evo tab.

The link opens a filtered view of the Copilot Documents widget.

title: Configure iCues to appear in Feed
text:
The Feed is a notification hub across Access products. PeopleXD can deliver personalised prompts and reminders through the Feed to individual users about actions and tasks they may need to complete.

 

You can customise the alerts that appear through the iCues functionality. For example, you can create an iCue for the following scenarios that will appear in the Feed:

Alert an employee when they have a large annual leave balance remaining.

Alert a manager when one of their employees is approaching the sick leave threshold.

 

To create a Feed iCue, using Insight reports that you or your colleagues have created, watch the video or follow the steps below: 

 

Navigate to the Report Store tab on the Insight Dashboard, then click the iCues tab.

Search for and select your iCue, then click Download Report.

Once downloaded click the iCues tab, expand the three dot menu on the relevant iCue then click Manage.

A list of all employees that meet the criteria displays.

Expand the Actions menu then click iCue.

Click the iCue Schedule tab and select the iCue frequency.

Click the iCue Type tab then tick Feed and select the iCue Recipients.

Use the iCue Header & iCue Body tabs to customise the notification.

Use the Suggested Prompt tab to add a link to Copilot, to help users complete their task.

Select the relevant plugin skill and enter the prompt text. 

Use the Call to Action tab to add a button, that will direct the user to a select system area.

Select the relevant system area e.g., My Approval Notifications.

Once finished, click Save.

Note: Feed iCues are triggered overnight on the frequency selected.

 

Note: This article is only applicable to PeopleXD solutions that have upgraded to Evo

title: Access Evo organisation member settings
text:
Note: The following information is only related to organisations using PeopleXD in Access Evo. If you use Access Button inside PeopleXD, read the relevant article.

 

As an Access Evo (previously Access Workspace) administrator, you have access to the Members area in Access Evo where you can view the users' access to associated products and manage their permissions in your Access Evo organisation.
​
​Tip: Member record in Access Evo is the user account in PeopleXD with an email address in the employee record.

 

View all member records

To view your organisation members, click your avatar, select Organisation Settings then click Members. Alternatively, simply click the members icon.

 

Search and filter member records

To search for a specific member, enter their name in the search bar and to filter the results, click the funnel icon.

To select all the users, click the All Selection  icon.
To refresh the list, click the Refresh  icon.
​
A member can have one of the following statuses: 

Status

	

Description




Added

	

The user is set up as a member in Access Evo but has not logged into Access Evo.




Active

	

The user is set up as an active member in Access Evo. 




Deactivated

	

Previously set up as a member but is no longer active. For example, they've left and their portal access was deactivated. 


In Access Evo, your members only have the User or Administrator role.
​
​Tip: You can have users with different roles for different products.

 

Add member records

Once you add an employee to PeopleXD, their member account is automatically created and activated in Members within Access Evo via the Access Evo sync with PeopleXD. 
​
​Note: Do not add new members to Access Evo using the Add option within Members.

 

Other Member options

You have other options to use for members, however, we only recommend using the Export Members feature. To do so, in Members, click the cog wheel icon. 
​

 

Manage member records

To manage a member record, click the three dots on the member card. We describe each option in the table below:
​ 

Option

	

Description




View member

	

You can view the following:

Whether a user's account is an email account or a username account.

Member's role, department, job title and location.

Access Evo Role: Either User or Administrator  

Products such as:

Analytics : Either No Access or Administrator.  

Tip: Administrator can view the read only dashboards available in analytics.   

Learning : Either No Access, User or Administrator.

Tip: Only administrators of Learning Lite have this set to the Administrator Role.  

Engage : Either No Access, User or Administrator.

Tip: Only administrators of Engage Lite have this set to the Administrator Role.  

PeopleXD: All users have User role.

Tip: You manage the admin access role in PeopleXD.




Manage tags

	

The PeopleXD tags such as Job Title, Department, and Location feed to Access Evo as part of the nightly sync.

If you need to update any of the PeopleXD tags, ensure you do it in People Management.  

If you update these in Access Evo, the nightly sync reverts your changes to the values in PeopleXD again.




Manage roles

	

You can manage the access to products in Access Evo.   
​
To update the role for the organisation or product, select the relevant role then click Save Changes. 

Organisation role

This is equivalent to the Access Evo role.   

User: For most of your organisations' users, this is User. These don't have access to the Members area or other Organisational Setting in Access Evo.   

XD Admin: Grants limited access to Access Evo Settings and Members.

Administrator: Grants full access to Access Evo settings and Members, this should be granted to super users.

Leaver: Assigned as part of the leaving process where you have leaver profiles set up to grant access after an employee's leave date. 

Products role

Analytics: Either No Access or Administrator role.

No Access: The user doesn't have access to the Analytics dashboards in Access Evo.

 Administrator: Analytics administrators have access to the read only Analytics dashboards in Access Evo. This is what most users have access to outside of the central admins.  

Learning: Either No Access, User or Administrator role.

Tip: This is to support users who have access to Learning Lite in Access Evo.   

User: Most users of the system.  

Administrator: Only administrators of Learning Lite have this role.

No Access: User doesn't have access to Learning Lite in Access Evo.   

Engage: Either No Access, User or Administrator role.

Tip: This is to support users who have access to Engage Lite in Access Evo.   

User: Most users of the system.  

Administrator: Only administrators of Engage Lite have this role.  

No Access: User doesn't have access to Engage Lite in Access Evo.  

PeopleXD: All users have User role.

Tip: You manage the admin access role in PeopleXD.

Note: Rejoiners aren't automatically assigned PeopleXD product roles, this must be manually assigned.




Manage Features

	

Depending on how you site has been set up you may be able to assign or remove access to Evo features, including Feed and Copilot.

Each feature on your site will be set up with one of the below settings:

On for all users – read only user access.

On by default – with the option to remove user access.

Off by default – with the option to grant user access.

To update the role for the feature, select the relevant role then click Save Changes. 




Change name

	

Do not update the name directly in Access Evo. 
​
The name feeds across from PeopleXD via the overnight sync. If you need to change the name, do this in People Management in PeopleXD.




Change username

	

Do not update.




Change email address

	

The email address feeds across from PeopleXD via the overnight sync. If you need to change the email address, do this in People Management in PeopleXD.   




Change password

	

As an Access Evo administrator, update users' password in Access Evo where the person has been synced to Members as a username account.  




Switch to email account

	

Do not update.




Switch to username account

	

Do not update.




Deactivate

	

Do not update.
​
When a user becomes a leaver and has a leave date populated in PeopleXD then the user becomes a deactivated member in Access Evo. 




Groups

	

Currently, Groups is not applicable in the PeopleXD solution.
​
To view the Groups in Access Evo, follow the steps below:

Click your avatar then select Organisation Settings.

Select Groups.

title: Manage users and Access Evo members FAQs
text:
📌Note: The following information is only related to organisations using PeopleXD in Access Evo (previously Access Workspace).

 

Check out the most common queries in relation to PeopleXD working in Access Evo:

Question
	
Answer



What is Access Evo Members?

	

Access Evo Members is the place you go to manage your users on Access Evo. 
​
Prior to the integration with PeopleXD, if you already had other Access Products within Access Evo, this is where you would go to manage users for those Products, including:

Add new users.

Update their details such as Name, Tags.

Manage their access to other Access Evo applications.

Revoke access.

When the integration is active, the Member records will be managed from PeopleXD. This means that you no longer need to manage them in Access Evo. Now you can go here to:

Look up an employee record that has been synced

Manage their access to other Access Evo applications. 

Of course, if you have instances where non-employee users need to be given access to Access Evo, this can be managed as before.




Who can see Access Evo Members?

	

This depends on your Access Evo configuration.
Members can be set up to be:

Available to all users.

Available to users with the Administrator and/or XD Admin organisation role only.

Within the Migration Checklists cited at the start of this document, recommendations are given on how your organisation should carefully consider who is responsible for this role.




Who are my Access Evo Administrators?

	

Any user with access to Access Evo Members can look this up.

Click the Members icon. 

The screen defaults to show all active users.

In the Search box at the top right of the screen, click the Filter icon. 

Update Organisation Role to XD Admin or Administrators.

The filter applies automatically.




How do I set up a Access Evo Administrator?

	

Users with the XD Admin or Administrator organisation role can do this in Access Evo.

Click the Members icon. 

Search for the user.

Click the three-dot menu for the user then click Manage Roles.

Update the Organisation Role to XD Admin to grant limited access or Administrator to grant super user access. 

Click Save.




How do I remove access for an existing Access Evo Administrator?

	

Users with the XD Admin or Administrator organisation role can do this in Access Evo.
​

Click the Members icon. 

Search for the user.

Click the three-dot menu for the user then click Manage Roles.

Set the Organisation Role to User. 

Click Save.

Note: You can do this step before or after the integration has been set up.




Who can update Access Evo Members settings?

	

Any user with the XD Admin or Administrator role organisation role.
​
The following settings can be managed. Please note our recommendation for these settings when the PeopleXD integration is active. However, this is a decision for your organisation and depend on your own use of Access Evo.

Allow all users to see members: When this is on, all users of Access Evo will see the Members icon, and will be able to look up all Active, Added and Inactive users. Access to members is all or nothing, for example, if you have it, you cannot further restrict this to only show certain users or data items.
Our recommendation is to turn this off when the integration is active.

Allow all users to view hierarchy: When this is on, Members will show who an employee reports to in the form of an org chart. This is based on the reports to email synced from PeopleXD. 
Our recommendation is to turn this off 

Allow users to edit their names: Users can change their own name. 
Our recommendation is that this is off. Name changes should be made in PeopleXD only. 

Hide users email addresses: Hides the users’ email address in Members.

Allow users to hide their email address: Allows users to specify if they want to hide their email address. 

To update these settings:

Click your account name at the top right of the screen.

Click Organisation Settings.

Click the Members Options tab.

Update options as required. 

Click Save.




Who can create or update Access Evo Members?

	

XD Admins have limited access to create and update Members to ensure actions that should be completed in XD aren't available. 
​
Administrators need to take care to avoid the following actions:

Add users, edit usernames, edit emails

Updating synced data fields such as changing name or updating tags like Department, Job Title, Location.

Changing user account type.

Changing a user's status.




How do I turn off Access Evo Members for regular users?

	

Users with the XD Admin or Administrator organisation role can do this in Access Evo. 

Click your account name at the top right of the screen.

Select Organisation Settings.

Select General. 

Select Members Options on the left-hand menu.

Turn OFF the setting Show Members for users who are not Administrators.

Click Save at the top right of the screen.




Can I update users directly on Access Evo?

	

Employee: Role Assignments for other Products.

Employee Tags: Access Evo Administrators only - excluding those that are synced from PeopleXD such as not Department, Job Title or Locatios.

Non-Employee: No restrictions.




How do I set up non-employee users on Access Evo?

	

A non-employee user is any user that needs to login to Access Evo to access any of your Access Evo applications. 
​
The assumption is that if they are not employees, they will not be set up on PeopleXD and therefore not synced to Access Evo Members. 
​
The Access Evo Administrators can still create users directly on Access Evo for these scenarios. There is no change to how you currently manage this i.e. create the user, send an invitation email, assign their role to the products they require, deactivate the user when they no longer require access. 




Can I update the Tags that are synced from PeopleXD?

	

The following Tags are synced from PeopleXD:

Department 

Job Title

Location

You must not edit the value for any of these tags directly in Access Evo. If a Tag is not synced from PeopleXD, you can continue to manage this directly in Access Evo i.e. add new values, update values, assign to Members etc. 

Updating Synced Tags: If you need to edit the value of one of the Tags, you need to do this in PeopleXD - this will in turn update the employee record and trigger an update to Access Evo, for example, if you were to fix a spelling error for a Department

Adding New Values for Synced Tags: The new value must be added in PeopleXD e.g. a new Department, Location, or Job Title. When that is associated with an employee record, it will be synced to Access Evo as a new value for the existing System Tag.




Does the known as field sync?

	

The sync does typically pull across the forename field, but if there’s a value in the ‘Known As’ field, then that’s what will sync across to Access Evo instead.




Does the sync from PXD to Access Evo overwrite the existing ‘Roles’ in Access Evo (e.g. Admin roles etc) as linked by email. Also, what happens when a user hasn’t already been allocated a role?

	

Correct, Product roles and the Access Evo Admin role for existing users will not be overwritten.  
For new Members, they will automatically be assigned the user role for Access Evo. And the PXD user role will be auto assigned. 




We often login as other users in PXD UAT for testing purposes – will we still be able to do this when it is in Access Evo?

	

Yes, once the move to Access Evo for PeopleXD is complete, we will create a UAT Access Evo org to link to your UAT XD environment.
​
You will still be able to logon as other users but the steps to take over an account will be different. 
​ 

Remove the email address from the employee record. There are two types of accounts as part of PXD Access Evo integration. An email account and a username account. On Access Evo, you cannot take over an email account without a user’s permission (through Impersonation). But you can take over a username account

In PXD Security, flag the user as a username account for Access Evo. This step will allow the record to sync to Access Evo without an email address

In PXD Security add the employee as an authorised user for non-Production. This will sync the user to Access Evo members. 

Reset Access Evo Identity Password. 




If we add someone to Access Evo directly, then later add that person to PXD, will the accounts automatically link up?

	

Yes, we will link a Member record if you subsequently add the personnel record in PXD where the email addresses match. However, we recommend that the Member record is always created from PeopleXD if the person is being created on People Management




Where an employee is set up in PXD with a personal email how do we prevent this from being seen by other users before it is changed to a corporate email?

	

We advise switching off Members for all users except admins by disabling the highlighted option below called “Show Members for users who are not Administrators”. 




To ensure there are no USERNAME-based Access Evo accounts, as these will link on employee reference as opposed to email.
How do we check the account type on a WS record?

	

You can check this by completing a Members Export from Access Evo.
​ 
A username account won’t have an email address, and will have a value in the Username column.




When an email address is changed and a user needs to create a new Evo password can this process be completed on mobile devices, or does it need the full desktop version?

	

It can be completed on a mobile device. Users will be directed to change the password on their mobile browser.




Do we need to match work email addresses for employees who are now leavers? Assuming only active employees will be pushed over?

	

Correct we will not sync employees that are leavers. So leavers do not need to be checked/matched.
