​
The following settings can be managed. Please note our recommendation for these settings when the PeopleXD integration is active. However, this is a decision for your organisation and depend on your own use of Access Evo.

Show Members for users who are not Administrators: When this is on, all regular users of Access Evo will see the Members icon, and will be able to look up all Active, Added and Inactive users. 
Access to members is all or nothing, for example, if you have it, you cannot further restrict this to only show certain users or data items.
Our recommendation is to turn this off when the integration is active.

Show relationships in Members: When this is on, Members will show you who an employee reports to in the form of an org chart. This is based on the reports to email synced from PeopleXD. 
Our recommendation is to turn this off 

All users to edit their names: Users can change their own name. 
Our recommendation is that this is off. Name changes should be made in PeopleXD only. 

Hide email address from Members: Hides the users’ email address.

All users to hide their email address in Members: Allows users to specify if they want to hide their email address. 

To update these settings:

Click your account name at the top right of the screen.

Select Organisation Settings.

Select General.

Select Members Options on the left-hand menu.

Update options as required. 

Click Save.




Who can create or update Access Evo Members?

	

Any user with the Access Evo organisation Administrator role.
​
However, when the data is synced from PeopleXD for employees, Administrators need to take care to avoid the following actions:

Create user.

Updating synced data fields such as changing name or updating tags like Department, Job Title, Location.

Changing user account type.

Making a user inactive.




How do I turn off Access Evo Members for regular users?

	

A Access Evo administrator can do this in Access Evo. 

Click your account name at the top right of the screen.

Select Organisation Settings.

Select General. 

Select Members Options on the left-hand menu.

Turn OFF the setting Show Members for users who are not Administrators.

Click Save at the top right of the screen.




Can I update users directly on Access Evo?

	

Employee: Role Assignments for other Products.

Tags, excluding those that are synced from PeopleXD such as not Department, Job Title or Locations.

Non-Employee: No restrictions.




How do I set up non-employee users on Access Evo?

	

A non-employee user is any user that needs to login to Access Evo to access any of your Access Evo applications. 
​
The assumption is that if they are not employees, they will not be set up on PeopleXD and therefore not synced to Access Evo Members. 
​
The Access Evo Administrators can still create users directly on Access Evo for these scenarios. There is no change to how you currently manage this i.e. create the user, send an invitation email, assign their role to the products they require, deactivate the user when they no longer require access. 




Can I update the Tags that are synced from PeopleXD?

	

The following Tags are synced from PeopleXD:

Department 

Job Title

Location

You must not edit the value for any of these tags directly in Access Evo. If a Tag is not synced from PeopleXD, you can continue to manage this directly in Access Evo i.e. add new values, update values, assign to Members etc. 

Updating Synced Tags: If you need to edit the value of one of the Tags, you need to do this in PeopleXD - this will in turn update the employee record and trigger an update to Access Access Evo, for example, if you were to fix a spelling error for a Department

Adding New Values for Synced Tags: The new value must be added in PeopleXD e.g. a new Department, Location, or Job Title. When that is associated with an employee record, it will be synced to Access Evo as a new value for the existing System Tag.




Does the known as field sync?

	

The sync does typically pull across the forename field, but if there’s a value in the ‘Known As’ field, then that’s what will sync across to Access Evo instead.




Does the sync from PXD to Access Evo overwrite the existing ‘Roles’ in Access Evo (e.g. Admin roles etc) as linked by email. Also, what happens when a user hasn’t already been allocated a role?   

	

Correct, Product roles and the Access Evo Admin role for existing users will not be overwritten.  
For new Members, they will automatically be assigned the user role for Access Evo. And the PXD user role will be auto assigned. 




If we add someone to Access Evo directly, then later add that person to PXD, will the accounts automatically link up?

	

Ongoing new users added through PeopleXD will always be created in Access Evo as username accounts.

 

To ensure that an account first added in Access Evo directly links up correctly to a new account added in PeopleXD, you should ensure that the account in Access Evo is correctly configured as a username account and that their username matches their personnel number in PeopleXD.

 

If the user is setup as an email account in Access Evo, you should switch them to a username account.

text:
To give users the necessary access to your new Access Evo Hosted Products i.e. Access Engage Lite, Access Learning Lite and PeopleXD HMRC Notifications, you must assign this within the Access Evo Members area.

Products in Access Evo can be assigned 3 different access levels:

User: No admin access to the Product.  

Administrator: Administrators of the Product.

No Access: User doesn't have access to the Product.

 

Step 1 – Assign an Access Evo Admin to manage user access in Access Evo:

Confirm who will be your Access Evo Administrator, this can be 1 or more people who will have control over users access to Products in Access Evo primarily.

Note: If your organisation embarks on adopting further Access Evo products and Features you may require more in-depth management of Members, Organisation settings and general Access Evo features. Send the email addresses of who you have nominated to become your Access Evo Administrators to PeopleXD.EvoProjects@theaccessgroup.com

Once the Access Group have confirmed go live of PeopleXD Evo, and activated your Access Evo Administrators, Administrators can access the Access Evo Members area.

Administrators can adjust each members level of access to suit the business/function needs.

 

Step 2 - Manage User access to Access Evo Hosted Products

Open Access Evo. Note: if you are using Access Button inside PeopleXD administrators can open Access Evo by clicking Access Button then Spaces.

Click Members  .

Search for the user(s):

To search for a specific member, enter their name in the search bar.

To filter the results click the funnel  icon .

To select all users, click the All Selection icon.

Expand the 3-dot menu for the user and click Manage Roles.

Under the Product section use the dropdown options to set the relevant user access level per product. e.g., User/No Access.

Click Save.

title: Email verification - domain verification
text:
Domain Verification allows you to add your organisation's email domains and once verified any email address from these domain(s) will be set to verified.
​
The Domain Verification widget can be found on the System Overview tab within the Security Dashboard.
​
To learn how to add and verify a domain, watch this video, or follow the steps below:
​
​

 

Add a domain

To add a domain follow the steps below:

 Navigate to Security > System Overview > Domain Verification

Click Add Domain

Enter your company domain (text after @ in an email address) and click OK

The domain will now display on the Domain Verification widget with a status of Domain Unverified.

Take a note of the CODE opposite the unverified domain and ADD this to your Organisation’s DNS. Note, You will need assistance from your internal IT team to complete this. (see DNS TXT Record below for instructions).

Once the TXT record has been added to your organisation’s DNS settings, click on 3-dot menu opposite the unverified domain that you have added on the Domain Verification widget and click “Verify Domain”.  The status should change to Domain Verified.

Please note it could take up to 24-48 hours for the DNS record to be fully updated.
​ 

 

Domain verification - DNS TXT record

The Verification Code obtained in Step 5 above needs to be added as a TXT record in your organisation’s DNS settings, this will need to be completed by your internal IT team. 
​
Adding this TXT record won't impact your website at all; it's something you can only view through a special tool (i.e. the domain verification widget in XD) which performs DNS lookups. Note: you can only create the TXT record through the company whose nameservers your domain name uses, please refer to their specific guidance on how to set up DNS entries.
​
Use the following information to create your TXT record:
Host: @
Type: TXT
Value: The entire verification code 
​
Once your internal IT team have completed this you will need to verify your domain. To do this refer back to Step 6 above.

title: Access Evo login and key navigational changes
text:
Note: The following information is only related to clients using PeopleXD Evo in an Access Evo (previously Access Workspace) tab.

As a PeopleXD user, you log in via the Identity login page. Once logged in, you will be presented with Access Evo and can access your PeopleXD dashboards from 

 Access button.

 

📌Note: If you're currently using PeopleXD and migrating to Access Evo, if this is the first time that you’re logging into Access Evo, check how to log in for the first time.

 

 

Log in and open PeopleXD

Regardless of user role, as a new user, log in using the new URL. For example, the URL has this format https://go.accessacloud.com/o/tenantid
​ 

🤓Tip: The tenantid is the same as your PeopleXD environment.

 

​
To open PeopleXD in an Access Evo tab, click Access Button     and choose your required dashboard from the Products menu area. 
​
​Note: 

When logging into Access Evo for the first time, ensure you click Access Button 

  to open your relevant PeopleXD dashboard. Then PeopleXD opens in an Access Evo tab. The next time you log in, you can view this tab by default unless you choose to close it.

When PeopleXD is already open in an Access Evo, if you click Access Button 

  then select the same PeopleXD dashboard again, you will jump to the existing PeopleXD tab containing that same dashboard.

 


Introducing Access button

  Access button is your one place for everything you need from PeopleXD and Access Evo, including your PeopleXD dashboards as well as your other Access products. 

 

 

There are five areas contained in the Access button:

Products:This is where you can find your PeopleXD dashboards, alongside any other Access Evo products.

Spaces: Here is where you can find your company's shared dashboards and your personal dashboards. 

Copilot: This is a confidential personal assistant that leverages AI.  

Feed: Helps you keep track of tasks in PeopleXD.

Help and Support:  this is where you’ll find our Access Evo Interactive Guide and Customer Success portal through Get Help.

 

 

Close or duplicate Access Evo tabs

You can have up to 10 PeopleXD tabs open at any time. For example, you can be in the Employee Dashboard in one, Manager Dashboard in another, and Payroll in another. Hovering over the tab will display a label to indicate what is open within the tab (e.g. People Management or Payroll).

Closing tabs: To close individual tabs, expand the three dots then select Close.   

Duplicating Tabs: To open another tab, expand the three dots then select Duplicate.

 

 

 

 

PeopleXD My Profile  

You can now access the PeopleXD My Profile from the left-hand side profile photo, which is referred to as an avatar.  This is no longer available from the PeopleXD settings menu.
​

 

Items moved under My Profile  

You can now find the following items under My Profile:

Language Preferences​.  

Classic UI toggle: Previously in PeopleXD Account Settings.​  

Fitbit integration: Previously in PeopleXD Account Settings​.

 

 

Profile photos  

You upload profile photos to Access Evo. Profile photos uploaded via Social Hub or Native App are saved to Access Evo directly. 
​
To upload a photo, follow the steps below:

In Access Evo, click your avatar then select My Settings.

Under Avatar, select Browse and upload a photo.  

Select Save.

Top right PeopleXD cog wheel   

The PeopleXD cogwheel was previously a person’s avatar in standalone PeopleXD. This has been changed to a cogwheel as the avatar in Access Evo has replaced the PeopleXD avatar.  

From the avatar, the Account Settings has been renamed to Security.  

🤓Tip: Contains Recent Account Activity for the last 90 days.

 

   

 

 

Payslip and bank details password

📌Note: When viewing your payslip or updating your bank details in PeopleXD, you no longer get asked to enter a password.

 

My Account – options not relevant to non-administrator

The following administrator options are visible to all users but only Access Evo administrators maintain these: 

Domains.

Security Policies.

Clients.

 

 

Security dashboard  

As an administrator, you can now view the UI changes that have been made to the Security dashboard.

Language


​

title: User management overview
text:
Have a look at the user management changes in place when using PeopleXD in Access Evo (previously Access Workspace):

You now maintain Portal user accounts via member records in Access Evo. The Access Evo member record replaces the PeopleXD Portal account:

The member record links to the PeopleXD employee record via:

The user's email address which is a contact type of EMAIL if the account type is Email. 

The user's personnel number if the account type is username account. 

You change passwords and maintain authentication configuration in Access Evo Identity.

With Access Evo invites, you replace the PeopleXD self-registration.  

You can still manually maintain the menu profiles in PeopleXD. 

You can still maintain access to employees in People Management, Payroll, WFM, and other products within PeopleXD. 

In summary… 

User management in PeopleXD Security still controls access to employees and dashboards and widgets in PeopleXD. 

Access Evo Members control a user’s authentication and access to the PeopleXD product and other Access Evo products.

Existing users and new starters are auto-assigned product access to PeopleXD as well as Learning Lite and Engage. There is no additional step required to assign product access for PeopleXD. 

Access an existing user’s account 
Search for a user 

To search for a user and manage their account, follow the steps below:

Select the Security dashboard then select User Management.
​

Tip: Only system and HR administrator can view Security.
​

Enter the user's name.
​

Tip: By default, you can see all of the active Access Evo accounts on PeopleXD, but you can change the search filter.


Search filters 

The drop-down list of options controls the list of users displayed on the System Users widget. This defaults to All Active Evo Accounts. You can switch to a different search filter. For a description of each of the options available, see the table below:
​ 

Option

	

Description




All Active Evo Accounts 

	

All Access Evo user accounts that are currently active. 




All Evo Accounts 

	

All Access Evo user accounts, including inactive accounts. 




Non-synced Accounts 

	

All employees in People Management that have not synced to Access Evo due to not having an email contact type in their PeopleXD employee record.




All Active Portal Accounts 

	

All active Portal user accounts excluding Access Evo accounts. This option is no longer applicable with PeopleXD in Access Evo.




All Portal Accounts 

	

All Portal user accounts, including inactive accounts. This option is no longer applicable with PeopleXD in Access Evo.




All Back-Office Accounts 

	

All active and dormant PeopleXD Back Office accounts.

 

View account 

To view a user’s account or to troubleshoot an error when syncing an employee, follow the steps below: 

Select the Security dashboard then select User Management.

Enter the user's name.

Ensure you use the relevant filter depending on the user you're searching for.  

Click the three-dots icon and select Manage Account. 

Evo user accounts
Header

For a description of each header area of a user’s Evo account, see the table below:
​ 

Item

	

Description




HR Person Link 

	

The employee name that the user account is linked to. 




Username

	

The employee’s username. 




 Evo Status 

	

The user’s current status: Added, Active or Deactivated. 




Menu Groups 

	

The number of menu profiles the user has access to.  




Menu Options Access 

	

The combined number of menu options that the user has access to for the menu profiles enabled. 




Last Activity 

	

The last time the user logged in, including the duration of the session and a timestamp for the activity. No activity appears if they have never logged in. 




Last Sync Date 

	

The date that the users record was last synced with Access Evo. 

 

Menu profiles 

This is where menu profiles are assigned to user accounts. This is what controls the user’s access to functionality on PeopleXD. The following table outlines what information is stored here. 
​ 

Item

	

Description




Search

	

Search for the menu profile name. 




Filter

	

Filter by menu profiles that have been assigned to the user already, or those who have not been assigned yet. 




Results

	

This list reflects all of the menu profiles that are configured on PeopleXD. If the Active indicator is on, this means that the user has that menu profile and therefore can access all the features controlled by the menu options enabled on it. 

 

Assign menu profiles 

For users to be able to access the PeopleXD screens and features they require, you need to assign them to one or multiple menu profiles. 
​
To assign a menu profile for a user: 

Search for the menu profile. 

Click the Active indicator to assign a menu profile to the user.  

To revoke a menu profile, i.e. remove a user’s access: 

Search for the menu profile. 

Disable the Active indicator.  

Get access to PeopleXD in Access Evo as a new user 

Access to Access Evo is granted to users via invites sent to the user’s email address. It's not possible to set up a password on behalf of an employee unless using username accounts as we explain below. However, we recommend to use email accounts where possible as they are more secure.  
​
To view how to gain access to PeopleXD in Access Evo as a new employee set up in People Management, read the guidance below:

Employee’s HR record is setup in People Management with an email address.  

Employee record syncs to Access Evo Members in real time and is automatically created there. 

The user automatically receives the user role for PeopleXD in Access Evo Members. 

An invite to Access Evo triggers that night as part of the overnight job.

Alternatively, you can manually trigger the invite to the employee if you choose to not wait for the automatic sync to complete. Read more >  

Employee receives the invite and sets up their account to log on to PeopleXD via Access Evo. 

Username accounts 

If a user is set up in People Management without an email held in the EMAIL contact type, their account is known as a username account. Read more >

title: Evo Configuration widget overview
text:
You only need to complete the set-up of the Evo Configuration widget. 
​
With the Evo Configuration widget, you can: 

Enable automatic invite emails from Access Evo (previously Access Workspace) when a new employee is set up in PeopleXD.

Enable the menu matrix rules or a default menu profile for new starters. 

Manage access to non-production environments.

Manage the Access Evo parameters.

 

 

Set up the Evo Configuration widget

To access the Evo Configuration widget, follow the steps below:

Quick jump to the Security dashboard.

From the System Overview tab, scroll to the Evo Configuration widget.

Ensure you enable the following menu options for the Security menu profile on the baseline: 
​ 

Menu option
	
Description



WS_SYSTEM_MENU.PATCH_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_INVITE

	

Update Access Evo configuration invite.




WS_SYSTEM_MENU.GET_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_INVITE

	

Get Access Evo configuration invite.




WS_SYSTEM_MENU.GET_WORKSPACE_CONFIG

	

Get Access Evo configuration.




WS_SYSTEM_MENU.GET_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_PARAMETERS
​ 

	

Get Access Evo configuration parameters.




WS_SYSTEM_MENU.GET_WORKSPACE_INVITE

	

Get Access Evo invite.




WS_SYSTEM_MENU.PATCH_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_PARAMETERS

	

Update Access Evo configuration parameters.




WORKSPACE_CF_MENU.WORKSPACECONFIG

	

System - Evo Configuration Widget.




WORKSPACE_CF_MENU.WORKSPACEINVITES

	

Evo Configuration - Evo Invites.




WORKSPACE_CF_MENU.WORKSPACEMENUMATRIX

	

Evo Configuration - Evo Menu Profile Matrix.




WORKSPACE_CF_MENU.PARAMETERS

	

Evo Configuration - Evo Parameters.

Read more >

 

 

Access Evo invites

In Access Evo invites, you can configure the settings for automatic invites. Find more details on each item on the screen in the table below: 

Item
	
Description



Enable automatic invites

	

Enable this to automatically send email invites to new employees. After they click the Join link within the email, they set up their password for Access Evo.
​
​Note: If single sign on (SSO) is configured for their email address domain, the user signs in.




Send invites to future new starters

	

Enable this to send invites to future starters.
​
​Note: When this option is disabled, only the current employees receive the invites.




Start date trigger

	

Enable this to set your preferred value. This way, you only send invites where an employee's start date is your preferred number of days before today. ​

 

 

Bulk send invites

You can send invites on demand, rather than waiting for the overnight sync. To do this, follow the steps below:

Quick jump to the Security dashboard.

From the System Overview tab, scroll to the Evo Configuration widget.

Click  Evo Invites then click Bulk Send Invites.

Click OK.

🤓Tip: You can also send Access Evo invites to individual employees. Once they receive the invitation and click the Join link, they can log into Access Evo and navigate PeopleXD.


Restrict email invites

You can only restrict email invites when you enable automatic invites. This is helpful when you need to restrict automatic invites to certain groups of employees, based on the reference data in their employee record. To do this, follow the steps below:

Quick jump to the Security dashboard.

From the System Overview tab, scroll to the  Evo Configuration widget.

Click Evo Invites then click Restrict Email Invites.

Click Add then enter a name for your criteria group.

🤓Tip: By default, the type is set to Evo Email Invites.

Click the relevant reference data.

Select the relevant attributes from the Available column and use the arrow to move it to the Assigned column.

🤓Tip: You automatically save the list. 

Return to the Restrict Email Invites screen and then from the relevant three-dot menu, add more groups, or edit and delete existing criteria groups.

 

Auto-assign menu profiles

When the employee logs in for the first time, they activate their Identity account and depending on how you set up the menu profile auto-assignation rules, they get a menu profile.
​
​Note: In the Evo menu matrix, you can configure the settings for automatically assigning menu profiles to new starters once they log into their Access Evo account. Read more >

 

Authorised non-production users

To add a user to the list of authorised users who have access to non-production environments, follow the steps below: 

Quick jump to the Security dashboard.

From the System Overview tab, scroll to the Evo Configuration widget.

Click Authorised Non-Production Users, then click Add User.

From the Person list, select a relevant user.

Click OK.

The user will now be synced.

text:

title: Authentication overview
text:
📌Note: You may already have authentication configured via Access Identity if you currently have an existing Access Evo (previously Access Workspace) organisation. As part of the pre-configuration checklist, you're prompted to reach out to your Access Evo administrator who should be able to confirm this. If authentication is already configured for your Access Evo organisation and your users, you don't need to review this article.

 

Access Identity definition

Access Identity is the authentication provider for Access Evo – Identity determines the security configuration, for example, password policies and timeout details to align with your organisation’s security policies, SSO configuration where required, and so on.
​
As all PeopleXD users are now customers of the Access Group, you too get to benefit from the security policies that we refer to as Access Identity.
​
This new login process is shared across the wide range of products offered by the Access Group and allows you to log into other products including Access Evo. 


Benefits of Access Identity

Security Policies: Govern your whole domain and the users in the organisation through a security policy. Control users' session lengths, authentication for all users in the domain, such as password length, CAPTCHA and failed sign in attempts.

SSO: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect supported services through Federation.

Users can enable two factor authentication to add an additional layer of security on their account.

Mixed authentication: This is available because Authentication type is configured at the organisation’s email domain level as a Security Policy, for example, a customer could be SSO for the @companydomain1.com users and native or local for their @companydomain2.com users. 

A security policy can be linked to multiple email domains, but an email domain can only be linked to one security policy. 

Impersonation allows you to grant someone else the ability to sign into Access Evo as you without them having to know your password with 

 

Authentication Types in Access Identity

To configure the required authentication type for each of your domains, review the relevant article below:

Native or local authentication.

Single sign on (SSO).

Two factor authentication:

Two factor authentication is available as standard with native or local Identity authentication.

The requirement to use two factor authentication is optional by default for a user. All users can enable two factor against their account. 

To make two factor authentication mandatory for users against that policy, you can enable the Identity Security Policy called Force Two Factor Authentication Required.


Email Domains and Security Policies

In Access Identity, details such as password policies and session timeout for users are configured against a security policy. 

The security policy is configured at the level of the organisation’s email domains. 

You can only link a security policy to an email domain that the company owns. Domains like gmail.com are not valid. 

At least one security policy must be configured to link to your domains. 

If a security policy is not linked to a domain, then a default security policy is used. 

The setup of the default security policy is detailed below and cannot be changed:  

Setting
	
Value



Users must sign in every

	

8 hours




Automatically extend the session if the user is active

	

Yes




Access Tokens expire after

	

1 hour




Failed sign in attempts before temporary lockout

	

3 attempts




Lockout duration

	

1 minute




Stay signed in option allowed

	

Yes




Allow Impersonation

	

Yes




Allow user reveal password when entering  

	

Yes




Validation method

	

Advanced




Require a strong password

	

Yes




Minimum password length

	

10




Use blacklist of known passwords

	

Yes




Passwords expire after

	

Never

title: Configure manual authentication
text:
If you use native authentication in PeopleXD and need to configure local or native authentication in Identity, for example, directly logging in using a username and password, follow the steps described in the table below.

📌Note: When you do not configure the manual authentication, the default Identity security policy applies to all users logging into Access Evo (previously Access Workspace).

Step number
	
Step name
	
Details



1

	

Identify your domains

	

Your domains are on the right-hand side of your email addresses after the @ symbol for your users. Usually, it's your company name followed by .com or .co.uk, for example, the email: test.test@companydomain1.com, the domain would be compaydomain1.com.
​
To complete the following steps, gather at least one email address from each domain you wish to register and ensure that you have the ability to test email messages with at least one user per domain that is to be registered.
​
If in doubt, your IT team should be able to support you with understanding what your domains are.




2

	

Identify who manages your domain

	

Typically, someone from your IT department has access to the domain DNS. You need to locate whomever can add a TXT record to this to verify ownership of the domain.




3

	

Identify who manages your authentication

	

Usually, your IT department manages your domain and associated security policies.




4

	

Register for identity

	

To register each domain with Access Identity, you need to register at least one email address per domain. To do this, go to https://identity.accessacloud.com/ or http://identity.eu.access-evo.com/ (EU hosted customers) and click Create New Account.
​
​Note: If you already registered with Access Identity due to using other Access products, when you click the link you can either enter your password or reset your password to access your Identity account if you have forgotten this.
​
You need to do this with one email per domain you wish to set up. Ideally, this person should be someone with administration rights in your business in case you need to come back and edit this later, such as a central IT team member. 
​
This is a once off task with one user per domain. 




5

	

Setup Security Policy or Policies

	

Once you've registered, you need your IT team or your domain manager to follow and complete the steps in our security guide once per domain.




6

	

Run a test

	

Once you have done this, sign out of Access Identity. To test your setup, go back to the homepage https://identity.accessacloud.com/ or http://identity.eu.access-evo.com/ and login again.




7

	

You're good to go

	

If you can do this and successfully get back to Access Identity, your domain is set up, and all users with the same email domain will be ready to login via the security policy you have created.

title: Access Evo: Members sync overview
text:
A number of employee or user data points or information items are synchronised between PeopleXD and Access Evo (previously Access Workspace).
​
This section details what the Members Sync between PeopleXD and Access Evo is, and how it creates and maintains Access Evo Member records based on the Employee records in PeopleXD where PeopleXD is the source-of-truth.

📌Note: Members represent Access Evo users.

 

PeopleXD user fields syncing with Access Evo

View the fields from PeopleXD that sync with Access Evo in the below table.

PeopleXD field(s)
	
Type
	
Tag
	
Description



Email Address

	

Conditional

	

 

	

PeopleXD only syncs with Access Evo if the contact type is EMAIL.

Note: When PeopleXD is in an Access Evo tab, email syncs by default. When PeopleXD isn't in an Access Evo tab, email doesn't sync by default.

Conditional

Job Title,

and Location

These fields become Access Evo members tags for the member record:

Job Title: Job Title Tag 

Department: Department Tag 

Location: Office Tag 

If the member tag reference data such as Business Analyst doesn't exist in Access Evo, it's automatically created. 

 

 

Already have Access Learning

If you already have Access Learning, to support the Auto-Assignment of Training Courses, up to five additional Org Structure items can be synced from PeopleXD.

 

This is configured as part of the PeopleXD and Access Learning integration via Hubble. 

 

View the organisation structures from PeopleXD that sync with Access Evo in the table below.

Description

Customisable

As per Org Structure Item 1 above.

 

 

Access Evo organisational role 

The sync will automatically assign the user role. You can edit the organisation role if the user requires administrator access to the Access Evo organisation. The roles available are as follows.

Role
	
Description



User

	

The User role is assigned to all employees to grant them access to Access Evo and allow them to log in.




XD Admin

	

The XD Admin role disables certain admin privileges on Access Evo, primarily to remove access to fields that should not be updated when XD is the source of truth.

 

Note: The XD Admin role is only available to PeopleXD in a tab customers.




Administrator

	

The Administrator role grants full access to Access Evo settings and privileges, this should be granted to super users.




Leaver

	

The Leaver role is assigned to users as part of the leaving process where you have leaver profiles set up to grant access after an employee's leave date.

 

Note: The Leaver role and process is only available to PeopleXD in a tab customers.  

 

 

Access Evo member status

The status life-cycle for Access Evo members is as follows.

Status
	
Description



Added

	

Members are initially set as added when the user has synced but is yet to log in.

 

Note: When PeopleXD is outside of a Access Evo tab, the added status is not applicable. Users are set as active when synced.




Active

	

Members become active once they log in for the first time.




Deactivated

	

Deactivated members are employees processed as leavers in PeopleXD with a leaving date in the past and/or an expired leaver profile. 
​
​Note: If you remove the leaving date, for example, in a re-joiner scenario, the member status is set to active.

 

 

Sync frequency

You have two types of sync, nightly and real-time.

 

Nightly sync

The sync runs nightly as a batch job. This supports syncing the records with Access Evo members where one of the fields has changed in PeopleXD since the last members sync.

📌Note: Employee records aren't synced if none of the fields that sync have changed since the last time the user record was synced.

 

Real-time sync

The following changes in PeopleXD trigger the sync to Access Evo members to happen in real-time.

Creation of employee records.

Creation of external user.

title: Configure single sign on (SSO)
text:
Access identity SSO is linked directly to a domain rather than to a user. Once a domain is set up for SSO, all users with email addresses that use that domain will be covered by the SSO.
​
Most companies have only one or very few setup steps, and your users, even those newly added, will not need to perform any steps to utilise the SSO path once the below is completed.

Step number
	
Step name
	
Details



1

	

Identify your domains

	

Your domains are on the right-hand side of your email addresses after the @ symbol for your users. Usually, it's your company name followed by .com or .co.uk, for example, the email: test.test@companydomain1.com, the domain would be compaydomain1.com.
​
To complete the following steps, gather at least one email address from each domain you wish to register and ensure that you have the ability to test email messages with at least one user per domain that is to be registered.
​
If in doubt, your IT team should be able to support you with understanding what your domains are.




2

	

Identify who manages your domain

	

Usually, someone from your IT department has access to the domain DNS. You need to locate whoever can add a TXT record to this to verify ownership of the domain.




3

	

Identify who manages your authentication

	

Usually, your IT department will manage your domain, and they're able to set up an OIDC endpoint to interact with Access Identity.
​
Common providers are ADFS and Azure AD for which we supply example steps, however, most authentication providers support this protocol.
​
Someone needs to be able to set this up for you. Ideally, this person should be someone with administrator rights in your business in case you need to come back and edit this later, such as the central IT team member. 




4

	

Register for identity

	

To register each domain with Access Identity, you need to register at least one email address per domain. To do this, go to https://identity.accessacloud.com/ or http://identity.eu.access-evo.com/ (EU hosted customers) and click Create New Account.
​
​Note: If you already registered with Access Identity due to using other Access Products, when you click the link, you can either enter your password or reset your password to access your Identity account if you have forgotten this.
​
You need to do this with one email per domain you wish to set up. Ideally, this person should be someone with administrator rights in your business in case you need to come back and edit this later.
​
This is a once-off task with one user per domain. Once set up is complete, all other users are automatically moved to Access Identity, without any impact on how they login in.




5

	

Setup SSO

	

Once you've registered, you need your IT team or your domain manager to follow and complete the steps in our federation document once per domain. The document details how to configure AD FS 2016 and Azure AD. The steps for other OpenID Connect Identity Providers will be very similar.
​
Regardless of your provider, however, the key fields that are required during setup will be the Authority URL, Client ID, and Client Secret.
​
Within the Federation document, this states you need to contact your account manager to enable the user federation, this is not applicable during this domain set up and you do not need to contact your account manager. 




6

	

Run a test

	

Once you have done this, sign out of Access Identity. To test your setup, go back to the homepage https://identity.accessacloud.com/ or http://identity.eu.access-evo.com/ and type your email address in. When you click next, you're automatically diverted to your internal authentication server and be able to authenticate yourself.




7

	

You're good to go

	

If you can do this and successfully get back to Access Identity, your domain is set up, and all users with the same email domain are ready to use SSO when you are migrated to identity.

 

FAQs

We answer the most common queries on SSO in the table below.

Question
	
Answer



What do we do if we don't have a company domain?
​ 

	

If you do not own a domain and user emails contain iCloud or Yahoo and so on, the users are unable to log in via the SSO mechanism. These domains need to log in with an Identity username and password.




Users are getting asked to login with email and password?

	

If users are asked to log in manually, double check with your IT team that the domains have been registered correctly.

title: Access Evo: Grant access to PeopleXD non-production environment
text:
📌Note: The following information is only related to organisations using PeopleXD in an Access Evo tab.

PeopleXD users created as part of your initial PeopleXD project solution can access your non-production PeopleXD environment through Access Evo. 

 

The UAT environment is accessed by clicking your company name/logo in the top-bar of Access Evo, which reveals the organisation drop-down menu.

 

There are 4 steps to this process, which are:

Create your PeopleXD employee: Typically, your employee record already exists in the UAT system. If that is not the case, you can complete this step in PeopleXD.

Create authorised non-production users: This simply highlights specific users as suitable for accessing your UAT environment. This step is completed in your PeopleXD non-production environment.

Assign PeopleXD Product Role in Access Evo: Ensure the Access Evo user has the PeopleXD product role. This step is completed in your Access Evo UAT environment.

Log-in to the non-production PeopleXD environment: Finally, log in to your UAT environment. This step is completed in your Access Evo UAT environment.

 

 

Create authorised non-production users

To set authorised users for non-production environment access, as a PeopleXD admin, follow the steps below. 

Navigate to the Evo Configuration widget on the Security dashboard in your non-production environment.

Click Authorised Non-Production Users.

🤓Tip: In this widget, you define the authorised users that should have access to non-production environments.

Click Add User, then select a user from the Person list.

Click OK. The user is now synced to your non-production Access Evo site. 

📌Note: A clone from your production environment to your UAT doesn't overwrite the list of authorised users.

 

 

Assign XD Product Role on Access Evo

To grant the newly authorised non-production user access to the PeopleXD product, follow the steps below. 

Navigate to your non-production Access Evo site, then click Members.

Search for the user, click the three-dot menu, then click Manage Roles.

Select User from the PeopleXD drop-down, then click Save Changes.

Send an Access Evo invite to the user in PeopleXD.

 

 

Log into the non-production PeopleXD environment

After the user has accepted the Access Evo invite, they can log into the non-production environment. To do this, follow the steps below.

Log into Access Evo as an authorised non-production user.

Expand the my organisations menu, located beside your Access Evo organisation name.

Authorised users now display the option to select a number of Access Evo sites, production (P) or non-production (U or C).

title: Access Evo: Sync reconciliation
text:
A sync reconciliation can be run to compare user records on PeopleXD and Access Evo, and flag the following discrepancies. 

Users with an email address on PeopleXD, that do not have a corresponding Email Type Member record on Access Evo.

Users identified as a username account on PeopleXD, that do not have a corresponding Username Type Member record on Access Evo.

Users that have an Email Type Member record on Access Evo, which has not been linked to a PeopleXD record.

Users that have a Username Type Member record on PeopleXD, which has not been linked to a PeopleXD record.

📌Note: If a sync hasn't been run before, you may need additional access.

 

 

Run the sync reconciliation

To run a sync reconciliation, follow the steps below.

📌Note: The table will be cleared down before each new run of the sync reconciliation so that only current data is returned.

Navigate to the Evo Configuration widget on the Security dashboard.

Click Open Evo Parameters.

Click Reconcile Sync.

A popup displays when the sync reconciliation was last ran, click OK to run the job.

 

 

Review the results in Insight

Once the reconciliation is complete, you can review the details by creating a report in Insight. To do this, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, select Insight.

Click Actions then click Create Report.

Enter the name of the report then click OK.

To add columns, click Add, then click Column.

From the Filter Columns by View drop-down menu, select Reconcile (Statistics)

Click the columns you would like to add to the report.

Click OK.

 

 

Columns available in the Insight report

The table below outlines the columns available in the Insight report.

Column name 
	
Description



Personnel No

	

Blank if an Access Evo record has not matched with a PeopleXD record.




Workspace Id

	

Unique ID between the PeopleXD and Access Evo record.




Date Updated

	

Date and time that the sync reconciliation was run.




Email Account Not In Ws

	

When Y, the user has an email address in PeopleXD but the record has not synced to Access Evo.




Username Account Not In Ws

	

When Y, the user is marked as a username account in PeopleXD but the record has not synced to Access Evo.




Email Account Not In Xd

	

When Y, an Email Type account exists in Workspace Members but has not been linked via email address to a record in PeopleXD.




Username Account Not In Xd

	

When Y, a Username Type account exists in Workspace Members but has not been linked via username/personnel number to a record in PeopleXD.




Error

	

Displays the error if a person has not synced from PeopleXD to Access Evo – i.e. if 'Email Account Not In Ws' or 'Username Account Not In Ws' are Y.

 

 

Common errors and solutions

The table below outlines common errors and solutions.

Error
	
Reason
	
Solution



You cannot assign a Reports to relationship to someone who is already under the hierarchy of this person.

	

PeopleXD attempts to sync an employee whose manager is below them in the hierarchy. This does not stop the sync but the user us synced without a manager.

	

Correct the reporting line PeopleXD.




forename.surname@domain.com already exists as a guest. Please invite them instead.

	

The user has already been set up on Access Evo as a Guest Member.

	

From Workspace Members, click Add, and chose 'Using an Email Address'. Enter the required details. Once this is completed an invite will be sent to the employee. By accepting the invite they will be added to your Access Evo organisation.




Cannot insert duplicate key row in object platform. User with unique index IX_User_EmailAddress_OrganisationId. The duplicate key value is (forename.surname@domain.com, a76a4258-ce08-4b5f-bf1a-230bc7da587a). The statement has been terminated

	

A member record with this email already exists on Access Evo.

	

Review the employee's email address and correct it. If the email address is correct on PeopleXD, then check for the email address on Access Evo, including deactivated members. If a deactivated record has the email address on Access Evo, then change the record to a username account on Access Evo to remove the email address from the deactivated record. Then, resync the employee from PeopleXD.




forename.surname@domain.com already exists within this organisation.

	

An email invite for Access Evo was attempted from PeopleXD for a user who has an email address that is already active on Access Evo.

	

As above for 'Cannot insert duplicate key row in object platform...'




Invalid status change

	

Usually occurs when PeopleXD tries to de-active an added member that has left the organisation. An added member is someone that has not activated their Access Evo account.

	

Delete the added user in Workspace Members. Also, raise a support ticket to remove the Access Evo record from PeopleXD.




Invalid email address

	

The format of the email address is incorrect - e.g. space in email.

	

Correct the email address in PeopleXD.




You must enter an email address which ends in @domain.com

	

Whitelisting is enabled on Access Evo and the user has an email address for a domain that has not been whitelisted.

	

Correct the email address in PeopleXD or add the domain to the organisation's whitelist via Avatar > Organisation Settings > Email Domain Whitelist.




Invalid user ID

	

PeopleXD is trying to sync a record but the workspace ID held on PeopleXD does not match a member record on Access Evo.

	

Raise a support case to remove the Access Evo record from PeopleXD and re-sync the record.

title: Copilot HR Documents plugin does not return policy documents
text:
When you ask Copilot a question about a company policy using PeopleXD Skills, it should retrieve information from your organisation's uploaded policy documents. If it returns a message such as ‘I couldn’t find specific information in the company documents’, or suggests you check with your HR department or manager,  one or more configuration issues may be preventing access.

The sections below explain the most common causes and how to resolve them.

 

Top causes

The following are the most common reasons Copilot may not return policy documents, listed from most likely to least likely.

 

The prompt is not specific enough to trigger the correct skill

Copilot uses automatic skill selection to decide which skill to use based on your prompt. If your question is too general, Copilot may not select PeopleXD Skills and will not search your organisation’s uploaded documents. 

For example, a prompt like "tell me about probation" may be too vague. A prompt such as "what is our company probation policy?" clearly indicates that Copilot should search company documents. To confirm this:

Check the skill label shown above Copilot’s response. If it doesn't say PeopleXD Skills, the HR Documents plugin wasn't used.

Rephrase your question to refer explicitly to company policies or documents.

Select PeopleXD Skills manually from the skill picker before asking your question. If Copilot then returns the expected document, the issue is related to automatic skill selection rather than the document itself.

 

No criteria group has been assigned to the document

Every policy document must have a criteria group assigned before it can be accessed by anyone through Copilot. Even if the document has been uploaded and saved, Copilot will not return it unless a criteria group is applied. 

🤓Tip: If the document should be available to all employees, assign a criteria group with no restrictive rules.

To assign a criteria group, follow the steps below:

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, then click Policy Documents.

Click the three-dot menu for the relevant policy, then click Criteria Groups.

Click Assign New Group, then select a criteria group from the dropdown list.

📌Note: If no suitable criteria group exists, you can create a new one.

 

The user does not meet the criteria group for the document

Criteria groups control which employees can access specific policy documents. If the user asking the question does not meet the criteria rules, such as company, department, or location, Copilot will not return the document.

 

To resolve this, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click Open, then click Policy Documents.

Click the three-dot menu for the relevant policy, then click Criteria Groups.

Note the criteria group assigned, then click Manage Criteria Groups.

Click the three-dot menu for the relevant group, then click Edit.

In the left-hand menu, review the criteria applied.

📌Note: Applied criteria are identified by a red circle showing the number of rules in use.

If the criteria exclude the user, update the existing group or create a new one.

⚠️Warning: Changes made to an existing criteria group apply wherever else it's used.

 

The document was not saved correctly after upload

When uploading a new policy document, you must click Save to trigger the indexing process. The Upload button in the actions menu is only used to re-index a document that has already been saved. 

 

To save the document correctly, follow the steps below:

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click Open, then click Policy Documents.

Click the three-dot menu for the relevant policy, then click Edit.

Click Upload, then click Click or drop files here to upload.

Select your document in the explorer window, then click Open.

Click OK, then click Save.

🤓Tip: Large documents may take additional time to process after saving. 

 

The document is in an unsupported format

The HR Documents plugin only supports .pdf and .doc file formats. Documents saved as other formats, for example, .docx, .xlsx, or .txt, are not indexed and cannot be found by Copilot.

 

Convert the document to a supported format, then upload it again using Policy Documents.

 

Required menu profile options are not active

The employee’s menu profile must include the required Copilot web service options. If any of these options are missing, Copilot cannot communicate with the HR Documents plugin.

 

Ask your system administrator to check that the employee menu profile includes all of the required Copilot web service options. Further guidance is available if required.

 

Temporary processing delay for large documents

Large documents can take over a minute to process after saving. During this time, the document may temporarily appear unavailable to Copilot.

 

If you recently uploaded a large document, wait a few minutes, then try your Copilot query again.

 

 

Troubleshooting checklist

Use the table below to check each possible cause. Start at the top and stop once you identify the issue. 

Check
	
What to look for
	
How to resolve



Is the correct skill selected? 

	

The skill label above Copilot’s response does not show PeopleXD Skills.

	

Rephrase your question to be more specific. To confirm, or select PeopleXD Skills manually before asking.




Has a criteria group been assigned?

	

No criteria group is linked to the policy document.

	

Assign a criteria group. Use a group with no rules to allow access for all users.




Does the user meet the criteria group?

	

The user’s contract details do not match the assigned criteria.

	

Review the criteria group and verify the user’s contract details.




Was the document saved correctly?

	

The document was uploaded but not saved using Save.

	

Edit the policy document, upload the file again, then click Save.




Is the document format supported?

	

The document is not a .pdf or .doc file.

	

Convert the file to a supported format and upload it again.




Are the menu profile options active?

	

Required Copilot web service options are missing.

	

Ask an administrator to review the employee menu profile.




Has enough time passed for processing?

	

The document was saved recently and is large.

	

Wait a few minutes, then try your query again.




Does the XD Assistant plugin work for this user?

	

XD Assistant queries work but HR Documents do not.

	

Focus troubleshooting on document upload and indexing.




Still unable to resolve the issue?

	

None of the checks resolve the problem.

	

Contact the support team for further assistance.

title: Access Evo impersonation
text:
Impersonation allows a user to grant someone else the ability to sign into Access Evo on their behalf, without sharing their password. 

 

As an organisation administrator, you can control whether impersonation is permitted across your organisation and restrict which users (internal and external) are able to request it, i.e. sign into your account.

 

When enabled at organisation level, all users can grant impersonation access to others.

📌Note: Only domain owners can access and edit the Security Policy setting described in this article.

 

Access your Security Policy

To access your Security Policy, follow the steps below.

Go to MyAccount then select Security Policy.

Locate the Security Policy already set up and attached to your domain.

Beside the relevant security policy, click Edit.

 

 

Enable impersonation for the organisation

Within the Security Policy, there is a setting called Allow impersonation. Once enabled, users within your organisation will be able to grant impersonation access to others via their own account settings. To do this, follow the steps below.

From the Security Policy edit screen, locate the Allow impersonation setting.

To make this option available to all users, turn on Allow impersonation.  

To save changes, click Save.

 

 

Setting up an impersonation whitelist

You can restrict impersonation by allowing only a defined list of users or email addresses to request access. Manage this setting from the Security Policy screen. To configure it, follow the steps below.

After enabling Allow impersonation, locate the Impersonation white-list field.

In the Impersonation white-list field, enter the email addresses or users you wish to permit.

To apply the changes, click Save.

📌Note: Only users on the whitelist can receive impersonation access from others in the organisation

 

 

Granting impersonation access (user steps)

Once impersonation is enabled at the organisation level, individual users can grant access. To do this, follow the steps below. 

In the top right-hand corner of the screen, click your name then select My Account.

You will be taken to the Manage your Access account screen in a new tab.

Under My Account, click Impersonations.

Under Add a new impersonator, fill the following fields: 

Email address: Enter the relevant email address.

Expires after:  Set the value to an appropriate timeframe.

To confirm, click Add.

 

 

Audit and login activity

📌Note: PeopleXD Audit does not explicitly identify when a session was accessed by an impersonator. 

 

However, the system records login activity, which you can review in PeopleXD Settings > Security (table: cp_portal_activity) or the Logon History view in PeopleXD Insights.

title: PeopleXD Evo administrator organisation roles overview
text:
When PeopleXD is synced with Access Evo, two distinct administrator organisation roles are available. Having two roles prevents accidental changes in Access Evo members that could create sync conflicts with PeopleXD, whilst ensuring Access Evo administrators can still manage platform settings, branding, and user access to products and features. 

 

For example, the ability to change email address is not available for an XD Admin as changes to member email addresses should come from PeopleXD to ensure that PeopleXD and Access Evo are kept in sync​. 

 

The two administrator organisation roles available are:

Access Evo Administrator: This role grants full access to manage all Access Evo platform settings, member records, and configurations.

XD Admin: This is a limited version of the Access Evo Administrator role that restricts access to member management actions.

 

 

PeopleXD organisation role comparison

The following table compares the capabilities of each role.

Action
	
Access Evo Administrator
	
XD Admin



Add Members

No

Yes (non-synced users only)

	

No




Manage user status

	

Yes (non-synced users only)

	

No




Assign tags to Members

	

Yes

	

No




Create and edit tags

	

Yes

	

No




View organisation hierarchy

	

Yes

	

No




Create and edit custom roles

	

Yes

	

No




Switch account type

	

Yes

	

No




Grant access to Access Evo products

	

Yes

	

No




Maintain Access Evo platform branding

	

Yes

	

No




Whitelisting domains for users

	

Yes

	

No

 

Synced employee data restrictions

For synced employees, the following fields sync from PeopleXD and must not be updated in Access Evo Members.

Forename

Surname

Email address

Reports to manager.

Job title

Department

Location

Status (active or inactive)

📌Note: If you have non-employee users accessing other Access Evo products, Administrators can add and manage these members without sync conflicts.

 

 

Assign an administrator organisation role in Access Evo

To assign a user either the Access Evo Administrator or XD Admin role, follow the steps below.

Log in to Access Evo then click the Members icon.

Search for the user, then click the three-dot menu.

Click Manage Roles.

From the Organisation Role drop-down menu, select Administrator or XD Role.

Click Save Changes.

 

Assign an organisation role in bulk

To assign a user an organisation role in bulk, follow the steps below. 

Log in to Access Evo then click the Members icon.

To select the relevant members, click the tick icon.

In the Actions menu, click Add then select Assign Organisation Role.

From the list, select an Organisation role then click Set Role. 

Click Apply.

title: View your product roadmap in Access Evo
text:
The Living Roadmap gives you direct visibility of what Access is building for your products. Available within Access Evo, it shows you the roadmap for every product in your licensed Product Suite, so you can see what has just been released, what is coming next, and what is planned for the future. You no longer need to wait for a scheduled review with your account team to find out what is in the pipeline.

 

You can also register your interest in upcoming features, putting yourself forward as a stakeholder in the development process or as an early adopter when a feature becomes available for preview.

 

What you can see

The Living Roadmap groups features into four categories for each product in your Product Suite:

General Release — features available to all clients now.

Preview — features available for early adoption before general release.

Coming soon — features currently in development.

Futures — features planned to start development within the next six months.

📌Note: Only products in your licensed Product Suite are shown. Contact your Access account team if you expect to see a product that is not listed.

 

 

View your roadmap

Open Access Evo.

Click the Access Button, then click the Living Roadmap icon.

 

 

Select a product to see its roadmap.

 

 

 

Register interest in a feature 

For features in Preview, Coming soon, and Futures, you can register your interest to be considered as a stakeholder or early adopter.

Open the Living Roadmap and select the relevant product. 

Find the feature you are interested in. 

Click Register interest on the feature. 

 

 

📌Note: Registering interest doesn't automatically enrol you in a preview or early adoption programme. The Access team will be in touch if you're selected.

 

 

Give a member of your organisation access to the Living Roadmap

You can control which members of your organisation can see the Living Roadmap through the Members section of Access Evo.

⚠️Important: You need the Access Evo Admin role to manage member access. If you do not have this role, contact your system administrator.

Open Members in Access Evo. 

Find the member you want to give access to and click the three-dot menu against their name. 

Select Manage roles.

 

 

Find Living Roadmap in the roles list and turn on access.

📌Note: Changes to member access take effect immediately.

text:

This feature is available to all clients. 

Access the Bank Details quick action

From the Navigator tab, select the Bank Details quick action.

Your bank details

title: Book leave in Access Evo Navigator
text:
The Book Leave quick action gives employees a self-service way to submit leave requests directly from the Access Evo Navigator tab. Leave requests are automatically routed to the line manager for approval through the existing XD Payroll workflow. The quick action has three tabs: Book Leave, Leave Requests, and Balances. 

This feature is available to all clients. 

Access the Book Leave quick action 

Log in to Access Evo Navigator. 

From the Navigator tab, select the Book Leave quick action. 

The Book Leave right panel opens on the Book Leave tab. 

Book Leave tab 

The Book Leave tab contains the leave request form. Complete the following fields to submit a request: 

Field
	
Required
	
Description



Select Appointment

	

Yes

	

Select the payroll appointment to book leave against. Employees with multiple appointments must select the relevant one. 




Leave Type

	

Yes

	

Select the type of leave. Available types are configured in XD and may include Annual Leave, Certified Sick, Flexi Leave, Jury Service Leave, Maternity Leave, Adoption Leave, and others. 




Day Duration

	

Yes

	

Select Full Day or Part Day. Part Day is only available when a single date is selected. 




Select Dates

	

Yes

	

Select the date or date range on the calendar. Use the arrows to navigate between months. The selected period is shown at the bottom of the panel. 

 

 

The calendar is colour-coded to show existing leave at a glance: Approved leave (solid green), Pending leave (amber), and Part-day leave (light green outline). The selected period is confirmed at the bottom of the panel before submission.

 

 

Submit a leave request 

On the Book Leave tab, select your Appointment and Leave Type. 

Select Full Day or Part Day, then select the date or date range on the calendar. Part Day is only available for a single date. 

Select Submit Request. The selected period is confirmed at the bottom of the panel before you submit. A confirmation message is displayed on successful submission, and the request is routed to your line manager for approval. 

Leave requests are synchronised with PeopleXD Payroll and routed automatically through the existing approval workflow. 

📌Note: All required fields must be completed before Submit Request becomes active. Available leave types are configured in PeopleXD by your payroll administrator and may vary. 

 

 

Leave Requests tab 

Select the Leave Requests tab to view your leave request history. Each request card shows the leave type, date, appointment, and the date it was submitted. Requests can be filtered by status using the tabs at the top of the list:

Pending — submitted and awaiting line manager decision.

Approved — approved by the line manager, with the approval date shown.

Taken — approved leave that has passed.

Rejected — declined by the line manager, with the rejection date shown.

Cancelled — requests that have been cancelled.

 

 

Balances tab 

Select the Balances tab to view your current leave balances. Balances display your total entitlement, leave taken to date, and remaining balance for each leave type. Balance information is drawn in real time from PeopleXD Payroll.

 

 

Menu options required

title: View, download, and upload your documents in Access Evo Navigator
text:
The My Documents quick action gives employees instant, self-service access to their personal HR and payroll documents from the Access Evo Navigator tab. Documents can be viewed in-app, downloaded, and searched or filtered. Visual indicators highlight new and unread documents. Employees can also upload documents where permitted. Document visibility and upload rights are controlled by PeopleXD permissions.

This feature is available to all clients.

Access the My Documents quick action

Log in to Access Evo Navigator.

From the Navigator tab, select the My Documents quick action.

The My Documents right panel opens on the My Documents tab, showing your full document list.

My Documents tab

The My Documents tab displays all your personal HR documents. Each document shows the file name, document type, and upload date. Documents marked with an Unread badge are new since your last visit. The following actions are available for each document:

Action / Feature
	
Description



View

	

Opens the document in-app without downloading. Supported file types include PDFs, images, and Office documents. Viewing a document marks it as read.




Download

	

Saves the document to your device. Downloading also marks the document as read.




Search

	

Use the search bar to find documents by file name. Results update in real time as you type.




Filter

	

Filter the document list by unread status (Show unread only) or by document type using the Document Types dropdown.




Sort

	

Documents are sorted by newest first by default. Use the sort control to change the order.




Upload Document

	

Select Upload Document to add a new document. Supported file types include all common formats up to 10 MB. You will be prompted to select a document type on upload.




Refresh

	

Select the refresh icon to reload the document list and check for newly added documents.

 The total document count and number of unread documents are shown at the top of the panel. Documents available to view and download are determined by your PeopleXD permissions.

Payroll Documents tab

Select the Payroll Documents tab to view payroll-specific documents such as P60s, P45s, and P11Ds.

Each payroll document shows its document name, document type (for example, P60), and tax year. Use the Document Type filter to narrow the list.

Select View to open the document in-app or Download to save it to your device.

Documents are retrieved from PeopleXD in real time. Document visibility and upload permissions are controlled by your organisation's PeopleXD configuration.

📌Note: Uploaded documents must be 10 MB or under. If a document you expect to see is not visible, contact your HR or payroll administrator — access is controlled by PeopleXD permissions.

The My Pension quick action gives employees instant visibility of their pension scheme details and contribution amounts, directly from the Access Evo Navigator tab. Your pension information

Field
	
Description

The name of the pension scheme.

Whether the scheme is Active or Inactive.

The employee's contribution shown as a Percentage, Per pay period amount, and Year to Date total.




Employer Contribution

	

The employer's contribution shown as a Percentage, Per pay period amount, and Year to Date total.




Additional Voluntary Contribution (AVC)

	

Any additional voluntary contribution shown as a Percentage, Per pay period amount, and Year to Date total.




Total Contributions (Year to Date)

	

The combined total of all contributions for the current year to date, highlighted in the card.




Scheme Start Date

	

The date the employee joined this pension scheme.




Last Updated

	

The date the pension record was last updated in XD.

Making changes to your pension

The My Pension quick action is a read-only view. No changes to pension scheme details or contribution rates can be made through Access Evo Navigator.

A Need Help? prompt is displayed at the bottom of the panel with guidance on who to contact for pension queries or changes.

text:
The Submit Clocking quick action gives employees a convenient way to record their working time directly from the Access Evo Navigator tab. The same validation rules as the native app are applied, ensuring consistency and accuracy in attendance records. Clock events sync immediately to the WFM time tracking system.

This feature is available to all clients.

Access the Submit Clocking quick action

The clocking form

Required?
	
Description

Yes

No

	

An optional free-text comment to add context or notes about this clocking entry.

If location services are unavailable on your device, a warning is displayed and the clocking entry will be registered without tracking your movement direction. Select Register Time to submit the clocking entry.

 

Register your time

In the clocking form, select your Appointment and Activity.

If applicable, tick Business Absence or Overtime, and add an optional Comment.

Select Register Time. The clocking entry is recorded with the current timestamp and synced to the WFM time tracking system immediately.

Clock events sync immediately to the WFM time tracking system. The same validation rules as the native app are applied — including scheduled shift checks, maximum hours, and duplicate prevention.

📌Note: Your Clocking History is displayed below the form. Filter by All, Today, or This Week to review recent entries. Each entry shows the clocking type (e.g., Register Time, Sign In), date and time, and any applicable tags such as Business.

title: Submit a request in Access Evo Navigator
text:
The Submit Request quick action gives employees a single, self-service portal to find and submit any organisation-defined form, directly from the Access Evo Navigator tab. Forms are configured in PeopleXD and may include requests such as career break applications, paternity requests, or hire car requests. Drafts can be saved at any time, and submitted forms route automatically through the existing PeopleXD approval workflow.

This feature is available to all clients. The forms available depend on your organisation's configuration in PeopleXD.

Access the Submit Request quick action

Log in to Access Evo Navigator.

From the Navigator tab, select the Submit Request quick action.

The Submit Request right panel opens on the Available Forms tab.

Available Forms and My Drafts

The Submit Request panel has two tabs:

Tab
	
Description



Available Forms

	

Lists all forms available to you, based on your permissions in PeopleXD. Use the search bar to find a form by name. Each form shows a Start Form button. Forms with a saved draft show a Continue Draft and Start New Form button, along with the most recent appointment context and when the draft was last saved.




My Drafts

	

Lists all your saved drafts with the form name, appointment context, and last saved date. The tab displays a count of saved drafts. Select Continue to resume a draft or delete it if no longer needed.

Forms are organised by category and listed alphabetically within each category. Only forms you have permission to submit are shown. The forms available depend on your organisation's PeopleXD configuration.

Complete and submit a form

On the Available Forms tab, find the form you want to submit and select Start Form. If you have a saved draft, select Continue Draft to resume it, or Start New Form to begin a fresh submission.

Complete the fields in the form. Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are required. Some forms include document upload fields or a confirmation checkbox. Select Save as Draft at any time to save your progress without submitting.

When ready, select Submit Request. All required fields are validated before submission. A confirmation message is displayed on successful submission.

Submitted requests are routed automatically through the existing PeopleXD approval workflow. Drafts are saved to your account and can be resumed at any time from the My Drafts tab.

📌Note: Some forms are contract-specific and will prompt you to select the relevant appointment before the form opens. Drafts are not validated on save — validation only runs on Submit Request. If a form is not visible, contact your HR administrator — form visibility is controlled by PeopleXD permissions.

Menu options required

To enable the Submit Request quick action, administrators have two options: 

 

Option 1 — Navigator Configuration screen

title: Action Required and Approvals in Access Evo Navigator
text:
Access Evo Navigator surfaces two related features for managing actions and approvals. The Action Required section appears on the Navigator dashboard and alerts employees and managers to items requiring their attention. The Approvals quick action gives managers a dedicated view to review and act on pending approval requests from their team. Both features retrieve data in real time from PeopleXD and are kept in sync automatically.

These features are available to all clients. Action Required cards and Approvals are displayed based on the user's role and permissions in PeopleXD.

The Action Required section

The Action Required section is displayed on the Navigator dashboard, between the Quick Actions grid and any quick sections. It surfaces items from the activity feed that require attention from the current user.

Each card in the Action Required section shows the priority level, the type of action (for example, Missed Clockings, Leave Requests), the number of items, a short description, and a View link. Selecting View opens the relevant quick action or system view to complete the action.

Action Required cards are generated automatically based on activity in PeopleXD. Current action types include missed clocking approvals, leave request approvals, expense approvals, employee form approvals, manager form approvals, and shift swap approvals. Additional action types will be added as new features are released.

The Approvals quick action

The Approvals quick action is available to managers and gives a dedicated view of all pending approval requests from their team. Select Approvals from the Quick Actions grid to open the panel. The panel shows the total count of pending approvals and a list of individual requests. Each approval card shows:

Item
	
Description



Employee name and avatar

	

The name and avatar initials of the employee who submitted the request.




Date

	

The date the request was submitted.




Request description

	

A short description of the request (e.g., Annual Leave request submitted. Action required.).




Type badge

	

Indicates the category of the approval request, such as Leave, Expense, Car, or Missed Clocking.




New badge

	

Displayed on approval requests that have not yet been viewed.

Use the Search by employee name bar to filter the approval list. Select any approval card to open the full Approval Details view.

Review and action an approval

In the Approvals panel, select an approval card to open the Approval Details view. Review the request information including the employee name, request description, Unrostered Hours, Appointment ID, leave or request type, Duration, Date, and Job Title.

If applicable, select View Unrostered Bookings to review any unrostered hours. Check any attached documents. Enter an optional Comment (maximum 500 characters).

Tick I confirm that I have checked the details, then select Approve or Reject. A confirmation message is displayed and the item is removed from the pending approvals list.

Approval decisions are written directly to PeopleXD immediately. The employee is notified of the outcome. The request status is updated in the relevant PeopleXD module, and the approved action — such as a leave booking, expense payment, or clocking correction — is processed through PeopleXD automatically. Access Evo Navigator and PeopleXD are kept in sync in real time: activity in PeopleXD generates Action Required cards in Navigator, and actions taken in Navigator flow back into PeopleXD for processing.

📌Note: The confirmation checkbox must be ticked before Approve or Reject becomes active. What appears in Navigator is determined by three layers: first-time content seeded by The Access Group based on role; org admin availability configured by your Customer Evo Org Admin; and product access control, which is the final filter. If a user does not have a licence or permission for the underlying PeopleXD product, the item will not appear in Navigator — regardless of persona or availability settings. The types of approvals displayed will expand as new features are released.

title: View your leave summary in Access Evo Navigator
text:
The Leave Summary quick section is a dashboard widget in Access Evo Navigator that surfaces key leave information in a single, convenient location. It displays upcoming leave, pending requests, and leave balances by leave type, all retrieved in real time from XD. This is a read-only view - to book leave, use the Book Leave quick action.

Panel
	
Description

Displays a Book Time Off button to navigate to the Book Leave quick action. Shows the Next Approved Leave date, leave type, and how many days away it is. Also shows summary counts for Upcoming Leave, Pending Requests, and Future Approved Leave. Select the arrow beside each row to see further detail.

Leave data is retrieved in real time from XD. Balances and request counts update automatically as leave is approved or taken. The Leave Summary is a read-only view — leave requests must be submitted through the Book Leave quick action.
