title: View your pay summary in Access Evo Navigator
text:
The My Pay Summary quick section is a dashboard widget in Access Evo Navigator that gives employees instant access to their key pay information in one place. It displays the latest payslip, rate of pay, next pay date, year-to-date figures, pension contributions, and a chart of recent payments. This is a read-only view — no changes can be made through this quick section.

This feature is available to all clients.

Access the My Pay Summary quick section

From the Navigator tab, select the My Pay Summary quick section.

The My Pay Summary dashboard widget opens, displaying a quick overview of your pay information.

What the My Pay Summary shows

The My Pay Summary is divided into the following sections:

Section
	
Description



Latest Payslip

	

Displays your most recent net pay amount, payslip date, and payment date, along with Gross pay and Expenses Recouped. Select the arrow to open the full payslip in the My Payslip Viewer.




Rate of Pay

	

Displays your current salary or rate of pay per annum, your pay frequency (e.g., Monthly), Full Time Equivalent (FTE), and Tax Code.




Next Pay Date

	

Displays the date of your next scheduled payment. Shows Not yet scheduled if no future payment date is available.




Year to Date

	

Displays cumulative figures for the current tax year: Gross Pay YTD, Tax Paid YTD, NI Contributions YTD, and Net Pay YTD.




Pension Contributions

	

Displays the Employee and Employer pension contribution percentage, current period amount, and YTD total. Shows the active pension scheme name, or None if no scheme is active. Select the arrow to open the My Pension quick action.




Most Recent Payments

	

A bar chart showing up to six recent payments. Each bar is split into net pay (teal) and total deductions (red), with the payment amount and date shown. When values are hidden, amounts display as dots and deductions are labelled Total Deductions: Hidden.

Select Show Details in the top right to reveal monetary values, which are hidden by default. Select Hide Details to mask them again.

Navigating from My Pay Summary

Select the arrow on the Latest Payslip card to open the full payslip in the My Payslip Viewer, where you can also access payslip history and download PDFs.

title: Access your PeopleXD Evo UAT environment
text:
Your PeopleXD Evo UAT environment gives you a safe space to test processes and validate changes before implementing them in your live system. Each PeopleXD instance syncs with a unique Access Evo organisation, giving you separate production and non-production environments with their own URLs.

📌Note: PeopleXD Evo UAT gives you access to the People XD solution only. Other products you have from the Access Group aren't available in the UAT environment, but Access Evo features like Copilot remain available for testing.

 

 

Switch between production and UAT environments

If you have access to both environments, you only need to sign in once through Access Identity to access both organisations. You can do this in two ways:

Go directly to your UAT URL, and you'll automatically sign in.

Or

Click your organisation name at the top of the screen.

From the drop-down menu, select your UAT organisation.

 

 

Manage UAT authorised users

You need to control who can access your PeopleXD Evo UAT organisation by designating them as UAT authorised users. This setting is managed in PeopleXD Security and ensures only approved team members can access the testing environment.

📌Note: External users can also be synced as UAT authorised users using the same approach.

 

To set up a UAT authorised user in PeopleXD Security, grant them user access and send them an invitation. To do this, follow the steps below.

Log in to your PeopleXD production environment.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Evo Configuration.

Next to Authorised Users, click Open then click Add User.

From the list, select the employee then click OK.

Check the user's Evo Member sync status displays as Synced.

Log in to your PeopleXD UAT environment.

Click the Members icon then search for the user.

Click the three-dot menu then select Manage Roles.

From the PeopleXD drop-down menu, select User.

Click Save Changes then on their Members record, click the three-dot menu.

Select Send the invite.

The user can complete their account setup and first-time sign in using the link in the invitation email.

 

Set up standalone test users

You can create standalone users in your UAT environment for testing employee process flows without designating them as UAT authorised users.

 

Follow the same process you use in your production environment to create a new employee in People Management. These test users don't need to exist in your production organisation and don't require UAT authorised user status.

title: Moving to Access Identity authentication
text:
Customers using SAML, AD, or LDAP 

If your organisation has been using SAML, AD, or LDAP authentication methods to log in to PeopleXD, you now need to configure SSO using OIDC in Access Identity.

 

Is OIDC secure?

Yes. Configuring SSO using OIDC in Access Identity is a secure authentication approach.

 

You're still connecting your PeopleXD login experience to your existing Identity Provider (IDP). Only the underlying protocol connecting to your IDP is changing.

 

The benefits remain the same:

Passwords never pass through Access Identity. Authentication happens with your IDP.

Encrypted connections protect all data in transit.

Your corporate security policies remain in effect.

You maintain centralised control over how your users access your systems.

 

What's different?

The key difference is that SSO configuration is directly linked to the domain of the email address for each user logging in. It's not a system-wide setting for all users.

Multiple domains: Configure a security policy per domain. This provides greater flexibility where you require different authentication policies for different domains.

You don't own a user's email domain: You can't force an SSO authentication flow if you don't own the user's email domain.

 

 

Customers using PeopleXD ESS

ESS login allows users to sign in with a username and password. When you move to Access Identity, this uses email and password as the standard login method.

Email: The system uses the EMAIL contact type stored for each user in PeopleXD.

Password: You can configure password policies based on each user's email domain. This provides flexibility when different domains need different authentication policies.

📌Note: You cannot enforce a specific security policy if you don't own the user's email domain.

 

Users without email addresses

You should capture email addresses for all employees who need to log in to PeopleXD. Email addresses enable the most secure authentication approach and support key features:

Joiners: PeopleXD Evo sends automated invitations directly to the employee's email address. Employees complete their account setup and verify their email address as part of this process.

Forgotten passwords: Employees can use the Forgotten Password feature on the login screen. The system verifies their identity during the password reset process, following your organisation's password policy.

 

If you cannot provide an email address for an employee, you can set them up as a username account. This provides a limited authentication experience:

The system doesn't send automated invitations. Administrators must manually sync the user to Access Evo, set a temporary password, and share the login details.

Employees cannot use the Forgotten Password feature. Administrators must manually set a temporary password and provide it to the user.

The system applies only the default security policy. You cannot enforce two-factor authentication or company-specific password rules for these users.

 

 

Customers using two-factor authentication via Twilio

When you move to Access Identity, you no longer need a Twilio account. Access Identity provides two-factor authentication as a standard authentication option with three methods:

SMS: Users receive a token by SMS to their registered mobile number.

Authenticator app: Users complete a task in their chosen authenticator app.

FIDO2/UDF: Users authenticate using biometrics or a hardware security key.

You can configure your security policy to force two-factor or offer it as an option.

 

Forced two-factor authentication

Access Identity configures forced two-factor by email domain only. If your organisation has multiple domains, you can configure a security policy per domain. This gives you flexibility to apply different authentication policies for different domains.

⚠️Important: You cannot force a 2FA authentication flow if you do not own the user's email domain.

 

Opt-in two-factor authentication

Users can configure their preferred two-factor method from the Access Identity login screen. They can choose from all three of the available methods. 

 

 

Changes to self registration

Self registration in PeopleXD Security lets you control how you invite employees to complete their PeopleXD Portal account setup and enforce multi-factor authentication. 

 

When you use Access Identity to log in to PeopleXD Evo, the self registration feature is no longer required. Access Identity handles user invitations, verification, and multi-factor authentication.

	
How it's managed in PeopleXD Evo 



Invites

	

Access Evo manages user invitations directly and triggers them through the new joiner process in PeopleXD. You can create rules to define how and when you send invites.




Verification

	

Access Identity sends email invites to the employee's email address, including a link to complete their account setup. This process verifies the user as the account owner.




Multi-factor authentication

	

You define Access Identity security policies to control authentication for your users. You can configure two-factor authentication or single sign-on login flows to enforce multi-factor authentication for users. This is only possible where the user's email is based on a domain that you own.

You can apply IP restrictions to PeopleXD modules only, not to the Access Identity login page. Users can sign in to Access Identity, but if you've configured IP restrictions for a specific module, that module won't be available to the user.

 

Self-registration widget

The Access Evo invitation process replaces the self-registration widget. When you invite users through Access Identity, they receive automated email invitations to set up their accounts.

 

For more information, see our Access Evo invitation process guidance.

 

Security questions

Security questions, previously used in the self‑registration process, no longer apply. Access Identity uses email verification instead.

 

Integrity test

The integrity test showed the user’s account creation and setup details. You can now view all relevant information directly on the Manage Account screen in Access Identity.

 

Manage Portal Account screen

The following options in the Manage Portal Account screen are no longer relevant.

Tab
	
Details



General 

	

The General tab controlled account status (such as locking or deactivating users) and authentication type. Access Identity now manages these settings centrally.




Header 

	

The following header items relate to authentication now managed by Access Identity:

Two Factor.

Authentication.

Password Changed.

Password Expiration.

Login Status.

Actions menu.

CorePortal password policy

Access Identity manages password policies centrally. The CorePortal password policy applied only to accounts signing in directly to PeopleXD and is no longer required.

title: Changes to user management in PeopleXD Evo
text:
With the upgrade to PeopleXD Evo, user management now integrates with Access Identity. This changes how user accounts are created, how users log in, and how security is managed across your system.

 

User management integrates with Access Evo

User accounts are automatically created in PeopleXD Security from your employee records. You can continue to use the user management area to define system access through menu profiles.

 

User accounts automatically sync to Access Evo as member accounts, where Access Identity manages user authentication, including:

Login methods such as email and password, two‑factor authentication (2FA), or single sign-on (SSO) via OpenID Connect (OIDC).

Security policies such as session, authentication, and password management.

Forgotten password management, which users manage on the login screen.

 

 

Email address is the unique identifier

In PeopleXD Evo, the login experience uses email address as the verified unique identifier for each account holder.

 

As part of the update, all users sync to Access Evo with their email address as their new login ID. Users receive an email invitation to complete their first time login through Access Identity.

📌 Note: If a user doesn't have an email address, you can create a username account for them. However, this provides a limited authentication experience.

 

 

Automated email invites for account setup

Users are automatically created and invited by email to complete their PeopleXD account setup. How they complete their login depends on your Access Identity security configuration.

 

You can define rules in PeopleXD Security to control when the invites are sent and exclude groups if needed. 

 

You can manually resend invitations to any user who hasn't completed their setup, for example, if they can't find the original invite.

⚠️Important: The PeopleXD Security Self Registration feature is no longer applicable in PeopleXD Evo.

 

 

Accounts deactivate automatically for leavers

Subject to your existing leaver profile rules, a user's account is automatically deactivated when an employee is made a leaver.

 

By default, the employee's account becomes inactive the day after their leaving date.

 

If you use PeopleXD leaver profiles to provide access for a defined period after their leaving date, the employee can continue to log in until the end of that period. During this time:

They have access to their limited view of PeopleXD.

They have no access to other Access Evo products.

📌 Note: During your upgrade, only active employees sync to Access Evo.

 

 

PeopleXD employees sync as members

PeopleXD employees sync to their Access Evo members record. A member is the name of the user account for Access Evo. This ensures that if you use other Access Evo connected products, your employees already exist as users and only need their permissions updated.

 

If you already use Access Evo for another Access Group application, the PeopleXD user syncs to the existing member account using the email address as the unique identifier.

 

 

IP restrictions apply at module level only

PeopleXD Security allowed system-level IP restrictions. In PeopleXD Evo, restrictions apply only at module level. This means a user can log in to Access Evo but, if module restrictions are in place, they can't access the corresponding PeopleXD dashboards.

 

 

PeopleXD Security screens reflect Access Evo sync

Updates have been made to PeopleXD Security to reflect how user management aligns with Access Evo and Access Identity.

 

This includes:

New categories on the System Users screen for Access Evo users.

An updated user account view showing whether a user synced successfully, whether they completed account setup, and the option to resend their invitation.

Password policy profiles are no longer applicable to PeopleXD and are now replaced by Access Identity security profiles.

The Self Registration widget is no longer applicable and is replaced by the default automated invitation process for new users.

For more detail on PeopleXD Security features that no longer apply in PeopleXD Evo, read our additional guidance.

title: Log in after the PeopleXD Evo update
text:
After the PeopleXD Evo update is applied, employees must set up their Access Identity account details when they first log in.

 

Employees using email and password authentication

 

Complete your first login

Access Evo automatically sends you an email invitation containing a link to complete your PeopleXD Evo account setup. How and when you receive this email invitation depends on the rules set in PeopleXD Security during the update project.

 

To complete your first login, follow the steps below.

Open the Access Evo email invitation, then click the link.

On the Access Identity 'Set your password' screen, enter a new password.

📌 Note: If your company configured a security policy for the email domain, the password you set must meet those requirements.

Click Set my password.

Log in using your email address and new password.

Click the Access Button, then click Products.

Select a PeopleXD dashboard.

 

Subsequent logins

To log in to PeopleXD Evo after completing your first login, follow the steps below.

Go to your PeopleXD Evo URL.

Enter your email address, then click Next.

Enter your password, then click Sign in.

Open PeopleXD.

 

Troubleshooting
Issue
	
Guidance
	
Resolution



Invalid email address

	

If you see an 'Invalid email address' validation message on screen, you may be attempting to log in using your old PeopleXD username. Email address is now the required option. During your first login, your email address is pre-filled from the email invitation link.

	

Enter your email address instead of your old username.




Set password prompt on future logins

	

If you're prompted to set a password on future login attempts, you may have clicked the link in the invitation email again. This link is for account creation only and should not be used for subsequent logins to PeopleXD Evo.

	

Use your PeopleXD Evo URL for all future logins.




Redirect from old URL without following email invite

	

If you're redirected to the new URL from the old PeopleXD URL without using the email invitation, you cannot complete your login until you fully verify your account. You must use the link in the invitation email to set your password and complete your first login.

 

In this scenario, you will see the new login screen when you enter your email and click Next. On the password screen, there is no option to set a password, and you cannot proceed.

	

Complete your account setup using the invitation you received from Access Evo.

🤓 Tip: You can use the 'Forgot your password?' link at this stage. An email is sent with a link to reset your password. This only works if you've already been issued the invite to complete your account. Alternatively, your Access Evo administrator can resend the invitation email.




Additional setup tasks on first or future login

	

If you're prompted to complete additional setup tasks on first login or during a future login, your company has configured enhanced authentication options for your email domains.

	

Check with your IT team to see if this was requested by another team in your company. This can occur if another team is rolling out a new Access Evo-enabled product and has configured a more secure login.

 

 

Employees using SSO authentication

 

Complete your first login

The first time you log in to PeopleXD Evo, you must complete your account setup.

📌 Note: Access Evo automatically sends an email containing a link to complete your PeopleXD Evo account setup. How and when this email invite is shared depends on the rules set in PeopleXD Security during the update project. 

Open the Access Evo email invitation, then click the link.

In the IDP authentication screen, complete the required steps 

In Access Identity, enter your email address, then click Next.

Click the Access Button, then click Products.

Select a PeopleXD dashboard.

 

Subsequent logins

After your initial account setup, log in to PeopleXD Evo using your email address.

Go your new PeopleXD Evo URL, then enter your email address.

🤓 Tip: Using the domain provided in your email address, Access Identity directs you to the relevant SSO login flow.

Click Next and complete the authentication.

Open PeopleXD.

 

Troubleshooting
Issue 
	
Resolution



User is asked to provide a password

	

Check that you've provided an email address with a domain configured for your SSO security policy. If you're using a correct email domain and your Access Identity Security policy has been tested and verified, contact Customer Support for assistance.

 

 

Using the PeopleXD mobile app

When your organisation moves to Access Identity for login, the way you access the PeopleXD mobile app changes depending on whether you're already using the app or downloading it for the first time.

 

Current users of the app

Users logged in to the app

	

If you're already logged in to the PeopleXD mobile app when your organisation moves to using Access Identity, you can continue using the app without any immediate changes. You can still use your PIN or device biometric authentication to open the app.




Users logged out of the app

	

If you log out of the PeopleXD mobile app after your organisation migrates to Access Identity, you must use your Access Identity credentials to log back in.

 

The mobile app login process matches the browser version - for example, asking for an email and password or SSO authentication.

 

First-time logins

Existing PeopleXD users

	

If you're an existing PeopleXD user who hasn't downloaded or used the mobile app before, you must use your Access Identity credentials to log in to the PeopleXD app.




New PeopleXD users

	

When you're set up as a new user in PeopleXD, you receive an email invitation to complete your account setup.

 

If you open the invitation email on your mobile device and have downloaded the PeopleXD app, you can complete your first login directly in the app using your Access Identity credentials.

title: Sync PeopleXD to an existing Access Evo organisation
text:
Syncing PeopleXD to your existing Access Evo organisation unlocks unified platform capabilities. PeopleXD becomes your source of truth, automatically syncing starters, movers, and leavers to Access Evo. This means you only need to update permissions for your other products as required.

 

The benefits include:

Simplified administration: Other teams control access to their products without managing user setup, invites, or deactivation.

Seamless user experience: One login for all Access products with automatic onboarding and consistent navigation.

Common secure foundation: Unified security policies via Access Identity with centralised access control.

 

 

Plan for the integration

Before syncing PeopleXD to your existing Access Evo organisation, complete the following planning steps. 

Engage with existing Access Evo users.

Review and clean up user accounts.

Determine Access Evo organisation administrators.

Check Access Identity configuration.

Check if Evo features are enabled.

 

Engage with existing Access Evo users

Contact colleagues who already use Access Evo before scheduling the sync. When PeopleXD is synced, current users and administrators are impacted:

Employees see PeopleXD options in Access Button.

Administrators no longer add or deactivate accounts for joiners, movers, or leavers.

⚠️Important: Do not schedule the sync until you have consensus with existing Evo organisation owners.

 

Review and clean up user accounts

PeopleXD employee records automatically sync to existing Access Evo members based on email address. If the sync cannot match on email, a new member record is created.

 

We recommend you review the users already set up as Access Evo members and identify any clean up required before employees are synced from PeopleXD.

 

Consider the following:

Are users on email or username accounts?

Are there active accounts for leavers?

Are there different email addresses in use for the same person, for example, a personal email on Access Evo and a company email on PeopleXD?

 

Determine Access Evo administrators

Identify the right people or teams who should have administrator permission for your Access Evo organisation. We recommend you review this in line with your organisation's platform administration processes.

 

Consider the following:

Should the IT team take ownership of system configuration and user management?

Should the PeopleXD system owners take on this responsibility?

Can existing administrators retain that permission, or should they be set back to standard user permissions as part of this update?

 

Check Access Identity configuration

Your domains may already be configured in Access Identity based on your organisation's authentication requirements. If so, you do not need to configure this again. The existing configuration will be available to validate on the PeopleXD Evo UAT or non-production environment as part of the update project.

 

Alternatively, this may be an opportunity to upgrade your authentication. For example, users may be logging in today using email and password only, but you require SSO for PeopleXD. The project team supports this setup and validation.

⚠️ Important: Any changes you apply in Access Identity immediately impact existing Access Evo users.

 

Check if Evo features are enabled

The PeopleXD Evo update does not include the PeopleXD integration with Copilot AI Assistant or the feed. 

 

If Copilot AI Assistant or feed are already enabled on the Access Evo organisation, you can manage features in Members to restrict access to new users synced from PeopleXD.

 

 

Frequently Asked Questions

Check out the most common queries relating to syncing PeopleXD to an existing Access Evo organisation.

 

Are non-employee users supported?

Yes. If you need to set up a non-employee user on Access Evo, add them directly in Access Evo using the Add Member process. This is the current process your Access Evo administrators use whilst PeopleXD is not integrated.

 

How do I know if we have an existing Access Evo organisation?

If you are not already aware of this, do not worry. We will identify where an Access Evo organisation is already in place for your organisation, and provide specific guidance as to how this shapes the PeopleXD Evo update for you.

 

Can we update to PeopleXD Evo without connecting our existing Access Evo organisation?

We do not recommend this, as one of the primary goals of Access Evo is to simplify how you access your Access Group products. This means all of your products are connected on a single instance of Access Evo.

 

Multiple Access Evo organisations can create user experience issues:

Single url and log in: As there is a single Access Evo URL and log in, a user will have access to multiple Access Evo organisations, each with a different set of products. Users may think that they have lost access to particular products, not realising they need to switch organisations.

Manually switching organisations: Users need to recognise they are not in the correct Access Evo organisation, then switch to the correct one using the dropdown list.

Maintaining multiple sites: Ongoing management of multiple sites is subject to risk for example, new members could be added to the wrong Access Evo organisation.

title: Grant data access to user in People Analytics
text:
Access to data in People Analytics depends on a user’s existing People Management data access rights. However, administrators can grant additional access using criteria groups.

Understanding data access

In People Analytics, users have specific data access based on their roles. For instance, consider the following scenarios:

Jane's Access: Jane initially has access to departments A and B in People Management. By employing criteria groups, she is granted additional access to department C. As a result, Jane can now access departments A, B, and C within People Analytics.

John's Access: Initially, John has no access to People Management data. However, by using criteria groups, he gains access to department C. John can now access department C within People Analytics.

 

To apply additional data access to enhance user access, follow these steps: 

Create criteria groups 

Create a data acccess group and assign it criteria groups. 

Assign users to the data access group.

Criteria Groups 

To create and manage criteria groups, follow the steps below in portal.

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Click Data Centre.

Beside the People Analytics Configuration, click Open. 

Click the Data Access tab then click Actions. 

Click Manage Criteria Groups  then click Add.

In the Name field, enter a name then click OK. 

Select a reference data option from the left-hand menu.

Beside the relevant criteria, select the checkbox. 

To move the user to the Assigned column, click the right arrowicon.

Repeat for all required criteria.

Data access group 

To create a data access group, follow the steps below in portal.

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Click Data Centre.

Beside the People Analytics Configuration, click Open. 

Click the Data Access tab then click Actions. 

Click Create a Data Access Group. 

In the Group Name field, enter a name. 

From the Copy Data Access Group drop down menu, select whether to copy an existing group.

Click OK then click Assign Access. 

Select the Criteria Groups then click OK. 

Assign data access 

To assign users to the data access group, follow the steps below in portal. 

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Click Data Centre.

Beside the People Analytics Configuration, click Open. 

Click the Data Access tab then click Users. 

Beside the relevant user, select the checkbox. 

Click Assign Access.

Select Data Access Group then click OK.

title: Definition of each standard pay type
text:
Before you complete your pay type mapping it’s recommended to review the below table to better understand the People Analytics pay types available and how they map to total cost of workforce. 

People Analytics Pay Type

	

Description

	

TCOW Mapping (i.e. where a pay type/element rolls up into the TCOW Model)




Agency Costs

	

Agency costs are the monies paid to recruiting agencies for the sourcing or hiring activities they perform on behalf of the organisation.

	

Agency Costs > Workforce Events > Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Base Pay

	

Base pay is the regular compensation provided directly to employees for their work contribution to the organisation. Base pay describes the most common form of compensation paid to employees. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee base pay.

Examples of base pay include:

Salary

Hourly pay

Commission-based draw

	

Base Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Bonus

	

Bonus is provided as a reward for good performance.

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Commission

	

Commissions are a form of compensation where the amount paid is directly related to the achievement of set targets. For example, commissions are common in sales roles where a percentage of total sales is awarded as compensation for the work done. Commission costs are highly varied, and costs are only incurred for the results achieved.

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Contingent Workforce Costs

	

Contingent workforce costs cover the work of people who are not classified as employees and who do work on behalf of the organisation. These people are not on payroll and do not hold employment contracts directly with the organisation. These costs are often incurred through a 3rd party such as a staffing agency and cover work done by contract staff, temporary / agency staff, consultants etc.

	

Contingent Workforce Costs > Employer Costs for Labour > Labour Costs > TCOW




Employer Insurance And Taxes

	

Employer insurance and taxes are workforce costs related to taxes and insurance premiums that must be paid based on the workforce employed (e.g. unemployment insurance, payroll taxes, workers compensation insurance etc.).

	

Employer Insurance & Taxes > Employer Costs for Labour > Labour Costs > TCOW




Employer Pension 

	

Benefits relating to employer pension contributions.

	

Employer Pension > Benefits > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Health Benefits

	

Health benefits are the per employee costs directly associated with providing medical benefit cover to employees and their families. This includes all of the cost items related to providing insurance cover, either directly or indirectly, for medical events that happen to an employee. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee health benefits.

Examples of health benefits include:

Medical plan

Dental plan

Vision plan

	

Health Benefits > Benefits > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Long Term Incentive

	

Long-term incentive pay is the current cash value of any long-term incentives that have been granted to employees, and for which the employee is currently eligible. These are workforce costs related to incentives which payout over a time frame of longer than one year. This measure deals with the actual costs, not the calculated present value or projected future value of an item such as a share option or RSU. This measure represents only the monetary or equivalent value that is paid to or budgeted for an employee based on their long-term incentive eligibility. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee long-term incentive pay.

Examples of long-term incentives include:

Stock options

Restricted stock

Performance shares

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Other Supplemental Pay

	

Other supplemental pay are other unclassified compensation costs related to supplemental pay rewards.

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Other Variable Pay

	

Other variable pay are unclassified variable compensation costs relating to a non-fixed monetary rewards. (e.g. spot bonuses, etc.).

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Other Workforce Events

	

Other workforce events costs are unclassified workforce overhead costs associated with any events that impact employees (e.g. office relocation, employment related M&A costs, etc.).

	

Other Workforce Events > Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Overtime Pay

	

Overtime pay are workforce costs for that are paid for hours worked beyond the contracted working hours. Overtime costs will typically recognise these additional hours at an increased hourly rate e.g. 1.5x etc based on agreed overtime rules. There can be many different types of overtime pay and pay rates. Not all employees are eligible for overtime.

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Pay for Time Not Worked

	

Pay for time not worked are the workforce costs associated with time off for which the employer continues to pay the employee, or the monetary value which is provided in lieu of time off. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee pay for time not worked.

Examples of pay for time not worked include:

Vacation or holiday

Bereavement

Family leave

	

Pay for Time not Worked > Benefits > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Premium Pay

	

Premium pay are supplemental workforce costs for pay for employees who are eligible for a premium over and above the standard pay agreement. Premium pay can be awarded to workers who have achieved specialist skill sets or who are working in particular situations which require a temporary or conditional increase in pay.

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Recognition Overhead

	

Recognition program costs are workforce overhead costs associated with managing and/or outsourcing costs for internal recognition programs, not including supplemental pay (e.g. processing charges for rewards, vendor premiums, etc.).

	

Recognition Overhead > Workforce Events > Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Recognition Rewards

	

Recognition rewards are variable workforce costs associated with organisational recognition programs where employees will receive monetary rewards in recognition of specific achievements e.g. a gift card for £50 based on the amount of peer recognition received in a given period.

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Referral Cost

	

Referral costs are workforce costs associated with payments to employees for referring a successful candidate.

	

Referral Cost > Workforce Events -> Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Relocation Cost

	

Relocation costs are the hiring costs associated with moving employees from their current location to the location where they will be working. This can be attributed to new hires or employees who must change locations.

	

Relocation Cost > Workforce Events -> Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Workforce Allocations

	

Workforce allocations are workforce overhead costs for employee enablement items (e.g. IT tools and support expenses, HR programs and support, expenses, etc.).

	

Workforce Allocations > Workforce Overhead > TCOW

title: Insight and Analytics comparison
text:
People Analytics and Insight are both powerful tool you can use to analyse and better understand your data. The table below described the differences between each tool and when you would use them:
​

 

	

People Analytics

	

Insight 




Purpose

	

Aimed at exploring and extracting deeper insights from the data across multiple sources within a dashboard. The data is built up over time and modelled and stored in a way that supports exploration and drilldown without need for specialist BI knowledge by the user

	

Primarily designed to generate standardised, scheduled reports. These operational reports provide information on specific items like absence. Data is modelled in standard BI Views by business area.




Focus

	

Supports interactive exploration, trend analysis, forecasting, and strategic decision-making (e.g., predicting turnover trends, identifying cost-saving opportunities).

	

Provides an actual snapshot by summarising past data (e.g., payroll details, attendance records), and current data (e.g. headcount, payroll details, attendance records)




Decision Making

	

Empowers users to identify trends, forecast future outcomes, and make proactive, data-driven strategic decisions.

	

Offers a clear and concise view of what has happened, which is essential for supporting day-to-day operational activities 




Audience

	

Generally used by data analysts or decision-makers who need to delve into the specifics and trends of HR and payroll data.

	

Suited for a broad audience, including HR and Payroll staff and managers who need quick, reliable reports for checking/confirming information




Point in time analysis

	

Snapshots over time that are stored for comparison. For example, headcount numbers for specific points in time in the past as well as current. It is possible to look at data across different dimensions (e.g. time or by management unit) and drill down into the information.

	

Insight is limited to real-time/live data in some areas - for example, contract/hierarchy data is difficult to report on over time 




Routine Operations

	

 

	

HR administrators and payroll specialists use reporting tools to generate standardised reports such as monthly payroll reports, current headcounts,  absence reports and ad-hoc reports as required.




Transactional data

	

 

	

Managers rely on reports to view attendance records, or salary records, ensuring that they have a consistent and clear record of past and current activities.




Regulatory Compliance

	

 

	

Compliance officers use the preformatted reports to quickly verify that payroll and HR practices meet legal and regulatory standards. Insight can also be used to retrieve data to act as input to your statutory reporting requirements.




Data Exploration

	

HR analysts and strategic planners use analytics tools to drill down into data, identifying trends like turnover rates, hiring patterns, and cost fluctuations.

	

 




Forecasting and Decision Making

	

Analytics utilises models to based on past data to allow Senior management leverages these tools for predictive and what if insights, such as forecasting future staffing needs or assessing the financial impact of changes in payroll policy.

	

 




Custom Investigations

	

When specific questions arise—like understanding the drivers behind absenteeism—analytics tools allow users to perform ad hoc queries, segment data, and interact with dynamic visualisations to uncover patterns and actionable insights from the data.

title: Set default currency in People Analytics
text:
To set a default currency in People Analytics and add exchange rates for converting from your default currency to another, you need to select a default currency in portal.

 

Doing so will enable you to choose a default currency for displaying your payroll information. This is particularly useful if your PeopleXD solution processes payroll in both the UK (£) and Ireland (€).

Note: By default, the solution’s currency is set to GBP 

Default solution currency

To set a default currency, follow the steps below in portal.

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Click Data Centre.

Beside People Analytics Configuration, click Open. 

Click the Currency tab.

From the Select Default Currency drop-down menu, select a default currency.

Click Save.

Add Currency rates 

The solution employs a process called constant currency when converting values to a single currency. It uses only one exchange rate per currency for calculations, regardless of how many periods are involved. The exchange rates are based on the last day of the selected period in the Time picker.

 

The constant currency method effectively analyses cost changes over time. If varying exchange rates were applied, differences in values could arise from the fluctuations, which would not be visible in the analysis as they occur before display. By using constant currency, trends in costs and trend line slopes are represented through a consistent exchange factor, offering a clearer and more reliable view of cost changes between periods.

 

To add currency rates, follow the steps below in portal. 

From the dashboard menu, select People Management.

Click Data Centre.

Beside People Analytics Configuration, click Open. 

Click the Currency tab then click Add Exchange Rate. 

From the Currency drop-down menu, select a currency.

From the Currency Rate drop-down menu, select a currency rate. 

From the Date Effective drop-down menu, select a date( i.e the date the currency rate should apply) 

To apply all changes, click OK.

Note: For premier users, to ensure that People Analytics uses the exchange rate set in the PeopleXD configuration area, select Use admin default as your display currency in the Preferences tab of People Analytics.

title: Understanding standard pay types in People Analytics
text:
Before you proceed with the mapping steps, we advise you to review the table below. This table outlines the available People Analytics pay types and provides descriptions for each one. The TCOW mapping column shows how each pay type integrates into the TCOW model.

 

People Analytics pay type 

	

Description

	

TCOW Mapping (i.e. where a pay type/element rolls up into the TCOW Model)




Agency costs 

	

Agency costs are the monies paid to recruiting agencies for the sourcing or hiring activities they perform on behalf of the organisation.

	

Agency Costs > Workforce Events > Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Base pay 

	

Base pay is the regular compensation provided directly to employees for their work contribution to the organisation. Base pay describes the most common form of compensation paid to employees. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee base pay. Examples of base pay include:

Salary

Hourly pay

Commission-based draw 

	

Base Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Bonus 

	

Bonus is provided as a reward for good performance.

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Commission

	

Commissions are a form of compensation where the amount paid is directly related to the achievement of set targets. For example, commissions are common in sales roles where a percentage of total sales is awarded as compensation for the work done. Commission costs are highly varied, and costs are only incurred for the results achieved. 

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Contingent workforce costs 

	

Contingent workforce costs cover the work of people who are not classified as employees and who do work on behalf of the organisation. These people are not on payroll and do not hold employment contracts directly with the organisation. These costs are often incurred through a 3rd party such as a staffing agency and cover work done by contract staff, temporary / agency staff, consultants etc.

	

Contingent Workforce Costs > Employer Costs for Labour > Labour Costs > TCOW 




Employer insurance and taxes 

	

Employer insurance and taxes are workforce costs related to taxes and insurance premiums that must be paid based on the workforce employed (e.g. unemployment insurance, payroll taxes, workers compensation insurance etc.)

	

Employer Insurance & Taxes > Employer Costs for Labour > Labour Costs > TCOW




Employer pension 

	

 Benefits relating to employer pension contributions.

	

Employer Pension > Benefits > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Health benefits 

	

Health benefits are the per employee costs directly associated with providing medical benefit cover to employees and their families. This includes all of the cost items related to providing insurance cover, either directly or indirectly, for medical events that happen to an employee. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee health benefits.

Examples of health benefits include:

Medical plan

Dental plan • Vision plan  

	

Health Benefits > Benefits > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Long term incentive 

	

Long-term incentive pay is the current cash value of any long-term incentives that have been granted to employees, and for which the employee is currently eligible. These are workforce costs related to incentives which payout over a time frame of longer than one year. This measure deals with the actual costs, not the calculated present value or projected future value of an item such as a share option or RSU. This measure represents only the monetary or equivalent value that is paid to or budgeted for an employee based on their long-term incentive eligibility. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee long-term incentive pay. Examples of long-term incentives include: 

Stock options

Restricted stock

Performance shares 

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Other supplemental pay 

	

Other supplemental pay are other unclassified compensation costs related to supplemental pay rewards.

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Other variable pay 

	

Other variable pay are unclassified variable compensation costs relating to a non-fixed monetary rewards. (e.g. spot bonuses, etc.). 

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Overtime pay 

	

Overtime pay are workforce costs for that are paid for hours worked beyond the contracted working hours. Overtime costs will typically recognise these additional hours at an increased hourly rate e.g. 1.5x etc based on agreed overtime rules. There can be many different types of overtime pay and pay rates. Not all employees are eligible for overtime.

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Other workforce events 

	

Other workforce events costs are unclassified workforce overhead costs associated with any events that impact employees (e.g. office relocation, employment related M&A costs, etc.). 

	

Other Workforce Events > Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Pay for time not worked 

	

Pay for time not worked are the workforce costs associated with time off for which the employer continues to pay the employee, or the monetary value which is provided in lieu of time off. Use this metric to quickly see how much your costs are for employee pay for time not worked.

Examples of pay for time not worked include:

Vacation or holiday

Bereavement

Family leave 

	

Pay for Time not Worked > Benefits > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Premium pay 

	

Premium pay are supplemental workforce costs for pay for employees who are eligible for a premium over and above the standard pay agreement. Premium pay can be awarded to workers who have achieved specialist skill sets or who are working in particular situations which require a temporary or conditional increase in pay.

	

Supplemental Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Recognition overhead 

	

Recognition program costs are workforce overhead costs associated with managing and/or outsourcing costs for internal recognition programs, not including supplemental pay (e.g. processing charges for rewards, vendor premiums, etc.)

	

Recognition Overhead > Workforce Events > Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Recognition rewards 

	

Recognition rewards are variable workforce costs associated with organisational recognition programs where employees will receive monetary rewards in recognition of specific achievements e.g. a gift card for £50 based on the amount of peer recognition received in a given period.

	

Variable Pay > Direct Compensation > Total Rewards > Labour Costs > TCOW




Referral cost 

	

Referral costs are workforce costs associated with payments to employees for referring a successful candidate.

	

Referral Cost > Workforce Events -> Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Relocation cost

	

Relocation costs are the hiring costs associated with moving employees from their current location to the location where they will be working. This can be attributed to new hires or employees who must change locations.

	

Relocation Cost > Workforce Events -> Workforce Overhead > TCOW




Workforce allocations 

	

Workforce allocations are workforce overhead costs for employee enablement items (e.g. IT tools and support expenses, HR programs and support, expenses, etc.)

	

Workforce Allocations > Workforce Overhead > TCOW

title: Sync frequency of data transfer from PeopleXD to People Analytics
text:
The table below outlines the frequency with which data is transmitted to People Analytics from PeopleXD. This information is essential for understanding the timing of data updates and ensuring seamless integration between the two systems. 

Data transferred to People Analytics 

	

Timings




Daily Deltas i.e. difference between data in PeopleXD today versus yesterday

	

Updated once per day.

Data difference is calculated as: data before 00:00 UTC today minus data that was sent yesterday.

The job to send this data to People Analytics starts from 00:00 UTC

The cut-off time for all data will be sent to People Analytics is 05:00 UTC.




Data Mapping, i.e. data that you have mapped in data mapping 

	

Mappings are updated once per day. 

Any data mapped before 00:00 UTC will be sent.

Same timings as daily deltas above.

Historical changes follow this same process. 




Security: User Management and User Groups i.e. applying access given in user management and user groups.

	

 Updated immediately




Data access i.e. what employee data you see based on People Management access

	

Updated every 2 hours.

title: Review compensation decisions
text:
The admin review stage is available to admins only. During this stage, you evaluate managers' proposed compensation decisions, assess the budget impact, and ensure alignment with your organisation's pay philosophy before finalising changes. You must complete all tasks in the review stage before you can move the cycle to communication.

 

Run an impact analysis

Before reviewing or adjusting any compensation decisions, run an impact analysis. This combines all compensation decisions from the cycle with historical data to give you a complete view of the proposed changes.

 

The impact analysis reveals:

Effects on employee expectations and satisfaction.

Changes to compensation ratios across your organisation.

Overall budget utilisation and distribution.

To run the impact analysis:

Go to Cycles and open the relevant cycle.

Click the Review tab, then click Review compensation.

Click Begin impact analysis.

Wait for the analysis to complete. This may take a few minutes, depending on your data size. 

📌 Note: The export options on the analysis are not available until you run the impact analysis. If you cannot see them, click Begin impact analysis to generate the analysis first.

 

 

Understand budget analysis and outlier analysis

Once the impact analysis completes, two analytical views are available: Budget Analysis (BA) and Outlier Analysis (OA). 

Analysis
	
What it shows



Budget Analysis

	

Monitors budget utilisation across your organisation by comparing actual base pay expenditure against planned allocations. Tracks remaining budget capacity for each team to ensure financial targets are met.




Outlier Analysis

	

Reviews how closely pay decisions align with system recommendations, with detailed breakdowns by gender and ethnicity. Helps identify potential bias in decision-making and supports equitable pay practices.

Click the Budget Analysis or Outlier Analysis tab in the analysis panel to switch between views.

 

 

Review and adjust compensation decisions

Once the impact analysis is complete, you can review all manager-submitted compensation decisions and make adjustments where needed. If you defined a holdback budget during cycle setup, this becomes available to you during the review stage, giving you flexibility to make additional adjustments.

In the Review tab, review the Budget and Equity sections.

Click Show details to expand a section.

To review a specific task in detail, click View task to open the manager's view.

To see a full breakdown of flagged decisions for base pay, bonus, or equity, click Open breakdown.

Make any necessary adjustments using the available budget, including any holdback funds. 

⚠️ Important: Document your reasoning for any adjustments you make — you will need to provide justification for changes.

 

 

Export an analysis

You can export the budget analysis or outlier analysis as a file to share with senior stakeholders outside Pay Planner. Three formats are available: 

Format
	
What's included



PDF

	

Full budget analysis or outlier analysis as a PDF document.




PowerPoint — full analysis

	

Complete analysis as a PowerPoint presentation.




PowerPoint — visuals only

	

Key charts and visuals as they appear in the expanded view.

To export an analysis: 

In the analysis panel, click the Budget Analysis or Outlier Analysis tab depending on which analysis you want to export.

Click the download icon in the top right corner of the analysis.

Select your preferred format:

Download analysis as PDF — export the full analysis as a PDF document.

Download analysis as PowerPoint — export the complete analysis as a PowerPoint presentation.

Download visuals as PowerPoint — export the key visuals only as a PowerPoint file.

 

 

Finalise the review

Once you have completed your review and made any necessary adjustments, you can close the review stage and move the cycle to communication. 

Click Start communication.

Confirm that you want to proceed, then click Start communication again to open the communication stage.

title: Bonus plans in Pay Planner
text:
Bonus plans define how to calculate bonuses in your compensation cycles. Set up your bonus plan formula once in Pay Planner settings. It applies when you create a cycle that includes bonus as a pay type. You need Pay Planner admin access to do this.

 

Available bonus formulas 

Pay Planner supports five standard bonus formulas. Each formula applies selected performance factors as multipliers against the budgeted bonus. Employees receive their full bonus only when all performance targets are met.

📌 Note: If your formula includes team performance, you must set team performance targets when you create a compensation cycle. Apply a single percentage across all teams, or adjust each team individually.

Budgeted bonus × company performance × individual performance.

Budgeted bonus × (company performance × company weight + individual performance × individual weight).

Budgeted bonus × (company performance × company weight + team performance × team weight) × individual performance.

Budgeted bonus × company performance × (team performance × team weight + individual performance × individual weight).

Budgeted bonus × company performance × team performance × individual performance.

 

 

Configure a bonus plan

To set up your bonus plan formula, follow the steps below. Changes to your bonus plan apply to new cycles only. Existing cycles are not affected. 

From the dashboard menu, select Pay Planner.

Click Settings, then click Incentive plans.

Click the pencil icon on the Overall bonus calculation row.

Under Select formula, select the required formula.

If your formula includes weight factors, enter one value under Add weights.

📌 Note: The other value will fill automatically. Adding both weights together will total 100%.

Under Select the frequency of the bonus period, select the frequency.

To apply a prorated calculation, select the Employment start date checkbox.

📌 Note: This prorates the bonus based on eligible days worked. For more flexibility, for example to account for leave of absence, upload individual proration factors per employee when setting up a compensation cycle.

Click Save.

title: Create a compensation cycle
text:
To create a new compensation cycle for your organisation, watch the video or follow the steps below. 

 

Create a compensation cycle

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Pay Planner.

Complete the wizard using the guidance below.

Click Create.

Step
	
Actions

Setup

Set a Holdback Amount, to cover budget overruns if required.

Set your company's Target Achievement Percentage.

To apply custom proration factors to individual employees, go to the Upload individual proration data section and click Upload file. Upload a CSV file containing two columns: Employee ID and Factor. Use the Download template link to get the correct file format. The proration factor is applied to each employee's calculated bonus, allowing you to account for scenarios that start-date proration cannot cover, such as leave of absence. The maximum file size is 25MB.

title: Close a compensation cycle
text:
To finalise your compensation cycle in PeopleXD Pay Planner, you can share decisions with employees and integrate data back into PeopleXD during the Communication stage. In this stage, you can download personalised pay letters for employees and export compensation data for upload into PeopleXD.

 

To close a compensation cycle, watch the video or follow the steps in each section below.

 

Review or configure pay letters

Before you close your compensation cycle, you need to review or configure your pay letters. This allows you to personalise communications to employees about their compensation decisions.

Open the compensation cycle, then click the Essentials tab, then Pay Letters.

Click the Pay Letters tab.

Turn on the Use pay letters and Give managers access to pay letters toggles, as required.

Upload your pay letter(s) using either the pre-built template or your own custom pay letter.

 

 

Configure segmentation for pay letters

To send tailored communications to different employee groups, you can segment your pay letters.

Open the compensation cycle then click the Essentials tab.

Click Pay Letters then click Configure segmentation.

Select your segmentation criteria then click Recreate configuration.

Expand the segmentation list then, on a segment, click the three-dot menu.

Upload the appropriate template then repeat this for each segment.

Click Save.

 

 

Close your compensation cycle

After configuring your pay letters, you can wrap up your compensation cycle. To move to the communication stage so you can generate pay letters and export data, follow the steps below.

Open the compensation cycle, then click the Communication tab.

Click Wrap up cycle.

📌 Note: Managers and configured support users receive automatic email notifications when pay letters are ready.

If required, click the Pay Letters tab, then download the files.

Click the Export tab, then click Export data for all available files.

⚠️ Important: Review all exported files before uploading them to PeopleXD as elements such as reason codes may need to be updated.

Click Close cycle, review the warning, the click Proceed.

title: Complete compensation allocation tasks
text:
Managers are responsible for completing the compensation allocation process for the employees assigned to them. Additionally, if you have a manager as a direct report, once they have submitted their tasks, you need to review them.

 

During this process, you’ll review personalised guidelines made for each employee based on the combination of their company's pay philosophy and each employee's data. 

 

To complete compensation allocation tasks, watch the video or follow the steps below.

Review compensation decisions

If you're a manager, you need to review your team’s compensation recommendations before submitting them. To do this, follow the steps below.

Review manager compensation decisions

Before they submit, you can monitor their progress, make sure they’re on track, and offer support if needed. Once they’ve submitted, review and approve their recommendations. To do this, follow the steps below.

title: Assign access to Pay Planner
text:
You can customise the level of access users have to Pay Planner functionality in PeopleXD:

User Access: Grants access to the Pay Planner dashboard.

User Groups: Determines what is available to users within the solution.

 

 

User access

To provide a user access to Pay Planner, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to People Analytics Configuration, click Open.

Click the User Management tab.

Search for and select the relevant users.

Click the right arrow to move the users to the Selected Users column.

Click Save.

 

 

User Groups

Once you give a user access, you can assign them the relevant Pay Planner access. This uses user groups and determines what is available to users within Pay Planner.

 

The table below outlines what each user group gives access to.

User Group
	
Description



Admin User

	

Create and manage cycles you create or cycles shared with you. You can also view all cycles, reassign ownership, and close all cycles, even those you didn't create.




Manager User

	

View and manage tasks within your hierarchy that are assigned to you.




Support User

	

Support users have the same rights as managers and admins can add them to tasks to support managers. You can also assign them to any task, unlike manager users whom you can only assign tasks within their hierarchy.

To assign a user to a user group, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to People Analytics Configuration, click Open.

Click the User Groups tab.

In the Selected Users section, select a user group from the drop-down list.

Search for and select the relevant users.

Click the right arrow to move the users to the Selected Users column.

Click Save.

title: Add exchange rates to support conversions
text:
You may need to add exchange rates in PeopleXD to convert your default currency to another. For example, if you pay UK employees in pounds and Ireland employees in euros.

 

When converting values to a single currency, PeopleXD Pay Planner uses constant currency. This means it applies one exchange rate per currency across all periods, based on the last day of the period selected in the time picker.

 

Add currency rates

To add currency rates, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to People Analytics Configuration, click Open.

Click the Currency tab, then click Add Exchange Rate.

Select the relevant currency then enter the currency rate.

In the Date Effective field, select the date the currency rate should apply.

Click OK.

 

 

Validation steps

To ensure PeopleXD Pay Planner accurately identifies the correct currency and applies appropriate conversion rates, you need to complete the following validation steps for employees not paid via PeopleXD Payroll.

Create a company per currency.

Set the correct currency for each company.

Link each company to the relevant pay group.

Link each employee to the relevant pay group.

title: Set up budget segmentation
text:
The Budget screen is your starting point for controlling budget allocation across your organisation. You can segment your budget by location, cost centre, or a specific level of your organisation structure.

 

To learn how to segment your budget, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu search for and select Pay Planner.

Click the Settings tab, then click Budget.

Select attributes to segment your budget by, for example, Location.

Click Add budget segment.

Select options to add to this budget segment, for example, all the locations in a specific region.

Click Next, review your selections, then click Add.

Click the three-dot menu next to the budget segment, then click Rename.

Fill in the new name, then click Save, 

Repeat steps 4 to 8 for all budget segments required.

 

Once your segments are set, they’re automatically applied when you create a new compensation cycle.

📌 Note: Once you start creating segments, you can't change the attributes you're segmenting by without starting from scratch.

 

 

Select a budgeting method

When creating your compensation cycle in the setup stage, you can select how manager budgets are calculated. There are two options to select from:

Budget Method
	
Description



Uniform Budgeting

	

Is where each manager's budget is based only on employee base pay. For example, if a manager has two employees, one earning £50K and the other £100K, and the merit increase is 10%, the budget would be £15,000.

 

This method doesn't take performance or recommendations into account, meaning managers may end up over or under-budget based on actual recommendations.




Flexible Budgeting

	

Uses your pay philosophy recommendations to calculate each manager's budget. For example, a team of high performers may be allocated a larger share of the budget.

 

It's a more dynamic approach, but requires careful management to stay aligned with overall strategy.

title: Monitor and review compensation decisions
text:
As an administrator, you can monitor all allocation tasks in the cycle to track progress and ensure alignment with your organisation’s pay philosophy. Once all tasks are marked Ready for review, move the cycle to the review stage to assess managers' decisions, budget impact, and overall alignment before finalising changes.

Monitor manager tasks

Tab

Pay decisions

Key highlights

	

Review decisions that are highlighted as possible deviations or outliers from what the pay philosophy suggests, and see budget breakdowns by task.

Monitor the status and progression of each task. Click View Task to make adjustments or complete manager tasks, if required.

 

 

Review stage

The review process brings together all compensation decisions made during the cycle to give you comprehensive oversight and control.

🤓Tip: If you defined a holdback budget during cycle setup, this reserved portion of your total budget was intentionally withheld from manager allocation. During the review stage, this holdback budget becomes available again, giving you flexibility to make strategic compensation adjustments where needed.

  

Your main tasks during the Review stage are to:

Run an impact analysis to assess proposed changes.

Review all Compensation Decisions against budget and pay philosophy.

Make adjustments using available budget, including holdback funds.

Finalise the review to proceed to communication.

 

To review and finalise compensation decisions:

Open the compensation cycle, then click the Allocation tab.

Ensure all tasks have the status Ready for review.  

Click Start Review, then click Start Review to confirm.

Click Review compensation.

title: Integrate performance data with Pay Planner
text:
Pay Planner can receive performance data through two methods:

Automatic integration: When using PeopleXD Talent Management, performance data flows automatically into Pay Planner. The system pulls the final rating from Performance History directly into Pay Planner.

📌Note: If you use another area of the Talent Management solution to capture performance ratings (e.g. Talent Factors), you need to export a report from PeopleXD Insight and upload the results using Data Migration.

Manual upload: If you do not use PeopleXD Talent Management, you can upload performance data using the Data Migration facility. Two templates are available for performance data upload:

Performance Rating File

Employee Performance File

 

 

Download Data Migration templates

To download the data migration templates required, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Migration Templates.

Search for Performance Rating File, then click the 3-dot menu.

Click Download Helper, then click Download Template.

Open the Performance Rating File on your device and fill in the fields.

🤓 Tip: Refer to Helper File for guidance on how to fill in the template.

Repeat steps 2-4 to download and complete the Employee Performance File.

 

 

Upload completed templates

Once the templates are complete, you can upload them into PeopleXD.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Migration Options.

Click Load File, then upload the Performance Rating File.

Select Process All Records, then wait for the status to update to Complete.

Repeat steps 1-3 to upload the Employee Performance File.

📌 Note: The Performance Rating File must be uploaded before the Employee Performance File.

title: Security: Portal password reset parameters
text:
A user resetting their password can be verified in the system in a number of ways. To configure these options, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, enter and select Security.

text:
This section details the key security changes when PeopleXD is in Access Evo: 

System Users widget.

Self Reg widget.

System users widget  

User accounts are now managed via Access Evo Members.  


Filters

Filter
	
Change

Manage account

​

Menu profile widget: Portal Users label changed to PeopleXD Users. 

Content Security Policy tab and widget: Label changed to PeopleXD Content Security Policy.

Password Policy widget: Still available on the Security Dashboard. This is required for back office password policies and Portal policies for the Flightpath standalone UAT solution. The password policy in PeopleXD does not apply to Identity accounts.

title: Manage user accounts
text:
The Security dashboard allows you to create and manage user accounts for PeopleXD. You can create portal accounts, reset passwords, lock or unlock accounts, and configure authentication settings.

 

 

Access the Security dashboard

To access the Security dashboard and manage user accounts, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click the User Management tab.

The System Users widget displays all user accounts.

 

 

Search for a user account

To find a specific user account, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the System Users widget, in the Search users field, enter the username.

From the drop-down menu, to refine your search, select  any of the filters: 

Filter
	
Description



All Active Portal Accounts

	

Portal accounts that are currently active.




All Portal Accounts

	

All portal accounts, including inactive accounts.




Logged In

	

Users currently logged in to the portal.




Logged Out

	

Users not currently logged in to the portal.




Locked Out

	

Users currently locked out of the portal.




Two Factor Not Enabled

	

Accounts without two-factor authentication.




Older Password Algorithm

	

Accounts using an older password algorithm.




DB Schema Linked Accounts

	

Accounts linked to the database schema.

 

 

View user account status

The Current Status widget on the System Overview tab displays a snapshot of all portal user account statuses.

 

To view users by status, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click the System Overview tab. 

On the Current Status widget, click VIEW beside one of the following:

Status
	
Description



Logged In

	

Users currently logged in. You can click LOG OUT to force a user to log out.




Locked Out

	

Users locked out due to invalid login attempts, manual locking, or system lockout.




Logged Out

	

Users not currently logged in.




Yet To Log In

	

Users with accounts who have never logged in.

 

 

 

Create a new portal user account

To create a new portal user account, watch the video or follow the steps below:

⚠️ Important: Link all employee accounts to their corresponding employee record. This ensures users see the correct information on the Employee Dashboard, Manager Dashboard, and other areas.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the System Users widget, click CREATE NEW USER.

From the User Type drop-down menu, select Portal.

In the Username field, enter a Username. Checks username availability.

Enter a Password that meets your organisation's password policy requirements.

To configure the account immediately, turn on the Manage Account on creation toggle.

Click OK.

From the drop-down menu, select an employee to link the portal account to an existing employee record.

Click OK.

 

 

Set a user's authentication type

The authentication type determines how a user logs in to PeopleXD. To set the authentication type, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the System Users widget, search for the user.

Beside the relevant user, click the three-dot menu. 

Click Manage Account. 

On the General tab, from the Authentication Type drop-down menu, select one of the following:

Basic ESS Authentication: Username and password are stored on PeopleXD and are subject to the COREPORTAL account profile password policy.

LDAP - OID Authentication: Username and password are managed via LDAP, such as Microsoft Active Directory, for single sign-on.

Changes save automatically.

📌Note: For users created through self-registration, the authentication type is set automatically based on the self-registration profile.

 

 

Reset a user's password

To manually reset a user's password, watch the video or follow the steps below:

To manually reset a user's password:

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the System Users widget, search for the user.

Beside the relevant user, click the three-dot menu. 

Click Manage Account then click Reset Password.

In the New Password field, enter a password that meets the COREPORTAL account profile requirements.

Click OK.

📌Note: The user can log in with the new password but will need to change it on their next login.

 

 

Lock or unlock a user account
Lock user account

To lock a user account and prevent access, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the System Users widget, search for the user.

Beside the relevant user, click the three-dot menu. 

Click Manage Account.

On the General tab, turn on the Locked toggle.

 

Unlock user account

To unlock a user account, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the Manage Portal Account screen, turn off the Locked toggle.

📌Note: A user account will be locked if the user exceeds the maximum number of allowed invalid login attempts set in the password policy, or if all users are locked out using the Lock System feature.

 

 

Activate or deactivate a user account

A user account will need to be active to log in to PeopleXD. For users who have left the organisation deactivate accounts.

 

Deactivate accounts

To deactivate a user account, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the System Users widget, search for the user.

Beside the relevant user, click the three-dot menu. 

Click Manage Account then on the General tab, turn off the Active toggle.

Reactivate accounts

To reactivate a user account, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

On the Manage Portal Account screen, turn on the Active toggle.

System
	
Menu option

User Management - Update.

title: Custom email invites on PeopleXD Evo
text:
You can customise the invitation emails sent to new users on PeopleXD Evo.  This allows your organisation to control messaging, branding, and tone during onboarding, rather than using the standard Evo invite.  Make sure the correct permissions are assigned to the admin profile.

 

Required permissions

The following web service permissions must be enabled:

WS_SYSTEM_MENU.PATCH_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_INVITE_CUSTOM

WS_SYSTEM_MENU.GET_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_INVITE_CUSTOM

Enable custom invites

To start using custom invitation emails:

Go to Security > Evo Configuration > Evo Invites

Turn on Enable custom invites

 

What happens next

Once enabled:

New users are automatically synced as active

Invitation emails are sent from your XD instance

Users receive your custom email instead of the default Evo template

Configure your custom invitation email

Set up the content and messaging of your invite.

Go to Security and click Evo Configuration.

Click Evo Invites.

Click Actions and select Custom Email Invites.

Enter an email subject (required).

Enter the email body (required).

Personalise your email

You can include dynamic fields that automatically populate user details:

<<PERSONNEL_NO>> — personnel number

<<FORENAME>> — first name

<<SURNAME>> — last name

🤓Tip: Use these fields to create a more personalised and engaging onboarding experience.

⚠️Important: The Evo invite link is automatically added to the end of your email body—you don’t need to include it manually.

Send invitation emails

Invitations can be triggered in two ways.

Manual bulk send

Go to Security > Evo Configuration

Select Bulk Send Invites

Automatic overnight job

The system runs a scheduled job each night

Invitations are automatically sent to eligible users

How invite sending works

Invites are only sent to users who have not already received one

This applies to both manual and automatic sending

⚠️ Important: Users will not receive duplicate invitations.
