title: Set up username accounts
text:
Username accounts allow employees to access PeopleXD Evo when a verifiable email address isn't available. However, email accounts are strongly recommended as best practice for authentication, security policy compliance, and self-service account management.

 

Active employees with email addresses on PeopleXD automatically sync to Access Evo Members. If an employee doesn't have an email address on their record, they don't sync automatically.

 

To set up a username account, an administrator must sync the account manually, set a temporary password, and email the login details to the user.

 

 

Username account limitations

Username accounts have the following limitations:

Users cannot manage their own password resets:  Access Evo administrators must set temporary passwords for account creation or when a user forgets their password. This creates additional administrative overhead for IT teams.

Cannot apply company security policies: Security policies manage user authentication and session management, and are defined based on email domains. If a user doesn't log in with an email address, only the Default Security Policy in Access Identity can be applied.

 

 

Set up a username account

 

Sync the employee as a username account

Log in to PeopleXD.

From the dashboard menu, search for and click Security.

Click User Management, then select Non-Synced Accounts from the list.

Search for the employee, then turn on the Username toggle.

Click the three-dot menu, then select Manage Account.

Click Run Sync, then click OK.

Log in to Access Evo, then click Members.

Search for the employee's name to confirm the sync is complete.

📌Note: If successful, the account displays with a username symbol and their username is their Personnel Number.

 

Set a temporary password and send to the employee

Log in to Access Evo, then click Members.

Search for the employee then click the three-dot menu. 

Click Change Password, then fill in the details.

On the confirmation screen, enter the temporary password you created.

Click Copy to copy the following:

Organisation URL

Username

Temporary password

Use the copied text to send the employee their login details.

📌Note: When the user logs in, they are prompted to change their password.

 

 

Switch from a username account to an email account

You can switch a username account to an email account by adding an email address to the employee's HR record in PeopleXD. When you update the email address, the Members Sync process automatically runs for that record:

The email address syncs to the Access Evo Member record.

The Access Evo account type updates to Email.

An invitation email is automatically sent to the user to complete their email account verification.

title: Set up a security policy - SSO via OIDC users
text:
Creating a security policy for your domain impacts all users who log in to Access Evo with an email address for that domain. If you have users actively logging in to Access Evo already, plan for this as part of your setup, testing, and rollout of the SSO login flow.

📌Note: Your organisation's identity provider must support OpenID Connect and be publicly available via HTTPS.

 

Before you begin, gather the following information from your identity provider:

Authority URL: The base web address for your authentication server.

⚠️Important: Do not include extra paths such as "/auth" or ".well-know/openid-configuration".

Client ID: Your unique Client ID generated on your identity provider when you register Access Identity as an authorised application.

🤓 Tip: If you use Entra ID:

Client ID is referred to as “Application ID”.

Authority URL will be https://sts.windows.net/ followed by your Entra Directory (tenant) ID e.g. https://sts.windows.net/178a7f3e-c149-48f5-85fe54a80e26e734.

 

 

 

Register Access Identity as an authorised provider with your identity provider

Before you can configure Access Identity, you need to register Access Identity as an authorised application with your identity provider. This tells your identity provider that Access Identity is an application you trust to connect to.

 

Your IT team needs one of the following Redirect URIs to complete the registration.

UK Redirect URI: https://identity.accessacloud.com/auth/oidc/callback

EU Redirect URI: https://identity.eu.access-evo.com/auth/oidc/callback

 

Once complete, your IT team can provide you with the Authority URL and Client ID you need for Access Identity configuration.

 

 

Create your Access Identity account

Your Access Identity account gives you access to the administration panel, where you manage domain verification and security policies. This is separate from your regular PeopleXD access.

⚠️ Important: At least two administrators from your organisation need to complete this process. If you only have one administrator and they leave the organisation or loses account access, you won't be able to manage authentication settings or security policies.

 

To do this, follow the steps below.

Open the Access Identity link relevant to your hosting location:

UK customer: https://identity.accessacloud.com/

EU customer: https://identity.eu.access-evo.com/

Click Create a new account then enter your work email address.

Complete the reCAPTCHA verification then click Sign up.

Open the verification email then click the link to verify your email address.

Create a password for your account and complete your login.

 

 

Create and test your security policy

You can create a security policy and apply it to the domain. This applies the policy to all users with email addresses from that domain.

Sign into your Access Identity account:

UK customer: https://identity.accessacloud.com/

EU customer: https://identity.eu.access-evo.com/

From the menu, click Security Policies then click Add Security Policy.

Enter a name for your policy then enter the owners' email addresses.

Select your verified domain.

In the Federation section, provide the settings that connect Access Identity to your single sign-on provider:

From the Identity provider list, select OpenID Connect.

Enter an Identity provider name. This is for display purposes in Access Identity only.

From the Grant type list, select the method that your OIDC compliant identity provider uses to return information to Access Identity. 

If you select Authorisation Code, fill in the Client secret.

Fill in the Authority URL. This is the base web address for your authentication server provided by your identity provider.

Fill in the Client ID. This is your unique Client ID generated on your identity provider when you register Access Identity as an authorised application.

Click Test these settings.

📌Note: If your OIDC identity provider has been correctly configured, you are directed to your provider's sign-in screen.

 

 

Set up and verify your domain

Domain verification ensures that only your organisation can create security policies for your email domain.

 

Add your domain

Sign into your Access Identity account:

UK customer: https://identity.accessacloud.com/

EU customer: https://identity.eu.access-evo.com/

From the menu, click Domains then click Add Domain.

Enter your organisation's domain name. For example, yourcompany.com.

To save changes, click Save.

 

Add domain owners

We recommend you add at least two domain owners per domain to avoid any risk of losing access to your configuration. This gives them full access to manage a domain.

From the menu, click Domains then click the relevant domain name.

In the Owners field, fill in the relevant email addresses.

Click Save Changes.

 

Verify your domain

You need to add a Domain Name System (DNS) record to your domain hosting provider or DNS management system to prove you own the domain. Your domain's DNS management system is typically managed by your IT department's DNS management portal, your domain registrar, or your hosting provider.

From the menu, click Domains then copy the verification code.

Open your DNS management system then fill in the TXT record information:

Host: @

Type: TXT

Value: The verification code you copied from Access Identity.

Return to the Domains screen in Access Identity then click Verify Domain.

📌Note: DNS changes can take up to 24 hours to propagate, though they often complete within an hour. You may need to wait before verification succeeds.

 

 

Assign the security policy to your domain

Once you have the configuration in place and have confirmed that it works by performing a test, you can add it to your domain. This setting applies to all users who log in with an email address for that domain. Once enabled, this updates their login flow.

🤓Tip: Take care to plan for this and communicate changes to existing users if required.

From the menu, click Domains then in Verified domains, click the relevant name.

Select a security policy from the list then select the Enable federation checkbox. 

Click Save Changes.

 

 

Enable your domain

Once you're ready, you can enable your domain. This applies the configuration to all impacted users.

From the menu, click Domains then in Verified domains, click the relevant name.

Select the Enable checkbox then click Save Changes.

 

 

Complete SSO setup

⚠️Important: This step is only required if you are moving from standalone PeopleXD to PeopleXD Evo using Access Identity for the first time.

Let your contact in Access Group know that you are ready to apply the changes to your environment. This is a standard step in a PeopleXD Evo update project, and your project team guides you on when this occurs and engages the required team in Access to update your system configuration.

title: Set up a security policy - email and password users
text:
Security policies in Access Identity let you control how users access your PeopleXD system using email and password authentication. You can configure session timeouts, authentication requirements, and password rules that apply to all users from your verified email domain.

 

Before you set up a security policy, you need to:

Have an Access Identity account with appropriate administrator rights.

Register at least two administrators as domain owners to ensure continuous access to authentication controls.

Have access to your organisation's DNS management system to verify domain ownership.

 

 

Create your Access Identity account

Your Access Identity account gives you access to the administration panel where you manage domain verification and security policies. This is separate from your regular PeopleXD access.

⚠️ Important: At least two administrators from your organisation need to complete this process. If you only have one administrator and they leave the organisation or loses account access, you won't be able to manage authentication settings or security policies.

UK Customer: https://identity.accessacloud.com/

EU Customer: https://identity.eu.access-evo.com/

Click Create a new account, then enter your work email address.

Complete the reCAPTCHA verification, then click Sign up.

Open the verification email, then click the link to verify your email address.

Create a password for your account, and complete your login.

 

 

Set up and verify your domain

Domain verification ensures that only your organisation can create security policies for your email domain.

 

Add your domain

Sign into your Access Identity account:

UK Customer: https://identity.accessacloud.com/

EU Customer: https://identity.eu.access-evo.com/

From the menu, click Domains.

Click Add Domain.

Enter your organisation's domain name, for example, yourcompany.com.

Click Save.

 

Add domain owners

We recommend you add at least two domain owners per domain to avoid any risk of losing access to your configuration. This gives them full access to manage a domain.

From the menu, click Domains.

Click the relevant domain Name.

In the Owners field, fill in the relevant email addresses.

Click Save Changes.

 

Verify your domain

You need to add a DNS record to your domain hosting provider or DNS management system to prove that you own the domain. Your domain's DNS management system is typically managed by your IT department's DNS management portal, your domain registrar, or your hosting provider.

From the menu, click Domains.

Copy the Verification Code. 

Open your DNS management system, and fill in the TXT record information:

Host: @

title: Configure automated invites
text:
When you set up a new joiner in People Management with an active email address, PeopleXD Evo automatically sends them an email containing a link to complete their account setup. This saves time for the HR team, removing the need to manually share the PeopleXD Evo URL and login instructions.

📌Note: The system doesn't send invitations for username accounts. You also need to whitelist the Evo invite IP address: 74.91.88.107

 

PeopleXD Evo processes email invitations as part of an overnight job and issues invites based on employee start dates. 

You cannot change or define the sync time for the overnight job.

You can configure the system to send invites on the employee's start date or before their start date.

You can manually force emails to be sent to a user before the overnight process where there is an urgent need.

 

 

Types of invitations

You can choose between a default Access Evo invite or a custom email invite:

Default Access Evo invite: This is a standard non-configurable email issued from Access Evo. The sender is noreply@accessacloud.com.

Custom Email Invite: You can configure your organisation's own invitation, including the subject and body. The sender is noreply@accessacloud.com.

 

 

Create a custom email invitation

To create a custom email invitation, follow these steps.

 

 

Set up automatic invites

To set up automatic invites, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Evo Configuration.

Next to Evo Invites, click Open then click ACTIONS.

Select Custom Email Invites then turn on the Enable automatic invites toggle.

If required, turn on send invites to future starters.

🤓Tip: By default emails are sent on the employee's start date. Turn on this option to send invites to future starters.

If required, fill in a start date trigger.

📌Note: If no value is set, invites are sent to all employees with a start date before and including today's date. If you set a value, such as 2, invites are triggered for all employees with a start date in the previous two days.

Click Save.

 

 

Restrict automatic invitations 

By default, invitations are sent to all new joiners. If there are groups of users that should not automatically receive an email, you can create a restriction rule using criteria groups. Invites are sent only to employees who are part of the defined criteria groups.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Evo Configuration.

Next to Evo Invites, click Open then click ACTIONS.

Select Restrict Email Invites then click ADD.

Enter a name for your group then from the left-hand menu, select the required reference data.

From the Available list, select the required values. 

Click the right arrow to move the criteria to the Assigned column.

Repeat steps 5 to 7 as required.

 

 

Send invitations manually

Where there is an urgent need to send an invite for a new joiner before the overnight job processes them, you can issue the invite manually to the user. 

 

You can also send invitations in bulk. This is typically used as part of a new implementation of PeopleXD Evo to push invites to all employees to complete their first time login to the system. 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Evo Configuration.

Next to Evo Invites, click Open then click ACTIONS.

Select Bulk Send Invites then click OK.

 

 

Troubleshooting
User hasn't received an invitation email.

If a user hasn't received their invite email, check the following:

Is their email address correct?

Are they excluded due to the setup of the Restrict Email Invites configuration?

Is their start date in the past, greater than the days set in the Start Date Trigger setting?

Has the email gone to a spam folder?

title: Manage system lockout
text:
The Lock System feature allows you to temporarily prevent all users from logging in to PeopleXD. This is useful during maintenance periods or when you need to restrict access to the system. 

 

You can set the system to unlock automatically after a specified time or unlock it manually. To do this, follow the steps below in Portal.

 

 

Lock the system

To lock all users out of PeopleXD, watch the video or follow the steps below.

📌 Note: During a lockout, users can access the login screen but see the lockout message when attempting to log in. Users on the exemption list can log in without issue.

From the dashboard menu, select Security. 

Click the System Overview tab.

On the Current Status widget, click LOCK SYSTEM.

Review the message that confirms your exemption status:

If you are not an exemption, you will be locked out and unable to log in to unlock the system.

If you are an exemption, you can continue to log in while the system remains locked.

Configure the unlock settings:

To enable automatic unlocking, turn on the Automatically Unlock toggle then in the Hours to Remain Locked field, enter the number of hours.

To require manual unlocking, turn off the Automatically Unlock toggle.

In the Lockout Message field, enter a message that will display to users who attempt to log in during the lockout.

Click LOCK SYSTEM.

Once locked, the Current Status widget will display the following:

Setting
	
Display



Manual unlock

	

Locked – Never Expires.




Automatic unlock

	

Locked – Expires [DATE] @ [TIME].

 

 

Unlock the system

To manually unlock the system, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, select Security. 

Click the System Overview tab.

On the Current Status widget, confirm the status displays Locked.

Click UNLOCK SYSTEM.

The system unlocks immediately, and all users can log in.

📌 Note: You can manually unlock the system at any time, even if the Automatically Unlock toggle is turned on.

 

 

Manage system lockout exemptions

Exemptions are user accounts that can log in while the system is locked. Add users to the exemption list before locking the system to ensure they can continue to access PeopleXD and unlock the system if required.

 

Add an exemption

To add a user to the exemption list, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, select Security. 

Click the System Overview tab.

On the Current Status widget, click LOCK SYSTEM.

Click the Exemptions tab then click ADD EMPLOYEE.

From the Person drop-down menu, select the user.

Click OK.

The user appears in the exemption list and the number on the Exemptions tab updates to reflect the total number of exempt users.

 

Remove an exemption

To remove a user from the exemption list, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, select Security. 

Click the System Overview tab.

On the Current Status widget, click LOCK SYSTEM.

Click the Exemptions tab.

Beside the user you want to remove, click REMOVE.

The user is removed from the list immediately.

 

 

Menu options required

To manage system lockout, users require the following menu options:

Menu option
	
System



System - Product Lockout

	

Security

title: Configure product access and security settings
text:
The Security dashboard provides additional settings to control product availability, IP address restrictions, content security policies, and user session management.

 

 

Configure product access restrictions

The Product Access Restriction Options widget allows you to control access to products in PeopleXD. You can disable products globally or restrict access to specific IP addresses.

⚠️Important: Do not update this widget without first contacting PeopleXD.

 

Enable or disable a product

To enable or disable a product for all users, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Under the Product Access Restriction Options widget, locate the product.

To enable the product, turn on the Available toggle.

To disable the product, turn off the Available toggle.

Changes apply to all users immediately.

 

Restrict a product by IP address

To restrict a product to specific IP addresses, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click the System Overview tab.

On the Product Access Restriction Options widget, beside the product, click VIEW.

Click Add then enter the IP Address or IP Address Range.

Click OK.

📌Note: Only users with a specified IP address can access the product; all other users will be denied access.

 

Remove an IP address restriction

To remove an IP address restriction, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click System Overview.

On the Product Access Restriction Options widget, beside the product, click VIEW.

Locate the IP address then click Remove.

 

 

Manage content security policy

By default, content hosted outside of PeopleXD cannot be viewed or embedded. This includes custom video pages used in features such as Social Onboarding. 

 

To display external content, you need to add the source to the Content Security Policy widget. 

 

To add a content source, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click XD Content Security Policy then click EDIT.

Add the required source URL to the appropriate key:

media-src:  For media content such as videos.

img-src: For images.

frame-src:  For embedded frames.

To save changes, click Save.

📌Note: Contact your security or technical team for guidance on the required sources for your content. If a source is not listed, the content will be blocked.

 

 

View user sessions

The User Sessions widget displays information about Back Office user sessions, including login history, connection details, and locked sessions.

To view user sessions:

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click the User Sessions tab. The widget displays all sessions.

You can use this widget to do the following: 

Identify redundant accounts.

Identify accounts where passwords are about to expire.

Identify locked sessions.

Kill sessions that are locking the database.

 

Lock all user accounts

To lock all back office user accounts, follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click the User Sessions widget then click Actions.

Click Lock All Accounts.

 

Unlock all user accounts

To unlock all back office user accounts,follow the steps below. 

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click the User Sessions widget then click Actions.

Click Unlock All Accounts.

 

 

Menu options required

To configure product access and security settings, users require the following menu options:

Menu option
	
System



• System - Product Access

• View Content Security Policy

• Update Content Security Policy

• User Session - View Only

• User Session - Update

	

Security

title: PeopleXD Evo members sync overview
text:
Members sync automatically creates and maintains Access Evo user accounts for your employees. When you set up a new employee in PeopleXD, their Access Evo member record is created automatically. When an employee leaves, their Access Evo account is deactivated based on your leaver rules.

 

 

How members sync works

PeopleXD is the source of truth for your employee records. Members sync transfers employee data from PeopleXD to Access Evo in one direction only. Changes made to member records in Access Evo don't sync back to PeopleXD.

 

 

How this supports other Access Evo applications

When you connect other applications to Access Evo, employees already exist as users. You don't need to set up and invite users again to the system. You just need to update their access to provide permissions to the other applications.

 

When an employee leaves, their record is automatically deactivated on Access Evo. This removes the risk of forgetting to revoke access for other applications they can access through Access Evo.

 

 

What data is synced

Members sync transfers these data points from PeopleXD employee records to Access Evo member records:

Email

Forename

Surname

Reports to manager

Job title

Department

Location

Status

You can't change which data points are synced. The list is pre-defined and not configurable.

 

 

When data is synced

Members sync runs at different frequencies depending on the type of update.

Frequency
	
What gets synced



Real time

	

New starter setup, including future hires

External user setup

Change of email address




Nightly

	

Changes to:

Forename

Surname

Reports to manager

Job title

Department

Location

📌Note: Only updates to the synced data points trigger a sync to Access Evo. If you update a non-synced field, such as category, this doesn't create a record sync for the employee.

title: Create external users in PeopleXD Evo
text:
If PeopleXD access is needed for someone who is not a company employee, such as a contractor or auditor, you need to create them as an external user. 

 

External users are created in PeopleXD Security and automatically sync with Access Evo Members as username accounts.

 

To do this, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select External Users.

Click CREATE EXTERNAL USER, then fill in the following details:

Username

Forename

Surname

Password

Click Save.

📌 Note: Creating an external user syncs to Access Evo members in real-time.

 

 

Share login details with the user

You need to share the account information with external users manually, as automated invitations are not available. After creating the external user, share the following details with them directly:

The PeopleXD Evo URL

Their username

Their password

📌Note: If the user forgets their password, you need to manually reset it in Access Evo members.

 

 

Revoke access for an external user

To revoke the access for an external user, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select External Users.

Search for the user, then click the three-dot menu.

Click Drop/Delete User.

title: PeopleXD People Management: HESA 2025/26 Release Notes
text:
This release includes the software changes required for the 2024/25 Higher Education Statistics Agency (HESA) Staff Collection. 

 

Schema Change Updates Provided by Access
C25025.xsd (Schema)

Reordering of the C25025.xsd file so that the position of Contract.REFUOA2029 to conform with the HESA standard for XML schema ordering.

 

Person.Nation (Schema)

Valid entry 97 (Not known) has replaced ZZ (Not Known) and related guidance updated to reflect this.

 

Person. PREVHEI (Schema) 

Valid entries updated to reflect new providers and name changes.

 

Person.PARLEAVE (Valid) 

Valid entries have been updated to include 6 'Neonatal care leave' and associated guidance has also been updated. 

 

 

Non-Schema Changes – Customer Requirement

Please note there are non-schema changes outlined by HESA for the Staff 20245/2026 that can be found here, that will require your attention and require you to update your reference data within the HESA module to reflect new coding and label changes for the fields that HESA has outlined above.

 

Person.PARLEAVE (Valid)

📌Note: This is a non-schema change but we included it as part of the Access changes to add the entry (6 'Neonatal care leave').

 

You can manage these updates within the HESA module within the HESA Record Type screen, highlight the field in question, and then select the HESA Reference Data item from the Options menu. You can start updating your HESA field reference data to align to the latest coding changes outlined.

  

 

Action Required

Please review the 2025/26 HESA Staff Collection specification changes published by HESA and assess the impact on your PXD HESA solution, i.e. what needs to change to ensure that your Staff Collection return meets the new requirements/specification.  These changes will require updates to PXD configuration & data which must be completed by each HE Provider.

 

 

How this version will be made available

This release will be applied as part of PeopleXD Automatic Patch 28.0.149.

Non-Production Release Date: 15 April 2026.

Production Release Date: 22 April 2026.

 

 

Additional information

Please refer to the following for additional information:

PeopleXD HESA User Guide.
